q.e: The common city pigeon is the rock dove (Columba livia), also called the rock pigeon. City pigeons descend from domesticated birds that escaped.

q: Dinosaurs lived during which geologic era?

q.e: Dinosaurs lived throughout the Mesozoic Era, which spanned from about 252 million to 66 million years ago and includes the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods.

q: The word dinosaur is a combination of two Greek words. One word means lizard. What does the other word mean?

q.e: The term dinosaur was coined in 1842 by English paleontologist Sir Richard Owen from the Greek deinos, meaning terrible, fearsome, or terrifying, and sauros, meaning lizard.

q: The name brontosaurus is derived from the Greek words sauros, which means lizard, combined with another word. What does the word bronte mean?

q.e: "Brontosaurus" means "thunder lizard", from the Greek "bronte" (thunder) and "sauros" (lizard). It's the name of a long-necked sauropod.

q: In the 1980s, who voiced the character of Dino, the pet dinosaur in the animated series The Flintstones?

q.e: Mel Blanc, the voice of Bugs Bunny and Barney Rubble, also provided Dino's yapping on The Flintstones. After his death in 1989, others took over.

q: In the book Jurassic Park, the fictional island Isla Nublar, where recreated dinosaur species live, is situated in which part of the world?

q.e: In Jurassic Park, Isla Nublar is an island off the west coast of Costa Rica, in the Pacific. The island is fictional.

q: The BBC series Walking with Dinosaurs, which won three Emmy Awards, consisted of how many parts?

q.e: Walking with Dinosaurs (1999), a BBC series, had six episodes and used CGI and animatronics. It won Emmy awards.

q: What kind of celestial body is the 9949 Brontosaurus?

q.e: 9949 Brontosaurus is an asteroid in the main belt, named after the dinosaur. Asteroids are given names once they're numbered.

q: What is the meaning of the term Triceratops, referring to a dinosaur genus discovered in 1888 in North America?

q.e: "Triceratops" means "three-horned face", from Greek words. It lived in North America around 68-66 million years ago.

q: Which one of these dinosaurs was bigger than a dog?

q.e: Triceratops was huge, around 9 m (30 ft) long and weighing up to 12 tons, much bigger than a dog. Some small dinosaurs, such as Compsognathus, were turkey-sized.

q: How many fingers did the Tyrannosaurus rex have on its forelimbs?

q.e: Tyrannosaurus rex had two clawed fingers on each tiny forelimb. Though short, its arms were strong.

q: Which one of these statements about the Seismosaurus, the Earth-shaking lizard, is wrong?
Its hind legs were shorter than its front legs.
It could reach 33 meters in length.
It was recognized as a species in 1991.

q.e: Seismosaurus (now thought to be Diplodocus hallorum) had longer hind legs than front legs, like other diplodocids. It was named "earth-shaking lizard".

q: Elephants express joy by spinning in circles, trumpeting, roaring, screaming, urinating, and flapping their ears. In which of these cases will an elephant not act this way?
after the death of an elderly elephant
when meeting a friend (elephant or human)
after the birth of a new baby elephant

q.e: Elephants show strong emotions, including grief. They have been seen mourning dead herd mates.

q: How many individual muscles are in an elephants trunk?

q.e: An elephant's trunk has about 40,000 muscle bundles and no bones. It can pick up a peanut or uproot a tree.

q: In Islamic history, 570 A.D. was The Year of the Elephant. Which of these happened in that year?
The Qur'an was written in book form

q.e: 570 CE is traditionally known as the "Year of the Elephant" in Islamic history, when an Abyssinian army with an elephant attempted to attack Mecca. It's also the traditional year Muhammad was born.

q: The elephant is a good swimmer.
The elephant is a good jumper.
The elephant is not a protected species.
An elephants skin is 2.5 inches thick.

q.e: Elephants are good swimmers and use their trunks as snorkels. They can swim for long distances.

q: This reef, that extends along the east coast of Australia, is home to countless animals and is considered one of the wonders of the natural world.

q.e: The Great Barrier Reef stretches for more than 1,400 miles (2,300 km) off the coast of Queensland in northeastern Australia and is the largest coral reef system on the planet.

q: Which of these animals is NOT native to Australia?

q.e: The dingo isn't native to Australia, since it arrived with humans about 3,500-4,000 years ago. Kangaroos, koalas and wombats are native.

q: What does the word Triceratops mean?

q.e: Named by Othniel Charles Marsh, Triceratops comes from the Greek words tri (three), keras (horn), and ops (face).

q: In what year was Triceratops first discovered?

q.e: Triceratops fossils were first found in 1887-1889 in Colorado and Wyoming, and O.C. Marsh named the genus in 1889. It's one of the best-known dinosaurs.

q: In what year was the Praying mantis placed on the Endangered Species List?

q.e: Praying mantises are ambush predators that eat other insects. Some species and populations are protected in certain areas.

q: What is the meaning of the name Stegosaurus?

q.e: "Stegosaurus" means "roof lizard" (or "covered lizard"), because early scientists thought its plates lay flat like roof tiles. In fact, the plates stood upright.

q: How many bony plates did a Stegosaurus have embedded on its back?

q.e: Stegosaurus had 17 bony plates on its back, as well as spikes on its tail (the "thagomizer"). The plates may have helped regulate temperature.

q: How many living species of bears are there?

q.e: There are eight living bear species: polar, brown, American black, Asiatic black, sun, sloth, spectacled and giant panda.

q: What famous beer brand uses the Clydesdale horse as its mascot?

q.e: Anheuser-Busch's Budweiser uses Clydesdale horses as its mascots since 1933, when they were used to celebrate the end of Prohibition. A team pulls the famous beer wagon.

q: What year was the Clydesdale Horse Society formally founded?

q.e: The Clydesdale Horse Society was founded in Scotland in the 1870s, to register the breed. Sources commonly say 1877.

q: What year was the Clydesdale horse introduced to North America?

q.e: Clydesdales came to North America in the 1800s, with large imports to Canada and the US around the mid-1800s. They were used for farming and hauling.

q: This dog breed, which originated in Mongolia and China, has very thick fluffy fur and a blue-black tongue.

q.e: The Chow Chow has a thick mane-like coat and a blue-black tongue. It is one of the oldest breeds, from northern China.

q: What is the meaning of the term apex predator which is related to carnivorous animals?
A predator that has no predators itself.
A very skilled predator that is highly specialized in killing animals.
It is a term for a human being.
An animal which consumes the highest number of animal species.

q.e: An apex predator sits at the top of the food chain and has no natural predators as an adult. Examples are lions, orcas and polar bears.

q: What does the term facultative carnivore mean?
A carnivore that also consumes plant food.
It is a synonym for scavenger.
Animal that has all characteristics of carnivores but is a herbivore.
It is a synonym for omnivore.

q.e: A facultative carnivore usually eats meat but can also eat plants. Dogs are an example of a facultative carnivore, while cats are obligate carnivores.

q: How many box turtle species are there in North America?

q.e: North America has a few box turtle species, including the eastern, ornate, Coahuilan and Gulf Coast box turtles. The count depends on classification.

q: The White Snake is a fairy tale included in the collection of fairy tales by this author.

q.e: "The White Snake" is a Grimm Brothers fairy tale where a servant eats the white snake and understands animal speech. A different Chinese legend with a similar name also exists.

q: What is the meaning of the figurative expression a white elephant?
Something that is idolized but that does not exist

q.e: A white elephant refers to a burdensome possession whose upkeep and maintenance costs vastly exceed its practical value. The idiom comes from the historic Southeast Asian monarchical custom of gifting rare albino sacred elephants to unliked courtiers to financially ruin them.

q: This dog breed, considered one of the first sighthound dog breeds, has very long fur and is quite tall, with long legs and ears.

q.e: The Afghan Hound is one of the oldest sighthound breeds, with a long silky coat. It was bred to hunt in the mountains of Afghanistan.

q: The Papillon is a small dog breed of the Toy group. What does the word Papillon mean in French?

q.e: Papillon means butterfly in French, given to the breed because its large, upright, fringed ears resemble the spread wings of a butterfly. A drop-eared variety of the same breed exists and is known as the Phalene, the French word for moth.

q: This dog breed was developed as a gun dog in Canada?

q.e: The Labrador Retriever originated in Newfoundland, Canada, where it descended from the St. Johns water dog and was used by fishermen to haul nets before being refined in Britain as a gun dog. The Pharaoh Hound, despite its name, is the national dog of Malta.

q: What creature is considered the most venomous on the planet?

q.e: The box jellyfish (Chironex fleckeri) is considered the most venomous marine animal, and its sting can kill a person within minutes. It lives in northern Australia and the Indo-Pacific.

q: The name of cobras, which are very venomous, comes from the Portuguese cobra de capello. What does this mean?

q.e: "Cobra" comes from the Portuguese "cobra de capelo", "snake with a hood". Portuguese explorers named it in India.

q: What kind of animal is the venomous Gila monster that is indigenous to southwestern United States and northern Mexico?

q.e: The Gila monster (Heloderma suspectum) is a heavy, slow-moving lizard native to the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. It and the closely related beaded lizards are among the few lizards in the world equipped with venom glands.

q: How is the body of the jellyfish oxygenated?

q.e: Jellyfish have no lungs, so oxygen diffuses through their thin skin. Their bodies are mostly water.

q: What is the deadliest jellyfish in the world?

q.e: The box jellyfish is considered the deadliest jellyfish. The tiny Irukandji jellyfish is also very dangerous.

q: How many different types of wolves including sub-species are there around the world?

q.e: There are three wolf species (gray, red and Ethiopian), and the gray wolf has many subspecies. Taxonomists disagree on the exact number.

q: What is the most amount of wolf pups ever recorded in a litter?

q.e: Wolf litters usually have four to six pups, and in rare cases more than ten. The mother digs a den to give birth.

q: What Gorilla is the largest primate on the planet?

q.e: The eastern gorilla, especially the eastern lowland (Grauer's) gorilla, is the largest living primate. Males can weigh over 200 kg (440 lb).

q: What is the largest living bird of prey on the planet?

q.e: The Eurasian black (cinereous) vulture is among the heaviest birds of prey, weighing up to 14 kg. The Andean condor has a larger wingspan.

q: A vampire bat will die if it doesnt find blood for how many nights in a row?

q.e: A vampire bat can die if it goes about two to three days without a blood meal. They share blood with hungry roost mates.

q: What actor directed and starred in the popular 1990 movie Dances with Wolves?

q.e: Kevin Costner directed and starred in Dances with Wolves (1990), which won the Oscar for Best Picture. It was his directorial debut.

q: What animal is the largest macropod and one of Australias heraldic animals?

q.e: The red kangaroo (Osphranter rufus) is the largest living marsupial and macropod, with large males standing over 1.8 meters (6 feet) tall and weighing up to 90 kg (200 lbs). Along with the emu, it serves as an official supporter on Australia's coat of arms.

q: Which of these marine mammals matches the description: Very large body, has tusks and whiskers?

q.e: The walrus is an arctic pinniped easily recognized by its prominent ivory tusks, which can reach up to 1 meter (3.3 feet) in length, and thick sensory whiskers called vibrissae. Male elephant seals possess a bulbous proboscis, but lack exterior tusks.

q: This marine mammal is known as the pilot whale, but it is not actually a whale. What type of animal is it?

q.e: Pilot whales are large dolphins in the family Delphinidae. Orcas ("killer whales") are also dolphins.

q: The natural habitat of the Chinchilla is this region in South America.

q.e: Wild chinchillas live in the Andes mountains of South America, mainly in Chile. They're endangered in the wild.

q: Which of the following behaviors is not typical for the Chinese Crested dog?

q.e: Chinese Crested dogs are often hairless, and their skin needs protection from sun and cold. They do pant like other dogs to cool down.

q: which of these stories and books have a fox character involved in the storyline?

q.e: In The Adventures of Pinocchio (1883), the Fox and the Cat trick the puppet into burying his coins. They are the villains.

q: What eminent musician released his album The Fox in 1981?

q.e: Elton John released The Fox in 1981. It included "Nobody Wins" and "Heartache All Over the World".

q: Guinea pigs are very intelligent, highly social animals that use special vocalization to communicate. What does their whistling or wheeking sound express?

q.e: A guinea pig's "wheek" is a loud whistle, often given when it's excited, for example when it hears food. Guinea pigs make several different sounds.

q: What kind of unique activity is characteristic of the African Pygmy Mouse, the smallest rodent in the world?
It piles up pebbles in front of its burrow.
It disguises its young using leaves.
It starts dancing when it feels threatened by a predator.

q.e: The African pygmy mouse is one of the world's smallest rodents, and piles small pebbles at the burrow entrance. The stones may keep out morning dew or hide the opening.

q: What is the reason for Hummingbirds short life-span?
They often get poisoned when feeding on nectar or insects.

q.e: Hummingbirds have the highest metabolic rate among birds, burning energy quickly. This is thought to contribute to their short lifespan of roughly 3-5 years.

q: Where does the Giant Cowbird, a passerine bird found in South America, lay its eggs?

q.e: The giant cowbird is a brood parasite and lays its eggs in other birds' nests, such as caciques and oropendolas. The host raises its chicks.

q: The vicuna, a South American animal, is a close relative of this other animal.

q.e: The vicuna is a wild South American camelid and a close relative of the domesticated llama and alpaca. Genetic studies confirmed that the alpaca was actually domesticated from the vicuna thousands of years ago.

q: What type of animal is the Gold tegu, found in South America?

q.e: The gold tegu (Tupinambis teguixin) is a large lizard from South America. It's a reptile.

q: What time of day does the tiger shark usually hunt?
They hunt at different times throughout the day

q.e: Tiger sharks are mainly nocturnal, hunting at night in shallow waters. They eat nearly anything.

q: Which of these statements is NOT true about the Common Raven, a popular omnivorous bird?
It would feed on animal feces
It feeds on human food waste

q.e: Common ravens are omnivores, and eat carrion, insects, eggs and small birds. They are among the smartest birds.

q: Which of these is not within the natural diet of the omnivorous Eastern Box Turtle?

q.e: The eastern box turtle eats earthworms, slugs, insects, berries and mushrooms. Small amphibians may occasionally be on the menu.

q: Skunks, which are omnivorous mammals, are one of the primary predators of these animals.

q.e: Skunks eat honeybees, rolling them on the ground to remove stingers. They also eat insects, eggs and small rodents.

q: What type of food do Tasmanian devils prefer in the wild?

q.e: Tasmanian devils are mostly scavengers and prefer carrion. They have one of the strongest bites of any mammal.

q: What is the name of the Tasmanian devil cartoon character from Looney Tunes by Warner Bros.?

q.e: Taz is the Tasmanian Devil in Looney Tunes. He first appeared in 1954's "Devil May Hare".

q: What is the usual size range of mature ants?

q.e: Worker ants range from under 1 mm to over 5 cm for the largest. Queens can be bigger.

q: Which of these mollusks is able to glide over in air for up to 50 meters (164 feet)?

q.e: Some squid, such as the Japanese flying squid (Todarodes pacificus), can glide for 30 m (100 ft) or more over water. They use jet propulsion to launch.

q: Which frog is a skilled glider, able to make two types of turns midair?

q.e: The Chinese gliding frog (Rhacophorus dennysi) can steer in mid-air, with its webbed feet. It lives in forests of China and Vietnam.

q: Where are the gliding membranes of the Draco lizard species positioned?
Between its front and hind legs
They do not have a gliding membrane

q.e: Draco lizards have gliding membranes supported by elongated ribs. They can glide between trees for 60 m or more.

q: What type of animal is the serval?

q.e: The serval is a medium-sized wild cat from Africa, with large ears and long legs. It's a member of the cat family (Felidae).

q: Adult Goliath beetles, found in Africas tropical forests, feed on what?

q.e: Adult Goliath beetles feed mainly on tree sap and fruit. They are among the heaviest insects.

q: This oceanic dolphin has distinctive yellow patches on its sides. It is mostly found in the northern latitudes of the Atlantic Ocean.

q.e: The Atlantic white-sided dolphin has a yellowish-white patch on the sides. It lives in the cold North Atlantic.

q: What kind of animal is the smallest known reptile on the planet?

q.e: The smallest known reptiles include tiny chameleons and geckos, such as Sphaerodactylus ariasae of the Dominican Republic. They're about 1.6 cm long.

q: What type of insect is the smallest known insect on the planet?

q.e: The smallest known insects are fairyflies, a kind of parasitic wasp, which are less than 0.2 mm long. They are among the tiniest of all animals with complex bodies.

q: The sound of what musical instrument does the call of the Macaroni Penguin resemble?

q.e: Macaroni penguins have loud, braying calls. Their yellow crests resemble hairstyles.

q: What large mammal is the national animal of India?

q.e: The Bengal tiger (Panthera tigris tigris) was declared India's national animal in 1973, replacing the Asiatic lion to emphasize tiger conservation under Project Tiger.

q: What type of Indian animals are included in the so-called Big Four selection?

q.e: India's "Big Four" snakes are the Indian cobra, common krait, Russell's viper and saw-scaled viper. They cause most snakebite deaths.

q: What is the only place in the world you can see platypuses in the wild?

q.e: Platypuses live only in eastern Australia and Tasmania. They are egg-laying mammals.

q: If the ears of a chinchilla turn red, it is a sign of this condition.
The animal is disturbed or angry.

q.e: A chinchilla's ears turn red and hot when it's overheating. Chinchillas are very sensitive to heat above 25 °C.

q: This cat breed, which appeared naturally in Thailand, has a slim body and short fur with point coloration.

q.e: The Siamese cat originated in Thailand (formerly Siam), and has a slim body and a pointed coat. It's one of the oldest breeds.

q: This exotic cat breed was developed in Kenya by crossbreeding between a Serval and a domestic cat.

q.e: The Savannah cat is a hybrid of a serval (an African wild cat) and a domestic cat. The first was bred in the US in 1986.

q: Which is the largest subspecies of ostrich on the planet?

q.e: The North African ostrich, also known as the red-necked ostrich, is the largest ostrich subspecies. Males can reach 2.7 m (9 ft) and weigh 150 kg.

q: Unlike other ostriches, this subspecies of ostrich has small feathers on its head.

q.e: The Masai ostrich is a subspecies in East Africa. Males' necks and legs turn pink-red in the breeding season.

q: Which subspecies of ostrich became extinct around 1966?

q.e: The Arabian (Middle Eastern) ostrich went extinct around 1966, due to hunting. It lived in the Arabian Peninsula and Syria.

q: Which elephant subspecies is the largest on the planet?

q.e: The African bush (savanna) elephant is larger than the forest elephant. It's the largest land animal.

q: What does the diet of elephants mostly consist of?

q.e: Elephants eat grasses, leaves, bark, roots and fruit, up to 150 kg a day. They're herbivores.

q: Cockroaches belong to the order Blattaria. What is the meaning of the Latin word blatta?

q.e: "Blatta" is Latin for cockroach, and gives the order Blattodea its name. The Latin word was used for insects that shun light.

q: What term is commonly used to refer to the young of the guinea pig?

q.e: Baby guinea pigs are called pups. They're born with fur and open eyes.

q: The guinea pig is unable to produce this substance in its own body and gets it from its food.

q.e: Like humans and other primates, guinea pigs lack the enzyme L-gulonolactone oxidase required to synthesize vitamin C, making dietary intake essential to prevent scurvy.

q: The representatives of what guinea pig breed have extremely long hair that never stops growing all over their bodies?

q.e: The Peruvian guinea pig has long, silky hair that grows continuously. Owners need to groom them.

q: What popular cartoon character from a 1995 animated movie keeps a raccoon as a pet?

q.e: Pocahontas (1995) has a pet raccoon, Meeko. She also befriends a hummingbird, Flit.

q: What distinctive feature is characteristic of the crocodile species called gharial, or Indian gavial?

q.e: The gharial has a long, thin snout with many sharp teeth, adapted for catching fish. Males have a bulb on the snout.

q: What is the the body length of an average mature sloth from head to tail?

q.e: A sloth is about 50-60 cm (20-24 in) long. It weighs 4-8 kg.

q: Which of the following statements is wrong?
There are seven living species of sloths.
Two-toed sloths have only six cervical vertebrae instead of seven.
Sloths hairs grow away from their extremities instead of towards them.
Three-toed sloths have nine cervical vertebrae instead of seven.

q.e: There are six living species of sloth: two kinds of two-toed and four kinds of three-toed. Seven is incorrect.

q: Which kangaroo species is the largest on the planet?

q.e: The red kangaroo is the largest kangaroo and the biggest marsupial. Males can stand 1.8 m tall.

q: What type of animal is a mudpuppy?

q.e: A mudpuppy is a fully aquatic salamander. It keeps its gills for life.

q: Which of these statements is true about the mudpuppy?
They live in and out of the water.
Their lifecycle is divided into three stages.

q.e: Mudpuppies are nocturnal. They hide under rocks by day.

q: Wombats are endemic to this geographical area.

q.e: All three living wombat species are native solely to southeastern Australia and the nearby island state of Tasmania.

q: What important bone-building mineral do the cartilage of bats finger bones lack, which makes them very flexible?

q.e: Bats' finger bones are less calcified, which makes them flexible. This helps wing movements.

q: What other common name is used for the Kittis Hog-nosed Bat, the smallest bat species in the world?

q.e: Kitti's hog-nosed bat, also called the bumblebee bat, is the smallest bat and possibly the smallest mammal by length. It lives in Thailand and Myanmar.

q: Ammonites became extinct at the end of what geological period?

q.e: Ammonites went extinct at the end of the Cretaceous Period, about 66 million years ago, along with the non-avian dinosaurs. Their coiled shells are common fossils.

q: What flower remedy would be most beneficial to a stand-offish horse that gets irritated quickly and has a hard time accepting change?

q.e: In Bach flower remedies, Beech is for intolerance and criticism. These remedies are an alternative therapy, with no scientific evidence of effect.

q: Up to how many different Bach remedies can you combine?
as many as you want to

q.e: Bach practitioners suggest combining a limited number of remedies, often no more than 7. Bach flower remedies are not proven medicines.

q: Salix vitellina is the scientific name of this essence usually given to a horse that appears to sulk, goes into moods and refuses any sort of attention.

q.e: Willow (Salix vitellina) is the Bach flower remedy for resentment and self-pity. It has no proven effect on animals.

q: What kind of animals are the colugos, or cobegos, which is found only in Asia?

q.e: Colugos, or "flying lemurs", are mammals from Southeast Asia that glide between trees. They are not lemurs and can't fly.

q: What sense of the Malayan Tapir, also called Asian Tapir, is underdeveloped?

q.e: Tapirs have poor eyesight and rely on smell and hearing. The Malayan tapir has a black-and-white coat that looks like camouflage.

q: What animal does the greater siren, a nocturnal amphibian, resemble externally?

q.e: The greater siren is an eel-like salamander with external gills and no hind legs. It lives in the southeastern US.

q: How many orders of trilobite are there?

q.e: Trilobites are divided into roughly nine to eleven orders, depending on classification. They were marine arthropods.

q: Approximately how many species of trilobite existed over the duration of the Paleozoic?

q.e: More than 20,000 trilobite species have been described, from the Cambrian to the Permian. They went extinct about 252 million years ago.

q: Which of these statements is true about the lemur Aye-aye?
It is the largest nocturnal primate on the planet.
It is the second smallest primate on the planet.
It is the second largest primate in the world.
It is the smallest nocturnal primate in the world.

q.e: The aye-aye is the world's largest nocturnal primate. It taps on wood and uses a long finger to extract grubs.

q: What is the name of the Aye-aye character from the 2005 animated comedy movie Madagascar?

q.e: In Madagascar (2005), Maurice is the aye-aye, voiced by Cedric the Entertainer. He's King Julien's advisor.

q: What term is used to refer to the infant koala, as well as to any other baby marsupial?

q.e: A baby kangaroo, koala or other marsupial is called a joey. Joeys develop in the pouch.

q: What is the largest living subspecies of giraffe on the planet?

q.e: The Masai giraffe is a very tall giraffe. Males can reach about 5.5 m (18 ft).

q: What is the term denoting a group of zebras that live together?

q.e: A group of zebras is called a herd, a dazzle or a zeal. A harem is a stallion with mares.

q: Which cartoon dog is one of Mickey Mouses best friends?

q.e: Goofy, who debuted in 1932 as Dippy Dawg, is an anthropomorphic dog and one of Mickey Mouse's closest companions alongside Donald Duck.

q: Which Rough Collie was awarded a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame?

q.e: Lassie was awarded a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1960, one of only a few fictional animal characters to receive the honor.

q: What is the real name of the dog who first played the fictitious dog Benji in the series of Benji films?

q.e: Higgins, a mixed-breed dog, played Benji in the 1974 film Benji. He was found at an animal shelter.

q: Name the Red Baron hunting Beagle from Charles Schultz popular comic strip, Peanuts.

q.e: In Charles Schulz's Peanuts comic strip, Charlie Brown's beagle Snoopy frequently fantasizes about flying his doghouse as a World War I flying ace chasing the Red Baron.

q: This cartoon Great Dane often needs his nephew headstrong nephew to protect him.

q.e: Scooby-Doo is a Great Dane, and his nephew is Scrappy-Doo, introduced in 1979. Scrappy is short and brave.

q: Which of these is the most distinctive feature of one of the largest marine creatures, which is also known to be the best diver - the sperm whale?
The unique curvatures of its fins

q.e: The sperm whale has an enormous, boxy head holding a huge organ of spermaceti. It's one of the deepest-diving mammals, going down 2,000 m or more.

q: Periplaneta americana, Blattella germanica and Gromphadorhina portentosa are all species of this insect.

q.e: Periplaneta americana (American cockroach), Blattella germanica (German cockroach) and Gromphadorhina portentosa (Madagascar hissing cockroach) are cockroaches.

q: The scarab, a sacred beetle to Ancient Egyptians, is commonly known as what?

q.e: Sacred scarabs are dung beetles in the family Scarabaeidae. Ancient Egyptians associated their habit of rolling dung balls across the ground with the sun god Khepri rolling the sun across the sky.

q: Which of these American zoos does NOT house Komodo Dragons?

q.e: Komodo dragons are shown at several US zoos, including the National Zoo and San Diego Zoo. Zoo collections change, so check with the zoo.

q: Which of these animals usually preys on black bear cubs?

q.e: Black bear cubs can be preyed on by cougars, wolves, coyotes and larger bears. Mothers protect their cubs fiercely.

q: How many eggs does a turkey usually lay?

q.e: A turkey hen lays about 8-15 eggs in a clutch. The eggs hatch in 28 days.

q: Which of these statements if true about a cat?
Their urine glows under a black light.
Normal body temperature for a a cat is 95 degrees Fahrenheit.
They take about 50 breaths per minute.
They walk on the bottoms of their feet.

q.e: Cat urine fluoresces under ultraviolet (black) light, which is used to find pet stains. It's a safe, common trick.

q: According to a survey, what percentage of American cat owners admit to blow drying their feline after giving it a bath?

q.e: Most cats dislike baths and clean themselves by licking. Vets recommend they only be bathed when necessary.

q: Which type of cat is almost always female?

q.e: Because the gene for orange fur is carried on the X chromosome, a cat must inherit two X chromosomes to display both orange and black patches alongside white. As a result, roughly 99.9% of calico cats are female.

q: What year was the very first cat show held?

q.e: The first modern cat show was held at the Crystal Palace in London in 1871, organized by Harrison Weir. The first major US show was in 1895 at Madison Square Garden.

q: Which of these is not one of the most popular names for female cats in the USA?

q.e: Popular names for female cats include Bella, Luna and Lucy. Names such as Socks are more common for male cats or varied.

q: Which of these is NOT a species of dolphin?

q.e: Real dolphins include the bottlenose, common, spinner and dusky dolphins. The eastern spinner dolphin is a subspecies.

q: What year was named by the United Nations as the Year of the Dolphin?

q.e: The UN-backed Convention on Migratory Species declared 2007 the Year of the Dolphin. The aim was to raise awareness of threats.

q: Which of these in NOT a species of raccoon?

q.e: Raccoon species include the common raccoon, the crab-eating raccoon and the Cozumel raccoon. There is no "tree raccoon".

q: How many young can an adult badger have at one time?

q.e: A badger sow gives birth to one to five cubs per litter, usually in a sett. The cubs are born blind.

q: Which of the following octopuses could most easily kill a human?

q.e: The blue-ringed octopus carries tetrodotoxin, a potent neurotoxin that can kill an adult human. It is small, but deadly.

q: Which of the following words is NOT related to the octopus?

q.e: Octopuses have eight arms, not tentacles. Tentacles (as in squid) are longer and have suckers only at the tips.

q: What king of habitat do Tomato Frogs live in?
in marshes, shallow pools, flooded meadows, and wetlands
in dessert areas that are very arid and dry

q.e: Tomato frogs live in marshes, shallow pools and flooded meadows in Madagascar. They are bright red when mature.

q: Some animals have an inborn instinct to swallow gastroliths in order to improve the breaking down of food inside their stomachs. What kind of objects are gastroliths?
Plants that are rich in digestive enzymes

q.e: Gastroliths are stones swallowed by animals, such as birds and crocodiles, to help grind food in the stomach. Some dinosaurs also had them.

q: Which of the following statements is true about mosquitoes?
All mosquitoes on the planet drink blood.

q.e: Only female mosquitoes bite humans and animals because they require the protein and iron in blood to develop their eggs. Male mosquitoes feed entirely on flower nectar and plant saps.

q: Koalas almost exclusively feed on this type of food.

q.e: Koalas eat almost only eucalyptus leaves, which are low in nutrition and toxic. They choose from about 50 types.

q: This fish, which resembles the Angel fish, is recognized by its brightly coloured and patterned body, as well as by the dark band across its eyes.

q.e: Butterflyfish have bright patterns and dark bands across their eyes, to confuse predators. They live on coral reefs.

q: The catfishes Physailia pellucida and Kryptopterus bicirrhis, found in the mid-waters of Southeast Asia, use what kind of camouflage?

q.e: Glass catfish are transparent, so you can see their skeleton and organs. Transparency helps them hide from predators.

q: The giant pandas diet is 99% this.

q.e: Giant pandas eat about 99% bamboo, even though they are classified as carnivores. They eat 12-38 kg a day.

q: Pandas spend 10-16 hours a day eating, the rest of the time they are usually resting. When are pandas most active?

q.e: Pandas are crepuscular, most active at dawn and dusk. They spend most of the day eating.

q: How many stomachs does a starfish have?

q.e: Starfish have two stomachs: a cardiac stomach that can be pushed out of the body, and a pyloric stomach. They digest prey outside their body.

q: There are two classes of starfish. Name them.

q.e: Sea stars (Asteroidea) and brittle stars (Ophiuroidea) are separate classes of echinoderms, with the starfish group sometimes split in two. Others are sea urchins, sea cucumbers and crinoids.

q: What is the average speed dolphins can reach?

q.e: Dolphins cruise at around 5-11 km/h (3-7 mph), and bottlenose dolphins can burst to 35 km/h. Speeds vary by species.

q: How many different species of dolphins are there in the world?

q.e: There are around 40 species of oceanic dolphins and a few river dolphins. Counts vary with classification.

q: In nature adult jaguars are apex predators in the food chain. What does this mean?
They are not preyed on by other predators.
They feed only on other predators.
They do not hunt on other predators.
Besides hunting they also feed on plants.

q.e: An apex predator has no natural predators once fully grown. The jaguar is the top predator in its habitat.

q: Jaguars closely resemble which other big cats in physical appearance?

q.e: Jaguars and leopards look remarkably alike, but jaguars are stockier and have larger rosettes with dark spots inside them. Leopards lack internal spots inside their rosettes, and cheetahs have distinct solid black spots rather than rosettes.

q: Jaguars appearance seems to vary across regions and habitats. How do forest jaguars differ from the jaguars in open areas?
Forest jaguars are generally darker and smaller
Forest jaguars are generally darker and larger
Forest jaguars are generally and more spotted
Forest jaguars are generally larger and lighter in fur color

q.e: Jaguars in dense forest tend to be darker and smaller than those in open areas. Black jaguars are called panthers.

q: What is the literal meaning of the word raccoon, which originates from the Algonquin word ahrah-koon-em and denotes a scavenging mammal?
One who rubs, scrubs and scratches with its hands
One who grasps with their hand just like a human
One who eats whatever is in front of them
One who washes their hands and their food before eating

q.e: "Raccoon" comes from an Algonquian word meaning "one who rubs, scrubs and scratches with its hands". It was written down by John Smith.

q: What hyena species is the largest surviving on the planet?

q.e: The spotted hyena is the largest living hyena species. Females are larger than males.

q: These parrots are believed to be the best at imitating sounds and human speech.

q.e: African grey parrots are renowned for their exceptional vocal learning and cognitive abilities, famously demonstrated by Alex, an African grey studied by Irene Pepperberg. While Amazon parrots are also strong mimics, African greys excel at contextual speech.

q: The heaviest parrot species on the planet is the Kakapo. What is the average weight that a normal mature Kakapo can reach?

q.e: The kakapo is the world's heaviest parrot, weighing 2-4 kg. It's flightless and nocturnal, and critically endangered.

q: This cat breed has a wild markings and is a crossbreed between an Asian Leopard Cat and a domestic cat.

q.e: The Bengal cat is a cross between an Asian leopard cat and a domestic cat, with leopard-like spots. The breed was developed in the US.

q: This old breed of cat has long fur. It originated in the Middle East, and some of its representatives have a flat face.

q.e: The Persian is an old long-haired cat breed from Persia (modern Iran). Many have a flat face.

q: This cat breed is believed to have developed naturally in China. It has short golden brown fur with the so-called broken striped pattern and a large strong body.

q.e: The Dragon Li (Chinese Li Hua) is a Chinese breed with a brown mackerel-tabby coat. It's a natural breed.

q: What cat breed, also called the Greyhound of the cats, has no hair except for down?

q.e: The Cornish Rex has a short, curly coat of down hair, and a slim body with long legs. It's often compared to a greyhound.

q: This breed of cat has a round head, large round eyes and very small ears bended forward and downward.

q.e: The Scottish Fold has ears that fold forward and down, because of a cartilage gene. The mutation can cause joint problems.

q: What is the place of rabbits in Japanese tradition and mythology?
They are believed to inhabit the Moon.
They are despised as being too timid.
Rabbits are not a part of Japanese mythology.

q.e: In Japanese folklore, the rabbit lives on the Moon, pounding mochi (rice cake). The "Moon rabbit" is also in Chinese and Korean tales.

q: What common name is used to refer to the insects from the subfamily Triatominae, mainly found in the Americas?

q.e: Triatomine bugs are called "kissing bugs" since they bite people near the mouth when sleeping. They can spread Chagas disease.

q: Why were the insects known as snakeflies given this interesting name?
They have snake skin color patterns on their back.

q.e: Snakeflies have an elongated neck-like thorax that looks like a snake when lifted. They are predators of other insects.

q: What distinctive anatomical feature does the beetle species Trogodendron fasciculatum possess?
A green W mark on the back

q.e: Trogodendron is a genus of beetles from Australia. Beetles are the most diverse group of animals.

q: What does the flamboyant flower beetle, also known as striped love beetle, feed on?

q.e: Flower beetles feed on pollen and nectar from flowers. The flamboyant flower beetle lives in Australia.

q: What belief about the European hornet, the largest European eusocial wasp, is widespread among the people who are afraid of it?
Three stings can kill an adult human, and seven can kill a horse.
If it stings you, youll never have children.
If it stings you on the arm or leg, that limb has to be amputated.
Stinging results in deep sleep that you may never wake up from.

q.e: The belief that three hornet stings can kill an adult human, or seven can kill a horse, is a myth. European hornets are less aggressive than commonly thought.

q: What animal costume did young Fred Astaire wear at his first ever stage performance?

q.e: Fred Astaire's first stage act, at age 7, had him in a lobster costume, in a vaudeville act with his sister Adele. They became a famous dance partnership.

q: George Clooney had this large animal as a pet between 1987 and 2006.

q.e: George Clooney had a pet pig, Max, from 1987 until the pig died in 2006. Max was a Vietnamese pot-bellied pig.

q: What animal is responsible for the most human deaths in the world?

q.e: Mosquitoes cause roughly 700,000 to over one million human deaths each year by transmitting lethal pathogens like malaria, dengue, and yellow fever, far exceeding the toll of any other animal.

q: What animal is the largest land predator?

q.e: The polar bear is considered the largest land carnivore, followed by the Kodiak bear (a brown bear subspecies). They are similar in size.

q: This enormous mythical white bird, which appears in 8th-century Middle-Eastern books, is said to be able to lift and eat even elephants.

q.e: The roc is a giant bird of prey from Middle Eastern legends, appearing in the tales of Sinbad. It's said to carry elephants.

q: What are the Latin terms that refer to plant and animal life?

q.e: Flora comes from Flora, the Roman goddess of flowers, while fauna stems from Fauna, a Roman goddess of fertility and animals. Together, they describe all the plant and animal life of a specific region.

q: Who is the hapless kitty villain who is constantly being outwitted by the little bird Tweety Pie?

q.e: Sylvester the cat chases Tweety Pie, and is always outwitted by the canary or Granny. Mel Blanc voiced both.

q: What is the fastest bird of prey?

q.e: The peregrine falcon is the fastest bird of prey and the fastest animal on Earth, reaching diving speeds of over 200 mph (320 km/h) when performing its hunting stoop.

q: The breathing sound of what animal was used for the breathing of the horrifying Tyrannosaurus rex in Steven Spielbergs 1993 science fiction thriller Jurassic Park?

q.e: Sound designer Gary Rydstrom created the T. rex's sounds by blending animal noises, including baby elephant and alligator sounds. The Jurassic Park sound design won an Oscar.

q: What animal was the color taupe named after?

q.e: Taupe is the French word for mole, after the mole's brownish-gray fur. The color was named in the early 1900s.

q: The African vampiric creature, known as Adze, was believed to take the form of this animal in order to hunt children.

q.e: In Ewe folklore from Togo and Ghana, the Adze is a vampire that takes the form of a firefly. It is said to prey on children.

q: The fish taco is generally cooked by what method?

q.e: Fish tacos from Baja California are traditionally battered and fried, though grilled versions are common. They're served with cabbage and sauce.

q: It is national flower of Venezuela, and its family consists of more than 25 000 species.

q.e: The orchid (Cattleya mossiae, the "flor de mayo") is Venezuela's national flower. Orchids are among the largest plant families.

q: What animal produces the aromatic ambergris that is used for the preparation of flavors and perfumes?

q.e: Ambergris is a waxy substance produced in the digestive tract of sperm whales. It's used in perfumes as a fixative.

q: What animal is used for the preparation of the French delicacy Escargot?

q.e: Escargot is a French dish of land snails, usually cooked in garlic butter. Burgundy snails are the most common.

q: Genetic tests of all known potato species show that this country was the place they originally came from.

q.e: Potatoes originated in the Andes of Peru and Bolivia, where they were domesticated around 8,000 years ago. Wild relatives are found from the US to Chile.

q: What type of fish is traditionally used for the making of the Spanish stew called Marmitako?

q.e: Marmitako is a Basque stew made with tuna (bonito), potatoes, peppers and onions. Its name comes from the cooking pot used by fishermen on their boats.

q: The world sirena refers to this mythical or folklore hybrid of a woman and an animal?

q.e: Sirena is the Spanish and Tagalog word for mermaid, stemming from the ancient Greek Sirens. In Philippine and Hispanic folklore, sirenas are depicted as half-human, half-fish sea creatures.

q: The discovery site of which species was listed by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site in 1987?

q.e: The Peking Man site at Zhoukoudian, near Beijing, became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987. The fossils belong to Homo erectus.

q: This bird is considered to be the master of the sky. It is the carrier of prayers, venerated for its courage and wisdom.

q.e: The eagle is revered in many cultures, including Native American traditions, as a messenger who carries prayers to the sky. Its keen eyesight and strength symbolize courage and wisdom.

q: The griffin is a legendary creature with the body of this animal and the head and wings of an eagle.

q.e: A griffin is a legendary creature with the body of a lion and the head and wings of an eagle. It symbolizes strength and vigilance.

q: What is the worlds smallest winged insect?

q.e: The smallest known winged insects are tiny parasitic wasps (fairyflies), less than 0.2 mm long. They lay their eggs inside the eggs of other insects.

q: These animals use their tail to communicate with other representatives of their species.

q.e: Squirrels use their tails to signal alarm, warning other squirrels of danger. They also use them for balance and warmth.

q: This gemstone originates as a soft, sticky tree resin and sometimes contains insects and other animal material.

q.e: Amber is fossilized tree resin that hardened over millions of years, frequently preserving delicate organisms such as insects, spiders, and plant fragments intact as inclusions.

q: Humans (Homo Sapiens) evolved from which hominid species?

q.e: Modern humans (Homo sapiens) evolved from earlier hominins, with Homo erectus as part of the lineage. Many scientists place Homo heidelbergensis closer to the direct ancestry.

q: The clue words are Burrowing, Animal, Stocky, Hairy and Claws.

q.e: An aardvark is a burrowing, stocky, mostly hairless African mammal with strong claws, that eats termites and ants. The name means "earth pig".

q: What is the state animal of the U.S. state of South Dakota?

q.e: The coyote is the state animal of South Dakota, designated in 1949. The animal is common on the Great Plains.

q: Naturally, or in the wild, all mice species are classified as which of the following?

q.e: Wild mice are omnivores. They eat seeds, grains, fruit and insects.

q: A Vermiculturist uses this animal to produce compost?

q.e: Vermiculture is the use of worms (usually red wigglers) to turn food waste into compost. The worm castings are a good fertilizer.

q: What President has an animal named after him, after refusing to shoot one such animal during a hunting party?

q.e: Theodore Roosevelt refused to shoot a captured bear in 1902 on a hunt in Mississippi. A cartoon about it inspired the "teddy bear".

q: Sleepy Hollow, Beetle Juice, Big Fish

q.e: Tim Burton directed Sleepy Hollow (1999), Beetlejuice (1988) and Big Fish (2003). His style is known for gothic fantasy.

q: I am an insect, I have very pretty wings. What am I?

q.e: Butterflies are insects with large, colorful wings covered in tiny scales. They go through complete metamorphosis.

q: Which fictional cat was forever chasing Tweety Bird?

q.e: Sylvester the Cat made his debut in 1945 and spent decades scheming to catch Tweety in classic Warner Bros. Looney Tunes cartoons. Tom, by contrast, pursued Jerry Mouse in the MGM franchise.

q: This is the largest terrestrial mammal in North America.

q.e: Male American bison can weigh up to around 2,000 pounds (900 kg) and stand roughly 6 feet (1.8 m) tall at the shoulder, easily surpassing moose and elk as the continent's heaviest land mammals.

q: What animal jumped over the moon in the nursery rhyme Hey Diddle Diddle?

q.e: In the traditional 16th-century nursery rhyme, the cow jumps over the Moon, while the little dog laughs to see such fun and the dish runs away with the spoon.

q: This animal is very popular in the USA. In fact, Benjamin Franklin wanted to make it, not the Bald Eagle, the national animal of the United States.

q.e: In a famous 1784 letter to his daughter, Franklin criticized the bald eagle as having bad moral character and praised the wild turkey as a much more respectable, native American bird.

q: This is a trilogy about half-man-half-animal mutants that fight crime.

q.e: The Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles are crime-fighting mutants (turtles). They started as a 1984 comic and have inspired films.

q: What semi-aquatic rodent is the national animal of Canada?

q.e: The North American beaver was officially recognized as a national symbol of Canada in 1975, celebrated for its historic role in the fur trade that shaped the country.

q: This species, considered to have colonized almost every landmass on Earth, is studied by myrmecology.

q.e: Ants are studied by myrmecologists and live on almost every landmass except Antarctica and a few islands. There are over 12,000 species.

q: Which animal has the longest gestation period?

q.e: The alpine black salamander (Salamandra atra) has one of the longest gestation periods of any animal, about two to three years in the mountains. Elephants carry young for about 22 months.

q: Typical for the animal cells only, lysosomes are organelles built in the Golgi apparatus that contain what type of enzymes?

q.e: Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles containing digestive enzymes that break down waste and cellular debris. They are found in animal cells.

q: The Peking Man is an example of what species of the genus Homo?

q.e: Peking Man was Homo erectus (Homo erectus pekinensis), who lived roughly 750,000 years ago. The fossils were found in the 1920s and 30s.

q: Every day this number of species of plants and animals become extinct.

q.e: Scientists estimate that dozens to hundreds of species go extinct every day, though the exact number is uncertain. Human activity is the main driver.

q: How many unsuccessful attempts did it take to finally create Dolly, the first successfully cloned mammal?

q.e: Dolly the sheep (1996) was the only successful result from 277 attempts, so 276 failures. She was cloned from a mammary cell.

q: The first successful experiment in which a cloned animal embryo reached an adult state, was carried out in what year?

q.e: Nuclear transfer experiments in the early 1950s (Briggs and King, 1952) cloned frog embryos. John Gurdon later produced adult cloned frogs and shared the 2012 Nobel Prize.

q: Which of these species has the most complex color vision known?

q.e: The mantis shrimp has 12-16 types of photoreceptors, far more than humans, who have three. How it uses them is still debated.

q: The egg of this animal contains the largest existing single cell.

q.e: An unfertilized ostrich egg yolk represents a single massive ovum cell, measuring around 3 to 4 inches across and weighing up to about 3 pounds (1.4 kg).

q: Which of the following is not true about the bird eggshell?
The eggshell does not contain protein.
The normal bird eggshell is porous.
The eggshell consists of roughly 95% calcium carbonate crystals.
The bird eggshell is covered by a structure called cuticle.

q.e: Bird eggshells are mostly calcium carbonate, but contain protein too. A membrane lies underneath.

q: What was the animal featured in the insignia of the Apollo 11 mission, the first mission to land a human being on the Moon?

q.e: The Apollo 11 mission patch features an eagle, carrying an olive branch, landing on the Moon. The lunar module was named Eagle.

q: Which stage of the virus life-cycle restricts it to infecting only a certain species (or group) of organisms?
Replication of the viral DNA or RNA

q.e: A virus's host range is limited mainly by attachment, where its proteins bind to specific receptors on host cells. Without the right receptors, it can't infect.

q: The term albino comes from the Latin word albus. An albino person or animal is characterised by what?
A lack of pigmentation in the skin, eyes and hair
Extremely dark pigmentation of the skin

q.e: "Albino" comes from the Latin "albus", meaning white. Albinism is a lack of melanin, which results in pale skin and hair and pink eyes.

q: Which cooking technique is considered to be best for preserving vitamins and minerals in meat and fish, during heat processing?

q.e: Vitamins are sensitive to heat and water, so gentler, shorter cooking such as steaming helps preserve nutrients. Boiling leaches vitamins into water.

q: This is a delicacy made from certain species of fish eggs, most notably the sturgeon.

q.e: Traditional caviar consists solely of salt-cured roe harvested from wild sturgeon native to the Caspian and Black Seas, including the beluga and sevruga species.

q: This type of orchid, discovered by Charles Darwin, is pollinated by the hawkmoth, an insect with a long tongue.

q.e: Darwin predicted a moth with a very long tongue to pollinate the Madagascar star orchid (Angraecum sesquipedale). The moth was found 21 years after his death.

q: Which species has the most complex color vision system in the animal kingdom?

q.e: Mantis shrimp have 12 to 16 photoreceptor types that allow them to process distinct spectral channels, including polarized and ultraviolet light, far exceeding any other animal.

q: How many hearts does an octopus have?

q.e: An octopus has one systemic heart that pumps oxygenated blood to the body and two branchial hearts that pump blood through each of its two gills.
The platypus and the four species of echidna are monotremes, the only surviving mammalian order whose females lay eggs rather than giving birth to live young.

q: What is the largest kind of shark?

q.e: Whale sharks (Rhincodon typus) are the largest sharks and the largest living fish, growing up to around 40 feet (12 m) long or more, feeding mainly on plankton.

Bamboo makes up about 99% of a giant panda's daily diet. Because bamboo provides little nutrition, an adult panda can spend up to 12 hours a day eating and consume roughly 26 to 84 pounds (12 to 38 kg) of it daily.

q: What is a group of flamingos called?

q.e: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance. The word suits their bright pink color.

q: What scientific suborder does the family Hyaenidae belong to?

q.e: The hyena family Hyaenidae belongs to the suborder Feliformia ("cat-like"). The aardwolf is also a member.

q: What is the Gray Wolf's scientific name?

q.e: The gray wolf's scientific name is Canis lupus. Dogs are a subspecies, Canis lupus familiaris.

q: What scientific family does the Aardwolf belong to?

q.e: The aardwolf is a member of the hyena family (Hyaenidae), and eats mainly termites. It lives in southern and eastern Africa.

q: What is the scientific name of the Budgerigar?

q.e: The budgerigar's scientific name is Melopsittacus undulatus, which means "melodious parrot with wavy lines". It's native to Australia.

q: Unlike on most salamanders, this part of a newt is flat?

q.e: Newts have a flattened tail, which helps them swim. Salamanders usually have round tails.

q: What is the name of the copper-rich protein that creates the blue blood in the Antarctic octopus?

q.e: Hemocyanin is a copper-based protein that makes octopus blood blue. It transports oxygen better in cold, low-oxygen water.

q: What is the collective noun for vultures?

q.e: A group of vultures feeding on a carcass is called a wake. When they are circling high in thermals together, they are typically called a kettle.

q: What is the scientific name for the Bald Eagle?

q.e: The bald eagle's scientific name is Haliaeetus leucocephalus, which means "white-headed sea eagle". It's the national bird of the US.

q: What is the average amount of chinchillas born into a single litter?

q.e: Chinchillas typically have litters of one to three kits, averaging two. They are born with fur and open eyes.
The mountain chicken is a large frog (Leptodactylus fallax) from the Caribbean islands of Dominica and Montserrat. It's critically endangered, partly due to chytrid fungus.

q: What was the name of the Ethiopian Wolf before they knew it was related to wolves?

q.e: The Ethiopian wolf was once called the Simien jackal, because it was thought to be a jackal. DNA studies showed it's related to wolves.

q: What type of creature is a Bonobo?

q.e: The bonobo is a great ape that lives in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It's one of our closest relatives.

q: Which of these is a colony of polyps and not a jellyfish?

q.e: The Portuguese man-of-war is not a true single jellyfish, but a siphonophore made of genetically identical specialized zooids working together. Sea wasps and Irukandji are true box jellyfish.

q: Which of the following is another name for the "Poecilotheria Metallica Tarantula"?

q.e: Poecilotheria metallica is known as the Gooty sapphire ornamental tarantula, from Gooty in India. It's critically endangered and has a bright blue color.

q: A 1935 ban on killing "right" types of which creatures was the first of its kind?

q.e: In 1935, an international agreement banned the hunting of right whales, the first such protection for whales. Later, the 1986 moratorium stopped commercial whaling.

q: The Cobra is at the top of the food chain, with only two main predators -- one is man and the other is this animal.

q.e: Cobras are preyed on by mongooses, known for their speed in killing snakes, as well as by humans and birds of prey. King cobras eat other snakes.

q: What type of dog did Richard Nixon receive from a Texan while he was a candidate for Vice President?

q.e: In 1952, Nixon gave his "Checkers speech" about a cocker spaniel named Checkers, which he received from a supporter in Texas. It helped him stay on the ticket.

q: This endangered turtle is the biggest of all living turtles, reaching a length of over 2.7 m (8.8 ft) and weight of 900 kg (2,000 lb).

q.e: The leatherback sea turtle is the largest living turtle, growing to over 2 m (7 ft) and weighing up to 900 kg. It's vulnerable to extinction.

q: This species of great apes with long arms and reddish hair suffer habitat destruction due to logging, mining and forest fires.

q.e: Orangutans are red-haired great apes from Borneo and Sumatra. Logging, palm-oil plantations and fires destroy their habitat.

q: This small nocturnal animal, whose natural habitat are the deserts of Northern Africa, is known to jump not only for hunting or protection, but also for pleasure.

q.e: The fennec fox lives in the Sahara and is known to jump and play. Its huge ears help it hear prey and lose heat.

q: What is the white tigers scientific name?

q.e: White tigers are a color variant of the Bengal tiger (Panthera tigris). The white coat comes from a rare recessive gene.

q: Which of the following is not a breed of pig?

q.e: Common pig breeds include Yorkshire, Duroc and Hampshire. The Rhodesian Ridgeback is a dog, not a pig breed.

q: What is the breed of animal created from the crossing of a male lion and a female tiger?

q.e: A liger is produced by a male lion and female tiger and is the largest known extant feline. A tigon is the reverse hybrid, sired by a male tiger and a lioness.

q: Which term refers to the group formed by frogs and amphibians?

q.e: "Herps" refers to reptiles and amphibians together; the study of them is herpetology. The word "herp" comes from the Greek for "creeping".

q: Which of the following statements about echidnas, mammals native to Australia, is wrong?

q.e: Echidnas are monotremes (egg-laying mammals), not marsupials. The platypus is also a monotreme.

q: Which term refers to the self-defense mechanism which allows lizards to break off their tails when captured?

q.e: Autotomy, from the Greek for self-amputation, allows animals like lizards to shed a body part to escape predators. Autonomy refers to self-governance, while apotemnophilia is a psychological disorder involving the desire to amputate a limb.

q: Which of the following characters is a chicken?

q.e: Foghorn Leghorn is a big rooster in Looney Tunes, with a Southern accent. He was inspired by a radio character.

q: Most lions only survive in Africa. But a population of the much endangered Asiatic lion lives in India. How many estimated lions live in India as of 2007?

q.e: About 350-400 Asiatic lions lived in India's Gir Forest in 2007. Their population has since grown to over 600.

q: A polar bear is used as the marketing icon for which of these popular products?

q.e: The Klondike Bar uses a polar bear as its mascot, and the slogan "What would you do for a Klondike Bar?". The brand began in 1922.

q: Beavers are the second largest rodents in the world after which animal?

q.e: Native to South America, capybaras are the world's largest living rodents, commonly weighing between 77 and 146 pounds (35 to 66 kg). Sea otters are actually marine mammals in the weasel family, not rodents.

q: The North American Beaver is Canadas National symbol that adorns which Canadian coin?

q.e: The beaver is on the Canadian five-cent coin (the nickel). It's the national symbol of Canada.

q: The expression social butterfly is often used to describe a woman. It means that she does this.
Flits from one person to another

q.e: A "social butterfly" is a person who goes around many gatherings and chats with many people. The phrase is used for both men and women.

q: Why do cats seem to be attracted to the one person who doesnt like cats?
Kitty sees that person as unintimidating
Kitty thinks that person has food
Kitty wants to win them over

q.e: Cats may approach people who ignore them, because staring is a threat in cat language. A person who avoids eye contact seems less threatening.

q: To which animal class do octopuses belong?

q.e: Octopuses belong to the taxonomic class Cephalopoda within the phylum Mollusca. The class name comes from the Greek words for head and foot, reflecting their distinctive body plan.

q: The ruler of the Mughal Empire Akbar the Great was very enamored with cheetahs and it is said he kept a stable of how many of these cats?

q.e: Mughal emperor Akbar is said to have kept about 1,000 cheetahs for hunting. Cheetah hunting was popular among Indian rulers.

q: What are the three basic parts of an ants body?

q.e: An ant's body has three parts: the head, mesosoma (thorax plus first abdominal segment) and metasoma (gaster). The antennae are on the head.

q: Which statement about ants is untrue?
Anteaters prefer ants to any other type of food.
An ant colony will eat its own larvae if there is no other food around.
Bullet ants are considered to have the most painful sting.
Ants are sometimes put into Thai salads.

q.e: Anteaters eat ants and termites, but ants make up only part of the diet of many species. Ants themselves are mostly omnivorous.

q: Although jellyfish may seem to you calm and harmless, an encounter with some species may leave you in excruciating pain and even kill you in minutes. Which of the following species of jellyfish is venomous enough to kill a man?

q.e: The sea wasp (Chironex fleckeri), a species of box jellyfish found in Indo-Pacific waters, produces venom potent enough to cause cardiovascular collapse and death in humans within minutes. Their venom can be injected through millions of microscopic nematocysts on their tentacles.

q: Which of these dinosaurs had dorsal plates and spikes?

q.e: Stegosaurus is an iconic herbivorous dinosaur from the Late Jurassic recognized for its alternating bony plates along its spine and four spikes on its tail. The other options are modern or extinct non-dinosaurs: Heloderma are venomous lizards and Hydrodamalis gigas is the extinct Steller's sea cow.

q: In the cartoon Dinosaucers, Bronto Thunder is what kind of dinosaur?

q.e: Dinosaucers (1987) is a cartoon about dinosaurs that evolved into humanoids. Bronto Thunder is an evolved Brontosaurus.

q: Which band recorded a song called Brontosaurus which includes the following verse: Now her daddys getting old And he seemed to lose control When the brontosaurus Stormed into the house to trap her.?

q.e: "Brontosaurus" was written by Roy Wood and recorded by The Move in 1970, a band that was a forerunner of ELO. Wood later formed Wizzard.

q: Which one of these dinosaurs was herbivorous?

q.e: Protoceratops was a small, sheep-sized herbivorous dinosaur from Mongolia. Velociraptor is thought to have fought one in a famous fossil.

q: It has been reported that in the period 1992-2008, Ringling Bros. and Barnum Bailey Circus had at least this many elephant deaths caused by abuse and neglect.

q.e: Ringling Bros. and Barnum & Bailey Circus ended its elephant acts in 2016 after public pressure and closed in 2017. It briefly returned in 2023 without animals.
"Mantis" is Greek for "prophet" or "seer", because of the insect's pose, that looks like it is praying. Praying mantises are ambush predators.

q: What dog breed has an elongated body, very short legs, short shiny coat and a long snout?

q.e: Dachshunds were bred in Germany to hunt badgers, where their elongated bodies and short legs allowed them to dig into burrows. Their name literally translates from German as badger dog.

q: This dog breed, developed in England, has an egg-shaped head, small eyes, and very strong muscular body with smooth short fur and short legs.

q.e: The Bull Terrier has a distinctive egg-shaped head, small triangular eyes, and a muscular body. It was developed in England in the 1800s.

q: What city is known as the White Squirrel Capital of the World, since it is home to the largest colony of albino squirrels?

q.e: Olney, Illinois, calls itself the "White Squirrel Capital of the World". Its squirrels are albinos.

q: This dog, which was once used as a personal defense dog, police dog and war dog, is often mistakenly believed to be very aggressive.

q.e: The Doberman Pinscher was bred in Germany by Louis Dobermann as a guard dog. Properly trained, they are loyal and not inherently aggressive.

q: What is another name for a nutria?

q.e: Nutria are also called coypu, large South American rodents. They've become invasive in places such as Louisiana.

q: What is a common nickname for the Yorkshire Terriers?

q.e: The Yorkshire Terrier was developed during the 19th century in Yorkshire, England, and is almost universally nicknamed the Yorkie. A Shorky is actually a designer hybrid cross between a Shih Tzu and a Yorkie.

q: What animals do wolves generally prefer to feed on?

q.e: Wolves mostly hunt ungulates, such as elk, moose and deer. They also eat smaller prey when needed.

q: Dolphins are considered some of the most intelligent animals on the planet. How are they classified according to their diet?

q.e: Dolphins are carnivores that eat fish, squid and crustaceans. They are toothed whales.

q: Translated in English, what does the name of the chinchilla mean?

q.e: "Chinchilla" is thought to mean "little Chincha", after the Chincha people of the Andes who wore their fur. The Spanish named it.

q: Which is the wrong statement about chinchilla breeding?
Chinchilla litters predominately consist of twins.
Chinchillas can breed any time of the year.
Little chinchillas are born furred and with eyes open.

q.e: Chinchillas have a long gestation of about 111 days, far more than a 45-day period. This is long for a rodent.

q: Name the two types of Chinese Crested dogs.

q.e: The Chinese Crested has two types, the hairless and the powderpuff. Both can appear in the same litter.

q: How are most foxes generally classified according to their diet?

q.e: Most foxes are omnivores. They eat small mammals, birds, insects, fruit and berries.

q: What fox species is considered to be the smallest on the planet?

q.e: Native to the Sahara Desert, the fennec fox (Vulpes zerda) is the world's smallest canid, weighing only about 2 to 3.3 pounds (0.9 to 1.5 kg) with massive ears reaching up to 6 inches (15 cm) long.

q: Chipmunks are small squirrel-like rodents belonging to the genus Tamias. What does the Greek word tamias mean?

q.e: "Tamias" comes from the Greek for "storer" or "steward", from the way chipmunks store food. Chipmunks hoard seeds in their burrows.

q: The Capybara is the largest rodent in the world. What is the meaning of its name, derived from a word of the Guaraní language?

q.e: "Capybara" is from the Tupi language, meaning "master of the grasses" or "grass eater". It's the largest living rodent.

q: What is the term for the state of temporary hibernation that Hummingbirds enter when food is not available?

q.e: Hummingbirds enter torpor at night or when food is scarce, lowering their heart rate and body temperature. This saves energy.

q: What is the smallest species of deer in the world, found only in South America?

q.e: The northern pudu is the world's smallest deer, standing about 32-35 cm tall. It lives in the Andes of Colombia, Ecuador and Peru.

q: Which of these is true about ants diet?

q.e: Most ants are omnivorous, eating sugary liquids, seeds and other insects. Some species are specialized.

q: This chemical is found in the venom of most ants and some other insects.

q.e: Formic acid gets its name from formica, the Latin word for ant, because English naturalist John Ray first isolated it in 1671 by distilling large numbers of crushed red wood ants.

q: In cetaceans, the species identification "rorqual" comes from the Norwegian word "rorhval" which means "furrow." These furrows are obvious on all rorqual whales. Which of the following is not a rorqual whale?

q.e: Rorquals (blue, fin, humpback) have throat pleats or furrows. The beluga is a toothed whale, not a rorqual.

q: Right and gray whales have been over-fished almost to extinction. Which of the following is a gray or right whale?

q.e: The bowhead whale is a right whale (family Balaenidae), while gray whales are in a separate family. Both were heavily hunted.

q: Males of this whale species have one tooth that can grow to be 10 feet (3 m) long.

q.e: The narwhal's famous tusk is actually an elongated, spiral-grooved canine tooth that erupts through the upper left lip of males, growing up to roughly 10 feet (3 m) in length and containing millions of sensory nerve endings.

q: Sometimes called the "hooked-finned" porpoise, this animal has a barely noticeable beak. It lives in the deep waters of the northern latitudes between North America and Asia, and is a very fast swimmer (up to 20 mph / 32 km/h). What is its name?

q.e: The Pacific white-sided dolphin is a fast swimmer of the North Pacific, with a short beak. It has a curved, "hooked" dorsal fin.

q: The representatives of this type of dolphins have very small eyes, making them virtually blind. They rely on echolocation to find food and swim in turbid waters. They include the baiji and boto. What are they called?

q.e: River dolphins have tiny eyes and rely on echolocation in murky waters. The group includes the Amazon river dolphin (boto) and the baiji.

q: What bacterium is believed to be the smallest living organism that is capable to grow and reproduce independently?

q.e: Mycoplasma genitalium has one of the smallest genomes of any free-living organism (about 580,000 base pairs). It's the basis of "minimal cell" studies.

q: What is the literal translation of the word lanigera in the name of the chinchilla species Chinchilla lanigera?

q.e: "Lanigera" is Latin for "wool-bearing". It refers to the chinchilla's dense fur.

q: This cat breed, developed by American breeder Ann Baker, is large and has blue eyes and soft fluffy coat with point coloration.

q.e: The Ragdoll was developed by California breeder Ann Baker in the 1960s. It's a large, blue-eyed cat that goes limp when picked up.

q: This large cat breed, created in the United States, has rabbit-like fur of medium length, rectangular body, and a fatty pad in the lower abdomen.

q.e: The Ragamuffin is a large cat breed developed from Ragdolls in the US. It has a rectangular body and a dense coat.

q: This cat breed occurred in Thailand, has very slim elongated body, short fur and very large ears.

q.e: The Oriental Shorthair has a slender body and large ears, and comes in hundreds of colors and patterns. It is related to the Siamese.

q: For which of these animals is the following description true: The gestation period lasts 35–58 days. Smaller species have 5-6 babies, and larger species - 3-4 babies. The young are born blind.

q.e: Hedgehogs have a gestation of about 35-58 days, depending on species, and litters of three to six hoglets. Hoglets are born blind with soft spines.

q: The Ramphotyphlops braminus, a harmless blind snake species, found in Africa and Asia, is often mistaken for this animal.

q.e: The Brahminy blind snake is often mistaken for an earthworm, as it's small, shiny and dark. It's the world's most widespread snake.

q: What is the smallest extant species of crocodilian on the planet?

q.e: The smallest crocodilians are dwarf caimans, such as Cuvier's dwarf caiman, at up to about 1.6 m. They live in South American rivers.

q: Which of these is true about the sloths diet?

q.e: Sloths are mostly herbivores that eat leaves, though they sometimes eat insects or small lizards. Their stomach has several chambers.

q: How is the lemur Aye-aye classified according to its diet?

q.e: The aye-aye is an omnivore, eating insect larvae, seeds, nuts, fruit and fungi. It extracts grubs with its long middle finger.

q: This fictional koala character, created by author Dorothy Wall, fist appeared in the 1933 book Jacko - the Broadcasting Kookaburra.

q.e: Blinky Bill is a koala character created by Dorothy Wall in 1933. He is a mischievous koala in Australian children's stories.

q: This artiodactyl mammal is the closest surviving relative of the giraffe.

q.e: The okapi (Okapia johnstoni) and the giraffe are the only two surviving members of the family Giraffidae. Though zebra-striped on its hindquarters, the okapi shares similar skin-covered ossicones and a long, prehensile purple tongue with the giraffe.

q: Unfortunately this fictional dog is constantly bullied by his buddy cat.

q.e: Odie, the dopey dog, is often bullied by Garfield the cat in Jim Davis's comic strip. Garfield started in 1978.

q: This dog, whose name means barker in Russian, became the first living creature from Earth to enter orbit.

q.e: Laika was launched into space aboard the Soviet spacecraft Sputnik 2 on November 3, 1957. A stray mongrel from the streets of Moscow, her name comes from the Russian verb 'layat', meaning 'to bark'.

q: What is the scientific name of the Common Raccoon?

q.e: The common raccoon's scientific name is Procyon lotor, meaning "before-dog washer". The species name refers to its habit of dousing its food.

q: When Tomato Frogs are in captivity at a zoo, what kind of food are they fed?
Small fish, such as minnows and guppies
The same food they would eat in the wild

q.e: In zoos, tomato frogs are fed insects such as crickets dusted with vitamins and calcium, and mealworms. Wild tomato frogs eat small insects.

q: Human skin has the unique ability to acquire a darker shade when exposed to UV-rays. What animals share this ability with us?

q.e: Some animals, like hammerhead sharks, can tan in strong sunlight. Pigs are also prone to sunburn.

q: This primitive shark, with a brown thin eel-like body, has six pairs of gill slits and trident-like teeth.

q.e: The frilled shark is a primitive deep-sea shark with an eel-like body and six gill slits. It has about 300 trident-shaped teeth.

q: What is the other name of Mola mola, a fish generally considered to be the most massive bony fish in the world?

q.e: Mola mola is known as the ocean sunfish because it often basks horizontally near the surface of the water, though in 2021 a related bump-head sunfish (Mola alexandrini) claimed the record for heaviest bony fish at nearly 6,000 pounds (2,744 kg).

q: Which is the smallest species of dolphin?

q.e: Maui and Hector's dolphins are the smallest dolphins, reaching only 1.4-1.7 m. Maui's dolphin is critically endangered, with only about 50 remaining.

q: All but one of the following activities are generally untypical for jaguars. Choose the one most natural to them.
Starting to eat their prey from the fleshy abdominal area

q.e: Jaguars are ambush hunters that stalk their prey and kill with a powerful bite to the skull. They also swim well.

q: What common name is used to refer to the scavenging animals, representatives of the order Opiliones?

q.e: Harvestmen (order Opiliones), also called daddy longlegs, are arachnids but not spiders. They scavenge on dead insects and plants.

q: Lions may be skilled predators, but they would also eat carrion. What animal is the lions preferred food?

q.e: Lions prefer large prey such as wildebeest and zebra. They also scavenge.

q: What cat breed has very thick short fur, large round eyes, round head and chubby cheeks?

q.e: The British Shorthair is a stocky cat with a dense coat, a round face and chubby cheeks. The blue-gray version is the best known.

q: What is the name of the communities formed by rabbits living together?

q.e: European wild rabbits live in social colonies inhabiting underground networks of interconnecting burrows called warrens. The terms herd, school, and flock refer to ungulates, fish, and birds respectively.

q: What name is used to refer to the scorpion species also known as Omdurman scorpion, and Israeli desert scorpion?

q.e: The deathstalker (Leiurus quinquestriatus) is a very venomous scorpion of North Africa and the Middle East. Its venom is studied for medical use.

q: Which is the official bird of Newfoundland?

q.e: The Atlantic puffin is the provincial bird of Newfoundland and Labrador. It breeds on the province's coastal islands.

q: A lion is part of which animal class?

q.e: Lions belong to the class Mammalia because they are warm-blooded vertebrates covered in fur that give birth to live young and nurse them with mammary glands.

q: Which of these fish is least likely to be found in seawater?

q.e: The tench is a freshwater fish of Europe and Asia. Tuna, cod and swordfish live in the sea.

q: What is found in plant cells, but not in animal cells?

q.e: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll to carry out photosynthesis and are unique to plant and algal cells. Both animal and plant cells possess mitochondria, cytoplasm, and ribosomes for cellular respiration and protein synthesis.

q: One of the two species, comprising the chimpanzee genus, is the Common Chimpanzee. What is the name of the other species?

q.e: The genus Pan consists of just two living species: the common chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes) and the bonobo (Pan paniscus). Bonobos were historically known as pygmy chimpanzees before being recognized as a distinct species in 1929.

q: What is the fastest ocean animal?

q.e: The sailfish is widely recognized as the fastest swimmer in the ocean, clocking bursts of speed estimated around 68 mph (110 km/h). Its streamlined body and specialized dorsal fin allow it to rapidly slash through schools of prey.

q: These people, who get active when it is dark, walk around gardens, parks, lawns to gather earthworms and sell them for fish bait.

q.e: Worm pickers collect nightcrawlers by hand at night with flashlights, and sell them as fishing bait. It's a business in Canada and the northern US.

q: I am the fastest animal on Earth. I can run reach speeds of 70 mph (110 km/h). What am I?

q.e: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, reaching up to about 110 km/h (70 mph). The peregrine falcon is faster in a dive.

q: I am a fish, I have a long mouth and I eat other fish. I come out at night. What am I?
