q.e: Using all seven letters to spell CHOKEYS yields 19 points from the individual letter values (C=3, H=4, O=1, K=5, E=1, Y=4, S=1). In standard Scrabble rules, playing all seven tiles in a single turn awards a 50-point bonus, bringing the total score to 69.

q: Which of the following spells in the card game Magic: The Gatheringcan destroy both creatures and enchantments?

q.e: Mortify costs one white, one black, and one generic mana to destroy target creature or enchantment. Putrefy is similar in black and green, but it destroys a creature or artifact instead.

q: This abstract strategy board game is the national game of Ghana. The board has two straight rows of six pits or cavities, called houses.

q.e: Oware is a traditional mancala pit-and-pebble game played extensively across West Africa, particularly among the Akan people of Ghana.

q: What is the Burmese variation of chess known as?

q.e: Sittuyin is the traditional Burmese descendant of the ancient Indian game chaturanga. A unique feature of Sittuyin is that players place their pieces in chosen formations behind a line of pawns before normal play begins.

q: The piece known as the noyon is found in this version of chess.

q.e: In shatar, a traditional Mongolian variant of chess, the noyon is the equivalent of the king and represents a prince or noble lord. Xiangqi is the Chinese variant, makruk is Thai, and chaturanga is the ancient Indian ancestor of modern chess.

q: The piece known as the rukh is found in this variation of chess.

q.e: In shatranj, the early Persian and Arab ancestor of chess, the rukh corresponds to the modern rook and depicted a chariot. The word passed through Arabic and Old French to become the modern chess 'rook'.

q: Capturing the opponents flag is the means of winning in this version of chess.

q.e: Luzhanqi is a Chinese land-battle board game similar to Stratego where players attempt to capture the opponent's flag. Ajedrez and shatranj are simply the Spanish word for chess and the historic Persian ancestor of chess.

q: Who was the author of the 1954 novel, "Lord of the Flies"?

q.e: William Golding published Lord of the Flies in 1954, about a group of schoolboys stranded on an island who descend into savagery. Golding won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1983.

q: Which famous spy novelist wrote the childrens' story "Chitty-Chitty-Bang-Bang"?

q.e: James Bond creator Ian Fleming wrote the 1964 children's book Chitty-Chitty-Bang-Bang for his son Caspar, inspired by real 1920s aero-engined racing cars.

q: Who was the original author of Frankenstein?

q.e: Mary Shelley wrote Frankenstein, published in 1818, when she was still a teenager. She began it in 1816 during a ghost-story challenge with Lord Byron and Percy Shelley.

q: American illustrator and writer Maurice Sendak is most well-known for writing which children's book?

q.e: Maurice Sendak published 'Where the Wild Things Are' in 1963, winning the prestigious Caldecott Medal for his iconic story of young Max and the Wild Things.

q: In what Harry Potter book was a Horcrux first encountered?

q.e: The first Horcrux in the series is Tom Riddle's diary, in Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets. Readers only learned what a Horcrux was in the sixth book.

q: What was the first ever entry written for the SCP Foundation collaborative writing project?

q.e: SCP-173, the statue that moves when you are not looking at it, was the first SCP Foundation entry, posted online in 2007. The project is a collaborative fiction wiki about anomalous objects and creatures.

q: What was Sir Handel's original name in "The Railway Series" and it's animated counterpart "Thomas and Friends?"

q.e: Sir Handel, a grumpy narrow-gauge engine on the Skarloey Railway, was originally called Falcon before being renamed. He appears in the Rev. W. Awdry's Railway Series, which inspired Thomas & Friends.

q: What's the second book in George R. R. Martin's 'A Song of Ice and Fire' series?

q.e: A Clash of Kings, published in 1998, is the second book in George R.R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire, after A Game of Thrones in 1996. The HBO series Game of Thrones is based on the series.

q: This play is generally considered to be the most adaptable of Shakespeare's works, and follows two "star-crossed lovers".

q.e: Romeo and Juliet, written in the mid-1590s, is probably Shakespeare's most adapted play, from ballet to West Side Story. The phrase "star-crossed lovers" comes from its prologue.

q: Who wrote "A Tale of Two Cities"?

q.e: Charles Dickens published A Tale of Two Cities in 1859, set in London and Paris around the French Revolution. It is one of the best-selling novels of all time.

q: Who wrote the young adult novel "The Fault in Our Stars"?

q.e: John Green wrote The Fault in Our Stars, published in 2012. It follows two teenagers, Hazel and Augustus, who meet in a cancer support group, and it became a hit film in 2014.

q: Who wrote "The Scarlet Letter", published in 1850?

q.e: Nathaniel Hawthorne published The Scarlet Letter in 1850, a story set in Puritan Boston about Hester Prynne, who is punished with a scarlet "A". It is considered a classic of American literature.

q: Who wrote the novel 'Fear And Loathing In Las Vegas'?

q.e: Hunter S. Thompson wrote Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas, which first appeared in Rolling Stone in 1971 and became a book. It's a wild, semi-autobiographical road trip and a landmark of "gonzo journalism".

q: What is the title of the first Sherlock Holmes book by Arthur Conan Doyle?

q.e: A Study in Scarlet, published in 1887, was Arthur Conan Doyle's first Sherlock Holmes story and the first time Holmes met Dr. Watson. Doyle went on to write four novels and 56 short stories about the detective.

q: Which is NOT a book in the Harry Potter Series?

q.e: The House Elf is not a Harry Potter book, although house elves like Dobby and Kreacher do appear in the series. The real titles are the seven books, such as Philosopher's Stone and Goblet of Fire.

q: What is the name of the fourth book in Stephen King's The Dark Tower series?

q.e: Wizard and Glass (1997) is the fourth book in Stephen King's The Dark Tower series. Much of it is a long flashback to the young gunslinger Roland's first love, Susan.

q: The book "The Little Prince" was written by...

q.e: French aristocrat, writer, and aviator Antoine de Saint-Exupéry published The Little Prince in 1943, writing it in the United States while in exile during World War II.

q: Which novel by John Grisham was conceived on a road trip to Florida while thinking about stolen books with his wife?

q.e: John Grisham's Camino Island (2017) is a heist novel about the theft of F. Scott Fitzgerald's manuscripts from Princeton's library. It is set on a Florida island.

q: What book series published by Jim Butcher follows a wizard in modern day Chicago?
My Life as a Teenage Wizard

q.e: The Dresden Files, by Jim Butcher, follows Harry Dresden, a professional wizard and private investigator in modern Chicago. The series began with Storm Front in 2000.

q: Which of these books was NOT written by the Czech author Karel Čapek?
Journey to the Center of the Earth
Dashenka, or the Life of a Puppy

q.e: Karel Čapek's play R.U.R. introduced the word "robot" to the world in 1920. A Journey to the Center of the Earth was written by Frenchman Jules Verne.

q: Mary Shelley is the author of what classic horror story?
Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde

q.e: Frankenstein, published in 1818 by Mary Shelley, is a classic horror and science fiction story about a scientist who creates a living being. Many people mistakenly call the monster "Frankenstein", but that is the name of his creator.

q: Which of the following authors was not born in England?

q.e: Arthur Conan Doyle, creator of Sherlock Holmes, was born in Edinburgh, Scotland, in 1859. The other choices were all born in England.

q: Which of the following is not a work authored by Fyodor Dostoevsky?

q.e: Anna Karenina was written by Leo Tolstoy, not Dostoevsky. Fyodor Dostoevsky's best-known works include Crime and Punishment, The Idiot and The Brothers Karamazov.

q: Which American author was also a budding travel writer and wrote of his adventures with his dog Charley?

q.e: John Steinbeck described his 1960 road trip around America with his poodle, Charley, in Travels with Charley: In Search of America. Steinbeck won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1962.

q: In the Lord of the Rings, who is the father of the dwarf Gimli?

q.e: Glóin, a dwarf who accompanied Bilbo in The Hobbit, is Gimli's father. He is also a member of the Fellowship's company in The Lord of the Rings.

q: The title of Adolf Hitler's autobiography "Mein Kampf" is what when translated to English?

q.e: Hitler dictated Mein Kampf, which translates to My Struggle, while serving time in Landsberg Prison following his failed 1923 Beer Hall Putsch.

q: What is the name of the gang that Ponyboy is a part of in the book, The Outsiders?

q.e: The Greasers are the working-class gang that Ponyboy Curtis belongs to in S.E. Hinton's The Outsiders (1967). They are rivals of the wealthy Socs, and Hinton began writing the book as a teenager.

q: In "The Lord of the Rings," who is the owner of Asfaloth, the horse which brings Frodo to Rivendell?

q.e: Asfaloth is the white horse of the Elf-lord Glorfindel, who rescues Frodo from the Ringwraiths and carries him to Rivendell. In the movies, Arwen takes that role instead.

q: In the "Harry Potter" novels, what must a Hogwarts student do to enter the Ravenclaw Common Room?
Rhythmically tap barrels with a wand

q.e: In the Harry Potter books, a bronze eagle knocker on Ravenclaw's door asks a riddle, and students must answer it to enter. Other houses use passwords or other entry methods.

q: What is the name of the author of book series 'Percy Jackson'?

q.e: Rick Riordan wrote The Lightning Thief in 2005, launching the Percy Jackson & the Olympians series based on bedtime stories he originally created for his son.

q: Who wrote the 1967 horror novel "Rosemary's Baby"?

q.e: Ira Levin wrote Rosemary's Baby, published in 1967 and filmed by Roman Polanski in 1968. Levin also wrote The Stepford Wives and The Boys from Brazil.

q: George Orwell's novel "Animal Farm" was inspired by which historical event?
The rise of communism and Stalin's policies.
The rise of Imperial Japan and Pacific control.
The rise of fascism and Hitler's influences.
Franklin D. Roosevelt's New Deal and its effects on The Great Depression.

q.e: George Orwell's Animal Farm (1945) is an allegory of the Russian Revolution and the rise of Stalin's Soviet Union. The animals' revolt against the farmer mirrors how a revolution can turn into a dictatorship.

q: In Michael Crichton's novel "Jurassic Park", John Hammond meets his demise at the claws of which dinosaur?

q.e: In Michael Crichton's novel, John Hammond is killed by a pack of small Procompsognathus, or "Procompys", after a fall. In the movie, however, Hammond survives.

q: In "Little Women", which of the March sisters married Laurie?

q.e: While Jo March famously turns down Laurie's proposal, he later reunites with and falls in love with her younger sister Amy while traveling in Europe. Jo eventually marries the older German scholar, Professor Bhaer.

q: What is the name of Eragon's dragon in "Eragon"?

q.e: Saphira is the blue dragon in Christopher Paolini's Eragon (2002). Paolini began writing the book at age 15 and his parents first published it themselves.

q: How many books are in the Chronicles of Narnia series?

q.e: C.S. Lewis published the seven fantasy novels between 1950 and 1956, beginning with The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe and concluding with The Last Battle.

q: Which Russian author wrote the epic novel War and Peace?

q.e: Leo Tolstoy published War and Peace in full in 1869, chronicling the French invasion of Russia in 1812 through the perspective of five aristocratic families.

q: The book "Fahrenheit 451" was written by whom?

q.e: Ray Bradbury published Fahrenheit 451 in 1953, setting the dystopian story in a future where firemen burn outlawed books to suppress critical thought.

q: Who is the protagonist of the book: "The Catcher in the Rye" by J.D. Salinger

q.e: Holden Caulfield is the cynical teenage narrator of J.D. Salinger's 1951 novel, wandering New York City after being expelled from his prep school.

q: This author of popular novels, who was a lecturer at Wellesley College, spoke fluent English, Russian and French and made chess problems in his spare time.

q.e: Vladimir Nabokov taught literature at Wellesley College in the 1940s, spoke Russian, English and French, and composed chess problems. He is best known for Lolita and Pale Fire.

q: Who is the author of the following short stories: The Iliad of Sandy Bar, Tennessees Partner, The Outcasts of Poker Flats, High Water Mark?

q.e: Bret Harte wrote stories of the California Gold Rush, including "The Outcasts of Poker Flat" and "Tennessee's Partner". They helped define the American Western genre.

q: In the Harry Potter universe, who does Draco Malfoy end up marrying?

q.e: Draco Malfoy marries Astoria Greengrass. Their son, Scorpius, appears in the epilogue of the last Harry Potter book and is a main character in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child.

q: In which classic novel is there a character named Homer Simpson?

q.e: Homer Simpson is a character in Nathanael West's 1939 Hollywood novel The Day of the Locust. The Simpsons' Homer has no connection; Matt Groening named him after his own father.

q: Which of these does Charlie NOT read in The Perks of Being a Wallflower?

q.e: The Perks of Being a Wallflower, by Stephen Chbosky (1999), is told through letters from a shy teenager named Charlie. His English teacher gives him books to read throughout the story.

q: In the Magic: The Gathering universe, which plane does the Homelands expansion take place in?

q.e: The Homelands expansion of Magic: The Gathering is set on the plane of Ulgrotha. It came out in 1995 and was known for its odd cards and unusual story.

q: In Margaret Atwood's "The Handmaid's Tale", what is Offred's real name is implied to be?

q.e: In Margaret Atwood's The Handmaid's Tale (1985), the narrator is called Offred, and hints in the text suggest her real name is June. The TV adaptation makes this explicit.

q: Which fictional English county was the setting for Thomas Hardy's novels?

q.e: Thomas Hardy set novels like Tess of the d'Urbervilles in a fictionalized version of Wessex, reviving the name of an ancient Anglo-Saxon kingdom centered around Dorset.

q: Which classic horror character killed Elizabeth Lavenza?
The Creature from the Black Lagoon

q.e: In Mary Shelley's Frankenstein, the creature kills Victor's bride, Elizabeth Lavenza, on their wedding night. It's his revenge for Victor's refusal to make him a companion.

q: In which classic novel by Mark Twain did a beggar and Prince of Wales switch clothes, and learn about social class inequality?

q.e: Published in 1881, Mark Twain's novel tells the story of Tom Canty, a pauper from London, and Prince Edward, son of King Henry VIII, who swap places after discovering their identical appearances.

q: Which author and poet famously wrote the line, "The female of the species is more deadly than the male"?

q.e: Rudyard Kipling published the line in his 1911 poem 'The Female of the Species', arguing that female animals and humans are fiercer defenders of their offspring than males.

q: What is the name of the town in which Lily and James Potter are buried?

q.e: Godric's Hollow is the village where Lily and James Potter lived, where Voldemort attacked them, and where they are buried. Harry's birthplace is also the home of Bathilda Bagshot.

q: The novel "Jane Eyre" was written by what author?

q.e: Charlotte Bronte published Jane Eyre in October 1847 under the male pen name Currer Bell. Her sister Emily Bronte published Wuthering Heights that same year under the pseudonym Ellis Bell.

q: What kind of animal is Scooby-Doo?

q.e: Scooby-Doo is an anthropomorphic Great Dane created in 1969 by writers Joe Ruby and Ken Spears for Hanna-Barbera Productions.

q: Which cartoon cat is always chasing Jerry?

q.e: Created by William Hanna and Joseph Barbera in 1940, Tom and Jerry debuted in the cartoon short Puss Gets the Boot, where the cat was originally named Jasper.

q: What is the name of Mickey Mouse's girlfriend?

q.e: Minnie Mouse debuted alongside Mickey in the 1928 cartoon short Steamboat Willie. Daisy Duck is Donald Duck's girlfriend, while Clarabelle Cow is a recurring bovine friend.

q: What type of animal is Bugs Bunny?

q.e: Bugs Bunny was introduced by Warner Bros. in 1940 as an anthropomorphic rabbit, though his animated shorts frequently play with hare puns, such as Hare Tonic and A Wild Hare.

q: What is lost in Hawaiian and is also the name of a little girl in a 2002 film which features a alien named "Stitch"?

q.e: "Lilo" means "lost" in Hawaiian. Lilo & Stitch (2002) is about a Hawaiian girl who adopts an alien experiment she thinks is a dog.

q: What is the name of the city that The Flintstones is based in?

q.e: The Flintstones live in the Stone Age town of Bedrock. The 1960 Hanna-Barbera series was the first prime-time animated sitcom in the US.

q: What type of animal is Disney's Bambi?

q.e: In Disney's 1942 animated classic, Bambi is a white-tailed deer. In the original 1923 Austrian novel by Felix Salten, Bambi was written as a roe deer native to European forests.

q: Which of the following is not a Flintstones character?

q.e: Fred, Wilma, Barney and Betty are the Flintstones' core cast, joined by Dino, Pebbles and Bamm-Bamm. Lord Rockingham IX isn't one of them.

q: What was the first Disney movie to use CGI?

q.e: The Black Cauldron (1985) was Disney's first animated film to use computer-generated imagery, in elements like the bubbles. It was a box-office flop.

q: Which of these cartoons had a character named Heinz Doofenshmirtz?

q.e: Dr. Heinz Doofenshmirtz is the villain in Phineas and Ferb (2007-2015), whose evil schemes are foiled by Perry the Platypus. The show's creators are Dan Povenmire and Jeff "Swampy" Marsh.

q: What is the relationship between Rick and Morty in the show "Rick and Morty"?

q.e: In the animated sci-fi series, the mad scientist Rick Sanchez is the father of Beth Smith, making him the maternal grandfather of Morty Smith.

q: Which cartoon family lives in 742 Evergreen Terrace, Springfield USA?

q.e: The Simpsons have lived at 742 Evergreen Terrace since the show began in 1989. The Griffins of Family Guy reside at 31 Spooner Street in Quahog, Rhode Island.

q: Who created the Cartoon Network series "Adventure Time"?

q.e: Pendleton Ward created Adventure Time, which began on Cartoon Network in 2010. It follows Finn the human and Jake the dog in the Land of Ooo.

q: Who was the villain of ''The Lion King''?

q.e: Voiced by Jeremy Irons, Scar is Mufasa's brother and Simba's treacherous uncle in Disney's 1994 animated feature The Lion King.

q: The song 'Little April Shower' features in which Disney cartoon film?

q.e: "Little April Shower" is from Disney's Bambi (1942), where it accompanies a spring rain. The film is based on Felix Salten's novel.

q: What was the name of the sea witch in the 1989 Disney film "The Little Mermaid"?

q.e: Ursula, voiced by Pat Carroll, steals Ariel's voice in exchange for human legs. Madam Mim is the eccentric witch in The Sword in the Stone.

q: Who voices for Ruby in the animated series RWBY?

q.e: Lindsay Jones voices Ruby Rose in RWBY, the web series created by Monty Oum and produced by Rooster Teeth. It started in 2013.

q: In South Park, what is Stan's surname?

q.e: Stan's full name is Stanley Marsh, and his parents are Randy and Sharon Marsh. Broflovski is Kyle's surname, Stotch is Butters's, and Tweak is Tweek's.

q: In the show "Steven Universe", who are the main two employees of The Big Donut?

q.e: Sadie and Lars work at the Big Donut in Beach City in Steven Universe (2013-2019), created by Rebecca Sugar. Lars is later revealed to be much more than a slacker.

q: Who voiced the Genie in Disney's "Aladdin"?

q.e: Robin Williams voiced the Genie in Disney's Aladdin (1992), improvising lots of his lines. The role helped shift Hollywood's use of celebrity voice actors.

q: Who is Winnie the Pooh's gloomy donkey friend?

q.e: Eeyore is A.A. Milne's gloomy, pessimistic stuffed donkey who lives in the Hundred Acre Wood and frequently loses his pinned-on tail.

q: What is the surname of one of the male teachers in the BBC series Postman Pat?

q.e: Mr. Pringle is the head teacher in Postman Pat, the BBC series set in the village of Greendale. The show began in 1981.

q: In the show "Foster's Home For Imaginary Friends", which character had an obsession with basketball?

q.e: Wilt is the tall, one-armed imaginary friend who loves basketball in Foster's Home for Imaginary Friends (2004-2009). He lost his arm in a game.

q: Which of these is NOT a catchphrase used by Rick Sanchez in the TV show "Rick and Morty"?

q.e: Rick Sanchez's catchphrases include "Wubba lubba dub dub" and "And that's the waaay the news goes". "Slam dunk, nothing but net!" isn't one of them.

q: Lightning McQueen crashes into Radiator Springs in which 2006 film?

q.e: Lightning McQueen, voiced by Owen Wilson, is the rookie race car who ends up stranded in Radiator Springs in Pixar's 2006 animated feature Cars.

q: Which 2008 animated film has Jedi Knights fighting a rampaging droid army?

q.e: Star Wars: The Clone Wars (2008) is a computer-animated film that introduced Ahsoka Tano, and was followed by a TV series. It takes place between Episodes II and III.

q: A magic flying carpet is a character in which 1992 Disney film?

q.e: Magic Carpet appears as a sentient companion in Disney's Aladdin, helping Aladdin and Abu escape the Cave of Wonders. The character was animated using groundbreaking computer graphics alongside traditional hand-drawn animation.

q: What 2003 animated Disney film did Joaquin Phoenix lend his voice to?

q.e: Joaquin Phoenix voiced Kenai, the Inuit boy who is turned into a bear, in Disney's Brother Bear (2003). Phil Collins wrote the songs.

q: What animal character did John Travolta voice in the 2008 animated movie Bolt?

q.e: John Travolta voiced Bolt, a dog who thinks he has superpowers because of his TV show. Disney's Bolt (2008) was nominated for an Oscar.

q: David Carradine was the voice of Junichiro on a 2002 episode of what animated series?

q.e: King of the Hill (1997-2010), created by Mike Judge and Greg Daniels, follows a propane salesman in Arlen, Texas. David Carradine, known as Kung Fu's Caine, guest-starred in an episode.

q: Nicole Kidman provided the voice of Norma Jean in what 2006 animated comedy?

q.e: Nicole Kidman voiced Norma Jean, Mumble's mother, in Happy Feet (2006). It won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature.

q: What character did Mel Gibson voice in the 1995 animated movie Pocahontas?

q.e: Mel Gibson voiced Captain John Smith in Disney's Pocahontas (1995). It is loosely based on the true story, with many events changed.

q: What position did cartoon character Snoopy play in Charlie Browns Little League baseball team?

q.e: Snoopy plays shortstop on Charlie Brown's baseball team in Peanuts. The team is famously terrible, losing most games.

q: In the cartoon series Calvin and Hobbes, what is Hobbes?

q.e: Hobbes is a stuffed tiger who looks alive to Calvin, but is stuffed to everyone else. Bill Watterson drew Calvin and Hobbes from 1985 to 1995.

q: Which of these Nickelodeon animated shows stars a big headed kid who also has a very big brain?

q.e: Jimmy Neutron has a huge head and an even bigger brain. His show The Adventures of Jimmy Neutron: Boy Genius started on Nickelodeon in 2002.

q: What are the names of the Princess and the Prince in the 1959 Disney animated feature, based on Charles Perrault classic tale Sleeping Beauty?
The Princess is named Aurora, the Prince is anonymous.

q.e: Disney's 1959 Sleeping Beauty introduced Princess Aurora (also known as Briar Rose) and Prince Phillip, who was named after Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh.

q: Which of these Disney animated features is not based on a book written by an European author?
The Many Adventures of Winnie the Pooh

q.e: Mulan (1998) is based on the Chinese legend of Hua Mulan. The others are based on European stories, such as Pinocchio (Italian) and Alice in Wonderland (English).

q: In the popular Disney animated film Maleficent curses baby Aurora: she will die when she pricks her finger on a spinning wheels spindle. Why does Maleficent arrive and curse the child?
She was not invited to the christening.
She was in line to inherit the kingdom before Aurora was born.
She is in love with the king.
She hates the queen, her sister.

q.e: In Sleeping Beauty (1959), Maleficent shows up at Aurora's christening because she wasn't invited, and curses the baby to die on her 16th birthday. The fairy Merryweather softens the curse to a sleep.

q: The three fairies in the animated film Sleeping Beauty decide to conceal Aurora in a cabin in the woods until her 16th birthday passes, but before the fairies take Aurora to the woods, what does the King do to stop the curse?
commands all spinning wheels be destroyed
tries to have another witch remove the curse

q.e: In Sleeping Beauty, King Stefan orders all spinning wheels in the kingdom to be burned. It doesn't work, as the curse can't be avoided.

q: In the animated movie Sleeping Beauty, just prior to Auroras 16th birthday, Maleficent is furious that she and her evil henchmen still cannot find Aurora. What does Maleficent do?
She sends out her raven Diablo to find Aurora.
She consults her crystal ball for Aurora.
She disguises herself as a peasant and searches for Aurora.
She puts the prince under a spell and sends him to search for Aurora.

q.e: In Sleeping Beauty, Maleficent sends out her raven Diablo to find Aurora. He sees her at the cottage.

q: In the animated movie Sleeping Beauty, the fairies enter Maleficents castle and free the prince and give him these two magical objects.

q.e: The fairies free Prince Phillip from Maleficent's castle and give him the Sword of Truth and the Shield of Virtue. Those magic items help him defeat the dragon.

q: In the animated film Sleeping Beauty, Aurora and Prince Phillip dance a waltz and do not notice the fairies magically changing the color of Auroras ball gown. As the book closes, Auroras gown turns this color and remains this color.

q.e: At the end of Sleeping Beauty, the fairies keep fighting over whether Aurora's dress should be pink or blue. The dress ends up pink as the film closes.

q: What was the first name of the animated 1980s hero Blackstar?

q.e: Blackstar was an astronaut named John Blackstar, who gets sucked into a black hole and lands on the planet Sagar. The Filmation cartoon aired in 1981.

q: How did Blackstar from the animated series of the same name get stranded in the alien world?
After falling in a black hole
After an impact with an asteroid

q.e: John Blackstar was an astronaut who was pulled through a black hole into the planet Sagar. There he becomes a hero using the Power Sword.

q: In what year were the Blackstar animated series first broadcast on American television?

q.e: Blackstar first aired on American TV in 1981, produced by Filmation, who also made He-Man. It was a short-lived series.

q: How many episodes of the animated series Blackstar ran on American television?

q.e: Blackstar ran for 13 episodes in 1981. It was Filmation's sword-and-sorcery space series.

q: In 1949 Disney released their animated versions of The Wind in the Willows and this short story.

q.e: Disney's The Adventures of Ichabod and Mr. Toad (1949) paired The Wind in the Willows with The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, a Washington Irving story. Bing Crosby narrated the Ichabod half.

q: What year did the animated series The Adventures of Jimmy Neutron: Boy Genius 1st air?

q.e: The Adventures of Jimmy Neutron: Boy Genius debuted as a series on Nickelodeon in 2002, after the movie came out in 2001. It was created by John A. Davis.

q: What are Libbys and Cindys last names on the animated show The Adventures of Jimmy Neutron: Boy Genius?

q.e: Libby Folfax and Cindy Vortex are Jimmy's friends in Retroville. Cindy is his rival and secret love interest.

q: What is the name of the cartoon cat that terrorizes the mouse, Jerry?

q.e: Tom, a cat, chases Jerry, a mouse, in Tom and Jerry. William Hanna and Joseph Barbera created them in 1940, and the cartoons won seven Oscars.

q: Name the first cartoon cat that was created for the screen.

q.e: Felix the Cat made his silent film debut in the 1919 animated short Feline Follies, quickly becoming cinema's first widely recognized cartoon superstar.

q: Which 1996 animated live-action film featured cartoon character Marvin the Martian?

q.e: Marvin the Martian serves as the referee in the 1996 movie Space Jam, officiating the climactic basketball game between the Tune Squad and the Monstars. He was chosen as a neutral party because he was considered both a Looney Tunes character and an alien.

q: Stan Smith is married to Francine and is the father of Hayley and Steve in this popular cartoon.

q.e: Stan Smith, a CIA agent, lives with wife Francine, daughter Hayley and son Steve in American Dad!. It was created by Seth MacFarlane and others, and began in 2005.

q: When was the animated feature Aladdin released?

q.e: Disney's Aladdin was released on November 25, 1992, and became the highest-grossing film of the year. A hand-drawn feature, it relied on Robin Williams' Genie.

q: What does the butler put into the cats night-time milk in the animated feature The Aristocats?

q.e: In The Aristocats (1970), the butler Edgar puts sleeping pills in the cats' milk before getting rid of them. He wants to make sure the cats don't inherit Madame's fortune.

q: In 1954 a British group released a full length animated version of this George Orwell novel.
Down and Out in London and Paris

q.e: Halas and Batchelor produced the 1954 animated adaptation of Animal Farm, which was notably funded in part by the American CIA as Cold War propaganda. Orwell's dystopian novel Nineteen Eighty-Four was adapted into a live-action film in 1956.

q: Who turns Pinocchio into a real boy in the 1940 animated Disney movie Pinocchio?

q.e: The Blue Fairy breathes life into Geppetto's wooden puppet in Disney's 1940 film and ultimately transforms Pinocchio into a real human boy after he proves himself brave, truthful, and unselfish.

q: This animated film was produced by Steven Spielbergs Amblin Entertainment. The films main character became a mascot for UNICEF.
The Adventures of the American Rabbit

q.e: An American Tail (1986) is about Fievel Mousekewitz, a Russian-Jewish mouse who emigrates to America. It was made by Steven Spielberg's Amblin and Don Bluth, and Fievel became a UNICEF mascot.

q: Nowadays most animated movies are made using CGI. What does CGI stand for?

q.e: CGI stands for Computer Generated Imagery, covering 2D and 3D computer graphics used in visual effects, video games, and animated films.

q: The first full length animated movie was made and released in this country.

q.e: The first feature-length animated film was El Apóstol (1917) from Argentina, by Quirino Cristiani. The film has been lost, so Snow White (1937) is often thought of as the first.

q: In 1935, a full length cartoon version of Gullivers Travels was made. What was unusual about it?
It told the story from a Communist point of view.
It uses much of the exact dialog from Swifts novel.
It is told as a flashback.
It combines animation and human actors.

q.e: The New Gulliver (1935) was a Soviet film by Aleksandr Ptushko that used puppet animation and a live boy, and retold Gulliver's Travels as a story of class struggle. Fleischer's Hollywood Gulliver's Travels came in 1939.

q: What was the first full length animated movie made by Disney?
Academy Award Review of Walt Disney Cartoons
Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs

q.e: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937) is generally listed as Disney's first full-length animated film. The "Academy Award Review of Walt Disney Cartoons" was a 1937 compilation of short films shown by Disney to promote Snow White.

q: What character did Bruce Willis voice in the 2003 animated movie Rugrats Go Wild?

q.e: Bruce Willis voiced Spike, the Pickles family's dog, in Rugrats Go Wild (2003), a crossover with The Wild Thornberrys. He was also in Rugrats-related projects as Spike.

q: For what purpose were the WALL-E robots designed in the 2008 computer-animated science fiction movie WALL-E?
To take care of human babies

q.e: In the film, WALL-E stands for 'Waste Allocation Load Lifter: Earth-Class', a series of solar-powered robots left behind to compact and stack trash after humanity abandoned the planet.

q: What famous actor and comedian voiced Mushu the Chinese dragon in the 1998 animated movie Mulan?

q.e: Eddie Murphy voiced Mushu the dragon in Disney's Mulan (1998). He later used a similar style as Donkey in Shrek.

q: Who directed the 2007 animated movie Meet the Robinsons?

q.e: Stephen J. Anderson directed Meet the Robinsons (2007), based on William Joyce's book A Day with Wilbur Robinson. It was his first film as director.

q: In the 2001 animated comedy movie Shrek, the donkey falls in love with what character?

q.e: In Shrek (2001), Donkey falls in love with the female Dragon who guards Fiona. They later have hybrid "Dronkeys" in the sequel.

q: What actor was offered a role in the 2001 animated movie Shrek but turned it down?

q.e: Shrek (2001), from DreamWorks, is loosely based on William Steig's picture book. Mike Myers voiced Shrek, after the late Chris Farley recorded a lot of the part.

q: How did Alexs parents recognize their son after so many years in the 2008 animated comedy movie Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa?

q.e: In Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa (2008), Alex's parents recognize him by the mole or beauty mark on his body. He was taken from Africa as a cub.

q: What is the special talent of Alex the Lion from the 2008 animated comedy movie Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa?

q.e: Alex the lion's talent in Escape 2 Africa is dancing. It's what he used to do in the zoo as "Alex the Lion".

q: What rapper and singer voices Moto Moto the Hippopotamus in the 2008 animated comedy Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa?

q.e: will.i.am of the Black Eyed Peas voiced Moto Moto, the hippo, in Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa. Moto Moto is liked by the ladies for being "a big boy".

q: What character did Whoopi Goldberg voice in the 1998 animated movie The Rugrats Movie?

q.e: Whoopi Goldberg voiced Ranger Margaret in the Rugrats movie series. She plays a ranger in a Rugrats outing.

q: What popular comedian and actor voiced the characters Ramon and Lovelace in the 2006 animated movie Happy Feet?

q: What animals pilot the airplane to Africa in the 2008 animated comedy movie Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa?

q: What is the name of the zebra voiced by Chris Rock in the 2008 animated comedy movie Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa?

q.e: Chris Rock voices Marty the zebra across the Madagascar animated film franchise. Alex the lion is voiced by Ben Stiller, and Melman the giraffe is voiced by David Schwimmer.

q: What actor voiced Makunga the Lion in the 2008 animated comedy movie Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa?

q.e: Alec Baldwin voiced Makunga in Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa. Makunga is Zuba's rival.

q: Who is Melman the Giraffe in love with in the 2008 animated comedy movie Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa?

q.e: Melman the giraffe loves Gloria the hippo in the Madagascar movies. In Escape 2 Africa, he finally says it.

q: What does King Julien the Lemur wish he could do in the 2008 animated movie Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa?

q.e: In Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa, King Julien the ring-tailed lemur, voiced by Sacha Baron Cohen, wishes he could do something he can't. Julien is the ruler of the lemurs.

q: This Walt Disney animated movie was released in 1989 and became one of the most successful films of the year.

q.e: Released in November 1989, The Little Mermaid grossed over 200 million dollars worldwide and launched what is widely known as the Disney Renaissance.

q: What animal did Whoopi Goldberg voice in the 1994 animated movie The Lion King?

q.e: Whoopi Goldberg voiced Shenzi, one of the three hyenas, in The Lion King (1994). Cheech Marin voiced Banzai.

q: What name do Ellie and Manny give to their first-born child in the 2009 animated movie Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs?

q.e: Ellie and Manny name their baby Peaches in Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs (2009). Her name is a reference to a fruit.

q: How does Nemo disappear in the 2003 animated movie Finding Nemo?

q.e: Nemo is taken by a scuba diver, a dentist, in Finding Nemo (2003). He ends up in a tank in Sydney.

q: What is the name of the 1998 animated movie in which Kevin Spacey voiced an evil grasshopper named Hopper?

q.e: Kevin Spacey voiced Hopper, the villainous grasshopper, in A Bug's Life (1998). It's Pixar's second feature.

q: What Academy Award-winning actress voiced the Queen Ant in the 2006 animated movie The Ant Bully?

q.e: Meryl Streep has won three Academy Awards, and voiced the Queen Ant in The Ant Bully (2006). She is a respected actress.

q: What type of animal character, named Master Shifu, did Dustin Hoffman voice in the 2008 animated movie Kung Fu Panda?

q.e: Master Shifu is a red panda, voiced by Dustin Hoffman, in Kung Fu Panda (2008). He trains Po.

q: What outfits did the creators of the animated sitcom South Park, Trey Parker and Matt Stone, wear at the 72nd Academy Awards ceremony in 2000?

q.e: Trey Parker and Matt Stone wore dresses to the Oscars in 2000, for South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut (nominated for Best Original Song). Parker wore a copy of Jennifer Lopez's dress.

q: #10 on the list of highest-grossing films is this Disney animated feature film, which came out in 1937 and earned $1,746,100,000.
Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs

q.e: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937) is on the list of highest-grossing films when adjusted for inflation. The money number is based on those adjustments.

q: In the animated film One Hundred and One Dalmatians, what distracts the Baduns long enough to allow Sergeant Tibbs to flee with the puppies?
A television show called Whats My Crime
A video game called Whats My Crime
A board game called Whats My Crime
A radio chat segment called Whats My Crime

q.e: In 101 Dalmatians (1961), the Badun brothers are distracted by a TV show called "What's My Crime?". Sergeant Tibbs, a cat, helps the puppies.

q: What animated movie won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature at the 74th Academy Award in 2002?

q.e: Shrek (2001) won the first-ever Academy Award for Best Animated Feature, presented at the 74th ceremony in 2002. The category was created that year.

q: Which of the following Oscar-nominated movies won the award for Best Animated Feature at the 2004 ceremony?

q.e: Finding Nemo (2003) won Best Animated Feature at the 2004 ceremony. It was the first Pixar movie to win that award.

q: What animated movie won the Best Animated Feature at the 75th Academy Awards in 2003?

q.e: Directed by Hayao Miyazaki and produced by Studio Ghibli, Spirited Away became the first hand-drawn, non-English-language film to win the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.

q: Which of these films was NOT produced by Pixar, the company Steve Jobs acquired in 1986?

q.e: The Princess and the Frog (2009) was made by Disney, not Pixar. Steve Jobs bought Pixar from Lucasfilm in 1986 for $5 million.

q: David Schwimmer, who co-starred in the television show Friends, plays a hypochondriac character in which animated movie?

q.e: David Schwimmer voiced Melman, a hypochondriac giraffe, in Madagascar (2005). He's afraid of germs and constantly checks his symptoms.

q: What 1967 animated Disney feature is this song from?

q.e: Disney's The Jungle Book (1967) was the last animated feature Walt Disney supervised before he died in 1966. Its songs include "The Bare Necessities".

q: In the Peanuts cartoon strip, who does Marcie call Sir?

q.e: Marcie calls Peppermint Patty "Sir" in Peanuts, even though Patty tells her to stop. It's a running gag.

q: Olympian Gods Hera, Zeus and Hades share the screen with mortal Meg in what Disney animated movie?

q.e: Disney released Hercules in 1997, featuring Megara, Hades voiced by James Woods, and Zeus voiced by Rip Torn.

q: Who is Fred Flintstones boss at the Slate Rock and Gravel Company?

q.e: Fred Flintstone works as a bronto-crane operator at the Slate Rock and Gravel Company under his quick-tempered boss, Mr. Slate.

q: Created by Australian Pat Sullivan, this cat was the star of the first talkie cartoon.

q.e: Felix the Cat, created by Pat Sullivan's studio (animated by Otto Messmer), was the most famous cartoon star of the 1920s. The first cartoon with synchronized sound that went big was Disney's Steamboat Willie (1928).

q: This elegant cartoon Persian cat was created for Walt Disneys 1970 animated feature, The Aristocats.

q.e: Duchess is the white Persian cat who is the mother of Marie, Toulouse and Berlioz in The Aristocats (1970). Eva Gabor voiced her.

q: What was Walt Disneys first animated feature film?
Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs

q.e: Released in December 1937, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs was not only Disney's first animated feature film, but also the world's first full-length cel-animated feature. Cinderella followed much later in 1950.

q: This 1984 comedy started a successful franchise under which 6 hilarious sequels, an animated TV series and a live-action TV series appeared.

q.e: Police Academy (1984) led to six sequels, a 1988 animated series and a 1997 live-action series. The films starred Steve Guttenberg and Kim Cattrall.

q: What year was Pixars computer-animated film Finding Nemo released?

q.e: Finding Nemo was released in 2003 by Pixar. It's about a clownfish father searching for his son.

q: Who voiced Nemos father, Marlin in the animated film Finding Nemo?

q.e: Albert Brooks voiced Marlin, Nemo's overprotective father, in Finding Nemo (2003). Ellen DeGeneres voiced Dory.

q: Pizza is the favorite food of these cartoon characters.

q.e: The Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles love pizza. The characters began as an indie comic by Kevin Eastman and Peter Laird in 1984.

q: Which cartoon character is known as the fastest mouse in all Mexico?

q.e: Speedy Gonzales debuted in 1953 and became a Warner Bros. regular in 1955, celebrated as the fastest mouse in Mexico and often shouting '¡Ándale! ¡Ándale! ¡Arriba! ¡Arriba!'.

q: What is the name of the potion that Donkey and Shrek take in the animated movie Shrek 2?

q.e: In Shrek 2 (2004), Shrek and Donkey drink the "Happily Ever After" potion, which makes Shrek human and Donkey a stallion. Fiona's father, King Harold, is the one who sets it up.

q: Which of these voice actors/actresses from The Simpsons series, is a Scientologist?

q.e: Nancy Cartwright, the voice of Bart Simpson, is a member of the Church of Scientology. She's also written about it publicly.

q: How many seasons did The Flintstones air?

q.e: The Flintstones aired for six seasons (1960-1966) on ABC. It was Hanna-Barbera's biggest hit for a while.

q: In the animated series The Flintstones, the Flintstones and the Rubbles lived in what town?

q.e: The Flintstones lived at 345 Cave Stone Road in the prehistoric city of Bedrock. The town featured stone-age technologies powered by animals, such as pterodactyl record players and woolly mammoth garbage disposals.

q: On The Flintstones, Fred and Barney are members of what lodge?
The Loyal Order of Water Buffaloes

q.e: Fred Flintstone and Barney Rubble belonged to Lodge No. 26 of the Loyal Order of Water Buffaloes, whose members famously wore blue furry hats sporting horns. The Stonecutters is a parody lodge from The Simpsons.

q: What was the name of the Rubbles pet on The Flintstones?

q.e: Hoppy the Hopparoo is the Rubbles' pet, a kangaroo-like dinosaur. Dino is the Flintstones' pet.

q: What is Freds nickname in the Bedrock bowling team, featured on The Flintstones?

q.e: Fred's nickname on the bowling team is "Twinkle Toes", a joke because he is large but nimble. The nickname appears in the 1960s episodes.

q: Gary, an accomplished snail-poet, is the pet of the main character in which cartoon?

q.e: Gary, who meows like a cat, is SpongeBob's pet snail. In an episode he writes a poem as a poet.

q: Spritle and his pet chimp, Chim Chim often got into trouble in this cartoon series.

q.e: Spritle is the mischievous younger brother of Speed Racer in the classic 1967 anime adaptation. He and his pet chimpanzee, Chim-Chim, frequently hid in the trunk of the Mach 5.

q: Santas Little Helper and Snowball are the pets of Bart, Lisa, Maggie, Homer and Marge, the popular characters from which animated sitcom?

q.e: Santa's Little Helper (a greyhound) and Snowball II (a cat) are the Simpsons' pets. Both showed up in the first season.

q: Bandit is Jonnys pet in this science fiction animated TV series, produced by Hanna-Barbera Productions.

q.e: Bandit is Jonny's pet bulldog in Jonny Quest (1964). The series was made by Hanna-Barbera and was an adventure show.

q: Which original member of the Pin Pals, Homer Simpsons bowling team, is forced by circumstances to give up his place in the team?

q.e: In "Team Homer" (1992), Homer forms a bowling team, the Pin Pals, with Moe, Apu, Otto and Lenny/Carl to win the league. They win the championship against Mr. Burns's team.

q: In The Simpsons, how much does homer pay for Professor Frinks matter transporter?

q.e: Professor Frink's matter transporter is sold to Homer for 75 cents in a Treehouse of Horror segment. The Simpsons are known for weird prices like that.

q: Who is the creator of the animated TV series Family Guy?

q.e: Seth MacFarlane created Family Guy, which debuted on Fox in 1999. He also voices Peter, Stewie, Brian and Quagmire.

q: What year was the animated series Family Guy created?

q.e: Family Guy began in 1999, after a pilot in 1998. Fox canceled it in 2002, but it came back in 2005.

q: Who does the voices of Peter, Stewie, Brian, Quagmire and Tom Tucker in the animated series Family Guy?

q.e: Series creator Seth MacFarlane voices many of Family Guy's central characters, including Peter, Stewie, and Brian Griffin, as well as neighbor Glenn Quagmire and news anchor Tom Tucker.

q: Fred Flintstone and Barney Rubble of The Flintstones were members of what club?
Loyal Order of Water Buffaloes Lodge

q.e: Fred and Barney belong to the Loyal Order of Water Buffaloes Lodge, a spoof of fraternal groups like the Elks. This was a play on The Honeymooners, which inspired The Flintstones.

q: On the animated sitcom Family Guy, Peter Griffin and his buddies can be found at which bar?

q.e: The Drunken Clam is the bar in Quahog where Peter, Cleveland, Quagmire and Joe drink. It's a regular setting in Family Guy.

q: These twins in the animated TV series, Rugrats enjoy playing in mud and eating worms and insects.

q.e: Phil and Lil DeVille are twins in Rugrats (1991) who like worms and mud. Their mother is Betty, and their brother is Chuckie's friend.

q: In the animated TV series, The Simpsons, Bart is how many years older than his sister Lisa?

q.e: Bart is 10 and Lisa is 8, so Bart is two years older. The Simpsons' ages are fixed even though the show has run for decades.

q: Which Hanna-Barbera cartoon featured a boy parachuting from a crashing plane and saved by a caveman?

q.e: Dino Boy in the Lost Valley (1964) was a Hanna-Barbera segment about a boy who survives a plane crash and is rescued by a caveman, Bronty. It was part of Space Ghost and Dino Boy.

q: Which of the following cartoons was not created by Hanna-Barbera?

q.e: Popeye was created by E.C. Segar in 1929 for the comic strip Thimble Theatre, not by Hanna-Barbera. Hanna-Barbera made The Flintstones, Yogi Bear and Scooby-Doo.

q: In the animated series The Flintstones, Fred and Barney were members of what lodge organization?

q.e: Fred and Barney belong to the Loyal Order of Water Buffaloes, a parody of fraternal lodges. The show was loosely based on The Honeymooners.

q: In the animated sitcom Family Guy, while the family dog is in Los Angeles in pursuit of career, he stays with whom?

q.e: In Family Guy, Brian stays with his friend Jasper, his gay cousin, when he goes to Los Angeles. Jasper first appears in season 3.

q: Which cartoon superheros perilous love interest was Sweet Polly Purebred?

q.e: Underdog's alter ego Shoeshine Boy was voiced by Wally Cox, and his recurring love interest and damsel in distress was television reporter Sweet Polly Purebred.

q: Created by William Hanna and Joseph Barbera, this cartoon sheriff was the high-falutinest, fastest shootinest cowboy you ever saw.

q.e: Quick Draw McGraw was a horse sheriff in Hanna-Barbera's 1959 cartoon. His sidekick was Baba Looey and he had the catchphrase "And I'll do the thinkin' round here".

q: The Flintstones featured several delightful musical performances provided by celebrity voice artists. Which one of these did not lend their vocal talents to the show?

q.e: The Flintstones had guest stars, like Ann-Margret as "Ann-Margrock" and Tony Curtis. Ricky Nelson also appeared in a 1962 episode as Ricky Stoneberg.

q: Yogi Bear debuted in 1958 as a supporting character in which animated series?

q.e: Yogi Bear first appeared in The Huckleberry Hound Show (1958), then got his own show in 1961. He is known for stealing pic-a-nic baskets.

q: In the animated television series The Simpsons, what was the last name of the long-suffering neighbor of the Simpsons?

q.e: Ned Flanders is the Simpsons' kind-hearted next-door neighbor, whose "-diddly-" speech is famous. Homer annoys him constantly.

q: What fictional character from popular television animated series, The Flintstones, was voiced by Mel Blanc?

q.e: Mel Blanc, "the Man of a Thousand Voices", voiced Barney Rubble in the first seasons of The Flintstones. He also voiced Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck.

q: What year did the great cartoon The Jetsons first hit the airwaves?

q.e: The Jetsons premiered in September 1962 as a prime-time show on ABC. It was Hanna-Barbera's space-age counterpart to The Flintstones.

q: What was the name of the Jetsons dog on the animated sitcom The Jetsons?

q.e: Astro is the Jetson family's loyal Great Dane, known for replacing initial letters with 'R' when speaking, such as his catchphrase 'Ruh-roh, Regge!'

q: What was the name of the high school that Judy Jetson attended on the 60s cartoon, The Jetsons?

q.e: Judy Jetson attends Orbit High School in The Jetsons. The show was set in 2062.

q: In what year did the animated Christmas classic Santa Claus is Comin to Town make its debut on American television?

q.e: Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town, a Rankin/Bass special, debuted on ABC in December 1970. Fred Astaire narrated it as S.D. Kluger.

q: What is the name of Krusty the Clowns illegitimate daughter on the animated TV show The Simpsons?

q.e: Sophie Krustofski is Krusty the Clown's daughter. His real name is Herschel Krustofski, the son of Rabbi Hyman Krustofski.

q: Who is the first Emperor of the Moon in the animated series Futurama?

q.e: Futurama has celebrity heads in jars, and Al Gore appears as a character in the show. The series was created by Matt Groening.

q: In what year did the Popeye the Sailor cartoon debut?

q.e: Popeye the Sailor made his cartoon debut in 1933 in a Betty Boop short, produced by Fleischer Studios. He first appeared in the comics in 1929.

q: What was the name of Popeyes hometown according to the popular cartoon?

q.e: Popeye is a sailor created by E.C. Segar, who first showed him in the comic strip Thimble Theatre in 1929. The cartoons were by Fleischer and later Famous Studios.

q: This vegetable gave cartoon character Popeye superhuman strength when he consumed it.

q.e: E.C. Segar gave Popeye his trademark can of strength-giving spinach in his comic strip around 1932, a trait that became even more prominent in the animated shorts.

q: Who created the animated series Family Guy?

q.e: Seth MacFarlane created Family Guy. He was only 24 when it first aired.

q: In the Family Guy animated series, what problem does Brian Griffin have?

q.e: Brian Griffin, the Griffins' dog, drinks too much and is shown as an alcoholic in the series. He's also a writer.

q: Who lives next door to the Simpsons on the popular animated show?

q.e: Ned Flanders lives at 744 Evergreen Terrace, directly next door to the Simpson family at 742 Evergreen Terrace.

q: Wayne and Lucien, from this cartoon series, are closely related but hate each others guts.

q.e: Wayne and Lucien Cramp are the title twins of The Cramp Twins (2001), a British-American cartoon. They fight constantly.

q: Which of these episodes is not in the fourth season of The Simpsons?

q.e: "Treehouse of Horror IV" is in season five (1993), not season four. It's the Halloween episode featuring "The Devil and Homer Simpson".

q: Who is Timmys evil babysitter in the animated series The Fairly OddParents?

q.e: Vicky is Timmy Turner's evil babysitter in The Fairly OddParents, who torments him. Only Timmy can see her cruelty.

q: What are the names of Timmy Turners fairy godparents in the popular animated series?

q.e: In Nickelodeon's The Fairly OddParents, green-haired Cosmo and pink-haired Wanda serve as Timmy Turner's magical, well-meaning fairy godparents.

q: In what year did Yogi Bear get his own animated series?

q.e: The Yogi Bear Show premiered in 1961, after he debuted on The Huckleberry Hound Show in 1958. It featured Boo-Boo.

q: In what year did the animated series Yo Yogi first hit the airwaves?

q.e: Yo Yogi! debuted in 1991 and showed the characters as teens at a mall. It was made by Hanna-Barbera.

q: What is the name of the substitute teacher in Saved by the Bell who takes over for Ms. Simpsons class when she injures her back?

q.e: Tony Crane is the substitute teacher in Saved by the Bell. The sitcom is about Bayside High students in California.

q: What is the Hills address on the animated show King of the Hill?

q.e: The Hills live at 84 Rainey Street in Arlen, Texas, in King of the Hill. Arlen is fictional.

q: Which was the first cartoon with a fully synchronized soundtrack?

q.e: Released in 1928, Walt Disney's Steamboat Willie made Mickey Mouse famous by synchronizing sound, voice, and musical score on film. While older cartoons used standalone audio recordings, Steamboat Willie printed the audio track directly onto the film strip.

q: In what year did the cartoon series The Simpsons debut?

q.e: After appearing as animated shorts on The Tracey Ullman Show starting in 1987, The Simpsons premiered as a standalone half-hour series on December 17, 1989, with a Christmas special.

q: In The Simpsons episode, Homer vs. Patty and Selma, Homer sells his Power Plant stock for how much?

q.e: "Homer vs. Patty and Selma" (1996) is a season 6 episode of The Simpsons. Homer and Marge's sisters, Patty and Selma, feature heavily.

q: What is Lisas teachers name on the TV show The Simpsons?

q.e: Elizabeth Hoover is Lisa's second-grade teacher in The Simpsons. She is voiced by Maggie Roswell.

q: What was the name of the building in which Looney Tunes were first created from 1935-1937?

q.e: Termite Terrace was the nickname of the ramshackle studio building where Warner Bros. animators like Tex Avery and Chuck Jones created Looney Tunes. It was on the Warner lot.

q: What is the first name of Dr. Hibbert, Springfields prominent doctor on The Simpsons?

q.e: Dr. Julius Hibbert is Springfield's doctor, known for his laugh. He's voiced by Harry Shearer.

q: Dont have a cow, man! and Eat my shorts! are the catch phrases used by what character on The Simpsons?

q.e: Bart Simpson's rebellious catchphrases became pop-culture sensations during the early 1990s. His father Homer is better known for yelling 'D'oh!' and 'Mmm... donuts'.

q: Who drives the school bus in The Simpsons?

q.e: Otto Mann is the school bus driver in The Simpsons. He's a heavy metal fan.

q: Who is The Simpsons doctor on the self-titled TV show?

q.e: Dr. Hibbert is the Simpsons' family doctor, and Dr. Nick Riviera is the less qualified doctor. The latter sells cheap procedures.

q: What was the original name given to the mouse later known as Jerry from the Tom and Jerry cartoon show?

q.e: In Tom and Jerry's first short, "Puss Gets the Boot" (1940), Jerry was named Jinx and Tom was called Jasper. They were renamed after a contest.

q: What peculiar voice characteristic does Sylvester the Cat from Looney Tunes possess?
He has a very deep husky voice.
He has a very high voice.

q.e: Sylvester the Cat has a lisp, saying "Sufferin' succotash". Mel Blanc voiced him.

q: What is Uncle Fester from The Addams Family animated series terrified of?

q.e: Uncle Fester Addams is a bald and eccentric character in The Addams Family. He lights bulbs in his mouth.

q: Johnny Bravo from the animated series of the same name has an obsession for this beauty product.

q.e: Johnny Bravo is vain about his pompadour, and is often shown combing it. The Cartoon Network show ran from 1997 to 2004.

q: Which of these cartoon characters has been Speedy Gonzales arch enemy?

q.e: Speedy Gonzales, "the fastest mouse in all Mexico", usually outsmarts Sylvester. Daffy Duck is his friend/foil in some cartoons.

q: What does Elmer J. Fudd usually hunt in the Looney Tunes animated series?

q.e: Elmer Fudd is best known for hunting Bugs Bunny, famously declaring that he is hunting 'wabbits'. While he also occasionally targets Daffy Duck during 'duck season', rabbits remain his primary quarry.

q: Which of these awards was actually given to a Scooby gang member at prom in season 3 of Buffy the Vampire Slayer?

q.e: At the Sunnydale High prom in Buffy season 3's "The Prom", Buffy is given a "Class Protector" award by her classmates. It's one of the show's most emotional scenes.

q: In what year did the animated series He-Man and the Masters of the Universe debut?

q.e: He-Man and the Masters of the Universe debuted in 1983 from Filmation. It was created to sell Mattel toys.

q: What was Lisas first word on the animated sitcom The Simpsons?

q.e: Lisa's first word was "Bart", in "Lisa's First Word" (1992). Maggie's first word was "Daddy".

q: Aqua Teen Hunger Force is a 15 minute show that airs on Cartoon Networks Adult Swim lineup. It is actually a spin-off from another Adult Swim show. What show did the Aqua Teens first appear on?

q.e: Aqua Teen Hunger Force's characters first appeared in an episode of Space Ghost Coast to Coast, a talk show parody. The ATHF premiered in 2000.

q: How many episodes of the animated show Top Cat were aired on television?

q.e: Top Cat aired 30 episodes on ABC from 1961 to 1962. It was inspired by The Phil Silvers Show.

q: In the 80s cartoon Thundercats what was the name of Lion-Os sword?

q.e: Lion-O wields the Sword of Omens, which houses the mystical Eye of Thundera in its hilt. The sword grants Lion-O powers like Sight Beyond Sight and can shoot energy blasts.

q: How many episodes of the animated series Thundercats were produced?

q.e: ThunderCats had 130 episodes between 1985 and 1989. Lion-O is the main character.

q: Who is Timmys teacher in the animated TV series The Fairly OddParents?

q.e: Mr. Crocker is Timmy's obsessed teacher in The Fairly OddParents, who tries to prove fairies exist. His name is Denzel Crocker.

q: What statement is true about Donatellos inventions on the TMNT cartoon?
They never have any practical use.

q.e: Donatello is the inventor of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, who wears a purple mask and fights with a staff. His inventions sometimes malfunction.

q: What is the favorite band of Phineas and Ferbs parents on the popular animated TV series?

q.e: Phineas and Ferb's parents love the band Love Händel. Lawrence Fletcher plays in it in the show.

q: How old is Brian on the animated show Family Guy?

q.e: Brian Griffin is the Griffins' talking dog. His age is often given in dog years.

q: How many people live in the Griffin household on the animated show Family Guy?

q.e: The Griffin home has Peter, Lois, Meg, Chris and Stewie, plus Brian the dog. It's at 31 Spooner Street.

q: What year did the animated series SpongeBob SquarePants first air?

q.e: Created by marine science educator and animator Stephen Hillenburg, SpongeBob SquarePants debuted on Nickelodeon on May 1, 1999, following the Kids' Choice Awards.

q: Who voices Penny Proud in the animated TV series The Proud Family?

q.e: Kyla Pratt voices Penny Proud in The Proud Family. She was also in Dr. Dolittle.

q: Which animator and cartoon director created two of the most famous Looney Tunes characters - Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck?

q.e: Tex Avery directed the first Daffy Duck cartoon, "Porky's Duck Hunt" (1937). He also developed Bugs Bunny in "A Wild Hare" (1940).

q: Which of these cartoon characters was created first in 1937?

q.e: Daffy Duck debuted in 1937 in "Porky's Duck Hunt". Bugs Bunny's official debut was 1940.

q: Which cartoon character, created by Robert McKimson in 1954, was based on a real Australian animal?
Wiley Coyote and the Road Runner

q.e: The Tasmanian Devil, nicknamed Taz, was created by animator Robert McKimson based on the carnivorous marsupial native to the Australian island state of Tasmania.

q: Where do Homer and his family go, after he wrote a song about Ned Flanders in an episode of The Simpsons fourteenth season?

q.e: In a season 14 Simpsons episode, Homer and the family go to a ranch. The show covers many different locations.

q: This popular animated sitcom had only two seasons before it was canceled. It starred Jon Lovitz and Nancy Cartwright.

q.e: The Critic (1994) is about movie critic Jay Sherman, voiced by Jon Lovitz, and ran for two seasons. Nancy Cartwright voiced Penny.

q: What is the name of the main character in the animated sitcom Futurama, created by Matt Groening?

q.e: Philip J. Fry is a pizza delivery boy accidentally cryogenically frozen on New Year's Eve in 1999, waking up in the year 2999. Matt Groening named the character after the late comedian Phil Hartman.

q: In what year did the popular cartoon character Pluto make his debut?

q.e: Pluto debuted in 1930, in The Chain Gang. He was originally an unnamed dog.

q: In "Avatar: The Last Airbender", which element does Prince Zuko bend?

q.e: Prince Zuko is the crown prince of the Fire Nation and an adept firebender who seeks to restore his honor by capturing the Avatar. Later in the series, he learns original firebending techniques directly from the Sun Warriors and ancient dragons.

q: What was Maggie Simpson's first canonical word, not including the Tracey Ullman shorts?

q.e: Maggie's first word was "Daddy", spoken in "Lisa's First Word" (1992). Elizabeth Taylor voiced the moment.

q: In the 1969 Cartoon show "Dastardly and Muttley in Their Flying Machines", which were NOT one of the lyrics in the opening theme?

q.e: Dastardly and Muttley in Their Flying Machines (1969) was a Hanna-Barbera show. Its theme song includes lines about stopping the pigeon.

q: In "Gravity Falls", the character Bill Cipher remarks that "the universe is what?"

q.e: Bill Cipher, the triangle demon in Gravity Falls, says the universe is a hologram. The show was created by Alex Hirsch.

q: Who voice acted the character Hiccup in the movie "How to Train Your Dragon"?

q.e: Jay Baruchel voiced Hiccup in How to Train Your Dragon (2010). The film is based on Cressida Cowell's books.

q: What town was "Springfield" from "The Simpsons" originally named after?

q.e: Matt Groening said he named Springfield after Springfield, Oregon, near his hometown of Portland. It's a very common name in the US.

q: What was the name of Jonny's pet dog in The Adventures of Jonny Quest?

q.e: Bandit is Jonny's pet bulldog. Jonny Quest first aired in 1964.

q: In the TV show "Rick and Morty", Rick uses the catchphrase "Wubba Lubba Dub Dub", which means what in Birdperson?
I am in great pain, please help me.
I pray that my life ends soon.
I am suffering, please help me.

q.e: In "Rick and Morty", "Wubba lubba dub dub" is revealed to mean "I am in great pain, please help me" in Birdperson's language. Rick uses it as a catchphrase.

q: A 50-foot, metal-eating robot befriends a boy in which 1999 film?

q.e: Directed by Brad Bird, The Iron Giant follows nine-year-old Hogarth Hughes in 1957 Maine as he protects an extraterrestrial metal giant voiced by Vin Diesel.

q: Cruella de Vil kidnapped which title brood?

q.e: Cruella de Vil targets Pongo and Perdita's litter of 15 puppies, eventually amassing 99 dalmatian pups to make a spotted fur coat. Dodie Smith created the villain in her 1956 novel, adapted by Disney in 1961.

q: This actor gave his voice to the popular animated cartoon cat Garfield. He was also known as the voice of Carlton, the doorman on the television comedy Rhoda, a spin-off of the Mary Tyler More Show.

q.e: Lorenzo Music voiced Garfield in the TV cartoons and also Carlton the doorman, unseen, on Rhoda. Bill Murray voiced Garfield in the films.

q: To which of these animated films has popular American actress and voice artist, Mae Questel not contributed?

q.e: Mae Questel voiced Betty Boop and Olive Oyl, but not Mickey Mouse, who was voiced by Walt Disney himself. She also appeared in New York Stories.

q: This remarkable ventriloquist voiced Scooby-Doo, Papa Smurf, Astro (the Jetsons dog), Hampton Pig, Boo-Boo (Yogi Bears buddy) and Ruff from Ruff n Reddy.

q.e: Don Messick was a voice actor who voiced Scooby-Doo, Papa Smurf and Astro, among others. He worked for Hanna-Barbera.

q: What animal character did Angelina Jolie voice in the 2008 animated movie Kung Fu Panda?

q.e: Angelina Jolie voiced Master Tigress, the fierce and stoic leader of the Furious Five martial artists. Jack Black voiced the titular giant panda, Po.

q: What animated television series aired Saturday mornings from September 14, 1991 on NBC, where the main character looked like and was voiced like Macaulay Culkin?
Make A Wish With Macaulay Culkin
The Magic Glove Of Macaulay Culkin

q.e: The Wish Kid (1991) was an NBC cartoon about Brant Bixby, who made wishes with a baseball mitt, voiced by Macaulay Culkin. It was based on a film star.

q: What character did actress Kathleen Turner voice in the 2006 animated movie Monster House?

q.e: Kathleen Turner voiced Constance, the "giantess" in Monster House (2006). The film was produced by Robert Zemeckis and Steven Spielberg.

q: Jennifer Lopez lent her voice to a character in which of these animated movies?

q.e: Jennifer Lopez voiced Azteca in Antz (1998), a DreamWorks film. The cast also included Woody Allen and Sharon Stone.

q: In addition voicing the character of Burnss son, Larry Burns, on The Simpsons, Dangerfield was also involved which of these animated films?

q.e: Rodney Dangerfield voiced Mr. Burns's son Larry in The Simpsons and starred in Rover Dangerfield (1991), an animated film about a dog.

q: In this animated film Michelle Pfeiffer voices Eris, the Greek goddess of chaos.
Sindbad: Legend of the Seven Seas

q.e: Michelle Pfeiffer voiced Eris, the goddess of discord, in Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas (2003). It was DreamWorks' last traditionally animated film.

q: In the Internet cartoon Homestar Runner, Strong Bad works with Homestar and The Cheat at an unnamed tech company, but what is his dream job?
universal make-out helper for hot girls
supreme ultralord of the international gazebo

q.e: Strong Bad is the character from Homestar Runner who answers emails. His dreams are shown in various cartoons.

q: What is the name of this legendary monster, which appears in Jewish folklore as an animated creature created from inanimate material?

q.e: A golem is a creature from Jewish folklore, made from clay or mud, which is animated to serve its maker. The Golem of Prague is the best-known story.

q: In the Looney Tunes cartoons, there was a little bird who was always trying to catch Foghorn Leghorn, Whats the name of this brave little brown bird?

q.e: Henery Hawk is the tiny chicken hawk who tries to catch Foghorn Leghorn in Looney Tunes. He first appeared in 1946.

q: Name the Disney animated feature which contains this quote: His destructive programming is taking effect. He will be irresistibly drawn to large cities, where he will back up sewers, reverse street signs, and steal everyones left shoe.

q.e: This quote comes from Lilo & Stitch (2002), where Jumba describes Stitch's programming. The movie is a Disney film set in Hawaii.

q: I shall call him squishy and he shall be mine and he shall be my squishy. is a quote from what Disney animated film?

q.e: Dory says "I shall call him Squishy" about a baby jellyfish, in Finding Nemo (2003). It's a nod to a line from a Looney Tunes cartoon.

q: What is the name of the paradisal land under the sea in the 1968 animated film Yellow Submarine?

q.e: Pepperland is the cheerful undersea haven protected by Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band until the Blue Meanies attack in the 1968 film.

q: What educational, non-fiction full length animated film was released in 1957?

q.e: Hemo the Magnificent (1957) is an educational film about blood, from Frank Capra's Bell Laboratory Science Series. It mixes animation with live action.

q: 1973 saw the release of this full length animated film which featured the great actress Agnes Moorehead.

q.e: Charlotte's Web (1973) is an animated adaptation of E.B. White's book. Agnes Moorehead voiced the Goose.

q: What type of fish is Nemo from the 2003 animated film Finding Nemo?

q.e: Nemo and his father Marlin are ocellaris clownfish, identifiable by their bright orange bodies and three white stripes. His companion Dory is a regal blue tang.

q: What 1950 animated Walt Disney film, based on a fairy tale by Charles Perrault, featured the songs A Dream Is a Wish Your Heart Makes, So This Is Love, Sing Sweet Nightingale, The Work Song, and the Oscar-nominated Bibbidi-Bobbidi-Boo?

q.e: Disney's 1950 animated classic Cinderella drew from Charles Perrault's 1697 version of the tale. The film rescued Walt Disney Productions from serious debt after World War II.

q: Which word refers to the frames used to make animated movies?

q.e: Cels, short for celluloid sheets, are transparent plastic sheets used in traditional hand-drawn animation to layer moving characters over static backgrounds. The technique became widespread after being patented by Earl Hurd in 1914.

q: What is the title of the oldest existing full length animated movie?

q.e: The Adventures of Prince Achmed (1926), by Lotte Reiniger, is the oldest surviving animated feature film. It used cut-out silhouettes.

q: Which character did Jennifer Aniston voice in the 1998 animated TV series Hercules?

q.e: Jennifer Aniston voiced Galatea in the animated Hercules TV series (1998). It was a spin-off of the 1997 Disney film.

q: What actor voiced Moses and God in the 1998 animated blockbuster movie The Prince of Egypt?

q.e: Val Kilmer voiced both Moses and God in DreamWorks' The Prince of Egypt (1998). The film also featured the song "When You Believe".

q: What character did Danny DeVito voice in the 1997 animated movie Hercules?

q.e: Danny DeVito provided the voice and physical mannerisms for Philoctetes, or 'Phil', the grumpy satyr who trains Hercules to become a true hero.

q: Which of these actors was not included in the voice cast of the 2003 animated blockbuster movie Finding Nemo?

q.e: Renée Zellweger was in Shark Tale (2004), not Finding Nemo. The cast of Nemo included Albert Brooks, Ellen DeGeneres and Willem Dafoe.

q: What is the Big Bad Wolf wearing all the time in the 2001 animated comedy movie Shrek?

q.e: In Shrek (2001), the Big Bad Wolf wears Granny's pink nightgown and bonnet. He appears in Lord Farquaad's castle and in Shrek's bed.

q: A great dog-hater, this villain ranked # 39 on AFI's list of the 50 top villains, is one of the three from the list coming from an animated film.
The Wicked Witch of the West

q.e: Cruella De Vil, from 101 Dalmatians, ranks #39 on the AFI's 100 Years...100 Heroes & Villains list (2003). Few animated characters made the list.

q: What character did actor and comedian Rowan Atkinson voice in the 1994 animated movie The Lion King?

q.e: Rowan Atkinson voiced the uptight red-billed hornbill Zazu, the royal advisor to King Mufasa, in Disney's 1994 animated feature The Lion King.

q: What is the name of the main antagonist/villainess in the animated feature One Hundred and One Dalmatians?

q.e: Cruella de Vil is the villain who plots to steal Dalmatian puppies to make a fur coat. Estella is her birth name introduced in the 2021 live-action backstory film Cruella, while Drizella and Anastasia are Cinderella's stepsisters.

q: Which movie won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature at the 77th Academy Awards in 2005?

q.e: The Incredibles (2004) won Best Animated Feature at the 77th Academy Awards in 2005. It was directed by Brad Bird.

q: People who do this job are responsible for making 3-D films look so real. They create the hairstyles of the animated characters.

q.e: Hair simulation supervisors are in charge of making hair and fur move realistically in computer animation. Pixar developed fur technology for Monsters, Inc. (2001).

q: Who wrote the fairy-tale picture-book Shrek, which was later adapted into a computer animated movie?

q.e: William Steig wrote and illustrated the book Shrek! in 1990. He also wrote Sylvester and the Magic Pebble.

q: This eponym comes from the name of a mentally slow character from a cartoon by E.C. Segar, the man who drew Popeye.

q.e: "Goon" was popularized by the Alice the Goon character in E.C. Segar's Popeye comic Thimble Theatre. The word now means a thug.

q: Who voices Peter Griffin in the animated show Family Guy?

q.e: Seth MacFarlane voices Peter Griffin. He does Stewie, Brian and Glenn Quagmire.

q: Tom from the popular Tom Jerry cartoon was known by what name in his debut short Puss Gets the Boot?

q.e: In "Puss Gets the Boot" (1940), Tom was named Jasper and Jerry was named Jinx. William Hanna and Joseph Barbera created them.

q: What is the name of the scare floor secretary in the animated movie Monsters, Inc.?

q.e: Roz is the grumpy slug-like monster who runs the scare floor's paperwork in Monsters, Inc. (2001). She is voiced by Bob Peterson.

q: Listen to the track and decide what animated Disney feature this song is from.

q.e: This song comes from Disney's Pocahontas (1995). Alan Menken and Stephen Schwartz wrote the songs, including "Colors of the Wind".

q: What is Lucy and Linuss last name in the cartoon strip Peanuts?

q.e: Lucy and Linus, along with their younger brother Rerun, share the surname van Pelt in Charles M. Schulz's comic strip Peanuts. Brown is Charlie Brown's surname.

q: Dr. Jumba Jookiba, Mrs. Hasagawa and Pleakley are characters in which Disney cartoon?

q.e: Dr. Jumba Jookiba, Mrs. Hasagawa and Pleakley are characters in Lilo & Stitch (2002). Pleakley is an alien who dresses as a woman.

q: Which cartoon character was the gentleman friend of Olive Oyle?

q.e: Popeye the Sailor, created by E.C. Segar in 1929, won the affections of Olive Oyl, constantly defending her from his burly rival Bluto (later also known as Brutus).

q: In the animated movie Finding Nemo, before it stung her, Dory wanted to make a baby jellyfish her pet and she wanted to call it by what name?

q.e: In Finding Nemo, Dory wants to name a baby jellyfish "Squishy". Her short-term memory loss is a running gag.

q: These two cartoon characters are in a constant chase. They appeared in 1940 under the pencil of William Hanna and Joseph Barbera. The original variation of the short series have won seven Academy Awards.

q.e: Tom and Jerry debuted in the 1940 short Puss Gets the Boot, originally named Jasper and Jinx, before tying with Walt Disney's Silly Symphonies for the most Oscars won by a cartoon series.

q: The characters of this 1997 cartoon are siblings, although they are from different animal species. The first episode was quite dramatic, sending the brother to Hell for smoking.
Wile E. Coyote and Road Runner

q.e: Cow and Chicken (1997) is a Cartoon Network show by David Feiss, with the siblings Cow and Chicken. In the first episode, Chicken goes to Hell.

q: This character from the animated movie Shrek 2 is the bartender at the Poison Apple.

q.e: Doris, the Ugly Stepsister, is a bartender at the Poison Apple Inn in Shrek 2 (2004). She is voiced by Larry King.

q: Where does the cartoon character SpongeBob work?

q.e: SpongeBob SquarePants works as the primary fry cook at the Krusty Krab, a fast-food restaurant owned by Mr. Krabs. Its rival across the street, the Chum Bucket, is run by Sheldon J. Plankton.

q: Which character from the animated series SpongeBob SquarePants spoke the words from the sound clip?

q.e: Squidward Tentacles, SpongeBob's grumpy neighbor, is a clarinetist. He's voiced by Rodger Bumpass.

q: Where did Fred Flintstones family come from in the TV series The Flintstones?

q.e: Fred Flintstone lives in the prehistoric town of Bedrock. Details of his family tree vary across the series.

q: Who voiced The Great Gazoo, a tiny green alien sent to Earth, on the animated show The Flintstones?

q.e: Harvey Korman voiced The Great Gazoo, a little green alien who appeared in later Flintstones seasons (1965). He was also a Carol Burnett Show regular.

q: The Flintstones was loosely based on what classic TV show?
The George Burns and Gracie Allen Show

q.e: The Flintstones creators William Hanna and Joseph Barbera acknowledged drawing heavy inspiration from The Honeymooners, with Fred and Wilma Flintstone mirroring Ralph and Alice Kramden, and Barney Rubble mirroring Ed Norton.

q: In this animated TV series Jane and George had a pet named Astro.

q.e: Astro is the lovable Great Dane-like family dog in Hanna-Barbera's 1962 animated series The Jetsons. His signature speech pattern involves adding an 'R' sound to the beginning of most words, notably his catchphrase 'Ruh-roh, Raggy!'-style bark.

q: In this animated series Dino is the pet dinosaur of Fred and his wife Wilma, who live in the fictional city of Bedrock.

q.e: Dino is a Snorkasaurus who acts like an energetic family dog in Hanna-Barbera's The Flintstones, which debuted in 1960. The Jetsons was Hanna-Barbera's futuristic counterpart featuring the space-dog Astro.

q: In Homer the Great, an episode from the sixth season of The Simpsons, Homer joins an ancient secret society, called what?

q.e: In "Homer the Great" (1995), Homer joins the Stonecutters, a secret society. Its song is "We Do".

q: In an episode from the fifth season of The Simpsons, Homer tells the story of the days when he used to participate in a quartet called The Be Sharps. What style of music did The Be Sharps win a Grammy for?

q.e: In "Homer's Barbershop Quartet" (1993), Homer says the Be Sharps won a Grammy for their barbershop music. George Harrison appears in the episode.

q: On The Simpsons, Bart Sells His Soul is the episode in which Bart declares to Milhouse he believes there are no such things as souls. In response, Milhouse tells Bart that hed like to buy his soul. How much does he pay Bart for his soul?
A coupon for a free Krustyburger

q.e: In "Bart Sells His Soul" (1995), Bart sells his soul to Milhouse for $5. He later regrets it.
