q: In the episode You Only Move Twice, what football team did Hank Scorpio, an evil genius, owner of Globex Corporation and Homer Simpsons new boss, buy for Homer to show his appreciation?

q.e: In "You Only Move Twice" (1996), Homer's boss Hank Scorpio buys him the Denver Broncos. Albert Brooks voiced Scorpio.

q: As revealed in The Day the Violence Died, an episode of The Simpsons, who was the original creator of Itchy?

q.e: Chester J. Lampwick is the creator of Itchy in "The Day the Violence Died" (1996), who sues for the rights. He is voiced by Kirk Douglas.

q: This cartoon series, which featured Boris and Natasha as villains, paralleled Cold War issues of the time.

q.e: The Rocky and Bullwinkle Show (1959) features spies Boris and Natasha, who parody Cold War enemies. It was created by Jay Ward.

q: What was the maiden name of Marge Simpson in the TV animated series The Simpsons?

q.e: Marge's maiden name is Bouvier, which she shares with her chain-smoking twin sisters, Patty and Selma. Her mother, Jacqueline Bouvier, was named as an homage to former U.S. First Lady Jacqueline Bouvier Kennedy.

q: What is the last name of the single mom and her spoiled son Eric in the animated comedy South Park?

q.e: Eric Cartman lives in South Park, Colorado, with his mother, Liane Cartman. He is a main character.

q: What was the name of the George Jetsons boss on the cartoon show The Jetsons?

q.e: Cosmo Spacely, commonly called Mr. Spacely, is George's short-tempered boss at Spacely Space Sprockets. Mr. Slate was Fred Flintstone's boss in The Flintstones.

q: Whose brother is the popular cartoon character Charlie Brown?

q.e: Charlie Brown is Sally's older brother, in Peanuts. He is also the owner of Snoopy.

q: Which actor voices the animated albino lab mouse Pinky, that is just like the Brain, but appears to be substantially less bright?

q.e: Rob Paulsen voices Pinky in Pinky and the Brain; Maurice LaMarche voices the Brain. The two mice try to take over the world every night.

q: What is the name of the town where the satirical animated series King of the Hill is set?

q.e: King of the Hill is set in Arlen, Texas, a fictional suburb. It ran from 1997 to 2010 and was revived in 2025.

q: Who is the baddie in the animated musical The Nightmare Before Christmas?

q.e: Oogie Boogie is the sack-shaped villain in Tim Burton's The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993). He is voiced by Ken Page.

q: Which member of the Star Trek cast was not taken to the forbidden planet, Omega 3 in the animated show Futurama?

q.e: In Futurama's "Where No Fan Has Gone Before" (2002), Leonard Nimoy refused to go to Omega 3, so was not taken. The episode featured the original Star Trek cast voicing themselves.

q: Peters friend Cleveland Brown on the Family Guy animated series is owner of which of these?

q.e: Cleveland Brown is Peter's neighbor in Family Guy. He later got a spin-off, The Cleveland Show, in 2009.

q: Who played Ulysses S. Grant in the Civil War Re-enactment in The Simpsons?

q.e: Barney Gumble plays Ulysses S. Grant in a Civil War re-enactment in The Simpsons. The show often features Barney in odd roles.

q: Which one of these characters appeared on a billboard in Poppas Got a Brand New Badge, an episode of The Simpsons?

q.e: "Poppa's Got a Brand New Badge" (1995) is a Simpsons episode in which Homer becomes a policeman. Superintendent Chalmers is a recurring character.

q: In the episode of The Simpsons See Homer Run, who put up a commercial against Homers Campaign?

q.e: "See Homer Run" is a Simpsons episode where Homer runs for office. Several characters campaign against him.

q: Which was Pixars first short animated film?

q.e: Luxo Jr. debuted in 1986 and was Pixar's first short film as an independent company. The titular desk lamp was so iconic that it became a permanent feature in Pixar's studio logo.

q: In the animated series American Dad, Roger is an alien who lives with the family. The family must keep Roger a secret, but he has left the house on a few occasions in various disguise. Which of the following is not a disguise worn by Roger?

q.e: Roger is an alien in American Dad! who lives with the Smith family as a pretend granny, and uses disguises. He is voiced by Seth MacFarlane.

q: What kind of store did Ned Flanders open in the Simpsons episode When Flanders Failed?

q.e: In "When Flanders Failed" (1991), Ned opens the Leftorium, a store for left-handed people. Springfield's customers ignore it at first.

q: In The Simpsons episode, entitled Skinners Sense of Snow, the snow storm is described on the radio as what?
A classic nor easter meeting a classic sou wester

q.e: In "Skinner's Sense of Snow" (2000), Springfield Elementary is snowed in during a storm. The kids and Skinner are trapped in school.

q: In Simpsons Christmas Stories, in the segment The Nutcracker... Sweet, Apu says that all he has left after the Christmas rush is what?

q.e: "Simpsons Christmas Stories" (2005) is a Simpsons Christmas episode with three stories. Apu's line is in the Nutcracker segment.

q: What brand of beer is sold in the fictional city of Shelbyville on The Simpsons?

q.e: Shelbyville has Fudd beer, a parody rival of Springfield's Duff. Shelbyville is Springfield's rival town.

q: What Simpsons character described the French as cheese-eating surrender monkeys?

q.e: Groundskeeper Willie called the French "cheese-eating surrender monkeys" on The Simpsons. The phrase became widely used in the early 2000s.

q: What is the name of the pet dog of the Simpsons in the popular animated sitcom The Simpsons?

q.e: Santa's Little Helper is the family's greyhound, adopted by Homer and Bart in the first full-length episode, "Simpsons Roasting on an Open Fire" (1989), after losing a race at the dog track.

q: What is the name of the animated series on Adult Swim that stars Killface, Xander Crews/Awesome X and the Xtacles?

q.e: Frisky Dingo (2006) was an Adult Swim series about Killface and Xander Crews. It ran for two seasons.

q: What animated series on Adult Swim centers around the day-to-day activities of a law firm staffed mainly by superheroes/villains from 1960s era cartoons?

q.e: Harvey Birdman, Attorney at Law, stars Hanna-Barbera heroes like Birdman as lawyers. The show started on Cartoon Network's Adult Swim in 2000.

q: This animated sketch debuted on The Dana Carvey Show before it moved to Saturday Night Live.

q.e: The Ambiguously Gay Duo was an animated sketch created by Robert Smigel on The Dana Carvey Show (1996). It moved to SNL.

q: What is the name of Perry the Platypus rival on the animated show Phineas and Ferb?

q.e: Dr. Heinz Doofenshmirtz is an evil scientist who heads Doofenshmirtz Evil Incorporated and constantly invents contraptions ending in '-inator', which secret agent Perry the Platypus thwarts.

q: What event was competed by Candaces and Jeremys grandmothers on the animated show Phineas and Ferb?

q.e: Phineas and Ferb is known for recurring gags, and Candace's grandmother is a recurring character. Details vary by episode.

q: What is the name of Jeremys band on the animated show Phineas and Ferb?

q.e: Jeremy Johnson's band in Phineas and Ferb is called The Incidentals. He plays the guitar.

q: This cartoon show aired on MTV from 1993 to 1997, and is stated to be highly influential upon 1990s youth language in America.

q.e: Created by Mike Judge, Beavis and Butt-Head debuted on MTV in March 1993 and popularized catchphrases like 'this sucks' and 'cool' among 1990s youth.

q: Marcia Wallce, who played Carol, Bobs receptionist on The Newhart Show, does the voice of what Simpsons character?

q.e: Marcia Wallace played Carol Kester Bondurant on The Bob Newhart Show and voiced Edna Krabappel on The Simpsons. She died in 2013.

q: Which cartoon ape was "for sale, won't you buy 'im"?

q.e: Magilla Gorilla, created by Hanna-Barbera in 1964, spent his days in Mr. Peebles' pet shop window accompanied by the theme song lyrics 'We've got a gorilla for sale'.

q: What character did Elizabeth Taylor play in the 1994 movie The Flintstones, co-produced by Steven Spielberg?

q.e: Elizabeth Taylor played Pearl Slaghoople, Wilma's mother, in the 1994 film The Flintstones. It was her last big-screen role.

q: What is the name of the character voiced by Michelle Pfeiffer in the 1998 Academy Award-winning animated movie The Prince of Egypt?

q.e: Michelle Pfeiffer voiced Tzipporah, Moses's wife, in The Prince of Egypt (1998). Sandra Bullock voiced Miriam.

q: What is the name of Mike and Sulleys boss in the great animated feature, Monsters, Inc.?

q.e: Mr. Waternoose is the boss of Monsters, Inc. He is voiced by James Coburn.

q: These two are a famous cartoon couple that made their first public appearance in 1929. Before becoming his partner, she was the star of Thimble Theater and ran in over 600 newspapers. At the time, she was not the skinny girl from the cartoon today.

q.e: Popeye debuted in Thimble Theatre in 1929, and Olive Oyl was already a star of the strip. The characters had cartoon shorts later.

q: On The Flintstones Freds pet dinosaur greets him at the door, knocking him down, every time Fred comes home. What kind of dinosaur is he?

q.e: Dino is Fred's pet "snorkasaurus" in The Flintstones. He knocks Fred down at the door.

q: What is the favourite TV show of SpongeBob, the main character in the animated series, SpongeBob SquarePants?

q.e: SpongeBob's favorite show is The Adventures of Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy. He is a huge fan.

q: Where did George Jetson work on the hit cartoon series The Jetsons?

q.e: George Jetson works at Spacely Space Sprockets for Mr. Spacely. His job is pushing a button.

q: The animated adventures of Pinky and the Brain aired on the WB Television Network from 1995 to 1998, and were created by what two men?

q.e: Tom Ruegger and Peter Hastings created Pinky and the Brain. It came from Animaniacs.

q: What animated series featured The Three Stooges?
The Three Stooges Go Around the World in a Daze

q.e: The New Three Stooges (1965) was an animated series featuring Moe, Larry and Curly Joe. It mixed live action and cartoons.

q: Who voices Agnes Skinner and Lindsay Naegle in Matt Groenings animated sitcom The Simpsons?

q.e: Tress MacNeille voices Agnes Skinner and Lindsay Naegle on The Simpsons. She also voiced Daisy Duck.

q: What is the name of Krustys father on the animated sitcom The Simpsons?

q.e: Hyman Krustofski is Krusty's father, a rabbi, in The Simpsons. Jackie Mason voiced him.

q: What was Barts first phrase on the animated show The Simpsons?

q.e: Bart Simpson's famous catchphrases include "Eat my shorts" and "Ay, caramba!". They became popular in the early 1990s.

q: What was the name of the floating city made by Heinz Doofenshmirtz on the animated TV show Phineas and Ferb?

q.e: Dr. Doofenshmirtz builds many inventions and schemes to take over the Tri-State Area in Phineas and Ferb. His home base is Doofenshmirtz Evil Incorporated.

q: What does Homer grow when he goes to live on a farm in an episode of the eleventh season of The Simpsons?

q.e: In "E-I-E-I-(Annoyed Grunt)" (1999), Homer grows "tomacco", a mix of tomatoes and tobacco. It is addictive.

Kryptonite is a radioactive mineral from Superman's destroyed home world of Krypton that weakens and can even kill him. It was first introduced in the 1943 radio serial before making its comics debut in 1949.
Marvel Comics was founded in 1939 by publisher Martin Goodman under the name Timely Publications, with its first release being Marvel Comics 1.

q: In the Marvel comic "The Superior Spider-Man", Peter Parker's body is taken over by which character?

q.e: In The Superior Spider-Man (2012), the villain Doctor Octopus (Otto Octavius) swaps minds with Peter Parker as he dies and takes over Peter's body. He sets out to be a "superior" hero.

q: Which superhero is known for his super speed?

q.e: Debuting in DC Comics in 1940, the Flash draws power from the extradimensional Speed Force, allowing him to run near or above the speed of light.

q: What is the alter-ego of the DC comics character "Superman"?

q.e: Clark Kent was raised in Smallville by Jonathan and Martha Kent before moving to Metropolis. Arthur Curry is Aquaman, and Bruce Wayne is Batman.

q: Which planet did Superman come from?

q.e: Superman was born Kal-El on the doomed planet Krypton and sent to Earth in a spacecraft by his father Jor-El just moments before Krypton exploded.
Billionaire industrialist Bruce Wayne took up the mantle of Batman following the murder of his parents, Thomas and Martha, debuting in Detective Comics 27 in 1939.

q: What is the full first name of the babysitter in Calvin and Hobbes?

q.e: Rosalyn is the babysitter in Calvin and Hobbes, and Calvin delights in tormenting her. Her boyfriend, Charlie, often ends up dealing with Calvin too.

q: This Marvel superhero is often called "The man without fear".

q.e: Blind lawyer Matt Murdock was introduced as Daredevil by Stan Lee and Bill Everett in 1964 with the moniker 'The Man Without Fear'. His heightened remaining senses and radar sense allow him to navigate Hell's Kitchen fearless of danger.

q: According to their longtime nickname, what kind of "duo" are Batman & Robin?

q.e: Batman and Robin have been known as the Dynamic Duo since DC Comics introduced Robin in Detective Comics 38 in 1940.

q: Which "Peanuts" character pines for the little red-haired girl?

q.e: Charlie Brown in Peanuts is hopelessly in love with the Little Red-Haired Girl, who never actually appears in the strip. Charles Schulz based her on a woman he loved in real life.

q: This superhero, who first appeared in the comic book Tales of Suspense, used his own invention to keep his heart pumping.

q.e: Iron Man debuted in Tales of Suspense issue 39 in March 1963. Tony Stark originally built an electromagnet chest plate to prevent shrapnel from reaching his heart after sustaining a battlefield injury.

q: These comic book superheroes were trained in Professor Xaviers School for Gifted Youngsters.

q.e: Created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby in 1963, the X-Men were founded by Charles Xavier at his Westchester mansion to train young mutants in controlling their powers.

q: Fellow Justice League members Superman and Martian Manhunter have something in common. What is it?
They are both reporters by day
They both grew up on a farm.
They both escaped from the phantom zone.

q.e: Superman and Martian Manhunter are both aliens living on Earth: Superman is from Krypton and J'onn J'onzz from Mars. Both are founding members of the Justice League.

q: What famous comic book company published Aquaman Comics?

q.e: Aquaman first debuted in More Fun Comics 73 in 1941, published by National Allied Publications, the company that evolved into DC Comics.

q: Who is credited with creating Batman?

q.e: Bob Kane officially held sole credit for creating Batman for decades, though writer Bill Finger is now co-credited after having contributed the iconic cape, cowl, and origin story.

q: Captain America made his first appearance in what comic book?

q.e: Captain America first appeared in Captain America Comics #1 in March 1941, created by Joe Simon and Jack Kirby, with a cover showing him punching Hitler. It came out about nine months before the US entered World War II.

q: What comic book is The Human Torch from?

q.e: The Human Torch (Johnny Storm) debuted alongside Mr. Fantastic, Invisible Girl, and the Thing in Marvel's Fantastic Four 1, published in November 1961. An earlier, android Human Torch had previously appeared in Timely Comics in 1939.

q: The Green Goblin is the arch enemy of which Marvel Superhero?

q.e: The Green Goblin, original alter ego Norman Osborn, debuted in The Amazing Spider-Man 14 in 1964 and remains one of Peter Parker's deadliest foes.

q: What does DC stand for in the comic which first introduced Batman?

q.e: DC Comics took its name from Detective Comics, the anthology series launched in 1937 where Batman made his first appearance in issue 27 in 1939.

q: What was Batmans original name, when he first appeared in DC comics?

q.e: Batman was first called "The Bat-Man" when he made his debut in Detective Comics #27 in 1939. Bob Kane and Bill Finger created him.

q: Why so serious? is a tagline from this Batman movie.

q.e: "Why so serious?" is the Joker's line in The Dark Knight (2008), played by Heath Ledger. Ledger won a posthumous Oscar for the role.

q: The actor who played the Scarecrow in 2005s Batman Begins originally auditioned for what part?
A Person from the League of Darkness

q.e: Cillian Murphy, who played the Scarecrow in Batman Begins, had originally auditioned for the part of Batman. Director Christopher Nolan liked him so much that he cast him as the villain.

q: What villain did Michael Keaton face in his first Batman movie?

q.e: Michael Keaton's Batman fought the Joker, played by Jack Nicholson, in Tim Burton's 1989 film Batman. The Joker's fall into a vat of chemicals created him in the movie.

q: This 2007 horror movie is based on the self-titled comic book miniseries and is set in Barrow, Alaska.

q.e: 30 Days of Night (2007) is based on a comic by Steve Niles and Ben Templesmith about vampires attacking Barrow, Alaska, which has a month of constant darkness each winter. The story takes advantage of the town's polar night.

q: Which comic book publisher did King Kong and Godzilla share?

q.e: Dark Horse Comics, founded in 1986, publishes Hellboy and has put out Godzilla comics. It is one of the biggest independent comics publishers in the US.

q: Aquaman, The Atom, Batman, The Flash, Green Arrow, Hawkman, Jonn Jonzz Martian Hunter, Superman and Wonder Woman are from which of these groups?

q.e: The Justice League of America is DC's superhero team, which first appeared in 1960 with heroes including Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman, the Flash and Aquaman. Others such as Green Arrow, Hawkman and the Atom joined later.

q: Cyclops, Beast, The Angel, Iceman and Marvel Girl are from this group.

q.e: The original X-Men were Cyclops, Beast, Angel, Iceman and Marvel Girl (Jean Grey), who first appeared in 1963 in a comic by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby. Professor X led them.

q: Bruce Wayne (Batman) has a butler named Alfred. What is Alfreds nationality?

q.e: Alfred Pennyworth, Bruce Wayne's loyal butler, is English. He is often shown as a former British intelligence agent or actor.

q: Who was Batgirl's father, portrayed by Neil Hamilton in the TV series Batman?

q.e: Barbara Gordon, the original Batgirl, is the daughter of Police Commissioner James Gordon. He was played by Neil Hamilton in the 1960s Batman TV series.

q: Adam West, who plays the caped crusader, Batman, in the TV series "Batman�, also voices the Mayor of Quahog in what animated TV series?

q.e: Adam West, TV's Batman, voices Mayor Adam West on Family Guy, set in the town of Quahog. He played a wacky version of himself.

q: Which of these stars, who all had guest roles on Batman, portrayed the villain Egghead?

q.e: Vincent Price, a horror film star, played the villain Egghead on the 1960s Batman series. Egghead is a bald, egg-obsessed criminal mastermind who was invented for the show.

q: What was the Commissioners name in the 1960s Batman series?

q.e: Commissioner James Gordon was Gotham's police commissioner in the 1960s Batman series and in the comics. He's famous for using the Bat-Signal to call Batman.

q: Who created the concept of Batman?

q.e: Bob Kane is credited as the creator of Batman, but writer Bill Finger shaped many of the character's key elements, such as his costume and Gotham City. Finger finally received official credit in 2015.

q: This member of the X-Men team, who has the power to control the weather, is captured by Sauron.

q.e: Storm, also known as Ororo Munroe, possesses the mutant power of atmospheric manipulation. In Uncanny X-Men issue 114, the pteranodon-like villain Sauron captures Storm and absorbs her life energy in the Savage Land.
Batman operates in Gotham City, created by Bill Finger and Bob Kane in 1939. Other DC heroes protect different fictional cities, such as Superman in Metropolis and the Flash in Central City.
Peter Parker was introduced in Amazing Fantasy 15 in 1962 by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko. Bruce Wayne is Batman, Clark Kent is Superman, and Tony Stark is Iron Man.
Black Panther, T'Challa, is the king and protector of Wakanda, a hidden, technologically advanced African nation. He debuted in Fantastic Four #52 in 1966.

q: What fictional metal is bonded to Wolverine's skeleton?

q.e: Adamantium is a fictional, virtually indestructible steel alloy bonded to Wolverine's skeleton and claws during the Weapon X program. Vibranium is the fictional metal associated with Wakanda and Captain America's shield.

q: In the Hellboy universe, who founded the BPRD?

q.e: Professor Trevor Bruttenholm (also called "Broom") founded the Bureau for Paranormal Research and Defense (BPRD) in the Hellboy comics. He also raised Hellboy after the demon was summoned in 1944.

q: Who was the inspiration for Cuthbert Calculus in the Tintin series?

q.e: Professor Cuthbert Calculus in Tintin was partly inspired by Auguste Piccard, a Swiss physicist and balloonist. Piccard also reached record heights in balloon flights.

q: Which of the following superheros did Wonder Woman NOT have a love interest in?

q.e: Wonder Woman has had romances with several heroes, including Steve Trevor, Superman and Batman in various stories, but not with Green Arrow, who is married to Black Canary. Her romances vary by version.

q: Who wrote the Batman comic series "The Killing Joke"?

q.e: Alan Moore wrote Batman: The Killing Joke in 1988, with art by Brian Bolland. It gave the Joker a possible origin story and had a lasting impact on Batman comics.

q: In the DC Comics 2016 reboot, Rebirth, which speedster escaped from the Speed Force after he had been erased from existance?

q.e: In DC Universe: Rebirth (2016), Wally West, the original Kid Flash and a Flash, returns from the Speed Force, where he'd been trapped and forgotten. His return brought back the classic legacy of the Flash family.

q: In Calvin and Hobbes, what is the name of Susie's stuffed rabbit?

q.e: Mr. Bun is Susie Derkins's stuffed rabbit in Calvin and Hobbes. Susie is Calvin's classmate and neighbor, who often tangles with him.

q: What is the real full name of Captain America?

q.e: Captain America's real name is Steven Grant Rogers, a frail young man from Brooklyn who is transformed by the Super-Soldier Serum. He's nicknamed "Steve".
Hank Pym, the original Ant-Man, created the artificial intelligence Ultron, who turned on his creator. Ultron first appeared in 1968 in The Avengers #54-58.

q: Who authored The Adventures of Tintin?

q.e: Hergé was the pen name of Belgian cartoonist Georges Remi, derived from the French pronunciation of his reversed initials (R.G.). He published the first Tintin adventure in January 1929 in the youth supplement Le Petit Vingtième.

q: Which "Green Arrow" sidekick commonly wears a baseball cap?

q.e: Roy Harper is Green Arrow's sidekick, Speedy, who later became Arsenal. He is often drawn in a red costume with a cap or headband.

q: What is the name of the comic about a young boy, and a tiger who is actually a stuffed animal?

q.e: Created by Bill Watterson, the comic strip Calvin and Hobbes ran from 1985 to 1995 and followed six-year-old Calvin and his stuffed tiger Hobbes, who comes to life in Calvin's imagination.

q: What otherworldly land does Thor come from?

q.e: Thor hails from the realm of Asgard in both Marvel Comics and traditional Norse mythology. Midgard is the Norse term for Earth.

q: In Calvin and Hobbes, what is the name of the babysitter's boyfriend?

q.e: Charlie is Rosalyn's boyfriend in Calvin and Hobbes, and he often appears when she babysits. Calvin loves to cause trouble for the couple.

q: In Calvin and Hobbes, what is the name of the principal at Calvin's school?

q.e: Mr. Spittle is the principal of Calvin's school in Calvin and Hobbes. Calvin often ends up in his office.

q: The success of DC Comics' Swamp Thing, Sandman, and other books in a similar style, led to the creation of what new imprint in 1993?

q.e: DC Comics launched Vertigo in 1993 as an imprint for mature comics like Sandman and Swamp Thing. It was guided by editor Karen Berger.

q: What's the name of Batman's parents?

q.e: Batman's parents are Thomas and Martha Wayne, who were murdered in Gotham's Crime Alley while young Bruce watched. That event inspires him to become Batman.

q: What is the designation given to the Marvel Cinematic Universe?

q.e: In Marvel's multiverse, the main comic-book reality is Earth-616, and the Marvel Cinematic Universe is Earth-199999. The numbering system was created to keep track of the many alternate universes.

q: Which Batman sidekick is the son of Talia al Ghul?

q.e: Damian Wayne is the son of Bruce Wayne and Talia al Ghul, and he becomes the fifth Robin. He's trained from childhood by the League of Assassins.

q: The stuffed tiger in Calvin and Hobbes is named after what philosopher?

q.e: Bill Watterson named the philosopher-tiger Hobbes after the 17th-century English thinker Thomas Hobbes, while Calvin was named after the 16th-century theologian John Calvin.

q: Cathy Guisewite ended which comic strip in 2010 after 34 years?

q.e: Cathy Guisewite ended her comic strip Cathy in 2010 after 34 years. The strip centered on a single woman's struggles with work, food, family and dating.

q: Which Dan Piraro comic began as a replacement for "The Far Side"?

q.e: Dan Piraro's Bizarro began in 1985 as a single-panel comic of surreal and offbeat humor. Each panel hides small secret symbols for readers to find.

q: What character did Arnold Schwarzenegger play in the 1997 movie Batman Robin?

q.e: Arnold Schwarzenegger played Mr. Freeze in Batman & Robin (1997). The villain's pun-filled one-liners about the cold are among the film's most memorable.

q: What popular fictional villain did Jack Nicholson portray in the 1989 movie Batman?

q.e: Jack Nicholson played the Joker in Tim Burton's Batman (1989), a role for which he was paid a reported $50 million. He took a percentage of the film's profits.

q: Nicole Kidman plays Dr. Chase Meridian in this 1995 superhero film also starring Val Kilmer.

q.e: Nicole Kidman plays psychologist Dr. Chase Meridian in Batman Forever (1995), the Batman film with Val Kilmer as the hero. She becomes a love interest for Bruce Wayne.

q: In this 1992 superhero film, Michelle Pfeiffer plays Selina Kyle, a timid secretary, who discovers her bosss evil plan to suck power from the city.

q.e: In Batman Returns (1992), Michelle Pfeiffer plays Selina Kyle, who is pushed out a window by her boss, Max Shreck, and comes back as Catwoman. It was directed by Tim Burton.

q: Director and producer Kevin Smith named his daughter after this villain from the Batman comic series.

q.e: Filmmaker Kevin Smith named his daughter Harley Quinn Smith after the Batman villain. She later became an actress and appears in some of his movies.

q: This Marvel Comics superhero, whose birth name was Peter Benjamin Parker, first used his new found superpowers as a professional wrestler.

q.e: Peter Benjamin Parker is Spider-Man, created by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko and first appearing in Amazing Fantasy #15 (1962). His first use of his powers is as a masked wrestler, before the death of Uncle Ben changes his course.

q: This comedic superhero, created by Ben Edlund, met an accountant named Arthur, after taking a long bus ride into The City.

q.e: The Tick is a bumbling, blue superhero created by Ben Edlund in 1986, and his sidekick is the accountant Arthur, who wears a moth suit. The Tick's war cry is "Spoon!".

q: Which Marvel Comics character became a ruthless vigilante, after witnessing his familys violent murder?

q.e: Frank Castle became The Punisher after his wife and two children were gunned down during a mob shootout in New York's Central Park. He debuted in The Amazing Spider-Man 129 in 1974.

q: This DC Comics superhero, whose true identity is Bruce Wayne, decided to train himself to the peak of physical perfection after witnessing the murder of his parents.

q.e: Batman, secret identity Bruce Wayne, trains himself to the peak of human ability after seeing his parents murdered. He has no superpowers, relying on skill, intellect and gadgets.

q: Which of these X-Men characters is not a member of the Summers family line?

q.e: The Summers family includes Cyclops, Havok, Corsair and their descendants. Mister Sinister is a villain who is obsessed with their bloodline but not a Summers.

q: Which of these X-men characters is not a mutant?

q.e: Juggernaut, Cain Marko, is not a mutant; he gained his power from the mystical Crimson Gem of Cyttorak. He's Professor X's stepbrother.

q: Who is the head of the X-Men in the Age of Apocalypse timeline?

q.e: In the "Age of Apocalypse" storyline, Magneto leads the X-Men after Professor Xavier is killed in the past. It's an alternate timeline ruled by the villain Apocalypse.

q: This member of the Hellfire Clubs inner circle, known as the White Queen, once fought against the X-Men.

q.e: Emma Frost, the White Queen of the Hellfire Club, is a telepath who was first a villain and later joined the X-Men. She can turn her body into diamond.

q: In the 1989 TV movie The Trial of he Incredible Hulk, the Hulk co-stars with what fellow superhero?

q.e: In The Trial of the Incredible Hulk (1989), a TV movie, Bruce Banner meets Daredevil, played by Rex Smith. It was a pilot for a possible Daredevil series.

q: In Detective Comics #267, a magical Kobold from another dimension decides to help Batman fight crime--what was his name?

q.e: Bat-Mite is a mischievous imp from another dimension who idolizes Batman and tries to help him. He debuted in Detective Comics #267 in 1959.

q: What is Calvins favorite subject according to the popular comics Calvin and Hobbes?

q.e: Calvin's strong interest in dinosaurs is a recurring theme in Calvin and Hobbes; he often imagines himself as one. He also invents alter egos like Spaceman Spiff and Stupendous Man.

q: What superhero does Hugh Jackman play in the X-Men series?

q.e: Hugh Jackman played Wolverine, a mutant with claws and healing powers, in the X-Men movies from 2000 to 2017. He played the role for 17 years.

q: Who played Alfred in the 2005 movie Batman Begins?

q.e: Michael Caine played Alfred Pennyworth in Batman Begins (2005) and its sequels. The earlier Batman films featured Michael Gough as Alfred.

q: Who played Clark Kent and Superman in the first Superman movie?

q.e: Christopher Reeve was chosen out of hundreds of actors to portray the Man of Steel in the 1978 film 'Superman', reprising the role in three sequels. Kirk Alyn played him in the original 1948 serial.

q: What is the name of the town that Clark Kent calls home in the Superman movies?

q.e: Clark Kent grows up on a farm in the fictional town of Smallville, Kansas, before relocating to the bustling city of Metropolis to work at the Daily Planet.

q: Who played Jor-El, the biological father of Superman in the 1978 Superman movie?

q.e: Marlon Brando received top billing and a then-record salary of 3.7 million dollars plus percentage points for just over ten minutes of screen time as Superman's father.

q: Batman has long been considered a loner and a bit of a rebel amongst superheroes. Despite this, hes had a few sidekicks, and worked in a number of teams. What was the name of the first team he worked in?

q.e: Batman was a member of the Justice Society of America, the first superhero team in comics, from the 1940s. The Justice League came later, in 1960.

q: In the Earth-Two DC Universe, who does Batman partner with, and eventually marry?

q.e: In the Earth-Two timeline, Bruce Wayne marries Selina Kyle (Catwoman), and they have a daughter, Helena Wayne, who becomes the Huntress. Earth-Two was DC's home of Golden Age heroes.

q: Who was Batmans love interest in the first Batman movie?

q.e: Vicki Vale, a photojournalist played by Kim Basinger, is Bruce Wayne's love interest in Tim Burton's Batman (1989). She works for the Gotham Globe.

q: What is the name of Gothams main newspaper in the movie Batman?

q.e: The Gotham Globe is the newspaper in Tim Burton's Batman (1989), where reporter Alexander Knox and photographer Vicki Vale work. In the comics, Gotham's main paper is the Gotham Gazette.

q: Who plays Mr. Freeze in the 1997 movie Batman and Robin?

q.e: Arnold Schwarzenegger played Mr. Freeze in Batman & Robin (1997). He was paid a reported $25 million.

q: What is the name of the newspaper editor who carries out a campaign against Spider-Man?

q.e: J. Jonah Jameson is the bombastic editor-in-chief and publisher of the Daily Bugle, known for declaring Spider-Man a menace. Perry White is the editor-in-chief of the Daily Planet in the Superman comics.

q: This actor plays Mac MacGuff in Juno. He is Spidermans boss in the Spiderman movies and a shrink on Law and Order.

q.e: J.K. Simmons played Mac MacGuff in Juno, J. Jonah Jameson in Sam Raimi's Spider-Man films and Dr. Emil Skoda on Law & Order. He won an Oscar for Whiplash in 2015.

q: Which two actors have played the Batman villain, Two-Face?

q.e: Two-Face has been played by several actors, including Billy Dee Williams, Tommy Lee Jones and Aaron Eckhart. Harvey Dent is a district attorney who becomes a villain after half his face is scarred.

q: What unforgettable character did actor Heath Ledger portray in the 2008 Batman movie The Dark Knight?

q.e: Heath Ledger portrayed the Joker in 'The Dark Knight', earning a posthumous Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his iconic performance.

q: The production of the 2007 movie Spider-Man 3 was one of the priciest in film history. What does Toby Maguires character study at the Columbia University?

q.e: In Spider-Man 3, Peter Parker is studying physics at Columbia University, as in most versions of the film series. Spider-Man 3 had a reported budget of about $258 million.

q: What comic book does the young man read every day next to the magazine vendor in the movie Watchmen?

q.e: In Watchmen, a young man reads Tales of the Black Freighter, a pirate comic, at a newsstand. The story-within-a-story echoes the main plot.

q: What actor portrayed Batman in the 2008 movie The Dark Knight, one of the highest-grossing movies of all time?

q.e: Christian Bale played Batman in The Dark Knight (2008), directed by Christopher Nolan. The film made over $1 billion worldwide.

q: What actress portrayed Catwoman in the 1992 movie Batman Returns?

q.e: Michelle Pfeiffer played Catwoman in Batman Returns (1992). Her costume was made of latex and was famously stitched together by hand.

q: What actor is not correctly matched with the character he played in The Avengers?
Chris Hemsworth - Dr. Bruce Banner / Hulk
Chris Evans - Steve Rogers / Captain America
Robert Downey, Jr. - Tony Stark / Iron Man

q.e: Chris Hemsworth plays Thor in The Avengers, not Bruce Banner. Bruce Banner/Hulk is played by Mark Ruffalo.

q: What Academy Award-winning actor plays the king of Asgard and father of Thor in Kenneth Branaghs superhero movie Thor?

q.e: Anthony Hopkins played Odin, king of Asgard and father of Thor, in Thor (2011). He won an Oscar for The Silence of the Lambs.

q: What year did the TV series "Batman� premiere?

q.e: The Batman TV series with Adam West premiered on ABC in January 1966, with a campy, comic style. It was a hit and helped to start a wave of "Batmania".

q: Who portrays Batman's sidekick, Robin, in the TV series "Batman�?

q.e: Burt Ward played Robin, Batman's young sidekick, in the 1960s TV series. His catchphrase was "Holy..." followed by a word, as in "Holy cow, Batman!".

q: Which villain on the TV series "Batman� was portrayed by the greatest number of actors?

q.e: Mr. Freeze was played by three different actors on the 1960s Batman series: George Sanders, Otto Preminger and Eli Wallach. It's one of the show's most popular villains.

q: Which nemesis of Batman was portrayed by Burgess Meredith in the "Batman� TV series?

q.e: Burgess Meredith played the Penguin, with his signature "wak-wak" laugh, in the 1960s Batman TV series. He also played Mickey in the Rocky movies.

q: Who portrays Batman's nemesis, The Joker, on the TV series "Batman�?

q.e: Cesar Romero played the Joker in the 1960s Batman TV series, and he famously refused to shave his mustache, so the makeup was applied over it. His cackling laugh became iconic.

q: What year did the TV series "Batman� go off the air?

q.e: The Batman TV series ended in March 1968 after three seasons and 120 episodes. Falling ratings led to its cancellation.

q: Which Lex was the arch enemy of the comics character Superman?

q.e: Lex Luthor, whose full name is Alexander Joseph Luthor, is Superman's arch-nemesis. He first appeared in Action Comics #23 in 1940.

q: This superhero, who has a pet named Speak, is the main character in a self-titled animated series.

q.e: The Tick, a satirical superhero who wears a blue suit with antennae, has been a comic, a cartoon and a live-action series. His battle cry is "Spoon!".

q: Which of these veteran actors played the evil Bookworm in the 60s Batman TV series?

q.e: Roddy McDowall played the villain Bookworm in the 1960s Batman TV series. He was also known for the Planet of the Apes movies.

q: Who played the Joker in Tim Burtons Batman?

q.e: Jack Nicholson played the Joker in Tim Burton's Batman (1989). The movie's villain is memorable for its violent, theatrical style.
Christopher Nolan directed Batman Begins (2005), the first film in his Dark Knight trilogy, with Christian Bale as Batman. The film reimagined the character with a darker, more realistic tone.

q: What year was Tim Burtons Batman released?

q.e: Tim Burton's Batman was released in 1989 and starred Michael Keaton and Jack Nicholson, with music by Danny Elfman. It became one of the highest-grossing movies of the year.

q: Frederick Dukes is the real name of which X-Men villain?

q.e: Frederick "Fred" Dukes is the Blob, a mutant villain in the X-Men comics, known for his huge size and immovable body. He's a member of the Brotherhood of Mutants.

q: What mutant tricked the Phoenix into thinking the X-Men were enemies and in doing so helped with the creation of the Dark Phoenix?

q.e: The mutant Mastermind, Jason Wyngarde, used illusions to turn Jean Grey into the Black Queen of the Hellfire Club. This helped create the Dark Phoenix in The Dark Phoenix Saga.

q: What is the name of the superhero cartoon character voiced by Jay Leno in the animated TV series The Fairly OddParents?

q.e: Jay Leno voiced the Crimson Chin, a superhero cartoon character that Timmy Turner admires, in The Fairly OddParents. The Crimson Chin fights crime with a very large chin.

q: In the Hellboy universe, what was Abe Sapien's birth name?

q.e: Abe Sapien, a fish-like member of the BPRD, was named Langdon Everett Caul when he was human. He lived in the 19th century, which is revealed in the Hellboy comics.

q: In what year did the first "The Walking Dead" comic come out?

q.e: The first issue of The Walking Dead comic was published in October 2003, written by Robert Kirkman with art by Tony Moore. It later inspired the hit TV series.

q: When Batman trolls the online chat rooms, what alias does he use?

q.e: Batman has used many aliases to investigate cases and hide his identity, both as Bruce Wayne and in disguise. Disguises and cover identities are an important part of his detective skills.

q: In the "Archie" comics, who was Jughead's first girlfriend?

q.e: Jughead Jones is Archie Andrews's best friend in the Archie comics, known for his crown-shaped beanie and his appetite for hamburgers. He's usually uninterested in romance.

q: Which of the following rings from the DC Comics' "Lantern Corps" are classified as Parasitic?

q.e: The rings in the Green Lantern universe are powered by the emotional spectrum: willpower (green), fear (yellow), rage (red), avarice (orange), hope (blue), compassion (indigo) and love (violet). Each color has its own corps.

q: What year was the first San Diego Comic-Con?

q.e: The first San Diego Comic-Con was held in 1970, as a three-day event with a few hundred attendees. It has since grown into a massive pop-culture convention with over 130,000 attendees.

q: What character did Marlon Brando portray in the 1978 movie Superman?

q.e: Marlon Brando played Jor-El, Superman's father on Krypton, in Superman (1978). He was paid a record $3.7 million for a few minutes of screen time.

q: What character did actor Christopher Walken portray in the 1992 movie Batman Returns?

q.e: Christopher Walken played the villain Max Shreck, a corrupt businessman, in Batman Returns (1992). The character's name is a nod to Max Schreck, the actor who played the vampire in the 1922 film Nosferatu.

q: What is the real name of Gambit who first appeared in the comic book The Uncanny X-Men?

q.e: Remy LeBeau, known as Gambit, is a Cajun mutant who can charge objects with energy, and he debuted in Uncanny X-Men #266 in 1990. He's often seen with a deck of cards.

q: Who were the creators of comics superhero Aquaman?

q.e: Aquaman was created by Paul Norris and Mort Weisinger and first appeared in More Fun Comics #73 in 1941. He's a king of Atlantis with the ability to communicate with sea life.

q: The original Batgirl was related to what familiar Batman character?

q.e: The original Batgirl was Betty Kane, the niece of Batwoman (Kathy Kane), who debuted in 1961. The better-known Barbara Gordon became Batgirl in 1967.

q: This Louisville-born actor was called the busiest actor in Hollywood because he got so many roles in so many movies. His most famous roles were in Deliverance in 1972, Network in 1976, and Superman in 1978.

q.e: Ned Beatty, born in Louisville, Kentucky, appeared in Deliverance (1972), Network (1976) and Superman (1978), where he played Lex Luthor's henchman, Otis. He was nominated for an Oscar for Network.

q: Who played Clark Kent/Superman in the 1948 Superman movie?

q.e: Kirk Alyn played Superman in the 1948 movie serial, the first live-action Superman on screen. It was a series of 15 chapters shown in theaters.

q: In 2007 Marvel started a series of comic books based on The Dark Tower. What is the name of the first volume?

q.e: Marvel's comic adaptation of Stephen King's The Dark Tower began in 2007 with The Gunslinger Born, written by Peter David. It tells the early life of the gunslinger Roland.

q: In the 1966 movie Batman, based on the ABC TV series, all but one of the villains listed were played by the TV series actors/actresses. Which character was not played by one of the original actors?

q.e: In the 1966 Batman movie, Lee Meriwether played Catwoman, because Julie Newmar, the TV Catwoman, was not available. The other main villains were played by their TV actors.

q: In the 2006 movie Superman Returns, opening titles reveal that Superman has been absent from Earth for five years. Where was he during this period?

q.e: In Superman Returns (2006), Superman leaves Earth for five years to look for the remains of Krypton. When he returns, he finds the world changed and Lois Lane has a son.

q: Which Batman movie does this quote come from? Mayor: What do we got? Lt. James Gordon: Nothing. No matches on prints, DNA, dental. Clothing is custom, no labels. Nothing in his pockets but knives and lint. No name, no other alias.

q.e: This quote is from The Dark Knight (2008), in a scene where police examine a mysterious man captured after a break-in. The film's villain is the Joker.

q: What anniversary was Gotham celebrating in the 1989 film Batman?

q.e: The 1989 film Batman begins with Gotham City celebrating its 200th anniversary. A parade for the occasion plays a part in the plot.

q: He wrote the screenplay for Batman Begins (2005), but hes probably more famous for writing the Blade movies (Blade, Blade II, and Blade: Trinity).

q.e: David S. Goyer co-wrote Batman Begins with Christopher Nolan, and he also wrote the Blade films starring Wesley Snipes. He later worked on Man of Steel too.

q: What is Adrian Viedts superhero identity in the movie Watchmen?

q.e: Adrian Veidt, called "the smartest man in the world", is the superhero Ozymandias in Watchmen. He's named after Shelley's poem about a fallen king.

q: Frank Gorshin, the man of 100 faces, was best known as an impressionist. He was often seen on The Dean Martin Celebrity Roasts and played this character on the TV series Batman.

q.e: Frank Gorshin, a comedian and impressionist, played the Riddler, a villain obsessed with puzzles, in the 1960s Batman series. He earned an Emmy nomination for the role.

q: In the X-Men animated series, after attempting to rescue a mutant from a mob of civilians, Cyclops and Jean Grey are kidnapped by what underground mutant society?

q.e: In X-Men: The Animated Series, Cyclops and Jean Grey are taken by the Morlocks, a group of mutants who live in tunnels under New York. The Morlocks first appeared in the comics in 1982.

q: Dr. Adler, the scientist in the X-Men series who claimed to have a cure for mutation, was actually which character in disguise?

q.e: Mystique, a shapeshifter who can imitate anyone, disguised herself as a scientist in the X-Men animated series. Her skills at deception made her a dangerous enemy.

q: This character in the X-Men series, sent by Magneto to destroy the X-Mansion, is a former enemy of Wolverine.

q.e: Sabretooth (Victor Creed) is a violent mutant with claws and fangs who is one of Wolverine's longest-running enemies. He's often hired by Magneto's Brotherhood.

q: Which of these characters of the X-Men series is the only person whom Rogue can touch and not absorb his/her powers?

q.e: Rogue absorbs the memories and powers of anyone she touches skin-to-skin, which is why she wears gloves and covers up. Her power makes physical contact difficult.

q: What is the name of the girl that X-Men member Cyclops meets and protects at a night club, while Jean Grey is in the hospital?

q.e: Dazzler, the mutant Alison Blaire, is a singer who can turn sound into light. In the X-Men animated series, she appears in a nightclub.

q: In the X-Men series, Graydon Creed, the leader of the Friends of Humanity, is the son of which mutant?

q.e: Graydon Creed, the anti-mutant leader of the Friends of Humanity, is the son of Sabretooth and Mystique, though he doesn't know it at first. He despises mutants.

q: In Marvel Comics, what is the homeworld of the cosmic herald Silver Surfer?

q.e: Norrin Radd sacrificed his freedom on the utopian world of Zenn-La to become the herald of Galactus in order to save his home planet. Hala is the capital of the Kree Empire, and Xandar is the homeworld of the Nova Corps.

q: This TV and voice actor is from a Jewish family from Greece. He has had many voice roles (numerous characters on the The Simpsons, Eddie Brock in the Spider-Man animated series), several Emmys, and roles in many movies and TV shows.

q.e: Hank Azaria voiced Eddie Brock/Venom in the Spider-Man animated series of the 1990s. He also voices Moe, Chief Wiggum and many other Simpsons characters.

q: What Batman villain formerly worked as a zoologist?

q.e: Man-Bat is Dr. Kirk Langstrom, a zoologist who turns himself into a bat-man hybrid with an experimental serum. He debuted in Detective Comics #400 in 1970.

q: Which one of these comics was the first comic Jim Davis created?

q.e: Jim Davis created Gnorm Gnat, a comic about a bug, in the early 1970s, before he created Garfield in 1978. Editors reportedly told him readers could not relate to a bug, so he switched to a cat.

q: Who is the Sun God of the Savage Land, featured in the X-Men series?

q.e: Garokk, the Petrified Man, is the Sun God of the Savage Land, a hidden prehistoric jungle in Antarctica. He first appeared in X-Men #62 in 1970.

q: Which fruit is said to "keep the doctor away"?

q.e: The common adage 'An apple a day keeps the doctor away' originated in Wales during the 1860s in the rhyming form: 'Eat an apple on going to bed, and you'll keep the doctor from earning his bread.'

q: Which country is pizza originally from?

q.e: Modern pizza originated in the southwestern city of Naples, Italy, where flatbreads were first topped with tomatoes, cheese, and basil in the late 18th and 19th centuries.

q: What is the main ingredient in guacamole?

q.e: Guacamole originated with the Aztecs in Mexico and relies on mashed ripe avocado as its creamy base, typically seasoned with salt, lime juice, cilantro, and onions.

q: Which country is famous for croissants and baguettes?

q.e: Both pastries are quintessential French culinary staples, and the artisanal French baguette was officially added to UNESCO's cultural heritage list in 2022. Interestingly, the croissant evolved from the Austrian kipferl before becoming a French icon.

q: Popcorn is made from which plant?

q.e: Popcorn comes from a specialized variety of maize (Zea mays everta) that has a hard, moisture-sealed hull; heating it builds up steam pressure inside until the kernel pops inside-out.

q: The poblano is a popular choice when making which stuffed dish "rellenos"?

q.e: Chiles rellenos means "stuffed chiles" in Spanish. Poblano peppers are typically roasted, filled with cheese, battered and fried.

q: Surimi ("formed fish") is sold labeled as what kind of "crabmeat"?

q.e: Surimi is a paste made from white fish, usually pollock, that has been shaped and flavored to mimic crab, lobster or shrimp. It's labeled "imitation crab" in the US.
Coffee contains caffeine, a natural stimulant. Tea, cola and energy drinks also contain it, while most herbal teas don't.

q: Which is the only food that never spoils?

q.e: Honey can last indefinitely because it is low in water and acidic, so bacteria can't grow. Archaeologists have found edible honey in ancient Egyptian tombs.

q: What was the first food to be microwaved?

q.e: Percy Spencer discovered microwave heating in the 1940s when a candy bar melted in his pocket near a radar tube. The first foods he tested on purpose were popcorn and an egg.

q: Lactose is a type of sugar consisting of two subunits (galactose and glucose), found primarily in what food?

q.e: Lactose is the main sugar in milk, made of glucose and galactose. People who are lactose intolerant lack enough of the enzyme lactase to digest it.

q: This drink was invented for a party given by Winston Churchills mother.

q.e: The Manhattan is said to have been created at the Manhattan Club in New York in about 1874, for a party thrown by Jennie Jerome, Winston Churchill's mother. Historians doubt the story, since she was in England at the time.

q: This country is the leader in beer consumption (per capita).

q.e: The Czech Republic has long led the world in beer drinking per person, at roughly 140 liters a year. The country's pilsner style is named after the city of Plzeň.

q: In which line the food is not matched with its place of origin?

q.e: Peaches originated in China, not Peru. Their scientific name, Prunus persica, comes from a mistaken belief that they came from Persia.

q: Retsina, sometimes referred to as the wine of the Gods, is produced in which country?

q.e: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavored with pine resin, a method that dates back to ancient times when amphorae were sealed with resin. It has a distinctive piney taste.

q: What other name is commonly used to refer to sweet and sour sauce in China?

q.e: Sweet and sour dishes are a classic of Chinese cooking, especially Cantonese cuisine. The sauce blends sugar and vinegar.

q: Which is the only US state famous for producing limburger cheese in the Chalet Cheese Co-op factory?

q.e: Limburger cheese is known for its strong smell. The Chalet Cheese Co-op in Monroe, Wisconsin, is the only US producer.

q: Which of these is best for cooling your mouth if you have just eaten very spicy food?

q.e: Capsaicin, the chemical responsible for the heat in spicy food, is oily and binds to mouth receptors. Milk contains the protein casein, which breaks down capsaicin and washes it away, whereas water merely spreads the oil around.

q: Ireland, New Zealand and Japan are three countries with very high consumption of this drink.

q.e: Ireland, the UK, Turkey and New Zealand are among the biggest tea drinkers per person. Tea is the world's second most consumed drink after water.

q: What is the most important ingredient for preparing brownies, a type of American dessert?

q.e: Chocolate (cocoa powder or melted chocolate) is the essential flavoring in brownies, along with butter, sugar and eggs. Brownies were first documented in American cookbooks in the late 1800s.

q: Tequila is named after a town with the same name in the country where it is a traditional drink.

q.e: Tequila is named for the town of Tequila in Jalisco, Mexico. By law it must be made mostly from blue agave.

q: In this country people drink gorilka. It is similar to vodka.

q.e: Gorilka (horilka) is a Ukrainian spirit similar to vodka. It's often flavored with honey or pepper.

q: Sangria is consumed all year round in this country. It is made of wine mixed with fruit and spices.

q.e: Sangria is a Spanish drink of red wine, chopped fruit and often brandy. Its name comes from the Spanish word for blood, "sangre".

q: Schnapps is a kind of fruit brandy and is typical for the country which gave the name of this beverage.

q.e: Schnapps is a strong spirit distilled from fruit, a German tradition. In the US, "schnapps" can also mean sweetened liqueurs.

q: Ouzo is the preferred drink in this country. It is produced from pressed grapes, herbs and berries.

q.e: Ouzo is a protected anise-flavored aperitif exclusive to Greece and Cyprus. When mixed with water or ice, the essential oils precipitate out in a chemical reaction known as the ouzo effect, turning the clear liquid milky white.

q: Ploughmans Lunch is traditional for this country. It consists of cheese, a bit of pickle and pickled onion, and a slice of bread.

q.e: A ploughman's lunch is an English pub meal of cheese, bread, pickles and onions. It became popular in the 1950s as a marketing campaign for pubs.

q: Zong Zi is a traditional food for this country. It is a rice dumpling wrapped in bamboo or reed leaves.

q.e: Zongzi are sticky rice dumplings wrapped in bamboo or reed leaves, eaten during the Dragon Boat Festival in China. They are linked to the poet Qu Yuan.

q: Quesadillas are folded tortillas, stuffed with cheese and then grilled.

q.e: In Spanish, "quesadilla" comes from "queso" (cheese). Mexican quesadillas are folded tortillas filled with cheese and sometimes other fillings.

q: What dish is traditionally served for breakfast in Cambodia, Thailand and Vietnam?

q.e: Soup is a common breakfast in Southeast Asia, such as pho in Vietnam and rice porridge in Thailand. Cambodia has kuyteav noodle soup.

q: The popular breakfast cereal dish muesli was invented in 1900 in which country?

q.e: Muesli was invented around 1900 by Swiss physician Maximilian Bircher-Benner for patients in his Zurich hospital. It combined oats, fruit, nuts and milk.

q: The traditional Malayan breakfast dish Nasi lemak includes soaking rice in what?

q.e: Nasi lemak is rice cooked in coconut milk, served with sambal, anchovies, peanuts and egg. It's considered Malaysia's national dish.

q: What type of food is Pancetta?

q.e: Pancetta is an Italian cured meat made from pork belly, similar to bacon, but typically cured with salt and spices and rolled into a cylinder rather than smoked.

q: Stilton is a cheese which originated in which country?

q.e: Stilton is an English blue cheese. It can only be made in Derbyshire, Leicestershire and Nottinghamshire, and has a protected designation.

q: This cocktail is as simple as mixing 1 oz vanilla liqueur and 1/2 fluid ounce cream.

q.e: This drink uses vanilla liqueur and cream, such as a cocktail, but the name "Little Beer" doesn't match a well-known recipe. Many cocktails are named after their look.

q: This popular cocktail, usually garnished with a cherry, contains rye or bourbon whiskey mixed with sweet vermouth.

q.e: A classic Manhattan combines whiskey, sweet red vermouth, and a dash of Angostura bitters, traditionally served with a brandied or maraschino cherry. A similar cocktail made with Scotch whisky instead is called a Rob Roy.

q: The first industrial production of cheese in the world started in 1815, in which country?

q.e: The first industrial cheese factory opened in Switzerland in 1815, in Thun. Swiss cheesemaking has a long tradition, including Emmental and Gruyère.

q: Risotto is made with special kinds of rice and is traditionally served with fish products or cheese. What country does this dish come from?

q.e: Risotto is an Italian rice dish, usually made with short-grain rice such as Arborio or Carnaroli. It originated in northern Italy, in the Po Valley.

q: What is the executive chef of the kitchen called?

q.e: The chef de cuisine, or executive chef, is the head of the kitchen. Under him are the sous-chef and chefs de partie in the French brigade system.

q: John Wagner, the first American to produce lager beer, had a brewery in which state?

q.e: John Wagner, a German immigrant, brewed the first American lager in Philadelphia in 1840. He used yeast brought from Bavaria.

q: The term cenosillicaphobia, related to drinking beer and alcohol as a whole, means what?
A fear of an empty glass
A fear of a falling glass
A fear of a broken glass
A fear of breaking a glass

q.e: "Cenosillicaphobia" is the fear of an empty glass, a humorous word. It's formed from Greek and Latin roots.

q: This is a mixture of red and white sparkling wine, that has a high sugar content.

q.e: Cold Duck is a mix of sparkling burgundy and champagne or other sparkling wine. It became popular in the US in the 1960s and 70s.

q: What happened to the first prototype of the bread-slicing machine?
It was destroyed in a fire.
It was destroyed by its inventor.
It was stolen by the people of Battle Creek, Michigan.

q.e: Otto Rohwedder's first bread-slicing machine prototype was destroyed in a fire in 1917. He built a new one and it was in use by 1928.

q: When was the first loaf of sliced bread sold?

q.e: The first commercially sliced bread was sold on July 7, 1928, in Chillicothe, Missouri. The phrase "the greatest thing since sliced bread" came later.

q: Who prompted the marketing of sliced bread in 1928?

q.e: The Chillicothe Baking Company's Frank Bench was the first to use the machine, and W.E. Long promoted "Kleen Maid Sliced Bread" in 1928.

q: Which of these ingredients is not used in the preparation of the Chinese dish called Ants climbing a tree?

q.e: "Ants climbing a tree" is a Sichuan dish of stir-fried glass noodles with minced pork. The "ants" are the pork bits that cling to the noodles; there are no ants and no fish.

q: What is the meaning of the name of the Suea Rong Hai dish that is popular in Thailand?

q.e: "Suea Rong Hai" means "crying tiger" in Thai. It's a grilled steak served with a spicy dipping sauce, so called because it's so hot it makes a tiger cry.

q: What type of meat is used in the preparation of the Indian dish called Bombay duck?

q.e: Bombay duck is not duck. It is a dried or fresh lizardfish (bombil), a dish from Mumbai.

q: What type of dessert is the Boston cream pie?

q.e: Boston cream pie is a cake with custard filling and chocolate glaze. It was named a pie because early cake pans were often pie tins.

q: The recipe for the German chocolate cake did not originate in Germany, but in this country.

q.e: German chocolate cake is American, named for Sam German, who developed a sweet baking chocolate in 1852 for Baker's. The recipe was published in Texas in 1957.

q: The dish called American fried rice is not in fact American. Where was it created?

q.e: American fried rice is a Thai dish (khao phat amerikan) created by adding ketchup, hot dogs and fried chicken to rice. It's said to have been inspired by American soldiers during the Vietnam War era.

q: In which of these season do the fruit of the apple tree ripen?

q.e: Apples ripen mostly in the fall, from late summer through October in the northern hemisphere. Some varieties ripen earlier or later.

q: What is the main ingredient of the popular French dessert Teurgoule?

q.e: Teurgoule is a Normandy dessert, a slow-baked rice pudding with cinnamon. It's served with fallue, a brioche.

q: This vegetable is the main ingredient of the traditional French dish Cassoulet.

q.e: Cassoulet is a slow-cooked stew from southwest France, made from white beans with pork, sausage and duck. The name comes from the earthenware dish "cassole".

q: What type of food is the French delicacy called Andouillette?

q.e: Andouillette is a French sausage made from pork intestines (tripe) with a strong smell. The French have a society that honors it.

q: Which of these is not among the traditional ingredients used for the making of the popular French dish Tartiflette?

q.e: Tartiflette is a dish from the French Alps made with potatoes, reblochon cheese, bacon (lardons) and onions. It doesn't include rice.

q: What type of meat is used for the preparation of the French dish called Pot-au-feu?

q.e: Pot-au-feu is a French beef stew, a "pot on the fire", with root vegetables. The broth and meat are often served as separate courses.

q: What common expression is used to refer to beer to point out its excellent nutritional properties?

q.e: Beer is known as "liquid bread", since it's made from grains and has been a staple food since ancient times. Monks used it during fasts.

q: What vegetable is the main ingredient of the popular Spanish soup called Gazpacho?

q.e: Gazpacho originated in the southern Spanish region of Andalusia and is traditionally served cold, blending ripe tomatoes with cucumbers, peppers, onions, garlic, and olive oil.

q: In what Asian country did the recipe for the Miso soup originate?

q.e: Miso soup comes from Japan, and is made with dashi stock and fermented soybean paste (miso). It is typically served at breakfast.

q: What type of milk is Brussels cheese made of?

q.e: Brussels cheese (Brusselse kaas) is made from cow's milk. It's a soft cheese from Belgium.

q: What type of cheese is the Roquefort, also called Rochefort?

q.e: Roquefort is a blue cheese made from sheep's milk and aged in caves at Roquefort-sur-Soulzon in France. It's one of the oldest known blue cheeses.

q: What does the name of the Mozzarella cheese mean?

q.e: Mozzarella gets its name from the Italian verb "mozzare", meaning "to cut off", from how the curd is cut after stretching. Real buffalo mozzarella comes from Campania.

q: In what country did the Castelo Branco cheese originate?

q.e: Castelo Branco cheese is Portuguese, made from sheep's milk and named for a town in the east of the country. It's soft and tangy.

q: What type of milk is Brie cheese traditionally made of?

q.e: Brie is traditionally made from cow's milk, in the Île-de-France region. It has a white rind and creamy center.

q: In what country did the Cheddar cheese originate?

q.e: Cheddar cheese originates from the village of Cheddar in Somerset, England, with records of production dating back to at least the 12th century. The caves of Cheddar Gorge provided the ideal humidity and temperature for maturing the cheese.

q: What texture does Gruyere cheese traditionally have?

q.e: Gruyère is a hard Swiss cheese, with a nutty flavor, that is used in fondue. It's aged from 5 to 18 months.

q: Which of these is the name of a popular Canadian blue cheese variety?

q.e: Dragon's Breath is a blue cheese from Nova Scotia, Canada, made by Armadale Cheese. It's one of the best-known Canadian blue cheeses.

q: What type of cheese is the Gorgonzola cheese?

q.e: Gorgonzola is a traditional Italian blue cheese made from unskimmed cow's milk, characterized by blue-green veining caused by the mold Penicillium roqueforti.

q: In what country did Raclette cheese originate?

q.e: Raclette originated in Switzerland, in the Valais region, and is also eaten in France and Savoy. The name comes from the French word "racler", to scrape.

q: What texture does Parmigiano-Reggiano, or parmesan cheese have?

q.e: Parmigiano-Reggiano is a hard, granular cheese aged for at least 12 months. It's made in a small part of northern Italy.

q: In what country of the UK was Dunlop cheese created?

q.e: Dunlop cheese is Scottish, from the village of Dunlop in Ayrshire. It's similar to cheddar but moister.

q: In what country was the Chihuahua cheese created?

q.e: Chihuahua cheese (queso menonita) was created in Mexico by Mennonite settlers who arrived in the 1920s. It's a melting cheese.

q: In what shape is the Caciocavallo cheese traditionally produced?

q.e: Caciocavallo is a stretched-curd cheese from southern Italy, shaped like a teardrop or gourd. It's tied in pairs and hung over a beam to age; its name means "horse cheese".

q: What type of milk is the Grana Padano cheese made from?

q.e: Grana Padano is made from cow's milk in northern Italy. It's a cheaper cousin of Parmigiano-Reggiano.

q: In what country did the bread called Flatkaka appear for the first time?

q.e: Flatkaka is an Icelandic flatbread made from rye. It's often eaten with smoked lamb or butter.

q: The Italian bread called Focaccia resembles this other traditional Italian dish.

q.e: Focaccia is an Italian flatbread, usually topped with olive oil and herbs, that is a close relative of pizza. It comes from Liguria.

q: What vegetable is used for the preparation of the traditional Norwegian bread called Lefse?

q.e: Lefse is a Norwegian flatbread made from potatoes, flour and cream, and cooked on a griddle. It's popular among Scandinavian Americans at Christmas.

q: The bread called Marraqueta was invented in this South American country.

q.e: Marraqueta (also known as pan francés) is a bread from Chile, with four segments that split. It's mostly eaten in Chile and Bolivia.

q: In what country did the bread variety called Tunnbrod originate?

q.e: Tunnbröd is a Swedish flatbread, soft or crisp, and was used to make the Swedish hot dog wrap. It originated in Sweden.

q: What type of meat is used for the preparation of the traditional Indonesian dish called Betutu?

q.e: Betutu is a Balinese dish of whole chicken or duck stuffed with spices and slow-cooked. It's often served at ceremonies.

q: What type of food is the Indonesian dish called Klepon?

q.e: Klepon is an Indonesian sweet: green rice-flour balls filled with palm sugar and coated with coconut. The sugar bursts when you bite.

q: What unusual ingredient does the traditional Indonesian food called Lawar contain?

q.e: Lawar is a Balinese dish of chopped vegetables, coconut and minced meat, and often mixed with fresh pig blood. It's eaten at ceremonies.

q: What does the name of the popular Indonesian dish Mie goreng mean?

q.e: "Mie goreng" means "fried noodles" in Indonesian. It's a street food made with sweet soy sauce, vegetables and egg.

q: What type of seafood is used for the making of the traditional Indonesian dish called Pempek?

q.e: Pempek is a fishcake from Palembang, Sumatra, made of fish and tapioca. It's served with a sweet-sour sauce called cuko.

q: What shape does the rice in the traditional Indonesian dish Tumpeng have?

q.e: Tumpeng is a cone of rice served at Indonesian celebrations, and the shape represents a mountain. It's surrounded by side dishes.

q: What type of meal is the traditional Indonesian dish called Gado-gado?

q.e: Gado-gado is an Indonesian salad of vegetables, tofu and egg served with a peanut sauce. The name means "mix-mix".

q: What is the meaning of the term iIkizukuri which is used in Japanese cuisine?

q.e: Ikizukuri means "prepared alive" in Japanese, a way of serving sashimi while the fish is still moving. It's controversial and banned in some countries.

q: What kind of meal is the traditional Japanese dish called Zoni?

q.e: Zōni is a Japanese soup with mochi (rice cakes), served at New Year. The broth varies by region.

q: What type of meat is used for the preparation of Basashi, a popular Japanese dish?

q.e: Basashi is raw horse meat sliced like sashimi, a delicacy in Kumamoto and other parts of Japan. It's served with soy sauce and ginger.

q: What is the meaning of the name of the popular spice saffron, which has an Arabic origin?

q.e: "Saffron" comes from the Arabic "za'faran", which is related to the word for yellow. It's the world's most expensive spice, made from the stigmas of crocus flowers.

q: What is the Native American sauce Mole de Cacahuate, or Peanut Mole, traditionally served with?

q.e: Peanut mole is a Mexican sauce usually served with chicken. Mole sauces blend nuts, chiles, and spices.

q: What type of meal is the Native American dish called Alegria?

q.e: Alegría is a Mexican candy made from amaranth seeds and honey. It dates back to the Aztecs.

q: What kind of drink is the traditional Native American beverage called Champurrado?

q.e: Champurrado is a warm Mexican drink of chocolate, masa (corn dough) and cinnamon. It's often drunk with tamales.

q: What is the popular Thai hot sauce Sriracha named after?

q.e: Sriracha is named after Si Racha, a coastal town in Thailand, where the sauce originated. The popular American version is from Huy Fong Foods in California.

q: What type of drink is the traditional Thai drink Kokkoh?

q.e: Kokkoh is a Thai rice-based drink or porridge. Rice milk is common in Southeast Asia.

q: What type of food is the popular Arab dish called baklava?

q.e: Baklava is a sweet pastry made with layers of phyllo, nuts and syrup or honey. It's popular in Turkey, Greece and the Middle East.

q: The Arabian dish Manakish is very similar to this very popular Italian food.

q.e: Manakish are Levantine flatbreads topped with za'atar, cheese or meat, similar to pizza. They are a common breakfast food.

q: What is the meaning if the word kibbeh which refers to a popular dish in the Arab world and in Brazil?

q.e: "Kibbeh" comes from the Arabic word for "ball", the shape of many versions. It's made from bulgur, minced meat and spices, and was brought to Brazil by Lebanese immigrants.

q: What plant is used in the preparation of the traditional Arab dish called Toum?

q.e: Toum is a Lebanese sauce made of garlic, oil, lemon and salt, whipped into a fluffy paste. It's eaten with grilled chicken.

q: What type of alcoholic beverage is the popular South African drink Umqombothi?

q.e: Umqombothi is a traditional South African beer made from maize and sorghum. It's often shared at ceremonies.

q: What kind of dish is the popular South African meal called Melktert?

q.e: Melktert (milk tart) is a South African dessert, with a custard filling in pastry, dusted with cinnamon. It came with Dutch settlers.

q: What type of rice is used for the preparation of the traditional Vietnamese dish Com tam?

q.e: Cơm tấm is a Vietnamese dish of broken rice, grains that have been fractured in milling. It's often eaten with grilled pork.

q: What is the main ingredient of the traditional Vietnamese dish Tiet canh?

q.e: Tiết canh is a Vietnamese dish made from raw blood (usually duck) mixed with herbs and meat. Health officials warn it can carry bacteria and parasites.

q: Which of these foods is generally poached in white wine?

q.e: Fish, such as sole, is often poached in white wine, as in French cuisine. The poaching liquid is then used for sauce.

q: Which ingredient for bread hurts the leavening (rising) ability?

q.e: Salt slows down yeast, so too much salt reduces how much bread rises. Bakers use enough to flavor the dough and control fermentation.

q: This country leads the world in per capita beer consumption:

q.e: The Czech Republic has the world's highest beer consumption per person. The average Czech drinks over 130 liters a year.

q: This country consumes the most beer.

q.e: China is the world's largest beer consumer by total volume, though its per-person consumption is lower than in Europe. The most popular brand is Snow.

q: At what time of the year is the Tom and Jerry cocktail served traditionally in the United States?

q.e: The Tom and Jerry is a hot Christmas cocktail made from a batter of egg, sugar and spices, mixed with rum or brandy. It's popular in the Midwest of the US.

q: In what country did the Kamikaze cocktail reportedly originate?

q.e: The Kamikaze (vodka, triple sec and lime juice) is said to have been invented in Japan by American servicemen after World War II. Its name refers to the Japanese suicide pilots.

q: What is often put on the glass rim when serving a Margarita cocktail?

q.e: A traditional margarita glass rim is coated with coarse salt, which balances the tart lime juice and sweet orange liqueur. Sugar rims are more typical for cocktails like the Sidecar or Lemon Drop.

q: What popular herb is added to the Mojito cocktail for a refreshing flavor?

q.e: A traditional Cuban Mojito combines white rum, sugar, lime juice, club soda, and muddled spearmint leaves.

q: What is the fruit of the coffee plant called?

q.e: The coffee "cherry" is the fruit of the coffee plant, and inside are usually two seeds, which we call coffee beans. The skin and pulp are sometimes used to make cascara tea.

q: What types of food should not be mixed, consumed or stored together according to Jewish dietary laws?

q.e: Kosher laws, from the Torah, prohibit mixing meat and dairy. Observant households have separate dishes for each.

q: What is the usual color of the gooseberry fruit?

q.e: Gooseberries are typically green, though some varieties are red, yellow or purple. They are tart and used in jams and pies.

q: Which U.S. state has the huckleberry for its state fruit?

q.e: Idaho has the huckleberry as its state fruit, adopted in 2000. Huckleberries grow wild in the Rocky Mountains.

q: In what country did the Damper bread variety originate?

q.e: Damper is a traditional Australian bread made by swagmen and stockmen in the bush, baked in ashes. It uses flour, water and salt.

q: What type of bread is the German bread variety called Dampfnudel?

q.e: Dampfnudel is a German dish: a steamed yeast dumpling served with vanilla sauce or savory. The name means "steam noodle".

q: In what Arab country did the Sangak bread variety originate?

q.e: Sangak is a traditional Persian flatbread from Iran, baked on hot stones. It's one of the country's most popular breads.

q: In what country did the bread called Pane carasau originate?

q.e: Pane carasau is a thin, crisp flatbread from Sardinia, Italy. It's also called "carta da musica" (music paper).

q: What type of flour is used for the preparation of the Thai bread Khanom bueang?

q.e: Khanom bueang are Thai crispy pancakes made with rice flour, filled with cream and topped with sweet or savory items. They're a street food.

q: In what Asian country was the Melonpan bread variety invented?

q.e: Melonpan is a sweet bun in Japan, with a cookie crust shaped like a melon. It doesn't contain melon, usually.

q: What vegetable is the main ingredient of the traditional Spanish soup Gazpacho?

q.e: Gazpacho is a cold Spanish soup from Andalusia, made from raw tomatoes, peppers, cucumber, garlic and olive oil. It's served in summer.

q: In what shape is the Spanish dessert Tortell traditionally prepared?

q.e: A tortell is a ring-shaped sweet bread from Catalonia, filled with marzipan or cream. It's eaten on Epiphany.

q: What type of food is the Spanish dish called Escalivada, which originated in Catalonia, Spain?

q.e: Escalivada is a Catalan dish of roasted vegetables, such as eggplant, peppers and onion, served cold as a salad. Its name comes from the Catalan for "ash-roasted".

q: In what country did the recipe for the Tiramisu cake originate?

q.e: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert made of ladyfingers soaked in coffee, with mascarpone cream and cocoa. It was created in the Veneto region in the 1960s or 70s, and its name means "pick me up".

q: In what country is the popular Spice cake believed to have originated?

q.e: Spice cake is an American cake containing spices, such as cinnamon and nutmeg, and sometimes raisins. It's a classic in American baking.

q: Which vegetables are considered taboo food in Buddhist tradition?

q.e: In some Buddhist traditions, garlic, onions and other pungent alliums are avoided because they are thought to inflame the passions. This is a rule for some monks.

q: It is generally accepted that the name of the ice cream dessert sundae originated from which of the following words?

q.e: The ice cream sundae was probably named for Sunday, with various towns claiming the invention in the 1890s. One theory is that it was made to avoid soda on Sunday.

q: Gelato, which is made with milk, cream, sugar, fresh fruit and nut purees, originated in this country.

q.e: Modern Italian gelato is traditionally traced back to Renaissance Florence and culinary pioneers like Bernardo Buontalenti in the 16th century.

q: Sangria is made of wine and fruits and is one of the most popular drinks in this country.

q.e: Sangria is a Spanish punch made from red wine, fruit and a bit of brandy. It's popular in Spain and Portugal.

q: In what US state is the Tillamook Cheese Factory located?

q.e: Tillamook Creamery is in Tillamook, Oregon. The farmers' cooperative was founded in 1909, known for its cheddar.

q: What type of meat is the German dish Hasenpfeffer traditionally made from?

q.e: Hasenpfeffer is a German rabbit stew, marinated in vinegar and wine. "Hase" means hare.

q: In what country was bread invented in the antiquity?

q.e: Egyptians are credited with developing leavened bread about 5,000 years ago, after flatbreads were made earlier. They used yeast from fermentation.

q: This word is the name of a fruit and a color.

q.e: Orange is both a fruit and a color. The color is named after the fruit, which was named from the Sanskrit "naranga".

q: Kiwi fruit or Chinese Gooseberries came from which country?

q.e: The kiwi fruit originated in China, where it is called "yang tao". New Zealand growers renamed it "kiwifruit" in the 1950s and 60s.

q: What is strange about the edible vegetable Salicornia, which Israel exports to Europe?
The vegetable is also used in glass-making.
It can only be eaten cooked.

q.e: Salicornia, or glasswort, is a salty plant that grows on coasts, and its ash was once used in glassmaking. It's also eaten as "sea asparagus".

q: What is the traditional food for Shavuot, a major festival in Judaism?

q.e: On Shavuot, Jews traditionally eat dairy foods, such as cheesecake and blintzes. Various reasons are given, including the idea that the Torah is like milk and honey.

q: Chop Suey, a pasta dish consisting of short noodles, was originally made and served in which country?

q.e: Chop suey is a Chinese-American dish of meat and vegetables in a sauce, not a pasta dish. It was developed in the US in the 19th century.

q: What does being obese in some countries with food shortages symbolizes?

q.e: In places where food is scarce, being overweight is often seen as a sign of wealth and good health. Attitudes differ across cultures.

q: If you needed a good source of iron, this food would be the best.

q.e: Liver, especially beef liver, is among the best sources of iron and vitamin A. Red meat and shellfish are also good sources.

q: The fruit of the poisonous Jerusalem cherry is very similar to which of these?

q.e: The Jerusalem cherry is a poisonous plant whose orange berries look like cherry tomatoes. It is toxic if eaten, and dangerous for children and pets.
