q: One of these four cities is not referred to as a big fruit.

q.e: New York is nicknamed "The Big Apple", and other cities have fruit nicknames. New Orleans is known as "The Big Easy".

q: What is the main ingredient in Boxty cakes, a traditional Irish dish?

q.e: Boxty is an Irish potato pancake made from grated and mashed potatoes. There's an old rhyme: "Boxty on the griddle, boxty in the pan".

q: Sushi, the icon of Japanese cuisine, is characterized by which of the following?
Soy based dipping sauces and wasabi

q.e: The key to sushi is its specially prepared rice, seasoned with vinegar, sugar and salt. "Sushi" refers to the rice, not the raw fish.

q: The dishes Tom yum soup, hummus, chicken tikka and Nasi goreng belong to the cuisine of what continent?

q.e: Tom yum (Thai), hummus (Middle Eastern), chicken tikka (South Asian) and nasi goreng (Indonesian) are all Asian dishes. The Middle East is part of Asia.

q: Haggis is a traditional Scottish dish, typically associated with this celebration.

q.e: Haggis is the centerpiece of Burns Suppers celebrated annually on January 25 to honor Scotland's national poet, Robert Burns. Burns famously penned the poem Address to a Haggis in 1786, welcoming the dish as the great chieftain o the puddin-race.

q: What type of meal is the traditional French dish called Bouillabaisse?

q.e: Bouillabaisse is a fish stew from Marseille, in southern France. It was traditionally a fishermen's stew made with leftover fish.

q: Blue crabs are the official state food of this U.S. state.

q.e: Maryland designated the blue crab (Callinectes sapidus) as its official state crustacean in 1989, celebrating its central role in Chesapeake Bay cuisine and heritage.

q: Champ is the name of a popular Irish dish. What does the popular Irish expression to be as thick as champ mean?
To be inflexible and unwilling to change
To be reticent and devoid of emotion

q.e: "Champ" is Irish mashed potato with scallions, and the saying "thick as champ" means someone is stupid. Slang uses "thick" to mean dim.

q: Which of the following is the most popular drink in all parts of India?

q.e: Tea (chai) is the most popular drink in India. The country is one of the largest tea producers and consumers in the world.

q: What is the English name commonly used to refer to the popular Indian dish Murgh Makhani?

q.e: Murgh makhani translates directly to butter chicken from Hindi, where 'murgh' means chicken and 'makhani' means buttery. The dish was developed in Delhi during the 1950s by the chefs at the Moti Mahal restaurant.

q: What fruit is used for the preparation of fenny, a popular Indian alcoholic beverage?

q.e: Feni is a spirit from Goa, made from cashew apples or from coconut palm sap. Both versions exist.

q: What is the meaning of the phrase Ropa vieja, which denotes a traditional dish very popular in Cuba?

q.e: "Ropa vieja" means "old clothes" in Spanish. It's Cuba's national dish of shredded beef in tomato sauce, so called because the shredded meat resembles tattered clothes.

q: In what country did the recipe for the popular German chocolate cake originate?

q.e: German chocolate cake isn't from Germany. It's named for Sam German, an American who developed the baking chocolate used in it.

q: What type of meat is used for the preparation of the traditional Cambodian dish Amok trey?

q.e: Fish amok is a Cambodian dish of steamed fish curry in coconut milk, cooked in banana leaves. It's considered a national dish.

q: What type of meal is the traditional Vietnamese dish called Pho?

q.e: Pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup featuring a fragrant, simmered bone broth, flat rice noodles (banh pho), herbs, and thinly sliced beef or chicken.

q: What vegetable is the main ingredient in the traditional Colombian soup called Ajiaco?

q.e: Ajiaco is a Colombian soup of chicken, corn, and several types of potato, flavored with the herb guasca. It's from Bogotá.

q: On what major holiday is the Venezuelan dish called Hallaca traditionally served?

q.e: Hallacas are Venezuelan tamales of corn dough with a meat stew, wrapped in banana leaves. They're made at Christmas.

q: What is the most popular traditional drink in Morocco?

q.e: Mint tea (made with green tea) is a sign of hospitality in Morocco. It's poured from a height to make foam.

q: The Cougnou Christmas bread is traditionally shaped like what?

q.e: Cougnou, a Belgian and northern French bread, is shaped like the baby Jesus in swaddling clothes. It's eaten around Christmas.

q: What type of dessert is the Pandoro, very popular in Italy around Christmas and New Year?

q.e: Pandoro is a sweet yeast bread from Verona, shaped like an eight-pointed star. The name means "golden bread".

q: The dessert called bibingka is traditionally prepared during Christmas in what country?

q.e: Bibingka is a Filipino rice cake, cooked in clay pots with banana leaves and coals. It's a traditional Christmas treat.

q: What sea food is traditionally present on the Christmas table in Spain?

q.e: Seafood such as shrimp, prawns and other shellfish is a traditional part of Spanish Christmas meals. Lamb and roast meat are also served.

q: The Christmas fruit cake stollen comes from what country?

q.e: Stollen originated in Dresden, Germany, where records mention the powdered-sugar-dusted fruit bread as far back as 1474.

Modern sushi originated in Japan as a form of street food known as nigirizushi in early 19th-century Edo (now Tokyo). It evolved from an ancient Southeast Asian preservation method called narezushi, where fish was fermented in soured rice.
Tofu is made by coagulating soy milk produced from soaked and ground soybeans, then pressing the resulting curds into firm white blocks.

q: What is the main ingredient of hummus?

q.e: Hummus is named after the Arabic word for chickpeas, which are cooked and blended with tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and olive oil.

q: Which nut is used to make marzipan?

q.e: Marzipan is made of ground almonds and sugar. It's used in candies and cakes, such as Stollen.

q: What primary ingredient gives traditional pesto sauce its green color?

q.e: Traditional pesto alla genovese gets its bright green hue and fragrance from fresh Genovese basil crushed with pine nuts, garlic, Parmesan, and olive oil.

q: Emily Post says corn should never be served this way at a formal dinner. How?

q.e: Etiquette writer Emily Post said corn on the cob should not be served at formal dinners, because it's messy. Kernels cut from the cob are fine.

q: Devonshire-style clotted ___ is the opposite of the whipped kind. What dairy product?

q.e: Clotted cream is a thick cream from Devon and Cornwall, served on scones. It's made by heating whole milk and letting it cool until the cream rises.

q: What company produces and distributes the citrus flavored soft drink Mello Yello?

q.e: Mello Yello is a citrus soda introduced by Coca-Cola in 1979, as a rival to Mountain Dew. It has caffeine.

q: What are the main ingredients of the traditional English dish Bubble and Squeak?

q.e: Bubble and squeak is a British dish of leftover potato and cabbage fried together. The name comes from the sounds made during cooking.

q: What word means a baked dish made mainly of eggs and milk?

q.e: A quiche is a French savory tart with a custard of eggs and cream or milk. The Lorraine version has bacon.

q: Sugar, a naturally occurring nutrient that makes food taste sweet, is classified in chemistry as what?

q.e: Sugars are carbohydrates, made of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Glucose, fructose and sucrose are common sugars.

q: The Hebrew word kosher , often translated as clean, refers to what kind of food?
That is fit for consumption according to the Books of Leviticus
That has been blessed before processing

q.e: "Kosher" means "fit" or "proper" in Hebrew, and refers to food that meets Jewish dietary laws from the Torah (Leviticus and Deuteronomy). It restricts pork, shellfish and mixing meat and dairy.

q: Sangria is a drink, traditionally served at Mexican weddings. Sangria contains all these ingredients, except one.

q.e: Sangria is a Spanish wine punch, not a Mexican wedding drink, and contains wine, fruit and brandy, but not tequila. In Mexico, "sangrita" is a different drink often paired with tequila.

q: In which American city is the fast-food restaurants chain McDonalds incorporated?

q.e: The first McDonald's restaurant was opened in San Bernardino, California, in 1940 by Richard and Maurice McDonald. Ray Kroc founded the corporation in Illinois in 1955.

q: The Polish food specialties, oscypek and bryndza are what type of food?

q.e: Oscypek is a smoked sheep's milk cheese from the Tatra Mountains, and bryndza is a soft sheep's milk cheese. Both are Polish regional specialties.

q: Pigs are known for their ability to smell what food really well?

q.e: Pigs have a keen sense of smell and have been used to find truffles. Dogs are now more commonly used because they don't eat them.

q: This food is a very good source of energy. It also contains phenylethylamine, which triggers the same reaction in the body as falling in love does.

q.e: Chocolate contains phenylethylamine, which is sometimes called the "love chemical". The amount in chocolate is small and mostly broken down, so the effect is modest.

q: As this drink relaxes and stimulates the senses, it is considered the proper drink for a romantic evening. The recommended quantity is one or two glasses, otherwise you will get sleepy and spoil the moment.

q.e: Wine is traditionally linked to romance, and moderate amounts can relax. Too much can cause sleepiness.

q: This drink is a widely known stimulant, but if you have too much, it becomes a depressant. Its active ingredient - caffeine - is known as the worlds most popular drug.

q.e: Caffeine is the world's most widely used psychoactive drug. It is a stimulant, and too much causes jitters, anxiety and poor sleep.

q: Rakia is a strong alcoholic drink made of various fruits, usually grapes, plums or apricots.

q.e: Rakia (rakija) is a fruit brandy popular in the Balkans, especially in Bulgaria, Serbia and Croatia. It's made from plums, grapes, apricots and more.

q: The first sales of the Coca Cola drink were made at Jacobs Pharmacy in Atlanta, Georgia, in what year?

q.e: Coca-Cola was first sold on May 8, 1886, at Jacobs' Pharmacy in Atlanta, Georgia, for five cents a glass. John Pemberton invented it.

q: This vegetable comes from the Andes in Peru and Bolivia, where people have known it for 2400 years. It became popular in Europe in 1780, when it first appeared in Ireland.

q.e: Potatoes were first cultivated in the Andes, by the Incas and earlier peoples, some 8,000 years ago. They reached Europe in the 1500s and became a staple in Ireland.

q: This low-carb vegetable was first seen along Atlantic coasts of Europe. Its in the same group as cauliflower, broccoli, kale, collards, kohlrabi, and Brussels sprouts.

q.e: Cabbage belongs to the Brassica family, along with broccoli, cauliflower and kale. It's low in calories and high in vitamin C and K.

q: Coq Au Vin is a typical dish for this country, and it is prepared in all its regions, though with slight changes in recipe. It is a kind of chicken stew.

q.e: Coq au vin is a French dish of chicken braised with wine, mushrooms and bacon. It's a classic of French home cooking.

q: The Shish Kabob is very popular in this country. It is often served with the traditional greens and tomato salad, tahini sauce and pita bread.

q.e: Shish kebab (grilled skewered meat) is popular across the Middle East and is a staple in Egypt, Turkey and Iran. The name comes from Turkish.

q: What soft drink brand has the same name as a Native American tribe of Northern California?

q.e: Shasta is a soft drink brand from California, named for Mount Shasta. Shasta people are a Native American group from northern California.

q: This cocktail is made of 2 oz vodka, 3 oz cranberry juice, 2 oz grapefruit juice. The ingredients are shaken with ice and then strain into a highball glass.

q.e: The Sea Breeze is a cocktail of vodka, cranberry and grapefruit juice. It's related to the Cape Codder and Bay Breeze.

q: Similarly to spinach, this fruit, called petia in Spain, contains plenty of iron.

q.e: Watermelon is mostly water (92%) and has little iron compared with spinach. It's rich in vitamin C and lycopene instead.

q: Who built the first restaurant from the McDonalds chain, one of the worlds largest chains of fast-food restaurants?

q.e: Richard and Maurice McDonald opened the first McDonald's in San Bernardino, California, in 1940. Ray Kroc joined in 1954 as a franchise agent, and later bought them out.

q: There are several renditions of the famed Long Island Iced Tea, but almost all of the recipes call for this carbonated drink.

q.e: Long Island Iced Tea includes vodka, gin, rum, tequila and triple sec, with a splash of cola. It contains no tea.

q: It is not the alcohol in wine that causes hangover. Hangover is actually caused by these.

q.e: Hangovers are caused by dehydration, the toxic by-products of alcohol breakdown (acetaldehyde), and congeners in darker drinks. It isn't just the alcohol itself.

q: The words No thing more excellent nor more valuable than wine was ever granted mankind by God belong to this Greek philosopher.

q.e: The saying is attributed to Plato, who wrote about wine in the Laws. He believed it should be consumed in moderation.

q: It is generally accepted that whiskey has been made in Ireland since Irish monks brought the distillation process from the Middle East. In Gaelic, the drink was known as Uisge Beatha, which means what in English?

q.e: Uisge beatha is a Gaelic translation of the Medieval Latin aqua vitae, which translates literally to water of life. Over centuries of English pronunciation, uisge gradually evolved into the word whiskey.

q: This green vegetable is number one on the list of foods that contain agents preventing cancer. The list contains about 30 such agents.

q.e: Broccoli is a cruciferous vegetable rich in sulforaphane, vitamin C and fiber. It's often listed among the best foods for cancer prevention, although evidence is mixed.

q: This snack food company, founded in 1906, is famous for its peanuts and the Mr. Peanut icon.

q.e: Italian immigrant Amedeo Obici co-founded the Planters Nut and Chocolate Company in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, in 1906. Mr. Peanut was created a decade later in 1916 after a 14-year-old schoolboy won a company logo contest.

q: The Juustoleipa cheese, traditionally made from reindeer milk, is typical of which region in Europe?

q.e: Juustoleipä (leipäjuusto) is a Finnish "bread cheese", traditionally from cow's or reindeer milk. It's served warm with cloudberry jam.

q: In 1536 cheese-makers in Veneto, Italy, created the oldest precedent of falsification by trying to make what cheese?

q.e: Cheese fraud has been known for centuries. Parmesan is one of the most imitated cheeses, which is why Parmigiano-Reggiano is protected.

q: What Greek cheese is made of 70% ewes and 30% goats milk?

q.e: Protected designation of origin rules require traditional Greek feta to be made with at least 70% sheep milk, with the remaining 30% or less coming from goat milk. Kasseri is another Greek sheep-milk cheese, but it is semi-hard and pale yellow.

q: Samuel Adams Triple Bock, produced by the Boston Beer Company, reaches what percentage of alcohol by volume?

q.e: Samuel Adams Triple Bock (1994) was about 17-18% ABV, a record for beer at the time. It was a strong, syrupy brew.

q: The national epic poem of which country includes an early ode to beer in Verse XX: Sing the songs of beer immortal!?

q.e: Finland's national epic, the Kalevala, includes a long poem about the origins of beer in rune 20. It was compiled by Elias Lönnrot in the 1800s.

q: This substance is a product of volcanic activity and is used as preservative in wine making.

q.e: Sulfur dioxide is a preservative in wine making. It protects wine from oxidation and bacteria.

q: This coenzyme is naturally produced by a specific algae. It is used for transforming food into energy that the body will use to perform all its activities. It is also a powerful antioxidant.

q.e: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) is made by the body and helps cells produce energy. It's an antioxidant also found in meat and fish.

q: When was Wonder Bread first marketed in the USA as pre-sliced bread?

q.e: Wonder Bread was first sold sliced in 1930 by Continental Baking Company. It was introduced in 1921.

q: This food was not on the Sopranos, but is a Taiwanese dish.

q.e: Baobing is a Taiwanese shaved-ice dessert topped with sweet ingredients such as beans, fruit and condensed milk. It's a popular summer treat.

q: This delectable chocolate dessert is named after fungi rooted out of the ground by pigs.

q.e: Chocolate truffles were named after subterranean fungi because their traditional shape, coated in cocoa powder, resembles the knobby edible truffle freshly dug from the ground.

q: What kind of cheese is one of the ingredients of the Insalata Caprese salad?

q.e: Insalata Caprese is an Italian salad of fresh mozzarella (traditionally from buffalo milk), tomato and basil. It's named after the island of Capri, and its colors match the Italian flag.

q: The Larb meat salad belongs to the cuisine of what Asian country?

q.e: Larb (laab) is a minced meat salad with lime, herbs and toasted rice powder. It's the national dish of Laos, and is also popular in northern Thailand.

q: This term refers to a kind of unfiltered beer, conditioned and served from the cask without additional pressure.

q.e: Cask ale is unfiltered, unpasteurized beer that continues to ferment in the cask and is served without added gas pressure. It's sometimes called "real ale".

q: Broccoli looks very similar to this vegetable and is often confused with it.

q.e: Broccoli and cauliflower belong to the same species, Brassica oleracea, and share very similar plant architecture aside from head color and bud density.

q: What vegetable is used for the making of the popular Portuguese and Brazilian soup called Caldo verde?

q.e: Caldo verde is a Portuguese soup made of potatoes, onion and thinly sliced kale or collard greens (couve galega), often with chouriço. It's from the Minho region.

q: What type of meal is the traditional Chinese Zha jiang mian dish?

q.e: Zhajiangmian is a Chinese noodle dish topped with a fried sauce made from ground pork and fermented soybean paste. It's associated with Beijing.

q: Bao yu, a prized ingredient used in many Chinese dishes, is what type of sea food?

q.e: Bao yu is the Chinese name for abalone, a sea snail with a prized, chewy meat. It's an expensive delicacy.

q: What do the nests of cave swifts consist of, which makes them edible and ranks them as a delicacy in Chinese cuisine?

q.e: Edible bird's nests are made from the hardened saliva of swiftlets, and used in bird's nest soup. They are among the most expensive animal products in the world.

q: In what type of leaves is Valdeon cheese traditionally wrapped before being sent to the market?

q.e: Valdeón is a Spanish blue cheese from the Picos de Europa, traditionally wrapped in sycamore or chestnut leaves. Its flavor is sharp and strong.

q: What should cows be fed on to produce the milk used for the making of Cantal cheese?

q.e: Cantal is a French cheese from Auvergne, made from the milk of cows that graze on mountain pastures and are fed hay in winter. It's one of the oldest French cheeses.

q: Zopf is a type of Swiss bread traditionally consumed on Sunday mornings. What does its name mean?

q.e: Zopf means "braid" or "plait" in German, and describes the braided shape of this Swiss bread. It is made with butter and milk and traditionally eaten on Sunday.

q: What makes the Japanese dish called Fugu unique?
It is made from poisonous fish.
It is prepared from an endangered animal.
It is prepared from tiger testicles.
It is made from the beating heart of a snake.

q.e: Fugu is prepared from pufferfish, which contain lethal amounts of tetrodotoxin in their organs. In Japan, chefs must undergo years of rigorous training and pass an examination to legally serve it.

q: Which of these is not among the traditional ingredients used for the making of the Japanese dish Nikujaga?

q.e: Nikujaga is a Japanese stew of meat (beef or pork), potatoes and onions, simmered in soy sauce and mirin. The name means "meat and potatoes".

q: What is the meaning of the Spanish word vainilla, from which the name of the spice vanilla originated?

q.e: "Vainilla" is the Spanish diminutive of "vaina", meaning "pod". Vanilla is the seed pod of an orchid native to Mexico.

q: What is the Native American drink called Asi associated with in the Native American tradition?

q.e: Asi, or the "black drink", was brewed from the leaves of the yaupon holly by Native Americans of the Southeast. It was used in purification ceremonies.

q: Why was the passion fruit given this interesting name?
Because it was considered an aphrodisiac.

q.e: The passion fruit was named by Spanish missionaries, who saw parts of the passion flower as symbols of the Passion of Christ. For example, the five stamens stood for the wounds.

q: What method of cooking is used in the preparation of the traditional Thai dish called Nuea pad prik?

q.e: Nuea pad prik is a Thai stir-fry of beef with chili peppers. Stir-frying in a wok over high heat is the common technique.

q: What unripened fruit is used for the preparation of the spicy Thai salad Som tam?

q.e: Som tam is a Thai salad made from shredded unripe green papaya, pounded with chilies, lime, fish sauce and peanuts. It comes from Isan and Laos.

q: What type of alcoholic beverage is the traditional Thai drink Sang Som?

q.e: Sang Som is a Thai rum made from sugarcane molasses and rice. It is one of Thailand's most popular spirits.

q: What is the literal meaning of the name of the dish Pad see ew, very popular in Thailand and Laos?

q.e: Pad see ew means "stir-fried with soy sauce" in Thai. It's a dish of wide rice noodles, soy sauce, egg and greens.

q: The Thai dish Khanom bueang is known under this name in the English-speaking world.

q.e: Khanom bueang are Thai crispy pancakes (crispy crepes), filled with sweet or savory toppings. They are a street food.

q: The leaves of which of these plants are most often used for the preparation of the popular Arab dish dolma, also known as sarma?

q.e: Dolma are vegetables or grape leaves stuffed with rice and meat. In Turkey and the Middle East, grape vine leaves are the most traditional wrapper.

q: What vegetable is used for the preparation of the traditional Arab dish called Baba ghanoush?

q.e: Baba ghanoush is a Levantine dip made of roasted eggplant (aubergine), tahini, lemon and garlic. It has a smoky flavor.

q: Which of these is not among the traditional ingredients used for the preparation of the Arab dish Matbucha?

q.e: Matbucha is a cooked salad of tomatoes and roasted peppers, from North Africa. It's vegetarian, so it doesn't have lamb.

q: What kind of food is Amasi, a meal very popular in South Africa?

q.e: Amasi is a fermented milk product, similar to yogurt, eaten in South Africa and Zimbabwe. It has a sour taste.

q: What kind of animal is the Gonimbrasia belina, popular food among the native inhabitants of South Africa?

q.e: Gonimbrasia belina is the emperor moth, whose caterpillar is the mopane worm, a popular source of protein in southern Africa. The worms are dried or fried.

q: How is meat processed to produce the traditional South African dish called Biltong?

q.e: Biltong is dried, cured meat from South Africa. It is made by curing strips of beef or game with vinegar and spices, then air-drying.

q: What type of jam is used for the preparation of the traditional South African dessert Malva Pudding?

q.e: Malva pudding is a sweet baked sponge dessert from South Africa, made with apricot jam and served with a hot cream sauce. It's considered a classic Cape dish.

q: What kind of food is the traditional South African meal Sosatie?

q.e: Sosaties are skewers of marinated meat from South Africa, derived from Cape Malay cuisine. The marinade often includes curry and apricot.

q: What does the very unusual dish Balut, popular in Vietnam, consist of?

q.e: Balut is a developing duck embryo boiled and eaten in the shell, popular in the Philippines and Vietnam. It's considered a high-protein street snack.

q: It is generally accepted that this drink, introduced in England by the Greek professor Servopoulos, acts as a stimulant. It invigorates the body, enhances the mental activity and fights drowsiness and fatigue.

q.e: Coffee houses opened in England in the 1650s, and coffee was seen as a stimulating drink for the mind. Caffeine is the active stimulant in coffee.

q: It is a widespread myth that vegetarians cannot provide this to their body, because it could only be supplied from meat. However, it is found in soy, beans, nuts, milk, cheese, eggs, etc.

q.e: Protein is found in many plant foods, including soy, beans, nuts and grains, so vegetarians can get enough. Eating a variety helps supply all essential amino acids.

q: This dessert was made in honor of a famous singer.

q.e: Chef Auguste Escoffier created the Peach Melba at the Savoy Hotel in London around 1892 in honor of Australian opera singer Nellie Melba. It combines peaches and raspberry sauce over vanilla ice cream.

q: Who is regarded as the first internationally recognized celebrity chef?

q.e: Marie-Antoine Carême (1784-1833) was a French chef who is considered the first celebrity chef. He cooked for royalty and is known as the "king of chefs and chef of kings".

q: By law German beer can only be made from these four ingredients:
Water, hops, malted wheat, carbon dioxide

q.e: Originally adopted in Bavaria in 1516, the Reinheitsgebot (German Beer Purity Law) originally specified only water, barley, and hops, with yeast later included once fermentation was understood.

q: What kind of alcohol is used for the preparation of the Bacardi cocktail?

q.e: The Bacardi cocktail is made with Bacardi rum, lime juice and grenadine. It's like a daiquiri with grenadine.

q: A wedge of what fruit is traditionally used as a garnish of the Cuba Libre cocktail?

q.e: The Cuba Libre is rum and cola served with a wedge of lime. The name means "Free Cuba".

q: What popular cocktail is made simply by mixing vodka and orange juice?

q.e: According to popular lore, American petroleum workers in the Persian Gulf discreetly mixed vodka into their orange juice and stirred it using screwdrivers.

q: The dewberry is closely related to this other berry fruit.

q.e: Dewberries are Rubus species closely related to blackberries, but they trail along the ground. Their fruit is similar but ripens earlier.

q: How is the traditional Jamaican bread called Bammy prepared?

q.e: Bammy is a Jamaican flatbread made from cassava, which is traditionally fried (or baked). It originated with the Arawak people.

q: What vegetable is used for the preparation of the Passion Cake, which probably originated in the United Kingdom?

q.e: Passion cake is a British carrot cake, often with a cream cheese frosting. Despite the name, it has no passion fruit.

q: What cocktail is made with vodka, triple sec, cranberry juice and lime juice?

q.e: The Cosmopolitan is a cocktail of vodka, triple sec, cranberry juice and lime juice. It became popular in the 1990s, partly thanks to Sex and the City.

q: What Roman Emperor, who ruled from 54 to 68, ordered ice to be brought from the mountains and combined it with fruit toppings?

q.e: The Roman emperor Nero (reigned 54-68) is said to have had snow brought from the mountains and flavored with fruit and honey. Accounts of this come from ancient writers.

q: Which of these popular types of cheese is not blue?

q.e: Gouda is a Dutch cheese, usually yellow, made from cow's milk. It is not a blue cheese like Roquefort and Gorgonzola.

q: Which spice is from the mint family?

q.e: Oregano is in the mint family (Lamiaceae), along with basil, thyme, rosemary and sage. Many herbs are from this family.

q: How did Jason Voorhees, the son of a camp cook-turned-murderer, die in the slasher movie Friday the 13th?
He was decapitated with a machete
He was stabbed with a knife.

q.e: In the Friday the 13th films, Jason Voorhees drowned as a child at Camp Crystal Lake, and his mother, Pamela, was the first killer. It's fiction.

q: The meringue dessert Pavlova is named after the famous Russian Anna Pavlova. What was Pavlovas occupation?

q.e: Anna Pavlova was a legendary Russian prima ballerina of the Imperial Russian Ballet. The meringue dessert was created in her honor during her 1920s tour of Australia and New Zealand.

q: This type of fruit gets its name from the name of an Australian fruit breeder.

q.e: Maria Ann Smith discovered the green seedling growing near a creek on her orchard in Eastwood, New South Wales, around 1868. Known locally as 'Granny' Smith, she propagated the tart, long-keeping variety that now bears her name.

q: How did the Wyandot peoples of North America mainly provide food for themselves?

q.e: The Wyandot (Huron) were farmers who grew corn, beans and squash, known as the "Three Sisters". They also hunted and fished.

q: This country has the highest number of breweries in the world, and beer plays a significant part of its culture. Among the numerous famous brands it produces are Krombacher, Warsteiner and Bitburger.

q.e: Germany has more breweries than any other country, with about 1,500. The Reinheitsgebot purity law dates back to 1516.

q: Efes Beverage Group, founded in 1969 and named after an ancient city, is the major beer producer in this country.

q.e: Efes is a Turkish brewery named after the ancient city of Ephesus. It was founded in 1969 and is one of Turkey's biggest beer makers.

q: Known as the worlds most finicky cat, he became the spokes-cat for Purinas 9 Lives cat food in 1969.

q.e: Morris the Cat has been the face of 9Lives since 1969. The original Morris was a rescued orange tabby.

q: If you have this health condition and drink coffee regularly, you will have about 30% fewer symptoms than non-coffee drinkers.

q.e: Some studies suggest caffeine has mild bronchodilating effects, so it may help asthma symptoms a little. It is not a replacement for medication.

q: People with these illnesses are not advised to drink coffee.

q.e: People with certain conditions, such as anxiety disorders or sleep problems, may be advised to limit caffeine. Check with your doctor.

q: For this cocktail you just need 1 1/4 oz. Cognac and 3/4 oz. Amaretto. Pour them over ice into a snifter and snifter.

q.e: The French Connection is a cocktail of cognac and amaretto, served over ice. It's named for the 1971 film.

q: Which part of Israel is famous fro producing wine?

q.e: The Golan Heights is a major wine-producing region in Israel because of its high elevation and volcanic soil. The Galilee is another.

q: Which of the following fast food meals has the most calories?
Subways 12 inch Double Meat Classic Tuna Sub on white
McDonalds Chicken Selects Premium Breast Strips (10 pc)

q.e: Fast-food sandwiches can be high in calories, particularly "double meat" footlongs with mayonnaise. Portion size matters.

q: All of the following foods contain cholesterol EXCEPT this food.

q.e: Cholesterol is found only in animal products, such as meat, eggs and dairy. Plant foods, such as okra, contain none, even if fried in vegetable oil.

q: This food is rich in omega – 3 fatty acids, magnesium and potassium.

q.e: Oatmeal is a good source of fiber, magnesium, potassium and some omega-3s. Its soluble fiber (beta-glucan) can lower cholesterol.
Saffron has been studied for mild to moderate depression, with some trials suggesting it helps. More research is needed.

q: Which of these is a major problem concerning nutrition value of food, served at restaurants?
Foods lacking whole grains and fibers

q.e: Oversized portions at restaurants are a major issue, adding calories. Many meals contain more than a day's worth of sodium.

q: Which of these is used to indicate the medication should be taken with food?

q.e: On prescriptions, "p.c." means "post cibum" (after meals) and "c.c." means "cum cibo" (with food). These are Latin abbreviations.

q: If you mix milk, eggs and sugar youll get this Christmas drink.

q.e: Traditional eggnog is made by blending milk, cream, sugar, and whipped eggs, often spiked with rum, bourbon, or brandy. Advocaat is a thicker Dutch liqueur traditionally made with egg yolks, sugar, and brandy without added milk.

q: Russians have another strange tradition for men. They get together and prepare a bottle of vodka for every three men. Then they drink until this happens.

q.e: In Russia, the tradition is to drink until someone falls. The saying "drinking for three" reflects the custom of sharing a bottle among three people.

q: Which of these is the biggest retail wine store in the USA?
Sams Wine and Spirits of Chicago
The New Yorker Wine and Liquor Pavillion

q.e: Sam's Wine & Spirits in Chicago is among the biggest wine retailers in the US. It's located on North Avenue.

q: The two buildings of Marina City, one of the first complexes referred to as the city within a city, are often compared to this food item.

q.e: Marina City in Chicago, designed by Bertrand Goldberg and completed in 1964, has twin towers that look like corncobs. They are on the Chicago River.

q: Which alcoholic beverage is one of the main ingredients in the Sea Breeze cocktail?

q.e: The Sea Breeze contains vodka, cranberry juice and grapefruit juice. It's sometimes made with gin instead.

q: One of the nicknames of the U.S. state of Georgia is derived from the name of this fruit.

q.e: Georgia is nicknamed the Peach State, because of its famous peaches. In fact, California grows more peaches.

q: Yorkshire pudding, a dish that originated in Yorkshire, England, is usually served with which of the following?

q.e: Yorkshire pudding is a baked batter that is eaten with roast beef and gravy in England. It's eaten as part of a Sunday roast.

q: What is the national fruit of India?

q.e: The mango, scientifically named Mangifera indica, has been cultivated in India for over 4,000 years and is revered as the king of fruits. It is also the national fruit of Pakistan and the Philippines.

q: What type of syrup is used for the preparation of the sweet Indian drink called Falooda?

q.e: Falooda is an Indian dessert drink of rose syrup, milk, vermicelli, basil seeds and ice cream. It came from Persia.

q: What type of food is the Filipino meal Halo-halo, also very popular on the island of Hawaii?

q.e: Halo-halo is a Filipino dessert, with shaved ice, sweet beans, fruit, jelly, milk and ice cream. The name means "mix-mix".

q: The juice of what fruit is used in the preparation of the very popular cocktail Blue Hawaii?

q.e: Blue Hawaii contains rum, vodka, blue curaçao, pineapple juice and sweet and sour mix. It was created at the Hilton Hawaiian Village in 1957.

q: What is the official state fruit of the U.S. state of Oregon?

q.e: The pear is Oregon's official state fruit. Oregon is known for the Pacific Northwest's pear orchards, such as in the Rogue Valley.

q: What is the official state snack food of the U.S. state of Illinois?

q.e: Popcorn is the official state snack food of Illinois, which is a major popcorn producer. The state made it official in 2003.

q: Which spice gives curry its yellow color?

q.e: Turmeric gets its vivid yellow-orange hue from the chemical compound curcumin, and it serves as both a primary coloring agent and key flavoring ingredient in standard curry powders.

q: Which pasta is shaped like little bow ties?

q.e: Farfalle is commonly known as bow-tie pasta or butterfly pasta because its name comes from the Italian word for butterflies.

q: Which woman's name can follow "chocolate" or precede "russe" in a dessert's name?

q.e: Charlotte is a dessert of custard or mousse in a mold lined with ladyfingers. A charlotte russe is made with Bavarian cream.

q: In 1997 a cocktail of cocaine and alcohol stimulated the narcotic frenzy of this actor. He bit a man, and tried to get a police officers gun. By that time he was already known as a person having drug and alcohol problems.

q.e: Christian Slater's 1997 incident involved an altercation while intoxicated. He was later sentenced and recovered.

q: What former New York Yankee has an older sister who is a famous food critic and cookbook writer?

q.e: Paul O'Neill, the Yankees right fielder, has a sister, Molly O'Neill, who was a New York Times food columnist. She's also an author of cookbooks.

q: Finish these lyrics from a song by Jimmy Buffett: Drink it up This ones for you Its been a lovely cruise Im sorry its ended Its sad but its true Honey its been .................

q.e: This is from Jimmy Buffett's song "A Lovely Cruise", and the line finishes with "a lovely cruise". Buffett is famous for his island lifestyle songs.

q: Which characters drink tea together with the March Hare at the neverending tea party in Alices Adventures in Wonderland?
The Dormouse and the Mad Hatter
The Duchess and the Mad Hatter

q.e: In Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, the March Hare, the Mad Hatter and the Dormouse have a never-ending tea party. It's always six o'clock for them.

q: If I mix the following ingredients together, what drink would I have? 1/2 fluid ounce vodka, 1/2 fluid ounce cointreau, 1 teaspoon fresh lime juice, 1 1/2 fluid ounces cranberry juice, 1 twist lime zest, garnish

q.e: A Cosmopolitan is made of vodka, Cointreau, cranberry juice and lime. It is served in a martini glass.

q: Which statement about fast food restaurants in the USA is not true?
The first Ben and Jerrys was opened on the campus of Dartmouth University.
The first Burger King was opened in Miami.
The first Wendys was opened in Columbus, Ohio.
The first KFC was opened in Salt Lake City.

q.e: Ben & Jerry's was founded in 1978 in Burlington, Vermont, in a converted gas station. It wasn't started at Dartmouth.

q: I ran to my room and my daughter brought me a bowl of vegetable soup, but I couldnt eat it due to my phagophobia. What was I afraid of?

q.e: Phagophobia is the fear of swallowing. It can be linked to a fear of choking.

q: This country is a democratic, parliamentary republic that has over 1500 islands, 700 rivers and streams, and 1000 lakes. During the winter, the shortest day is only 6 hours long. Smoked trout is a typical food there.

q.e: Estonia is a parliamentary republic on the Baltic Sea with over 1,500 islands. Its winter days are very short.

q: What is the name of the second most important vegetable fibre after cotton that is woven to make coarse cloth and sacks?

q.e: Jute is a plant fiber grown mainly in India and Bangladesh. It's used for burlap sacks and rope, and is the second most important vegetable fiber after cotton.

q: Its your first day on the job at your favorite diner! The waitress next to you yells out to the short order cook that she needs two cows, make them cry, and paint em red. What has she requested the short order cook to prepare?
Two hamburgers with onions, cover in ketchup
Two orders of beef liver and onions with ketchup
Double cheeseburger, no onions, special sauce

q.e: Diner lingo: "cry" means onions, and "paint it red" refers to ketchup. So the order is two hamburgers with onions and ketchup.

q: This very nutritious and rich in proteins seafood is stated to be the favourite one of Casanova. He was famous as one of the worlds greatest lovers and an ardent connoisseur of this food, which was always on his menu.

q.e: Casanova was said to eat dozens of oysters a day. Oysters have long been linked with romance because of their zinc content.

q: This is another sign ruled by Venus. The people under this zodiac sign are really material. Good food, good clothing and furniture, good sex can really make them feel wonderful. They are possessive, but are calm and have great inner peace.

q.e: Taurus is an earth sign ruled by Venus, associated with comfort, luxury and stability. These traits are astrological, not scientific.

q: This fresh, green vegetable comes from India, where people have been growing it for 3000 years. Although we regard it as a vegetable, it is actually a fruit and reproduces by seeds.

q.e: Cucumbers originated in India, where they were grown for around 3,000 years. Botanically, they are fruits.

q: According to historians this indigo-colored vegetable originates from India. However, there are some written accounts from the 5th century in China, which indicate its cultivation there as well.

q.e: Eggplant (aubergine) originated in India and was cultivated in China by the 5th century. Eggplants are in the nightshade family.

q: With a Latin name of Capsicum, this American vegetable has been known to the western hemisphere for a very long time. According to experts there is evidence it has been consumed since 7500 BC.

q.e: Chili peppers (Capsicum) originated in the Americas, and were eaten at least 7,500 years ago. Columbus took them to Europe.

q: This orange vegetable was first discovered in Afghanistan 5000 years ago. Paintings were found on the walls of temples in Egypt, where it is believed to have been used for treatment of diseases.

q.e: Carrots originated in Afghanistan, and were purple or yellow at first. The orange carrot was developed in the Netherlands in the 1600s.

q: This veggie comes from Mexico. It was later spread all over North America and from there, setters took it to Europe. Nowadays besides food, it is used in the manufacture of oils, paints, soaps, syrups, starches, and even for fuel.

q.e: Corn (maize) was domesticated in Mexico about 9,000 years ago. It's used for food, fuel and many products.

q: This member of the cabbage family was admitted to European and American cuisine in the beginning of the 20th century. However, it was very common in the Roman Empire and was first cultivated on the territory of present day Turkey

q.e: Broccoli was cultivated by the Romans and Etruscans in Italy. It became popular in the US in the 1920s.

q: This is a vegetable with no homeland, dispersed all over the world. In Egypt, it was worshipped for its spherical shape and concentric rings, believed to be symbols of eternity.

q.e: Onions are among the oldest cultivated vegetables. The ancient Egyptians saw their concentric layers as a symbol of eternal life.

q: This cocktail is prepared from 1 1/2 oz. dark rum, 1/2 oz. each: Orange Curacao and creme de noyaux, lime juice, dash of grenadine. You shake the ingredients with ice and serve in a Hurricane or decorative glass.

q.e: A classic Mai Tai has rum, orange curaçao, orgeat (almond syrup) and lime. Crème de noyaux is an almond-flavored liqueur used in some variations.

q: This summer cocktail requires 1 1/2 oz. vodka, 1/2 oz. lime juice, 1/2 oz. triple sec, 6 frozen watermelon cubes, 1/2 shaker of ice, 1/2 oz. chambord. The ingredients are placed into a shaker and mixed very well.

q.e: The Watermelon Martini is a summer cocktail of vodka, watermelon, lime and Chambord. It's served in a martini glass.

q: If you want to prepare this cocktail, you will need 3 oz pineapple juice, 3 oz orange juice, 3 oz lime juice, 8 dashes Angostura bitters, 6 oz rum and 2 oz simple syrup. Mix the ingredients in a shaker with ice.

q.e: A rum punch follows the rhyme "one of sour, two of sweet, three of strong, four of weak". It's a Caribbean party drink.

q: This is a type of punch. In a big bowl pour the following ingredients: 1 bottle red wine, shotglass of lime juice, 2 shots Bacardi and add random fruit. Chill the mixture overnight.

q.e: Sangria is a traditional Spanish punch that traditionally combines red wine, chopped fruit, and often a splash of spirits such as brandy. The other choices are individual mixed drinks: a Greyhound uses gin or vodka with grapefruit juice, while a Godfather mixes Scotch whisky and amaretto.

q: You just need 1 oz white creme de cacao and 1 oz white creme de menthe for this cocktail. They are poured over ice in an old fashioned glass.

q.e: The Peppermint Pattie cocktail combines white crème de cacao and white crème de menthe. It tastes like the chocolate mint candy.

q: This cocktail is a sweet combination of 4 oz. vodka, 2 oz. Midori and some Sprite mixed with ice.

q.e: The Midori Dream is a sweet cocktail made with vodka, Midori melon liqueur and lemon-lime soda. Midori was introduced in the 1970s.

q: This flowering plant, native to the eastern Mediterranean region and southwest Asia, is used as a spice in different liqueurs like raki and ouzo.

q.e: Anise has a licorice flavor and is used in liqueurs like ouzo, raki, sambuca and pastis. When mixed with water, these drinks turn cloudy.

q: Mace is one of the spices, derived from the fruit of this evergreen tree, indigenous to tropical southeast Asia and Australasia.

q.e: Both nutmeg and mace come from the Myristica fragrans tree; nutmeg is the inner seed, while mace is the reddish, lacy outer covering, or aril, surrounding it.

q: This dish is usually cooked in a large, flat pan. It is most typical for the region of Valencia, Spain and contains ingredients such as rice, saffron and olive oil.

q.e: Paella originated among agricultural workers in the Albufera lagoon area of Valencia. The traditional Valencian recipe features short-grain bomba rice, saffron, green beans, and rabbit or chicken rather than seafood.

q: Which of these dishes is a traditional Mexican dish, prepared out of a tortilla dipped in a sauce, containing peppers?

q.e: The word enchilada comes from the Spanish verb enchilar, meaning to season with chili. Polenta and baccala are Italian dishes, while jambalaya is a rice dish from Louisiana.

q: This Hungarian dish, meaning cowherd, is prepared with beef, onion, red peppers and paprika.

q.e: Goulash comes from the Hungarian word 'gulyás', which refers to a herdsman, as the stew was historically prepared by Hungarian cattle herders over open fires.

q: This Romanian dish, widely known around the world under the Italian name of polenta, is traditionally prepared of maize, cooked in an iron pot.

q.e: Mămăligă is a Romanian cornmeal porridge, similar to Italian polenta. It's traditionally cooked in a cast iron pot.

q: This delicacy, typical for 'The Country of the Rising Sun', usually only consists of thinly sliced raw seafood, dipping sauce and garnish.

q.e: Sashimi consists of fresh raw fish or meat sliced into bite-sized pieces and typically served with soy sauce and wasabi. It is distinct from sushi, which specifically requires seasoned vinegared rice.

q: Which of these is a French dish, whose main ingredients are veal, onions and mushrooms?

q.e: Blanquette de veau is a French dish of veal stew in a white sauce, with onions and mushrooms. The name means "white".

q: For its ability to reduce anxiety and tension, wine is considered to be this.

q.e: Wine is sometimes called a natural tranquilizer because alcohol is a depressant, and can relax people. Heavy drinking has the opposite effect, and it's not a treatment for anxiety.

q: Another research used mice to reveal that red wine can slow down the development of cancer cells and increase life expectancy of rodents. Researchers attribute this to the anti-oxidizing properties of these agents.

q.e: Red wine contains polyphenols, such as resveratrol, which are antioxidants. Mouse studies show effects, but it hasn't been confirmed in humans.

q: Famous also as Chinese gooseberry, this fruit is the richest in vitamins and minerals. However, it should not be served with dairy products, as its enzyme actinidin will start dissolving the milk proteins and leave a bitter taste in your mouth.

q.e: Originally called the Chinese gooseberry, the kiwifruit contains the protease enzyme actinidin, which breaks down milk proteins like casein into bitter-tasting peptides.

q: One of Wolfgang Pucks food handlers tested positive for Hepatitis A. What was the event Puck was catering that possibly exposed hundreds of people to Hepatitis.
Sports Illustrated annual swimsuit issue party
Playboys Playmate of the Year celebration

q.e: Hepatitis A spreads through contaminated food, often from an infected food handler who doesn't wash their hands. Vaccination can protect against it.

q: In 1666 the first legal document to mention cheese was issued in Toulouse and it referred to what sort of cheese?

q.e: Roquefort was the first cheese to receive appellation of origin protection in France, in 1925. It's aged in caves in Roquefort-sur-Soulzon.

q: In 1953, several European countries ratified this convention to protect some sorts of cheese from conterfeiting.

q.e: The Stresa Convention (1951) on the use of cheese names, signed by several European countries, protected names like Gorgonzola and Roquefort. It was an early example of protecting regional foods.

q: The first TV commercial for cheese was aired in 1968 for which sort of French cheese?

q.e: Boursin was famous for a 1968 French TV ad with the slogan "Du pain, du vin, du Boursin". The garlic and herb cheese was created in 1957.

q: Mascarpone is a vegetarian Italian cheese, traditionally included in the recipe for what layered dessert?

q.e: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert made by layering ladyfingers dipped in coffee with a whipped mixture of mascarpone cheese, eggs, and sugar, topped with cocoa powder. Its name translates to 'pick me up' in Italian.

q: What do you call an Austrian dessert that is a sweet almond paste dipped in chocolate?

q.e: Marzipan is a paste of almonds and sugar, popular in Austria and Germany. Mozartkugel are Austrian chocolate balls with pistachio marzipan.

q: This is a traditional dish in Austria and Germany made of a thin peace of veal meat coated with flour, egg and bread crumb.

q.e: Wiener Schnitzel is protected under Austrian and German law, requiring genuine Wiener Schnitzel to be made specifically from veal, while pork versions must be labeled 'Wiener Art' (Viennese style).

q: Which word refers to the water soluble pigments that give wine its red color?

q.e: Anthocyanins are water-soluble pigments that give red wine, red cabbage and berries their colors. They are also antioxidants.

q: Used to measure the concentration of sugar in wine, this scale was developed by a French pharmacist.

q.e: The Baumé scale, created by French pharmacist Antoine Baumé in 1768, measures the density of liquids, including sugar in grape juice. It's still used in winemaking in Europe.

q: What science studies all aspects of wine and wine making?

q.e: Oenology covers the science of winemaking and fermentation. Oology, which sounds similar, is the study of bird eggs.

q: This is a protein complex produced by the bacterium, Clostridium botulinum. It contains a toxin that causes food poisoning. However, when injected in small doses it smoothens existing lines and wrinkles.

q.e: Botox is a purified form of botulinum toxin, which is made by Clostridium botulinum. In tiny doses, it temporarily relaxes muscles and reduces wrinkles.

q: Sugar on snow is a popular New England treat. It is boiled maple syrup cooled in snow and placed on sticks. Which food item is not traditionally served with this candy?

q.e: Sugar on snow, made with hot maple syrup poured on snow, is served with plain donuts and sour pickles. Shortbread is not typical.

q: This is a Japanese dish made from thinly sliced, pickled ginger which is kept in a solution of sugar and water.

q.e: Gari is sweet pickled ginger served with sushi. It's eaten between pieces to cleanse the palate.

q: Which of these is a traditional Japanese breakfast dish?

q.e: Natto, fermented soybeans, is a traditional Japanese breakfast food. It has a strong smell and a sticky texture.

q: In Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, Uruguay, and Venezuela, where Italian cuisine is especially popular, there is a custom to eat this traditional Italian pasta on the 29th day of each month.

q.e: In Argentina and other South American countries, people eat gnocchi on the 29th of the month ("ñoquis del 29"). They put money under the plate for luck.

q: These are rectangular pasta sheets rolled with a savory stuffing and then covered with a sauce.

q.e: Cannelloni are large tubes or rolled sheets of pasta stuffed with filling and baked in sauce. The name means "large reeds".

q: Malt, one of the main ingredients of beer, undergoes a process in which the grain kernels are crushed and later the smaller pieces are separated from the husk. What is the name of the resulting product?

q.e: Grist is the crushed malted grain that is mixed with water to make wort in brewing. The husks form a filter bed.

q: This kind of beer, produced from wild yeast through a process called spontaneous fermentation, has a distinctive, cidery flavour with slightly sour aftertaste.

q.e: Lambic is a Belgian beer made through spontaneous fermentation by wild yeast and bacteria. It's made in the Senne valley, near Brussels.

q: In 1953, this New Zealander developed the technique of continuous fermentation, which is applied in the production of the famous beer brand Guinness.

q.e: Morton Coutts, a New Zealander, developed continuous fermentation for beer in the 1950s at Dominion Breweries. The method was applied in several breweries.

q: This type of Belgian beer contains alcohol by volume, ranging between 8 an 11 percent. A commercial example for this kind of beer is Unibroue la Fin du Monde.

q.e: Tripel is a strong golden Belgian-style ale of 7-10% ABV. La Fin du Monde is a tripel made by Unibroue in Quebec.

q: This is a drinking game played with 1 oz shots of beer and cards. The player must guess the rank that was dealt to another players card. At the end, one of the players has to drink many beer shots.

q.e: Hi-Lo is a drinking game with cards, where players guess if a card is higher or lower. Drinking games carry risks of excessive alcohol consumption.

q: Which of the following brands of beer is not German and is manufactured in an Asian country?

q.e: Kirin is a Japanese beer brand, as are Asahi and Sapporo. German beers include Beck's, Warsteiner and Paulaner.

q: Crepe is the name of a thin French pancake. What is the meaning of the Latin word crispa from which the name of the dish originated?

q.e: "Crêpe" comes from the Latin "crispa", meaning "curled". It describes the crinkled texture of the thin pancake.

q: What type of milk is used for the preparation of the Manchego cheese?

q.e: Authentic Manchego is a Spanish cheese protected under PDO rules, requiring it to be produced exclusively from whole milk of Manchega sheep in the La Mancha region.

q: Hummus is a popular meal in the Arab world and especially in the Middle East. What does the name of the dish mean?

q.e: "Hummus" means "chickpeas" in Arabic. The dish is chickpeas blended with tahini, lemon and garlic.

q: What animal part is used for the preparation of the traditional South African dish called Mala Mogodu?

q.e: Mogodu (tripe) is the stomach lining of cattle, and Mala Mogodu is a dish that is popular in South Africa. It's often served with pap.

q: To make this dish you would: leave your cheese outside covered with loose cheesecloth, allow flies to lay their eggs inside the cheese, the maggots will hatch and then spread it on toast. Enjoy!

q.e: Casu marzu is a Sardinian cheese that contains live insect larvae. It is illegal to sell in the EU, because of health concerns.

q: This dish of fresh squid is eaten alive and raw, even at the moment of swallowing it.

q.e: Ika sashimi is a Japanese dish of raw squid, and in some versions it's served while still moving. The movement is caused by nerve reactions to soy sauce.

q: This dish is prepared in Norway. Its name means cod soaked in plutonium. It is dried whitefish soaked in lye, a strong solution of sodium or potassium hydroxide.

q.e: Lutefisk is a Nordic dish of dried cod soaked in lye, then rinsed and cooked. It's a Christmas tradition in Norway and in Midwestern American communities.

q: Which of the the following is not a step in the brewing of beer?

q.e: Steeping is a step in malting, where barley is soaked in water, not in brewing. Brewing involves mashing, lautering, boiling and fermenting.

q: This cocktail was reportedly the first drink the American astronauts had when they returned to Earth in 1969.

q.e: In July 1969, the Apollo 11 astronauts returned from the Moon and were placed in quarantine. Many drinks have been named after the moon landing.

q: What Mexican dish is made with ground seasoned meat, packed in cornmeal dough, wrapped in corn husks and then steamed?

q.e: Tamales are made from a corn-based dough called masa, filled with seasoned meats or vegetables, wrapped in corn husks or banana leaves, and steamed until cooked.

q: Which of the following is not a French cheese?

q.e: Emmental is a Swiss cheese, with holes, not French. French cheeses include Brie, Camembert and Roquefort.

q: She wrote Mastering the Art of French Cooking in 1961 and had a television program entitled the The French Chef.

q.e: Julia Child co-wrote Mastering the Art of French Cooking (1961) with Simone Beck and Louisette Bertholle. Her TV show The French Chef premiered in 1963.

q: This person works with machines used to coat popcorn or other products with melted cheese.

q.e: In food production, specialized operators coat snacks such as popcorn with cheese using sprayers and tumbling drums. Cheese popcorn is a classic.

q: In 1519, in search of the Spice Islands, Portuguese navigator Ferdinand Magellan set out on an expedition with 241 men on five ships, called Concepción, San Antonio,Trinidad, Victoria and what else?

q.e: Magellan's fleet had five ships: Trinidad, San Antonio, Concepción, Victoria and Santiago. Only the Victoria completed the circumnavigation, in 1522.

q: Who does this quote belong to: Part of the secret of success in life is to eat what you like and let the food fight it out inside.?

q.e: This quote is attributed to Mark Twain. He was known for his humor.

q: Which cereal mascot said Trix has the fruit taste I like, theres orange and lemon in every bite.?

q.e: The Trix Rabbit is the mascot of Trix cereal and he always fails to get any. His slogan is "Silly rabbit, Trix are for kids!".

q: What was the mascot for Orange Julius, a franchise marketing a drink which was a blend of a dairy creamer and oranges, in the 1970s until Arizona State University threatened a lawsuit for stealing their mascot?
A Native American with a tomahawk

q.e: Orange Julius is a drink franchise founded in 1926 in Los Angeles, which blends orange juice with a creamy mix. It has been owned by Dairy Queen since 1987.

q: Who had a #1 hit in 1988 with the massive single Dont Worry, Be Happy, featured in the movie Cocktail?

q.e: Bobby McFerrin's "Don't Worry, Be Happy" reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1988, and won Grammy Awards. It was in the movie Cocktail.

q: This beer brand, which is a German language adjective for something from the city of České Budějoviceis, is often advertised as the King of Beers'.

q.e: Budweiser means "from Budweis" in German, the old name of České Budějovice. Anheuser-Busch's slogan is "King of Beers".

q: One of the most famous events in Munich, Germany is this two-week annual festival. It begins with a keg of beer tapped by the Mayor of Munich.

q.e: Oktoberfest originated in October 1810 to celebrate the wedding of Bavarian Crown Prince Ludwig to Princess Therese of Saxe-Hildburghausen. Today, the festival begins in Munich when the mayor taps the first keg and proclaims 'O'zapft is!' ('It is tapped!').

q: Name the phase in beer brewing in which the malted grains are crushed and soaked in warm water, as a result of which, enzymes turn starches into fermentable sugars.

q.e: Mashing is the brewing step where crushed malted grains are steeped in hot water. Enzymes convert starches to fermentable sugars.

q: This Michael acts and finished Culinary School of America while working as a chef before becoming a model. He also appeared in Japanese commercials.

q.e: Michael Paré studied at the Culinary Institute of America and worked as a chef before modeling and acting. He starred in Eddie and the Cruisers.

q: This cooking term refers to the process of gently simmering food in liquid, generally water, stock or wine.

q.e: Poaching involves submerging ingredients in liquid kept at relatively low temperatures, typically between 160 and 180 degrees Fahrenheit (70 to 82 degrees Celsius). Steaming cooks food purely via steam vapors above boiling liquid, whereas blanching involves brief submersion in boiling water.

q: This mixture of wheat flour and fat, cooked by stirring over heat, is the basis of Sauce béchamel, Sauce velouté, and Sauce Espagnole.

q.e: A roux is prepared by cooking equal parts by weight of flour and fat, usually butter, to eliminate the raw flour taste before adding liquid. It serves as the primary thickening agent for three of the French classical 'mother sauces': béchamel, velouté, and espagnole.

q: This is a cooking technique, generally done in a wok, but also possible in a frying pan; the food is tossed about in a hot pan with very little oil, in a process not unlike sauteing.

q.e: Originating in ancient China, stir-frying involves cooking bite-sized ingredients rapidly in a small amount of very hot oil while stirring or tossing continuously to preserve crispness and nutrients.

q: The cooking technique, whereby meats or vegetables are soaked in a flavoring liquid, such as soy sauce, wine, oil, or vinegar, is known as what?

q.e: Marinating uses acidic liquids like vinegar or citrus juice, or enzymatic ingredients like pineapple, to tenderize and infuse flavor into foods before cooking.

q: This famous dog is known as a party animal. He first appeared on the TV screen water skiing, laughing and skateboarding in a 1987 Bud Light beer commercial.

q.e: Spuds MacKenzie was the "party animal" mascot for Bud Light, a bull terrier, in the late 1980s. The campaign was dropped in 1989.

q: Take 2 oz. Gin or Vodka and splash a dash of Dry Vermouth. Mix the ingredients and stir with ice. Then strain into a chilled cocktail glass and garnish with skewered cocktail onions.

q.e: A Gibson is a martini garnished with a cocktail onion rather than an olive. Gin or vodka is used.

q: If you mostly drink soft drinks and no milk, your chances of getting this are increased.

q.e: Drinking a lot of soft drinks instead of milk may lower calcium intake, which can raise the risk of osteoporosis. The phosphoric acid in colas is also linked.

q: The circled-U symbol found on the labels of certain products shows that the Union of Orthodox Congregations have found the food is kosher. What was the first food product to have this symbol?

q.e: The OU symbol, from the Orthodox Union, was introduced in the 1920s. Its first use was on Heinz products.

q: The baobab, a genus of trees typical for arid areas, is known to be used by Indigenous Australians as a source of water, food and medical remedy. In the 1890s however, a large, hollow baobab located near Derby, Western Australia was adapted for what usage?

q.e: The Derby Prison Boab Tree in Western Australia is a hollow baobab (boab) tree, which was used to hold prisoners in the 1890s. It is now a tourist attraction.

q: Which of the following fast food items provides the consumer with the greatest amount of calories from fat?
Hardees 1/3 LB Mushroom and Swiss Thickburger

q.e: Calories from fat vary widely in fast food, with sauces and cheese adding a lot. Check nutrition information.

q: The group of nutrients at the base of the Food Pyramid contains breads, grains, cereals, and pastas, so these foods should predominate in our diet. Which of these represents one serving from this group?

q.e: The old USDA Food Pyramid put grains at the base, and a serving was one slice of bread or half a cup of cooked cereal. It was replaced by MyPlate in 2011.

q: When the white part of the egg is aerate or whipped to a light, fluffy consistency known as soft peaks and stiff peaks what sort of dessert or topping do you have?

q.e: Meringue is made by whipping egg whites with sugar, trapping air bubbles to create a stable foam used on pies or baked into light cookies.

q: Which of the following is not considered a Mexican dish?

q.e: Mofongo is a Puerto Rican dish made of fried plantains, not Mexican. Mexican dishes include tacos and enchiladas.

q: What root vegetable was carved and placed in windows to ward off evil spirits in traditional Celtic Halloween festivals?

q.e: In Ireland and Scotland, people carved turnips into lanterns for Halloween. The tradition moved to the US, where pumpkins were used.

q: The #1 fictional company on the Forbes List is called CHOAM. Headquartered on Planet Kaitain, they are a leading manufacturer of the spice melange drug. What movie is this drug featured in?

q.e: CHOAM is the intergalactic trading company in Frank Herbert's Dune. The spice melange is an important substance in the story.

q: What was the name of the Native American who assisted the Pilgrims by teaching them techniques to increase food production?

q.e: Squanto, a Patuxet man who spoke English after living in England, showed the Plymouth colonists how to cultivate corn by burying fish alongside the seeds as fertilizer.

q: An old Irish Halloween tradition was to serve a dish called 'colcannon' with prizes hidden in it. What are the main ingredients of this traditional Irish dish?

q.e: Colcannon is a traditional Irish dish of mashed potatoes with kale or cabbage, eaten at Halloween. Rings or coins were hidden in it as fortune-telling charms.

q: Which part of a chili pepper holds most of the heat?

q.e: The heat in chili peppers comes from capsaicin, which is concentrated in the white ribs and membrane (placenta). The seeds are only spicy because they touch it.

q: Which fruit is called the "king of fruits" in Southeast Asia?

q.e: Durian is widely celebrated across Southeast Asia as the 'king of fruits' due to its large size, thorny husk, and famously pungent aroma. The mangosteen is often affectionately referred to as the 'queen of fruits'.

q: Kimchi is a fermented dish from which country?

q.e: Kimchi is a traditional Korean side dish made of salted and fermented vegetables, most commonly napa cabbage and Korean radishes, seasoned with chili powder, garlic, and ginger.

q: Which Italian word for "angry" names a spicy pasta sauce?

q.e: Arrabbiata translates directly to 'angry' in Italian, a reference to the burning heat from the crushed red chili peppers cooked into its garlic and tomato sauce.

q: Moselle wines come from which country?

q.e: Moselle (Mosel) wines come from the Mosel River valley in Germany, famous for Riesling. The river also runs through France and Luxembourg.

q: Which fermented honey-and-water drink was a favorite of Thor?

q.e: Mead is produced by fermenting honey diluted with water and is widely featured in Norse mythology as the drink of gods and warriors in Valhalla.

q: In the e-mail secret recipes, Strong Bad claims he has a secret family recipe for cooking which of the following?

q.e: Strong Bad is a character in Homestar Runner, a Flash cartoon series. His "secret recipes" are comedic.

q: Hes quite the chef but if he asks you to bring a nice Chianti to his little dinner party, better stay home. He is incredibly lethal and totally amoral. He is guilty of murder, seduction and cannibalism. Which monsters only weakness is one pretty FBI agent?

q.e: Hannibal Lecter is the fictional psychiatrist and cannibal from Thomas Harris's novels. In The Silence of the Lambs, he assists FBI trainee Clarice Starling.

q: The town of Pilsen, famous for the production of beer, is situated in western Bohemia, in the Czech Republic. It became a town in 1295 when it received its civic charter from which ruler?

q.e: Plzeň was founded in 1295 by King Wenceslaus II of Bohemia. The first pilsner lager was brewed there in 1842.

q: The special Fanta flavour in Romania, based on a traditional local drink made from elderflower, is called by what name?

q.e: Fanta Shokata is a flavor of Fanta sold in Romania, based on a drink made from elderflower. It has since spread to other countries.

q: For this refreshing cocktail you need 2 oz tequila, juice of 1/2 lime and Coca-Cola. Mix tequila and lime juice over ice cubes in a the glass. Add cola, stir, and its ready.

q.e: The Mexicola is a mix of tequila, lime juice and cola. It's the Mexican take on the Cuba Libre.

q: This member of Czech cuisine, consists of a marinated sausage, usually served with slices of Czech bread.

q.e: Utopenec, meaning "drowned man", is a Czech pub snack of sausage pickled in vinegar with onions. It's served with bread.

q: This German dish, whose name means sow's stomach is popular in Palatinate, a region in south-western Germany.

q.e: Saumagen means "sow's stomach". The German dish from the Palatinate is a stuffed pig stomach, served by Chancellor Helmut Kohl to world leaders.

q: This term denotes the process of adding sugar to the must, the juice of the freshly pressed grapes, in order to increase alcohol content in wine.

q.e: Chaptalization is the addition of sugar to grape juice before fermentation to boost alcohol. It's named after Jean-Antoine Chaptal, a French chemist.

q: This is an Italian delicacy consisting of raw beef, tuna or veal that has been pounded and cut into very thin slices. It is served with a mustard sauce and is usually placed on a bed of arugula and green with an olive oil/lemon juice dressing.

q.e: Carpaccio was invented around 1950 by Giuseppe Cipriani at Harry's Bar in Venice and named after the Renaissance painter Vittore Carpaccio, known for his vivid reds. Retsina is a resinated Greek wine, not a food preparation.

q: First you catch herring, then gut them, and can them in brine. Next you leave them in a warm place for several months. When you see the middle of the can swell you open the can under water and put them on a plate or bowl and serve. What is this dish called?

q.e: Surströmming is fermented Baltic herring, from Sweden, known for its extremely strong smell. It's often eaten outdoors.

q: What was the first major North American root beer to contain caffeine?

q.e: Barq's root beer, created in Biloxi, Mississippi in 1898 by Edward Barq, contains caffeine, unlike most root beers. Its slogan is "Barq's has bite".

q: This pastas name is the Italian word for little bell. It has fluted, petal-like edges and a hollow center for capturing sauce. It is usually found in a casserole or served with a thick sauce.

q.e: Campanelle means "little bells" in Italian. The pasta has a ruffled edge.

q: What is the name of a traditional German wheat beer glass?

q.e: The Weizen glass is tall and curved, to show off the foam and aromas of wheat beer. It usually holds 0.5 liters.

q: Which of these is a Polish beer brand, established in 1629?

q.e: Tyskie is a Polish beer from Tychy, brewed since 1629. It is one of the best-selling beer brands in Poland.

q: Which of these is a traditional Japanese low-alcoholic sweet drink?

q.e: Amazake is a sweet, low-alcohol or non-alcoholic drink made from fermented rice. It's served at Japanese festivals.

q: What is the general term used for the food that is forbidden by the Jewish dietary laws?

q.e: "Treif" (or "treyf") is the Yiddish word for non-kosher food, meaning "torn". Kosher food is called "kosher".

q: According to Greek mythology, Lycaon, king of Arcadia, was turned into a werewolf-like creature because he served Zeus a dish of which of the following?

q.e: In Greek mythology, King Lycaon served Zeus a meal of human flesh, according to the story, and Zeus turned him into a wolf. The word "lycanthropy" comes from this.

q: This term refers to the fear of fats in food.

q.e: Lipophobia is a fear of fat, and "lipophobic" can also describe a molecule that repels fats. It's not a recognized medical condition.

q: He founded one of the largest fast food companies. Having amassed a $500 million fortune during his lifetime, he was included in the TIME 100 list of the worlds most influential builders and titans of industry.

q.e: Ray Kroc joined McDonald's as a franchise agent in 1954 and bought out founders Richard and Maurice McDonald in 1961 for 2.7 million dollars, turning the restaurant chain into a global fast-food giant.

q: It is stated in ancient texts that the earliest beers are Sumerian. Name the ancient Sumerian goddess of beer, daughter of Enki.

q.e: Ninkasi was the Sumerian goddess of beer. The Hymn to Ninkasi, from about 1800 BC, is one of the oldest known beer recipes.

q: This term refers to a technique of food preparation, whereby food is cut into long, thin, matchstick-sized strips.

q.e: Julienne is a cooking method where food is cut into thin matchstick strips. A related cut is the brunoise, which is a fine dice.

q: Plunging a food product into boiling water for a few minutes then in a cold water bath, to halt the cooking process, is known as what?

q.e: Blanching quickly scalds vegetables to deactivate enzymes that cause loss of flavor and color before cooling them in an ice water bath (a step known as shocking). Poaching, by contrast, gently cooks foods in barely simmering liquid without the cold-shock step.

q: This cocktail is made of 1/2 oz rum, 1/2 oz coconut-flavored rum, 1/2 oz grenadine syrup, 1 oz oj, 1 fluid ounce pineapple juice and 1 cup crushed ice. Blend, shake them until the drinks consistency is slushy.

q.e: The Bahama Mama is a tropical rum cocktail with orange juice, pineapple juice and grenadine. It is often served frozen.

q: You drink the coffee and turn the cup upside down. The reader predicts the future, deciphering various patterns formed inside the cup.

q.e: Tasseography, or tasseomancy, is the practice of fortune telling by reading tea leaves or coffee grounds. In Turkey, coffee cup reading is popular.

q: This peculiar tradition takes place in Spain too. Right at the peak of the tomato season a wild tomato battle develops as people pelt each other with ripe tomatoes. Rivers of tomato sauce run down the streets.

q.e: La Tomatina is a festival in Buñol, Spain, held on the last Wednesday of August. Participants throw tomatoes at each other.

q: This is Puerto Ricos national dish. The cuisine consists of pigeons peas and white rice mixed together; seasoned with a condiment called sofrito.

q.e: Arroz con gandules, rice with pigeon peas, flavored with sofrito, is considered the national dish of Puerto Rico. It's served at Christmas.

q: What restaurant-bar of Havana is the birth place of the Mojito cocktail, prepared since its opening in 1942?

q.e: La Bodeguita del Medio in Havana is known for the mojito, and claims Ernest Hemingway as a patron. The cocktail itself dates back much earlier.

q: How many days are in a leap year?

q.e: A leap year has 366 days instead of the usual 365 because an extra day, February 29, is added. This corrects for the fact that Earth takes roughly 365.2422 days to complete a full orbit around the Sun.

Standardized traffic signals place green at the bottom or far right to indicate proceed, while red indicates stop. Red was chosen for stop in 19th-century railway signaling because red wavelengths scatter least and signal danger clearly from a distance.

q: How many sides does a hexagon have?

q.e: A hexagon has six sides and six interior angles, which sum to 720 degrees. The prefix 'hex-' comes from the Greek word for six.

q: How many hours are in a day?

q.e: A standard solar day is divided into 24 hours of 60 minutes each, representing one full rotation of the Earth relative to the Sun.
In the standard Gregorian calendar, July is the seventh month of the year, directly succeeding June and preceding August.
Thermometers measure temperature, deriving their name from the Greek words 'therme' (heat) and 'metron' (measure). Early sealed liquid-in-glass thermometers were developed in the 17th century.
By definition in geometry, a triangle is a closed polygon with three straight sides and three interior angles that sum to 180 degrees. A square has four sides, while a pentagon has five.

q: How many sides does an octagon have?

q.e: An octagon has eight sides and eight interior angles, which total 1,080 degrees. The prefix 'octo-' comes from the Greek word for eight, and the shape is famously used worldwide for stop signs.

q: Which of these colours is NOT featured in the logo for Google?

q.e: Google's logo uses blue, red, yellow and green. It has no pink.

q: What nuts are used in the production of marzipan?

q.e: Traditional marzipan is a confection made primarily of finely ground almond meal and sugar or honey, sometimes enriched with almond oil or extract.

q: How many fingers does a single human hand have?

q.e: A hand has four fingers plus a thumb, five digits in total.

q: What is the name of Poland in Polish?

q.e: Poland is "Polska" in Polish, and its people are Polacy.

q: Which one of these is not a typical European sword design?

q.e: The scimitar is a curved sword associated with Persia and the Middle East. Typical European swords include the longsword and rapier.
VR stands for Virtual Reality, a computer-generated simulation of a three-dimensional environment that users can interact with using specialized electronic equipment like headsets.

q: What is the name of the alcoholic beverage made from potatoes or grains that originates from Poland and Russia?

q.e: Vodka is traditionally distilled from fermented cereal grains or potatoes, typically bottled at about 40% alcohol by volume (80 proof). Rum, by contrast, is distilled from sugarcane byproducts like molasses.

q: Which is the second largest native language spoken in Spain by numbers of speakers?

q.e: Catalan is spoken by over 9 million people across Catalonia, Valencia, and the Balearic Islands, making it Spain's second most common native language after Castilian Spanish.

q: Which restaurant's mascot is a clown?

q.e: Ronald McDonald, a clown in a yellow jumpsuit and red-and-white striped sleeves, was introduced in 1963 as the primary mascot for McDonald's. Burger King is represented by The King, while Whataburger and Sonic have no clown characters.

q: Which sign of the zodiac comes between Virgo and Scorpio?

q.e: In Western tropical astrology, Libra spans roughly September 23 to October 22, sitting directly between Virgo (August 23 to September 22) and Scorpio (October 23 to November 21).

q: What is the shortest month of the year?

q.e: February has only 28 days in common years and 29 days in leap years, making it the shortest month on the Gregorian calendar. All other months have either 30 or 31 days.

q: If you are traveling at a speed of 80 mph, how long will it take you to drive 80 miles?

q.e: Traveling at 80 miles per hour means you cover 80 miles in exactly one hour. Since there are 60 minutes in an hour, the trip takes 60 minutes.

q: What is the name of the extra pedal on a manual or standard transmission car?

q.e: In manual transmission vehicles, the clutch pedal disengages the engine from the transmission so the driver can change gears smoothly. It is operated with the left foot alongside the brake and accelerator pedals.

q: In what year did Canada stop producing the penny?

q.e: The Royal Canadian Mint struck its final one-cent coin in May 2012, officially taking it out of general circulation in February 2013 because manufacturing costs exceeded its face value.
