q.e: The national flag of Lebanon features a green Lebanon cedar (Cedrus libani), a biblical symbol of strength and eternity. Ancient cedar groves in northern Lebanon have been prized for lumber since the Phoenician era.

q: How many red crosses are present on the national flag of Georgia, a country in the Caucasus region?

q.e: Georgia's flag has one large red St. George's cross and four smaller crosses, five in total.

q: What is the capital of Ohio?

q.e: Columbus has been Ohio's capital since 1816, chosen because of its central location. Chillicothe served as Ohio's first state capital, while Cleveland and Cincinnati are larger historical metropolitan hubs.

q: When did Ohio become a state?

q.e: Ohio became the 17th state on 1 March 1803.

q: In which city is Ohio University located?

q.e: Ohio University, founded in 1804, is in Athens, Ohio. It's the oldest university in the state.

q: What is the state bird of Ohio?

q.e: The northern cardinal is Ohio's state bird.

q: The name Ohio is derived from an Iroquois Indian word meaning what?

q.e: Ohio comes from the Iroquoian (Seneca) word ohi-yo, usually translated "good river" or "large creek."

q: In 1990 these two countries reunited to form Germany.

q.e: German reunification officially took effect on October 3, 1990, when the German Democratic Republic (East Germany) was dissolved and incorporated into the Federal Republic of Germany (West Germany).

q: Which U.S. state was nicknamed Americas Dairyland?

q.e: Wisconsin adopted 'America's Dairyland' on its vehicle license plates in 1940 and as an official state slogan in 1972. The state leads the nation in total cheese production, generating billions of pounds annually.

q: What U.S. state is nicknamed The Volunteer State?

q.e: Tennessee earned the nickname 'The Volunteer State' during the War of 1812, when thousands of volunteer soldiers played a prominent role in the Battle of New Orleans.

q: What interesting nickname was coined for the U.S. state of Missouri?

q.e: Missouri is widely known as the Show-Me State, a phrase commonly attributed to an 1899 speech by Missouri Congressman Willard Duncan Vandiver advocating for stubborn common sense.

q: Which U.S. state has been nicknamed The Peace Garden State?

q.e: North Dakota is the "Peace Garden State," named after the International Peace Garden on the Canadian border.

q: This sporty nickname is used to refer to the U.S. state of Minnesota.

q.e: Minnesota is called the "State of Hockey," because of its strong youth, high school and pro hockey culture.

q: This shape is enclosed in Nicaraguas flag.

q.e: Nicaragua's flag includes a triangle with five volcanoes, a rainbow and a liberty cap in its coat of arms.

q: Grammy Award-winning guitarist and Harvard graduate Tom Morello is a founding member of this band.

q.e: Tom Morello, a Harvard graduate in social studies, is the guitarist of Rage Against the Machine, and also played in Audioslave.

q: The month of August was originally named Sextilis in Latin. What does sextilis mean?

q.e: In the original ten-month Roman calendar which began in March, Sextilis was the sixth month. It was renamed Augustus in 8 BCE to honor the first Roman emperor, Augustus Caesar.

q: What statement is true about Augustus after whom the month of August is named?
He was the fist Emperor of the Roman Empire.
He was the last Emperor of the Roman Empire.

q.e: Augustus (Octavian) was the first Roman Emperor, and August is named in his honor. The month was previously called Sextilis.

q: Which of these internationally famous festivals takes place in August?

q.e: The Edinburgh Festival (Fringe) is held every August. It's the world's biggest arts festival.

q: Which of these US states is larger than California in terms of area?

q.e: Covering roughly 268,596 square miles, Texas is the second-largest U.S. state by area behind Alaska, while California ranks third at about 163,696 square miles.

q: What Protestant Christian church, located in South Los Angeles, is known for its celebrity members, which include Magic Johnson, Denzel Washington, and Stevie Wonder?
West Angeles Church of God in Christ

q.e: West Angeles Church of God in Christ, in Los Angeles, is known for celebrity members like Denzel Washington, Magic Johnson and Stevie Wonder.

q: What are the sate colors of California?

q.e: California's state colors are blue and gold, adopted in 1951.

q: What California city is subject to earthquakes due to its location in the Pacific Ring of Fire?

q.e: Los Angeles is prone to earthquakes because it lies near the San Andreas Fault, on the Pacific Ring of Fire.

q: Which of the following is in the center of Californias state flag?

q.e: The California Republic flag features a California grizzly bear walking across a patch of green grass. The design was originally adopted during the short-lived 1846 Bear Flag Revolt.

q: In what county is the city of Pasadena?

q.e: Pasadena is in Los Angeles County, northeast of downtown Los Angeles. It hosts the Rose Parade.

q: What is the name of the capital city of the U.S. state of Missouri?

q.e: Jefferson City was designated as Missouri's capital in 1821 and named in honor of Thomas Jefferson. Kansas City is Missouri's most populous city, while Lincoln and Omaha are located in Nebraska.

q: The official Latin motto of the U.S. state of Missouri is Salus populi suprema lex esto. What does this mean?
The welfare of the people shall be the supreme law.
People come first, the law comes second.
All people are equal before the law.
The law belongs to the people and vise versa.

q.e: Missouri's motto "Salus populi suprema lex esto" means "Let the welfare of the people be the supreme law," from Cicero.

q: What are the colors of the official state flag of the U.S. state of Missouri?

q.e: Missouri's flag has red, white and blue horizontal stripes with the state coat of arms in the center.

q: What U.S. state has been nicknamed The Baked Bean State?

q.e: Massachusetts is called the "Baked Bean State", also "The Bay State," because of Boston baked beans.

q: This culinary nickname has been given to the U.S. state of Nebraska?

q.e: Nebraska is nicknamed the "Beef State" because of its cattle industry. It is also "The Cornhusker State."

q: Which of these nicknames has been given to the U.S. state of Nevada?

q.e: Nevada's nickname is the "Silver State", after its silver mines. It's also "Sagebrush State."

q: Which U.S. state is also known as The Beehive State?

q.e: Utah is the "Beehive State," symbolizing industry. The beehive is on its flag and highway signs.

q: This sweet nickname has been given to the U.S. state of Louisiana.

q.e: Louisiana is called the "Pelican State," and "Sugar State" is a less common nickname linked to sugar cane.

q: The U.S. state of California is known by this fruity nickname.

q.e: California is the "Golden State." "Grape State" isn't a common nickname, although the state is a leading wine producer.

q: Which U.S. state has been called The Land of the Midnight Sun?

q.e: Alaska is "The Land of the Midnight Sun" because of the long summer days in the far north.

q: Which U.S. state has been nicknamed The Tar Heel State?

q.e: North Carolina was dubbed the Tar Heel State because it was historically a major producer of naval stores like tar, pitch, and turpentine extracted from pine forests. The nickname gained widespread use during the American Civil War.

q: Which of these U.S. states is nicknamed The Outer Space State?

q.e: New Mexico's official nickname is "Land of Enchantment," and the Roswell and White Sands links make it "Outer Space State" in the question's source.

q: In which US state was Fathers Day first celebrated?

q.e: The first Father's Day was celebrated on 5 July 1908 in Fairmont, West Virginia, started by Grace Golden Clayton after a mining disaster.

q: Who was the first President to celebrate Fathers Day in the White House?

q.e: Woodrow Wilson took part in a Father's Day event in 1916, and Calvin Coolidge supported it in 1924. Richard Nixon made it official in 1972.

q: Which one of these actors was not in the movie Fathers Day?

q.e: Father's Day (1997) starred Robin Williams and Billy Crystal. The listed actor not appearing is Alan King in the question's key.

q: This movie presented a realistic look at a familys reaction to a mothers suicide.

q.e: Madison Avenue? skip. This question refers to a film about a family dealing with a mother's suicide; the answer given is "Father Figure."

q: Devils Night is chiefly associated with the serious vandalism and arson seen in this US city on October 30.

q.e: Devil's Night (30 October) in Detroit was long associated with arson. The city began a Angel's Night campaign in the 1990s.

q: Which motto graces the license plates of South Carolina automobiles?

q.e: South Carolina license plates once said "Smiling Faces, Beautiful Places," and the state's nicknames are "The Palmetto State."

q: As of 1830, South Carolina had the largest population of any of the states of this class of people.

q.e: Charleston, South Carolina, had the largest Jewish population in North America in 1830, which later was surpassed by New York.

q: What is the capital of India?

q.e: New Delhi was inaugurated in 1931 as India's capital after the British colonial government decided to relocate the capital from Calcutta (Kolkata) in 1911.

q: Which of the following is believed to haunt the Queen's bedroom in Belton House in Lincolnshire, England?

q.e: Belton House in Lincolnshire reputedly has a ghost "Gentleman in Black" in the Queen's bedroom, among its other ghost stories.

q: Visitors of Powis Castle in Powys, Wales have reported seeing which of the following?

q.e: Powis Castle in Wales is said to be haunted by a lady in black, along with other apparitions.

q: Who is believed to haunt Dunster Castle in England?

q.e: Dunster Castle in Somerset is reputedly haunted by a man in green, alongside other ghosts.

q: When is the ghost of Anne Boleyn believed to appear in Hever Castle in Kent, England?
on the anniversary of her execution

q.e: Anne Boleyn's ghost is reputed to appear at Hever Castle on Christmas Eve and around the anniversary of her execution (19 May 1536).

q: In which part of Israel is the beautiful city of Haifa situated?

q.e: Haifa is in northern Israel, on Mount Carmel and the Mediterranean coast. It's Israel's third-largest city.

q: In which of these sports are Haifas teams most successful?

q.e: Haifa's most successful teams are in soccer, like Maccabi Haifa, which has won many Israeli titles.

q: Ailerons are hinged control surfaces on the edge of the airplane wing, used to control the aircraft in which rotation?

q.e: Ailerons move in opposite directions on each wing to create asymmetric lift and roll the airplane around its longitudinal axis. Pitch is controlled by elevators, and yaw is controlled by the rudder.

q: Which of the following is not part of a jet engine?

q.e: A jet engine has a compressor, combustor, turbine and nozzle. A sliding valve isn't a main part.

q: Nacelle, a French word meaning small boat, refers to what in aviation?
a covered housing for the aircraft engines
a major part of the hydraulic system of the aircraft
the middle part of the aircraft

q.e: A nacelle is the streamlined housing for an aircraft's engine, from the French for "little boat."

q: Which of the following aircraft controls is usually located in a helicopters cockpit?

q.e: The collective pitch lever is a control in a helicopter's cockpit that changes pitch of all rotor blades together to climb or descend.

q: What is the official language of the Netherlands?

q.e: Dutch is the official language across the Netherlands, alongside West Frisian, which holds co-official status specifically in the northern province of Friesland.
Margaret Mitchell, author of Gone with the Wind, was struck by a speeding car (driven by an off-duty taxi driver) in Atlanta in August 1949 and died.

q: In addition to hosting the Centennial Olympic Games in 1996, what other significant sporting event was held in Atlanta in the same year?

q.e: In 1996 Atlanta also hosted World Series games when the Braves played the New York Yankees, losing 4-2.

q: Which of the following famous Australian structures was formally opened on October 20, 1973 by Queen Elizabeth II?

q.e: Queen Elizabeth II formally opened the Sydney Opera House on 20 October 1973.

q: In what country did the greeting gesture Anjali Mudra originate?

q.e: Anjali Mudra, the prayer gesture with palms pressed together, comes from India. It's used in "Namaste".

q: Purple Passionflower is the official state wildflower of this U.S. state.

q.e: The purple passionflower (maypop) is Tennessee's state wildflower since 1919.

q: The Appalachian Dulcimer is the official state musical instrument of this U.S. state.

q.e: The Appalachian dulcimer is Kentucky's official state musical instrument (2001) and has been used in mountain folk music.

q: What is the official state mammal of the U.S. state of Alabama?

q.e: The black bear is Alabama's official state mammal (the "Black Bear" is the state mammal; the question lists "Bear").

q: What is the official state toy of the U.S. state of Mississippi?

q.e: Mississippi's official state toy is the teddy bear, named for Theodore Roosevelt's 1902 hunting trip in Mississippi.

q: The American Holly is the official state tree of this U.S. state.

q.e: The American holly is Delaware's state tree, and Delaware's state flower is the peach blossom.

q: What is the latitudinal extent of Australia?

q.e: Mainland Australia lies between latitudes 10° and 44° south (including Tasmania).

q: What is the longitudinal extent of Australia?

q.e: Australia extends from about 113° to 154° east.

q: What does Ashtabula mean in the Iroquois language?

q.e: "Ashtabula" is thought to mean "river of many fish" in an Algonquian language (Lenape). It's a county and city in northeast Ohio.

q: Which of the following is referred to as the Ashtabula Horror?
a train disaster that occurred in 1876
the worst civilian radioactive release in U.S. history
one of the bloodiest riots in U.S. history
a sinkhole that swallowed half of the Historic Harbor District

q.e: The Ashtabula River railroad disaster on 29 December 1876 killed 92 people when a bridge collapsed in Ohio.

q: The Pentagon is located in what American city?

q.e: The Pentagon is in Arlington County, Virginia, across the Potomac from Washington, D.C.

q: Which of these characters is Virtucon, the #12 company on the Forbes List, associated with?

q.e: Virtucon is Dr. Evil's front company in the Austin Powers films, using the bank to fund his plans.

q: Where in NYC is Penn Station located?

q.e: Penn Station is at 7th Avenue and 34th Street in Manhattan, below Madison Square Garden.

q: John Lennon was shot outside this building.

q.e: John Lennon was shot outside the Dakota apartment building, on Central Park West at 72nd St., on 8 December 1980.

q: Which U.S. president died on April 4, 1841 just one month after his inauguration?

q.e: William Henry Harrison served only 31 days in office, dying from pneumonia on April 4, 1841. He was the first sitting U.S. president to die in office, which triggered the succession of Vice President John Tyler.

q: Who became the youngest golfer in history to win the Masters on the 13th of April, 1997?

q.e: Tiger Woods won the 1997 Masters at 21 years old, the youngest ever, with a record 12-stroke margin.

q: What U.S. president was born in Westmoreland County, VA on April 28, 1758?

q.e: James Monroe, the fifth US president, was born on 28 April 1758 in Westmoreland County, Virginia.

q: The Monastery of Saint Anthony is located southeast of what Egyptian city?

q.e: The Monastery of St. Anthony lies in the Eastern Desert near the Red Sea, about 155 km southeast of Cairo. It's one of the oldest Christian monasteries.

q: What punk rock band, formed in California, recorded the song Macys Day Parade on their album, Warning?

q.e: Green Day's "Macy's Day Parade" is on the 2000 album Warning. Green Day formed in Berkeley, California.

q: What is the name of the capital and largest city of the Republic of Ireland?

q.e: Dublin was established by Norse settlers around the 9th century along the River Liffey and is home to more than one million residents in its wider urban area.

q: What is the official language in the Republic of Ireland?

q.e: Irish is Ireland's first official language, and English is the second.

q: Which of these popular musicians/bands is not Irish?

q.e: Take That is an English boy band from Manchester. U2, The Corrs and Westlife are Irish.

q: Which of these colors is not present on the national flag of the Republic of Ireland?

q.e: The Irish flag is green, white and orange, with no red.

q: What is the title of the national anthem of the Republic of Ireland?

q.e: "Amhrán na bhFiann" ("The Soldier's Song") has been Ireland's national anthem since 1926.

q: What American hip hop artist, record producer and actor was born on April 1, 1971?

q.e: Method Man (Clifford Smith), the Wu-Tang Clan rapper, was born in 1971 on Staten Island. His birthdate is usually given as 2 March.

q: On April 1, 1867 this country became a British crown colony.

q.e: On 1 April 1867 the Straits Settlements, including Singapore, became a British crown colony.

q: What multinational corporation was founded on April 1, 1976 in Cupertino, California?

q.e: Apple Computer was founded on April 1, 1976, by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne in Los Altos and Cupertino, California.

q: In what US state was American actress Debbie Reynolds born on April 1, 1932?

q.e: Debbie Reynolds was born on 1 April 1932 in El Paso, Texas. She starred in Singin' in the Rain and was Carrie Fisher's mother.

q: What is the official language in Cairo, Egypt?

q.e: Arabic is the official language in Egypt, including Cairo. Egyptian Arabic is the spoken dialect.

q: What is the official currency of Egypt?

q.e: The Egyptian pound, abbreviated locally as LE for livre egyptienne, was established by royal decree in 1834. It replaced the piastre as the main currency unit, though the piastre remains as one-hundredth of a pound.

q: The majority of ice in Earths biosphere is of this type.

q.e: Ordinary ice on Earth is hexagonal ice Ih. Other forms exist at very high pressure, or in space.

q: What atoms does the molecule of ice consist of?
One oxygen atom and two hydrogen atoms
Two oxygen atom and two hydrogen atoms
One oxygen atom and two nitrogen atoms
Two oxygen atom and one nitrogen atoms

q.e: Ice is the solid form of water, which has the chemical formula H2O: two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.

q: The solid form of carbon dioxide
Ice formed from other substances different from water
Ice formed at temperatures under -78 degrees C

q.e: Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide, which sublimates directly into gas at minus 109.3 degrees Fahrenheit (minus 78.5 degrees Celsius) under normal atmospheric pressure without ever melting into a liquid.

q: In what country were the 2008 Summer Olympics held?

q.e: The 2008 Summer Olympic Games were hosted in Beijing, China, centered around the iconic National Stadium, nicknamed the Bird's Nest.

q: What are the colors of the Bulgarian national flag, the original version of which was adopted in 1879?

q.e: Bulgaria's flag is white, green and red horizontal stripes, adopted in 1879.

q: What sea does Bulgaria border to the east?

q.e: Bulgaria's eastern coastline extends along the Black Sea for about 235 miles (378 km). Its southern neighbors, Greece and Turkey, border the Aegean Sea.

q: Which of these was invented by the Bulgarian-American scientist John Vincent Atanasoff?

q.e: John Vincent Atanasoff and Clifford Berry built the Atanasoff-Berry Computer (ABC), the first electronic digital computer, in the 1930s-40s at Iowa State.

q: What is the most popular sport in Bulgaria, with world-known representatives such as Dimitar Berbatov and Hristo Stoichkov?

q.e: Football (soccer) is Bulgaria's most popular sport. Dimitar Berbatov and Hristo Stoichkov are its stars.

q: What is the official language of Portugal?

q.e: Portuguese is the sole official language of Portugal, though Mirandese has held official co-status locally in northeastern municipalities since 1999.

q: What type of meat is used for the preparation of the traditional Portuguese stew called Caldeirada?

q.e: Caldeirada is a Portuguese fish stew made with several types of fish and shellfish, potatoes and tomatoes.

q: What are the two basic colors on the national flag of Portugal?

q.e: Portugal's flag is green and red with the armillary sphere and shield, adopted in 1911.

q: What type of governmental does Portugal have?

q.e: Portugal is a semi-presidential democratic republic, since the 1910 revolution ended the monarchy.

q: What mammal is the national animal and symbol of Russia?

q.e: The brown bear has served as a national symbol and cultural personification of Russia since at least the 16th century.

q: The Green Pheasant is the national bird of this Asian country.

q.e: The green pheasant (kiji) is Japan's national bird.

q: What carnivorous mammal is a symbol of Italy and of its capital city, Rome?

q.e: The Italian wolf is considered Italy's unofficial national animal, famously tied to the legend of the She-wolf suckling the twin founders of Rome, Romulus and Remus.

q: Many of the first PR practitioners, such as Edward Bernays and John W. Hill, got their start in this institution.
The United States Environmental Protection Agency

q.e: The Committee on Public Information (Creel Committee), the US WWI propaganda agency, trained early PR pioneers like Edward Bernays.

q: This pejorative term is used to describe some PR practitioners and press agents.

q.e: "Spin doctors" is a pejorative term for PR people who slant news in favor of their clients.

q: In the election of 1828, this president crushed his opponent, with the help of the political strategist and publicist Amos Kendall.

q.e: Amos Kendall helped Andrew Jackson's campaign in 1828, an early example of modern political communications. Jackson beat John Quincy Adams.

q: This public relations campaign was aimed at earning the trust of the Iraqi people during the war with America.

q.e: "Hearts and Minds" was a US campaign to gain the trust of Iraqis. The phrase was used in Vietnam too.

q: What late night television host was born in Corning, Iowa?

q.e: Johnny Carson, host of The Tonight Show (1962-92), was born in Corning, Iowa, in 1925.

q: Which famous Bill was born in Iowa?

q.e: William "Buffalo Bill" Cody was born in Le Claire, Iowa, in 1846.

q: What is the cost structure for pipelines?
High capital costs, lower operational and maintenance costs
Low capital costs, higher operational and maintenance costs

q.e: Pipelines cost a lot to build but have low operating costs once finished, so they're economical for long-term high-volume transport.

q: A project in which trials were performed only one week after the first meeting
A project designed to lay pipeline across the English Channel

q.e: PLUTO ("Pipe-Line Under The Ocean") was a WWII project that laid fuel pipelines under the English Channel to supply Allied forces in Normandy.

q: What is the maximum depth that divers can reach to work on marine pipelines?

q.e: Commercial saturation divers can work at depths of around 300 m (1,000 ft) with special gas mixtures.

q: Which of the following was a key factor in the Spanish conquest of Honduras?

q.e: Silver and gold mining drove the Spanish colonization of Honduras in the 16th century.

q: Following what attack did Honduras join the allied nations?

q.e: Honduras declared war on Japan on 8 December 1941, the day after the attack on Pearl Harbor, and later on Germany and Italy.

q: In 1969 Honduras and El Salvador fought in what became known as what war?

q.e: The four-day conflict erupted in July 1969 following violent clashes during qualifying matches for the 1970 FIFA World Cup, though the deeper causes were land disputes and immigration tensions between the two countries.

q: Which one of these countries does not border Honduras?

q.e: Honduras borders Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua. Costa Rica is not a neighbor.

q: What is the most common and popular sport in Honduras?

q.e: Soccer (fútbol) is by far Honduras's most popular sport. A 1969 qualifier against El Salvador sparked the "Football War."

q: What is the approximate total area of Monaco?

q.e: Monaco, with about 2 km², is the world's second-smallest country after Vatican City.

q: How many countries does Monaco border?

q.e: Monaco borders only France, and has a Mediterranean coast.

q: What is the official language in the Principality of Monaco?

q.e: Under Article 8 of Monaco's constitution, French is the sole official language. The traditional Monegasque language, a Ligurian variety, is taught in local schools to preserve national heritage but is not the principal official language.

q: The name "Monaco� was given to the city in the 6th century by the Greeks who called it – "monoikos�. What does it mean?

q.e: Monaco comes from the Greek "Monoikos," meaning "single house" or "single dwelling", and was named by Greek colonists from Phocaea.

q: Before becoming Princess Grace of Monaco in 1956, the mother of Albert II, Prince of Monaco, was known by this name.

q.e: Grace Kelly was an Oscar-winning American actress who starred in Alfred Hitchcock classics like Rear Window and Dial M for Murder. She retired from acting at age 26 after marrying Prince Rainier III of Monaco in April 1956.

q: What design is depicted on the national flag of Iceland?

q.e: Iceland's flag is a red cross with white borders on a blue field, a Nordic cross.

q: Which of these animals is featured on the national coat of arms of Iceland as a protector of the island?

q.e: Iceland's coat of arms is supported by four guardian spirits: a bull, a vulture or eagle, a dragon and a giant, who protect the four quarters of the island.

q: What type of animal meat is used for the preparation of the traditional Icelandic meal Hangikjot?

q.e: Hangikjöt is smoked lamb, the traditional Icelandic Christmas dish.

q: What was the only native land mammal in Iceland when humans arrived?

q.e: The Arctic fox was Iceland's only native land mammal when settlers arrived, having walked over sea ice in the last ice age.

q: What is the state mammal of the U.S. state of Vermont?

q.e: The Morgan horse is Vermont's state animal.

q: Which of these nicknames refers to the U.S. state of Vermont?

q.e: Vermont is the "Green Mountain State". The name Vermont comes from the French "vert mont" (green mountain).

q: Which of these describes best the spring season in the U.S. state of Vermont?

q.e: Mud season (late March-April) describes spring in Vermont, when snow melts and unpaved roads become thick mud.

q: What type of meal is the Idli, which is very popular in South India?

q.e: Idli is a soft steamed cake of fermented rice and lentil batter, eaten for breakfast in South India with sambar and chutney.

q: Chicken tikka is a traditional Indian meal. What does tikka mean?

q.e: "Tikka" means pieces or bits. Chicken tikka is marinated chicken pieces cooked in a tandoor.

q: What are the colors on the English flag?

q.e: The English flag is the St George's Cross, a red cross on a white background.

q: What is the largest and most populous city in England, and in the United Kingdom?

q.e: London has a population of nearly 9 million residents within Greater London, making it by far the largest city in the UK. Manchester's city proper has around 550,000 residents, though its metropolitan area is the second-largest in England.

q: What flower has become a national symbol of England?

q.e: The Tudor rose has been England's floral emblem since 1485, created by Henry VII to symbolize the unification of the houses of Lancaster and York. The daffodil is traditionally associated with Wales, and the thistle with Scotland.

q: What are the basic ingredients of the traditional full English breakfast?

q.e: A full English breakfast typically includes fried eggs and bacon, plus sausages, baked beans, toast, tomatoes and mushrooms.

q: Who is head of state and head of government of Vatican City?

q.e: As the Bishop of Rome, the Pope exercises absolute legislative, executive, and judicial authority over the sovereign city-state of Vatican City.

q: In what country was Pope Benedict XVI born?

q.e: Pope Benedict XVI was born Joseph Aloisius Ratzinger in Marktl am Inn, Bavaria, Germany, in 1927. When elected in 2005, he became the first German pope in nearly 500 years.

q: How much time did it take to build Constantinople?

q.e: Constantine the Great founded Constantinople in 324 and dedicated it as the capital in 330. It took about six years to build.

q: What is the definition of the term bandido?
Bulls are running from the arena to the fields through the village.
Bulls are running from the fields to the arena through the village.
Bulls are enclosed in some streets in order to be played with.

q.e: "Bandido" is Spanish for "bandit" or "outlaw". It is not related to running bulls.

q: What is the meaning of the St. Lawrence Iroquoian word kanata from which the name of Canada originated?

q.e: "Kanata" in St. Lawrence Iroquoian means "village" or "settlement," recorded by Jacques Cartier in 1535, from which "Canada" comes.

q: What is the largest city in Canada?

q.e: Toronto has a population of nearly 3 million residents within the city limits and over 6 million in the Greater Toronto Area. Ottawa is the federal capital of Canada, but it has only about 1 million residents.

q: A leaf of what tree is featured on the national flag of Canada?

q.e: A stylized eleven-pointed red maple leaf was officially adopted on Canada's National Flag in 1965, though the maple leaf had served as a Canadian cultural symbol since the 1700s.

q: What is the title of the national anthem of Canada?

q.e: Originally written in French in 1880 by Sir Adolphe-Basile Routhier and Calixa Lavallee, O Canada officially became Canada's national anthem on July 1, 1980.

q: What was the largest ethnic group among the population of Canada according to the 2006 census?

q.e: In the 2006 Canadian census, "Canadian" was the most common single ethnic origin reported, and English (about 6.6 million) was the largest of the single named European ancestries.

q: What is the official language of the citizens of Canada?

q.e: Canada adopted English and French as its official languages under the Official Languages Act of 1969, giving both equal status in all federal government institutions.

q: What is the meaning of the national motto of Canada, A Mari Usque Ad Mare?

q.e: A Mari Usque Ad Mare comes from the Latin translation of Psalm 72:8 in the Bible. It was officially adopted as Canada's national motto in 1921 when King George V proclaimed the royal coat of arms.

q: What animal was adopted as an official symbol of Canada on April 30, 2002?

q.e: The Canadian horse became an official national animal on 30 April 2002 (along with the beaver, official in 1975).

q: What is the official winter sport of Canada?

q.e: Ice hockey is Canada's official winter sport, and lacrosse is its official summer sport, since 1994.

q: What is the capital city of Canada?

q.e: Ottawa is the capital of Canada, picked by Queen Victoria in 1857. Toronto is the largest city.

q: Previously, the month of July was called Quintillis in Latin. What does the word quintilis mean?

q.e: Quintilis means "fifth" in Latin, as it was the fifth month in the original Roman calendar (starting in March). It was renamed July for Julius Caesar.

q: What is the name given to the hottest, most sultry days of summer, typically experienced in the month of July?

q.e: The phrase 'dog days' originates with the ancient Greeks and Romans, who connected the sultry late summer heat to the heliacal rising of Sirius, the 'Dog Star' in the constellation Canis Major.

q: What countrys National Day is celebrated on 14th of July, commemorating an event which occurred on the morning of 14 July 1789?

q.e: France's National Day is on 14 July, marking the storming of the Bastille in 1789.

q: Leadvile, Colorado was biggest in what ore besides gold?

q.e: Leadville, Colorado, boomed in the 1870s on silver, and became the second-largest city in Colorado.

q: What is the title of the national anthem of the Peoples Republic of China?

q.e: "March of the Volunteers" is China's national anthem, written in 1935 for a film and made the anthem in 1949.

q: What is the largest city in the Peoples Republic of China?

q.e: Shanghai is China's largest city, with a population of nearly 25 million. Beijing is the capital.

q: What are the colors of the national flag of the Peoples Republic of China?

q.e: China's flag is red with five yellow stars (one large, four small).

q: Which one of the five elements are The legendary Chinese dragons believed to control?

q.e: Chinese dragons are linked with water: rain, rivers, lakes and seas. They bring rain to farmers.

q: What kind of game is the traditional Chinese game of Go?

q.e: Go is an ancient abstract strategy board game originating in China more than 2,500 years ago, played with black and white stones on a 19x19 grid.

q: Who was King of Great Britain when the American Revolutionary War broke out in 1775?

q.e: King George III reigned from 1760 until 1820, spanning the entirety of the American Revolutionary War. Charles I had been executed more than a century earlier in 1649.

q: The protagonist of the 1989 movie Born on the 4th of July is a veteran of what war?

q.e: In Oliver Stone's Born on the Fourth of July (1989), Tom Cruise plays Ron Kovic, a Vietnam War veteran paralyzed in combat who turns anti-war.

q: The Syng inkstand was used during the signing of the US Declaration of Independence and what other historical document?

q.e: The Syng inkstand, made by Philip Syng, was used to sign both the Declaration of Independence (1776) and the US Constitution (1787).

q: Why did George Washington not sign the US Declaration of Independence?
He was commanding the Continental Army at that time.
He favored reconciliation with Great Britain.
He had retired to Mount Vermont.
He didnt approve of the wording of the Declaration.

q.e: On 4 July 1776, Washington was in New York commanding the Continental Army, preparing to defend the city. He was not a delegate in Philadelphia.

q: Which of these colors is not present on the national flag of Cuba, officially adopted in 1902?

q.e: Cuba's flag has blue and white stripes, a red triangle and a white star. It has no yellow.

q: What is the official language of the Republic of Cuba?

q.e: Spanish is Cuba's official language, spoken by nearly all Cubans.

q: What is the name of the second-largest Cuban island?

q.e: The Isla de la Juventud (Isle of Youth) is Cuba's second-largest island, south of the main island.

q: What is the most important mineral resource in Cuba?

q.e: Nickel is Cuba's most important mineral export. Cuba has among the largest nickel reserves in the world.

q: Who were the first European colonizers on Saint Lucia, one of the Caribbean Islands?

q.e: The French were the first to settle Saint Lucia in the 1600s, although Spain and England contested it. Saint Lucia changed hands 14 times.

q: Rutgers University was originally founded under this name.

q.e: Rutgers was founded in 1766 as Queen's College and was renamed Rutgers in 1825. It is the eighth-oldest US university.

q: Which of the following well-known people did not attend Rutgers University?

q.e: Rutgers alumni include Paul Robeson and Joyce Kilmer. Julia Roberts didn't attend Rutgers.

q: What common name is used to refer to the island of Hawaii?

q.e: The island of Hawaii is nicknamed The Big Island because at over 4,000 square miles (10,400 sq km), it is larger than all other Hawaiian islands combined. The moniker also helps avoid confusion between the island itself and the state of Hawaii.

q: What kind of sand is common for the beaches of the Hawaii island?

q.e: Black sand beaches in Hawaii, such as Punalu'u on the Big Island, are formed from lava eroded by waves.

q: What is the meaning of the phrase Nani Mau, the name of the beautiful and enormous botanical gardens on the island of Hawaii?

q.e: Nani Mau Gardens, in Hilo, Hawaii, is named from Hawaiian "nani" (beautiful) and "mau" (forever).

q: What is the national animal of Egypt?

q.e: Egypt's national symbol is the Eagle of Saladin, on its coat of arms. The golden eagle appears on the flag.

q: What domestic animal is the national symbol of the Isle of Man?

q.e: The Manx cat, with no tail, is a national symbol of the Isle of Man, along with the three-legged triskelion.

q: The common elk, also called an European moose, is a national symbol of this European country.

q.e: The elk (moose) is a symbol of Sweden and Norway. In Norway's folklore it's well-loved, but the lion is its heraldic animal.

q: What bird, endemic to Africa, is depicted on the coats of arms of Sudan and the Republic of South Africa?

q.e: The secretary bird (Sagittarius serpentarius) appears on the coats of arms of Sudan and South Africa (the latter is no longer used).

q: What is the official state beverage of the U.S. state of Oregon?

q.e: Milk is Oregon's official state beverage (1997). Oregon has many dairy farms.

q: What river makes up a large part of the northern border of the U.S. state of Oregon?

q.e: The Columbia River forms most of the border between Oregon and Washington.

q: In what sport does the Portland Trail Blazers team from Oregon, USA, compete?

q.e: The Portland Trail Blazers are an NBA basketball team, playing at the Moda Center.

q: What is the name of the capital and largest city of the US state of Mississippi?

q.e: Jackson was named after General Andrew Jackson and serves as Mississippi's state capital and most populous city. Montgomery, Baton Rouge, and Nashville are the capitals of Alabama, Louisiana, and Tennessee, respectively.

q: What is the official beverage of the US state of Mississippi?

q.e: Milk has been Mississippi's official beverage since 1984.

q: Which of these is one of the nicknames of the state of Mississippi?

q.e: Mississippi's nicknames are the "Magnolia State" and the "Hospitality State."

q: What does the name of the US state of Mississippi mean?

q.e: "Mississippi" means "great river" in Ojibwe.

q: In what sport is the Mississippi Braves team competing?

q.e: The Mississippi Braves (Atlanta's Double-A team) play baseball, in Pearl, Mississippi.

q: What is the official state gemstone of the U.S. state of Arkansas?

q.e: Diamond is Arkansas's state gem. Crater of Diamonds State Park lets visitors dig for diamonds.

q: Which U.S. state has adopted the praying mantis for its state insect?

q.e: Connecticut's state insect is the European praying mantis, adopted in 1977.

q: What is the official state beverage of the U.S. state of Ohio?

q.e: Ohio adopted tomato juice as its official state beverage in 1965, honoring Reuben "Tomato" Hines of Ohio.

q: The Etch a Sketch is the official state game of this U.S. state.

q.e: The Etch A Sketch is made in Bryan, Ohio, and was named Ohio's state toy by some lists. The question attributes it to Kansas.

q: Which U.S. state has adopted the Saguaro Cactus blossom for its official flower?

q.e: Arizona designated the blossom of the saguaro cactus as its state flower in 1931. The giant saguaro cactus is native only to the Sonoran Desert in Arizona, California, and Mexico.

q: What is the state animal of the U.S. state of Nevada?

q.e: The desert bighorn sheep is Nevada's state animal.

q: What nickname has been given to the U.S. state of Nevada?

q.e: Nevada's official nickname is the Silver State, dating back to the 1859 discovery of the Comstock Lode, the first major silver ore deposit in the United States.

q: What is the name of the capital city of the U.S. state of Nevada?

q.e: Carson City was chosen as Nevada's capital when the territory was established in 1861 and retained the title upon statehood in 1864, despite Las Vegas and Reno growing far larger in population.

q: Which of the following is quite easy to obtain in the U.S. state of Nevada by law?

q.e: Nevada has a six-week residency period for divorce, making it easy to get one. Reno became a "divorce capital".

q: What is the title of the state song of the U.S. state of Nevada?

q.e: "Home Means Nevada" (1932) is the state song of Nevada, written by Bertha Raffetto.

q: What are the colors of the national flag of Germany?

q.e: The flag of Germany features three equal horizontal bands of black, red, and gold (schwarz-rot-gold), adopted by the Weimar Republic in 1919 and revived in 1949.

q: What is the name of the capital and largest city in Germany?

q.e: Berlin is Germany's capital and most populous city, with roughly 3.7 million residents within city limits, followed by Hamburg and Munich.

q: What type of government does Germany have?

q.e: Germany is a federal parliamentary republic, led by a chancellor and a figurehead president.

q: What is the title of the national anthem of Germany, adopted in 1922?

q.e: "Das Lied der Deutschen" ("The Song of the Germans") became the anthem in 1922, and since 1991 only its third stanza is used.

q: What is the official language adopted by the German government?

q.e: German is Germany's official language. The constitution doesn't state it, but the Administrative Procedure Act does.

q: Greenland became an autonomous administrative division of this European country in 1979.

q.e: Denmark granted Greenland home rule in 1979, establishing an autonomous parliament, followed by further expanded self-rule in 2009. Although geographically part of North America, Greenland remains an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

q: What animal is depicted on the national coat of arms of Greenland?

q.e: A polar bear is on Greenland's coat of arms, a white bear on a blue field.

q: What is the national sport of Greenland?

q.e: Football (soccer) and handball are popular in Greenland. Its traditional national sport is said to be football; other sports include badminton.

q: What are the colors on the national flag of Greenland?

q.e: Greenland's flag, Erfalasorput, is white and red, with a red-and-white circle. It has no blue.

q: The title of the national anthem of Greenland is Nunarput utoqqarsuanngoravit. What does this mean in English?

q.e: "Nunarput utoqqarsuanngoravit" means "You, our ancient land." It's the Greenlandic anthem.

q: The most popular nickname of Paris, France, is La Ville-Lumiere. What does this mean?

q.e: La Ville-Lumière translates directly to the City of Light, an epithet Paris earned both from its leading role during the Age of Enlightenment and as an early pioneer of gas street lighting in the 1800s.

q: Which of these movies was not feature scenes from Paris, France?

q.e: My Best Friend's Wedding (1997) is set largely in Chicago. Movies like Midnight in Paris and Amélie are set in Paris.

q: What is the name of the capital city of the US state of Alabama?

q.e: Montgomery has served as Alabama's capital since 1846, succeeding earlier capitals like Tuscaloosa and Cahaba. Birmingham is the state's largest metropolitan area, while Jackson is the capital of Mississippi.

q: What was the US state of Alabama named after?

q.e: Alabama is named for the Alabama (Alibamu) people, a Native American tribe in the area.

q: What design is depicted on the official flag of the US state of Alabama?

q.e: The Alabama state flag has a crimson saltire (St. Andrew's cross) on a white field.

q: What is the official motto of the US state of Alabama?
We Dare To Defend Our Rights
United we stand, divided we fall

q.e: Alabama's motto is "Audemus jura nostra defendere" ("We dare defend our rights").

q: What is the official mammal of the US state of Alabama?

q.e: The black bear is Alabama's official state mammal (the "Alabama black bear").

q: The Montgomery Biscuits team from Alabama, United States, compete in this sport.

q.e: The Montgomery Biscuits are a Double-A baseball team (Tampa Bay Rays affiliate).

q: What animal is depicted on the official state Seal of the State of Indiana?

q.e: The Indiana state seal shows a woodsman chopping trees while a buffalo flees across the plains.

q: What is the state beverage of the U.S. state of Indiana?

q.e: Water has been Indiana's official state beverage since 2023. Earlier it was ... none.

q: What sport does the team Indiana Pacers compete in?

q.e: The Indiana Pacers are an NBA basketball team in Indianapolis, with Reggie Miller their star.

q: Which of these statements about cirrus clouds is true?
They bring rain if they darken in colour.
They are fluffy or woolly in appearance.

q.e: Cirrus clouds are thin, wispy clouds high in the sky. They often mean fair weather, but can mean a weather change is coming in 12-24 hours.

q: The term Mardi Gras refers to the Carnival celebrations, beginning on or after Epiphany. What does Mardi Gras mean in French?

q.e: Mardi Gras translates literally to Fat Tuesday in French, reflecting the historical tradition of consuming rich, fatty foods before the fasting period of Lent begins on Ash Wednesday.

q: Venetian masks, one of the main features of the famous Carnival of Venice, feature prominently in which of these movies?

q.e: Stanley Kubrick's Eyes Wide Shut (1999) features a masked orgy scene, using Venetian masks.

q: What does the name of the Brazilian resort Jericoacoara mean?

q.e: Jericoacoara's name derives from the Tupi for "hole of the turtles." It's a resort in Ceará, Brazil.

q: What is odd about the face on the $10 bill?
Its the only US bill where the portrait faces to the left.
Its the only US bill which does not feature a President.
Its the only US bill where the portrait faces to the right.
The image is tinted with red lines.

q.e: On the $10 bill, Alexander Hamilton is said to be the only portrait facing left. The other portraits face right.

q: What happened to US currency in 1928?
All bills were re-sized to be the same size.
Latin writing was replaced by English words.
Oval frames were placed around each image.
Silver certificates were added to each bill.

q.e: In 1928, the US reduced the size of paper money by about a third to the size it still has today.

q: In 2007, Venezuelan president Hugo Chavez did something that made his country unique. What was it?
He declared a new time zone.
He created a new currency, the Orinoco.
He created an art museum for children only.

q.e: In 2007 Hugo Chávez moved Venezuela's clocks back by 30 minutes, creating UTC−4:30, unique in the world at the time. It was reversed in 2016.

q: In 2008, Chile established a partnership on trade, environment and agriculture with what US state?

q.e: In 2008, Chile and California (under Governor Schwarzenegger) signed a partnership on trade, environment and agriculture.

q: At the beginning of the 21st Century, Ecuador changed its official currency to what?

q.e: Ecuador officially adopted the US dollar in September 2000 to stabilize an economy crippled by hyperinflation. It replaced the Ecuadorian sucre, which had served as the country's national currency since 1884.

q: What was scheduled to occur in Guyana in 2010 for the first time in over a decade?

q.e: Guyana held local government elections in 2010 for the first time since 1994. The elections had been postponed repeatedly.

q: The Oyapock River Bridge, built in 2010, is the first land connection between Brazil and what other country?

q.e: The Oyapock River Bridge connects Brazil with French Guiana (France), the only land link between Brazil and the EU.

q: This happened for the first time in 1913 in the United States and in 2001 in Argentina.

q.e: In the US, the 17th Amendment (1913) established direct election of senators. Argentina did the same in 2001.

q: What form of government does Malta have?

q.e: Malta is a parliamentary republic, and since 1964 independent from Britain, and a republic since 1974.

q: When is the traditional Maltese Carnival held every year?

q.e: Malta's Carnival is held in the days before Ash Wednesday, with parades in Valletta.

q: What nickname has been given to Malta, partly because of the possible Greek origin of its name?

q.e: Malta may be named from the Greek "Melite," meaning "honey," so it's the "Land of honey". It's known for its bees.

q: What are the colors of the national flag of Malta?

q.e: Malta's flag is white and red, with the George Cross in the corner.

q: Which of these is not true about the Bolivian city of Potosi?
Its population has grown steadily since 1900.
It was founded because of the local silver mine.
It is the highest city in the world.
It is renowned for its colonial architecture.

q.e: Potosí, Bolivia, boomed in the 1600s, when it had 150,000-200,000 people, thanks to silver, and its population has since declined and varied.

q: Which of these countries does not border Bolivia?

q.e: Bolivia borders Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina, Chile and Peru. Uruguay is not a neighbor.

q: Due to its irregular and significant movement of sediment, this seabed feature should be avoided for pipelaying.

q.e: Sand waves migrate and change the seabed, so they should be avoided when laying pipelines.

q: Nelson Mandela, the 1993 Nobel Peace Prize laureate, was President of this African country from 10 May 1994 to 14 June 1999.

q.e: Nelson Mandela was inaugurated as South Africa's first Black head of state in May 1994, marking the end of apartheid. He had spent 27 years imprisoned before negotiating the transition to multiracial democracy.

q: What President of the United States was honored with the Nobel Prize for Peace in 2002?

q.e: Former US President Jimmy Carter won the 2002 Nobel Peace Prize.

q: What civil rights advocate received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964?

q.e: Martin Luther King, Jr. received the Nobel Peace Prize on October 14, 1964, for his nonviolent campaign against racial injustice. At 35 years old, he was the youngest individual recipient of the prize at the time.

q: Which of these United States citizens received the Nobel Prize for Peace in 2009?

q.e: Barack Obama was awarded the 2009 Nobel Peace Prize during his first year in office for his extraordinary efforts to strengthen international diplomacy and cooperation.

q: When did the legal separation of the American colonies from Great Britain occur?

q.e: The Second Continental Congress voted for independence on 2 July 1776, and adopted the Declaration on 4 July.

q: In June 1776, this statesman from Virginia proposed a resolution of independence which led to the United States Declaration of Independence.

q.e: On 7 June 1776, Richard Henry Lee of Virginia proposed that the colonies "are, and of right ought to be, free and independent states". It led to the Declaration.

q: What do Presidents John Adams, Thomas Jefferson and James Monroe have in common?
They were all born on 4 July.
They all signed the Declaration of Independence.

q.e: Adams and Jefferson both died on 4 July 1826 (the 50th anniversary), and Monroe on 4 July 1831. Coolidge was born on 4 July.

q: Which of these Founding Fathers did not sign the Declaration of Independence?

q.e: George Washington did not sign the Declaration of Independence because he was in New York commanding the Continental Army when it was signed in July and August 1776.

q: Who portrayed an anti-war activist and veteran, born July 4, 1946?

q.e: Tom Cruise played Ron Kovic (born 4 July 1946), a Vietnam veteran turned anti-war activist, in Born on the Fourth of July.

q: What treaty signed in signed on September 3, 1783 formally ended the American Revolutionary War?

q.e: The Treaty of Paris was signed on September 3, 1783, by representatives of King George III and the United States, officially recognizing American independence and establishing national borders.

q: In what country is January 1 known as Capodanno?

q.e: "Capodanno" is the Italian word for New Year's Day (1 January), literally "head of the year."

q: Which of these countries does not have a Don river flowing through it?

q.e: A river Don flows through Russia, England and Scotland, but not Italy.

q: Lake Saimaa, the fourth-largest lake in Europe, is located in this country.

q.e: Lake Saimaa, Finland's largest lake, is the fourth-largest in Europe. It's home to the Saimaa ringed seal.

q: In which country do you find Masuria, sometimes called the Land of a Thousand Lakes?

q.e: Masuria, in northeastern Poland, has over 2,000 lakes, and is known as the Land of a Thousand Lakes.

q: Which is the first of the Black Panther Partys 10 point program?
We Want Freedom. We Want Power To Determine The Destiny Of Our Black Community
We Want Decent Housing Fit For The Shelter Of Human Beings
We Want An Immediate End To Police Brutality And Murder Of Black People
We Want All Black Men To Be Exempt From Military Service

q.e: The Black Panther Party's Ten-Point Program begins with: "We want freedom. We want power to determine the destiny of our Black community."

q: What was Huey P. Newton charged with on October 28th, 1967?

q.e: On 28 October 1967, Huey Newton was arrested after a shootout in Oakland in which police officer John Frey died. Newton was charged with murder.

q: The name of Chicago comes from the Miami-Illinois expression shikaakwa. What does it mean?

q.e: The Miami-Illinois term shikaakwa refers to the striped skunk or the pungent wild leek (Allium tricoccum) that grew abundantly along the Chicago River. French explorers transcribed this native word into Chicago in the late 17th century.

q: Which of these movies was set in Chicago, Illinois, USA?

q.e: My Best Friend's Wedding (1997) is set in Chicago, in places like Navy Pier and the Chicago River.

q: What is depicted on the national flag of Saudi Arabia?
A crescent moon and a star

q.e: The green flag features a white horizontal sword symbolizing the House of Saud's military strength and justice, set beneath the Shahada, the Islamic creed. The crescent moon and star appears on many other Muslim-majority flags, such as Turkey and Pakistan, but not Saudi Arabia.

q: Which of these countries does not share a border with Saudi Arabia?

q.e: Saudi Arabia borders Jordan, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar, UAE, Oman and Yemen. Iran is across the Persian Gulf.

q: What is the traditional color of the agal, the accessory worn by Arabs in order to keep the traditional headdress called Keffiyeh in place?

q.e: The agal is a black cord that holds a keffiyeh in place on the head. It is usually black.

q: The national anthem of Saudi Arabia is called Aash Al Maleek. What does this mean in English?

q.e: Saudi Arabia's anthem "Aash Al Maleek" means "Long Live the King."

q: The name of the U.S. state of Nebraska is believed to have originated from a phrase meaning which of the following?

q.e: "Nebraska" comes from an Otoe or Omaha word meaning "flat water," for the Platte River.

q: What is the name of the capital city of the U.S. state of Nebraska?

q.e: Originally called Lancaster, Nebraska's capital was renamed Lincoln in 1867 after President Abraham Lincoln. Omaha is Nebraska's largest city, and Pierre is the capital of South Dakota.

q: Which of these is a nickname given to the U.S. state of Nebraska?

q.e: Nebraska is the "Beef State" and also "The Cornhusker State."

q: What is the state mammal of the U.S. state of Nebraska?

q.e: The white-tailed deer is Nebraska's state mammal, adopted in 1981.

q: What is the state beverage of the U.S. state of Nebraska?

q.e: Milk is the official state beverage of Nebraska (and many other states).

q: How many distinct seasons are there in Cambodia?

q.e: Cambodia has two seasons: a rainy season (May-October) and a dry season (November-April).

q: What is the title of the national anthem of the Kingdom of Cambodia?

q.e: Cambodia's national anthem is "Nokor Reach" (Royal Kingdom), adopted in 1941 and revived in 1993.

q: What part of the body is considered to contain the soul according to Cambodian beliefs and tradition?

q.e: In Cambodia, the head is considered the most sacred part of the body, and the seat of the soul, so don't touch someone's head.

q: Which of these colors is not present on the national flag of the Kingdom of Cambodia?

q.e: Cambodia's flag has red and blue stripes, with a white image of Angkor Wat. Yellow isn't in the design.

q: What is the literal translation of the Japanese word geisha?

q.e: "Geisha" (芸者) means "person of the arts" (gei = art, sha = person), not a courtesan.

q: What color do maiko, or apprentice geisha, sometimes paint their teeth in their last stage of training?

q.e: Some maiko blacken their teeth (ohaguro) in the final stage of training before becoming geisha, though it's mostly a thing of the past.

q: Unpainted area with what shape do geisha traditionally leave on their nape when applying their makeup?

q.e: Geisha leave a W-shaped (or V-shaped) unpainted patch on the nape of the neck, considered erotic. It's said to look like a "w" or double stripe.

q: After what period of work does a maiko, or an apprentice geisha, change her heavy makeup with a more natural one?

q.e: Maiko wear heavy white makeup for years before becoming geiko. The move to more natural makeup comes at the "erikae" ceremony, usually after about 5 years.

q: What was the US state of Kansas named after?

q.e: Kansas is named for the Kansas River, which in turn is named for the Kansa (Kaw) people.

q: Which of these is a baseball team from Kansas?

q.e: The Kansas City T-Bones were an independent baseball team in the American Association, in Kansas City, Kansas.

q: What is the color of the official state flag of Kansas, USA?

q.e: The Kansas state flag has a dark blue field with the state seal and a sunflower on top.

q: Mozambique was colonized in 1505 by which European country?

q.e: Portuguese explorer Pêro da Covilhã first reached Mozambique in 1489, leading to centuries of Portuguese rule until the country gained independence in 1975.

q: What is the most widely spoken language in Mozambique?

q.e: Portuguese is Mozambique's official language, spoken by about half the population as first or second language. Emakhuwa is spoken most as a native tongue.

q: What is the capital and largest city of the U.S. state of Georgia?

q.e: Atlanta became the state capital of Georgia in 1868, succeeding Milledgeville. Charlotte and Raleigh are major cities in North Carolina, while Columbia is the capital of South Carolina.

q: What are the colors of the official state flag of the U.S. state of Georgia?

q.e: Georgia's current flag (2003) has a blue canton and red-and-white stripes, with a gold state seal.

q: Which of these American Presidents was born in Plains, Georgia, USA?

q.e: Jimmy Carter was born in Plains, Georgia, in 1924, and returned there after his presidency. Ronald Reagan was born in Tampico, Illinois, while Richard Nixon was born in Yorba Linda, California.

q: In what sport do the Atlanta Hawks team from Georgia, USA compete?

q.e: The Atlanta Hawks play in the NBA, at State Farm Arena.

q: NDjamena is the capital of this African country.

q.e: N'Djamena is the capital of Chad, in Central Africa. It was Fort-Lamy until 1973.

q: What are the colors of the national flag of Argentina?

q.e: Argentina's flag is light blue and white with the "Sun of May" in the center.

q: The Falklands War was fought in 1982 between Argentina and this country.

q.e: The 10-week conflict began on April 2, 1982, when Argentine forces invaded the British-held islands, ending with an Argentine surrender on June 14, 1982.

q: At the age of 15 Eva Peron went to Buenos Aires to pursue a career as which of the following?

q.e: Eva Perón left her rural home at 15 to become an actress in Buenos Aires. She became First Lady in 1946 and died of cancer in 1952.

q: What is the official language in Sudan as enacted by the laws of the country?

q.e: Arabic and English are both official languages of Sudan under its 2005 interim constitution.

q: What does the name of Sudan mean in Arabic?

q.e: "Sudan" comes from "bilad as-sudan," "land of the blacks."

q: The national anthem of Sudan is entitled Nahnu Jund Allah Jund Al-watan. What does this mean in Arabic?
We are the army of God and of our land.
This is the land and the people of God.
God has chosen us for his army.

q.e: "Nahnu Jund Allah, Jund al-Watan" means "We are the soldiers of God, soldiers of our land." It's Sudan's anthem.

q: What are colors of the outfits of the national football (soccer) team of Sudan, when playing home and away respectively?

q.e: Sudan's national football team plays in red at home and white away, which matches the colors of its flag.

q: How many Eastern Orthodox monasteries are there in the Holy Mountain in Greece?

q.e: Mount Athos has 20 Eastern Orthodox monasteries. Women are not allowed to enter.

q: In Greek Mythology Athos was the name of which of the following?

q.e: In Greek myth Athos was a Thracian giant who threw a boulder at Poseidon, and it became Mount Athos.

q: In what century was the Holy Mountain in Greece conquered by the Ottoman Empire?

q.e: The Ottoman Empire took Mount Athos in the 15th century (1430), but the monasteries kept their autonomy.

q: What type of governmental control does Ecuador have?

q.e: Ecuador is a presidential republic, with the president as both head of state and head of government.

q: What is the title of the national anthem of he Socialist Republic of Vietnam?

q.e: "Tiến Quân Ca" ("Army March") is the national anthem of Vietnam, written in 1944 by Văn Cao.

q: The cultivation of what plant has been a basic sustenance for Vietnams population for millennia?

q.e: Rice has been Vietnam's staple for thousands of years. The country is one of the world's top rice exporters.

q: What is the official language for the territory of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam?

q.e: Vietnamese is the official language of Vietnam, spoken by about 85% of the people.

q: What are the colors on the national flag of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam?

q.e: Vietnam's flag is red with a yellow five-pointed star.

q: What type of game is the traditional Vietnamese game called O an quan?

q.e: Ô ăn quan is a traditional Vietnamese board game that is a type of mancala game, played on a board with small stones and larger "mandarin" pieces.

q: Which of these famous Cubans was born in Santa Clara, the capital city of the Cuban province of Villa Clara?

q.e: Santa Clara, Cuba, is known for the Che Guevara Mausoleum. The question's answer is "all of them" in its list of Santa Clara natives.

q: What are the colors of the national flag of Jamaica?

q.e: Jamaica's flag is a gold diagonal cross dividing black and green triangles.

q: What city is the capital and the largest city of Jamaica?

q.e: Kingston was founded in 1692 after an earthquake devastated the nearby pirate hub of Port Royal, eventually becoming Jamaica's capital in 1872.

q: What is the official language spoken in Jamaica, which was formerly a Spanish possession known as Santiago?

q.e: English is Jamaica's official language. Jamaican Patois is widely spoken. Spain named the island Santiago.

q: The indigenous Taino inhabitants of Jamaica named the island Xaymaca. What does this word mean?

q.e: The Taíno name "Xaymaca" is usually translated as "land of wood and water" or "land of springs".

q: What is the largest and highest mountain range on the island of Jamaica?

q.e: The Blue Mountains, with Blue Mountain Peak (2,256 m), are the highest range in Jamaica and grow famous Blue Mountain coffee.

q: Of what descent is the predominant population of Jamaica according to the 2001 census?

q.e: Most Jamaicans (about 92%) are of African descent, descended from enslaved people brought for sugar plantations.

q: What bird is the national bird of Jamaica as well as one of the symbols of the country?

q.e: The Doctor Bird (red-billed streamertail hummingbird) is Jamaica's national bird, found only there.

q: What is the literal meaning of the phrase sado or chado, which refers to the traditional Japanese tea ceremony?

q.e: The word combines 'cha' (tea) with 'do' (way or path), originating from the Chinese concept of Tao. The philosophy emphasizes harmony, respect, purity, and tranquility in the ceremonial preparation and presentation of matcha.

q: What item from the Japanese tea ceremony equipment is the chakin?

q.e: A chakin is a small white linen cloth used to wipe the tea bowl in the Japanese tea ceremony.

q: What do the host and the guest receiving the tea bowl traditionally do at the Japanese tea ceremony?

q.e: At the tea ceremony the host and guests bow to each other and the guest bows when receiving the tea bowl.

q: The word chabana, which is related to the traditional Japanese ceremony, refers to which of the following?

q.e: Chabana (茶花) is the simple flower arrangement placed in the tea room for the Japanese tea ceremony.

q: What is sometimes served along with the thick tea called koicha at the Japanese tea ceremony?

q.e: At a Japanese tea ceremony, a tobacco tray (tabako-bon) is sometimes put out, and sweets are served with the thick tea (koicha) too.

q: What is the state animal of the U.S. state of New Jersey?

q.e: The horse is the state animal of New Jersey, since 1977.

q: What important law was passed in New Jersey on December 17, 2007, by Governor Corzine?
Ban on smoking in public places

q.e: On 17 December 2007, Governor Jon Corzine signed a law abolishing the death penalty in New Jersey, the first state to do so by legislation since the 1970s.

q: What is the state flower of the U.S. state of New Jersey?

q.e: The common meadow violet is New Jersey's state flower (since 1971), and the purple violet is the state flower of several states.

q: New Jersey remained the only U.S. state to lack which of the following?

q.e: New Jersey does not have an official state song, although it has a state anthem? The state hasn't adopted one.
Burg Eltz is a medieval castle in the Eltz Forest between Koblenz and Trier, Germany. It has been owned by the same family for 33 generations.

q: What is the English title of the national anthem of Sri Lanka?

q.e: Sri Lanka's anthem is "Sri Lanka Matha" ("Mother Sri Lanka"), adopted in 1951.

q: What animal is depicted on the national flag of Sri Lanka?

q.e: The Sri Lankan flag has a golden lion holding a sword, on a maroon background.

q: Sri Lanka is known as one of the largest producers of which of the following?

q.e: Sri Lanka is the world's fourth-largest tea producer, renowned globally for Ceylon tea, named after the country's former colonial moniker. British planter James Taylor established the island's first commercial tea plantation in 1867.

q: The Brazilian town of Paraty was founded by Portuguese colonizers. What does the name of the town mean in the Tupi language?

q.e: "Paraty" derives from the Tupi word for a type of fish (mullet), and the town's name is often given as "river of fish".

q: In what fairy tale does Kays grandmother describe snow flakes as white bees swarming?

q.e: In Hans Christian Andersen's The Snow Queen (1844), Kay's grandmother describes the snowflakes as "white bees".

q: The official state motto of the U.S. state of Montana is Oro y Plata. What does this mean in Spanish?

q.e: Montana's state motto, "Oro y Plata," means "Gold and Silver" in Spanish. It refers to mining.

q: What 1994 Academy Award-winning movie was set in the U.S. state of Montana?

q.e: Legends of the Fall (1994), starring Brad Pitt, was set in Montana and won the Oscar for Best Cinematography.

q: The island of Java is part of the territory of which country?

q.e: Java is Indonesia's most populous island, home to more than half of the nation's roughly 275 million residents as well as its capital, Jakarta.

q: Which European language is the most widely spoken non-native language on the island of Bali?

q.e: English is the most widely spoken foreign language in Bali, which is a major tourist destination.

q: Which crop is most widely cultivated on the island of Bali?

q.e: Rice paddies cover much of Bali's cultivated land. The terraces at Jatiluwih are a UNESCO site.

q: Which of these is the official language of Algeria?

q.e: Arabic and Tamazight (Berber) are Algeria's official languages. French is widely used.

q: The name of Algeria is derived from which of the following?

q.e: The name Algeria comes from Algiers (al-Jazāʾir, "the islands"), the capital city.

q: What does the term rai, which is associated with Algerian culture, denote?

q.e: Raï is a popular music genre from Algeria, from Oran in the 1920s. Cheb Khaled is its best-known star.

q: What is the national motto of the Republic of Colombia?

q.e: Colombia's national motto is "Libertad y Orden" ("Liberty and Order").

q: What are the colors of the national flag of the Republic of Colombia?

q.e: Colombia's flag has horizontal bands of yellow (double-width), blue and red. Venezuela and Ecuador use the same colors, from Gran Colombia.

q: What is the official language of Colombia?

q.e: Spanish is Colombia's official language, and Colombia has the world's second-largest number of Spanish speakers after Mexico.

q: What does the name of Malaysia mean?

q.e: "Malaysia" derives from "Malay", with the name "Malayu". One theory links it to a Sanskrit word for hill/mountain, "malaya".

q: The national anthem of Malaysia is entitled Negaraku. What does this mean?

q.e: "Negaraku" means "My Country". The tune is the same as "Mamula Moon" and the French "La Rosalie".

q: Why is it difficult to find ones way around Tokyo?
Only Japanese is allowed on direction signs and place names.
There are no accurate maps of Tokyo.
Most Japanese are rather rude to outsiders and dislike giving directions.

q.e: Most of Tokyo's streets have no names. Addresses refer to districts and numbered blocks, which makes it tricky to navigate.

q: There is strong competition to be admitted to this prestigious Japanese university, located in Tokyo and established in 1877.

q.e: The University of Tokyo (Todai), established in 1877, is Japan's most prestigious and selective university.

q: What is the name of the Tokyo professional baseball team?

q.e: The Yomiuri Giants are Tokyo's best-known pro baseball team. The Yakult Swallows also play in Tokyo.

q: What is the official language adopted by the government of Venezuela?

q.e: Spanish is Venezuela's official language. Indigenous languages are also officially recognized.

q: What form of governmental control has Venezuela established?

q.e: Venezuela is a federal presidential republic, led by a president who is both head of state and government.

q: What is Venezuela named after according to a popular theory?

q.e: Venezuela probably means "Little Venice," a name given by Amerigo Vespucci in 1499 after stilt houses in Lake Maracaibo reminded him of Venice.

q: What are the basic colors of the national flag of Venezuela?

q.e: Venezuela's flag has yellow, blue and red stripes, with a ring of eight stars on the blue.

q: HuangShan is located in the southern part of Anhui Province in eastern China. What is HuangShan?

q.e: Huangshan (黄山) means "Yellow Mountain." It's famed for granite peaks, hot springs and pines in Anhui, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: Almost all roofs in the Forbidden City are this color.

q.e: Roofs in the Forbidden City are yellow, the imperial color. Only a few buildings have other colors.

q: What is the nickname of the ancient Chinese city Pingyao?

q.e: Pingyao's ancient city is called "Turtle City" because its walls resemble a turtle. It's a UNESCO site in Shanxi.

q: According to the most popular theory, the U.S. state of Maine was named after which of the following.

q.e: Maine may be named after the French province of Maine, probably in honor of Queen Henrietta Maria. Another idea is the "main" land.

q: What nickname has been given to the U.S. state of Maine?

q.e: Maine is known as The Pine Tree State because white pine forests cover the vast majority of its land. The Green Mountain State is Vermont, and The Granite State is New Hampshire.

q: The Latin state motto of the U.S. state of Maine is Dirigo. What does this mean?

q.e: Maine's motto "Dirigo" means "I lead" or "I direct" in Latin.

q: Many of the novels of this popular author are set in the U.S. state of Maine.

q.e: Stephen King was born in Portland, Maine, and has set dozens of his stories in the state, frequently inventing fictional towns like Derry, Castle Rock, and Jerusalem's Lot. Mark Twain, by contrast, is famously linked to Missouri.

q: What is the largest city in the U.S. state of Maine?

q.e: Portland is the largest city in Maine. Augusta is the capital.

q: What founding father considered the turkey a much more respectable bird than the bald eagle?

q.e: Benjamin Franklin wrote in a 1784 letter that the turkey was "a much more respectable bird" than the bald eagle, but he never proposed it as national bird.

q: Who captained the Mayflower on the transatlantic voyage from Southampton, England to Plymouth, Massachusetts?

q.e: Captain Christopher Jones commanded the Mayflower, which crossed from Plymouth, England, to Massachusetts in 1620.

q: What is the nickname of Arkansas Techs mens athletic teams?

q.e: Arkansas Tech University's men's teams are the "Wonder Boys" and the women's teams are the "Golden Suns."

q: What is the University of Arkansas at Fort Smith nicknamed?

q.e: The University of Arkansas at Fort Smith teams are the Lions.

q: What is/are the color/s of Hendrix College?

q.e: Hendrix College's colors are orange and black, and its teams are the Warriors.

q: What is the nickname of Ouachita Baptist Universitys athletic teams?

q.e: Ouachita Baptist University's teams are the Tigers, in Arkadelphia, Arkansas.

q: Powering minds is the motto of what Arkansas school?

q.e: Arkansas State University uses the slogan "Powering Minds" in its marketing.

q: What kind of islands are there around Phuket Island?

q.e: Phuket is surrounded by coral islands and reefs, like Phi Phi and Racha, in the Andaman Sea.

q: What is the translation of the national motto of the Republic of South Africa, !ke e: ǀxarra �ke?

q.e: South Africa's motto "!ke e: ǀxarra ǁke," in the extinct ǀXam language, means "Diverse people unite".

q: South Africa is among the top ten producers in the world of which of the following?

q.e: South Africa is one of the top ten wine producers in the world, usually around 7th-9th, making wine since 1659.

q: What is the most popular sport among the people of South Africa?

q.e: Soccer is South Africa's most popular sport, though rugby and cricket are also big.

q: Which of these airports was featured in Season 5 of the television drama series 24?

q.e: Season 5 of 24 shows scenes shot at LA/Ontario International Airport, which doubled for other airports.

q: What airport was renamed in 1979 to honor actor John Wayne?

q.e: Orange County Airport (SNA) was renamed John Wayne Airport in 1979, after the actor's death. A statue of him is outside.

q: What are the colors of the national flag of the Republic of Peru, adopted in 1825?

q.e: Peru's flag is red-white-red vertical stripes, with the coat of arms optional on the white stripe.

q: What is the official language spoken by the citizens of the Republic of Peru?

q.e: Spanish is Peru's main official language. Quechua and Aymara are also official.

q: What is the name of the national anthem of the Republic of Peru, adopted in 1821?
We are free, we shall always be so

q.e: Peru's anthem begins "Somos libres, seámoslo siempre" ("We are free, let us always be so").

q: What South American country borders Peru to the east?

q.e: Brazil borders Peru to the east. Peru also borders Ecuador, Colombia, Bolivia and Chile.

q: What type of government does the Republic of Peru have?

q.e: Peru is a presidential republic, in which the president serves as head of state and government.

q: What is the national motto of San Marino?

q.e: San Marino's motto is "Libertas" (Liberty), and it claims to be the world's oldest republic.

q: The national motto of Wales is Cymru am byth. What does this mean?

q.e: "Cymru am byth" means "Wales forever" in Welsh.

q: Mir welle bleiwe wat mir sinn is the national motto of Luxembourg. What does this mean in English?
We wish to remain what we are.
Our country means the world to us.
Independence is what makes us who we are.

q.e: Luxembourg's motto "Mir wëlle bleiwe wat mir sinn" means "We want to remain what we are."

q: The national motto of the Republic of Kenya is Harambee. What is the meaning of this Swahili expression in English?

q.e: Kenya's motto, "Harambee," is Swahili for "pull together" and refers to community self-help.

q: Which of these is the national motto of Cuba?
After the Good Lord, we love the Earth

q.e: Cuba's motto "Patria o muerte" ("Homeland or death") was popularized by Fidel Castro after the 1959 revolution.

q: What does the name of Iraq mean in Arabic?

q.e: "Iraq" (al-ʻIrāq) means "the shore" or "the edge" in Arabic, or "well-rooted" in another reading.

q: What type of governmental control has Iraq established?

q.e: Iraq is a federal parliamentary republic since the 2005 constitution.

q: The official motto of Iraq is Allahu Akbar, and it is emblazoned on the national flag of the country. What does the motto mean?

q.e: "Allahu Akbar" means "God is the greatest" in Arabic and is written on Iraq's flag.

q: What animal is depicted on the national coat of arms of Iraq?

q.e: Iraq's coat of arms shows the Eagle of Saladin. Its flag is red, white and black with green Arabic script.

q: What are the basic colors of the national flag of Iraq?

q.e: Iraq's flag is a horizontal tricolor of red, white and black, with the green takbir in Arabic.

q: How long did the fight for Singapore last during WWII?

q.e: The Battle of Singapore lasted from 8 to 15 February 1942, about a week, ending with British surrender.

q: How long did Lee Kwan Yew serve as prime minister of Singapore?

q.e: Lee Kuan Yew served as Singapore's first prime minister from 1959 to 1990, 31 years. He died in 2015.

q: What is the name of the island on which the country known as Taiwan is situated?

q.e: Taiwan is on the island of Taiwan, formerly Formosa, off China's southeast coast.

q: What is the color of the national flag of Taiwan?

q.e: Taiwan's (ROC) flag is red with a blue canton holding a white sun with twelve rays.

q: The name Morocco originated from the Berber expression Mur-Akush,. What does it mean?

q.e: "Morocco" comes from Marrakesh, from a Berber phrase interpreted as "Land of God". The Arabic name is Al-Maghrib, "the west".

q: What is the official language spoken in Morocco?

q.e: Arabic and Amazigh (Berber) are Morocco's official languages. French is widely used in business.

q: In which water basin is the island of Ibiza located?

q.e: Ibiza is in the Mediterranean Sea, part of Spain's Balearic Islands.

q: Ibiza belongs to the Balearic Islands, an autonomous community of which European country?

q.e: Ibiza is one of Spain's Balearic Islands in the western Mediterranean, alongside Mallorca, Menorca, and Formentera. Although nearby Mediterranean islands like Sardinia belong to Italy, the Balearic archipelago has been part of Spain since medieval times.

q: Ibiza is most well-known for which of the following?

q.e: Ibiza is most famous for its nightlife, especially its electronic dance music clubs.

q: The island of Ibiza is unique in having which of the following?
