q: In Formula 1, the Virtual Safety Car was introduced following the fatal crash of which driver?

q.e: The Virtual Safety Car was introduced in Formula 1 after Jules Bianchi's fatal crash at the 2014 Japanese Grand Prix. It makes every driver slow down to a set pace while a hazard is cleared.

q: Which of these track-and-field events is NOT included in the Olympic men's decathlon?

q.e: The men's decathlon includes shot put, discus, and javelin among its throwing events, but the hammer throw is excluded due to safety and logistical constraints.

q: Which NBA player has the most games played over the course of their career?

q.e: Robert Parish played 1,611 NBA games over 21 seasons and held the record for most games for decades. Newer players such as LeBron James have since challenged his mark.

q: Which darts player has won the most World Championship titles?

q.e: Phil 'The Power' Taylor dominated professional darts, winning a record 16 World Championships between 1990 and 2013 across both the BDO and PDC organizations.

q: Hockey player Wayne Gretzky was born in what Canadian province?

q.e: Wayne Gretzky was born in Brantford, Ontario, in 1961. He learned to skate on a backyard rink that his father flooded every winter.

q: At which bridge does the annual Oxford and Cambridge boat race start?

q.e: The Oxford-Cambridge Boat Race starts at Putney Bridge and finishes near Chiswick Bridge in Mortlake, covering about 4.2 miles of the Thames. The tradition goes back to 1829.

q: In what year did Steaua București win the European Cup, actual UEFA Champions League, against FC Barcelona?

q.e: Steaua Bucharest won the 1986 European Cup by beating Barcelona on penalties in Seville after a 0-0 draw. Their goalkeeper, Helmuth Duckadam, saved all four Barcelona penalties.

q: What national team won the 2016 edition of UEFA European Championship?

q.e: Portugal defeated host nation France 1-0 after extra time thanks to a 109th-minute strike by substitute Eder, earning their first major international trophy.

q: Which professional wrestler fell from the rafters to his death during a live Pay-Per-View event in 1999?

q.e: Owen Hart died at the WWF's Over the Edge event in Kansas City on May 23, 1999, when a harness release failed during a stunt to lower him into the ring from the rafters. It led to a lot of discussion about safety in wrestling.

q: What is Tiger Woods' all-time best career golf-score?

q.e: Tiger Woods' lowest competitive round is generally cited as 61. A typical tournament win takes four rounds in the high 60s.

q: Who won the 2018 Monaco Grand Prix?

q.e: Daniel Ricciardo won the 2018 Monaco Grand Prix for Red Bull even though a power problem cut his engine's output in the middle of the race. He kept control to hold off Sebastian Vettel.

q: Which country did Kabaddi, a contact sport involving tackling, originate from?

q.e: Kabaddi originated in ancient India, where it was played as a combat preparation game, and it became an official medal sport at the Asian Games starting in 1990 in Beijing.

q: Who was the topscorer for England national football team?

q.e: Wayne Rooney was England's all-time top scorer with 53 goals until Harry Kane passed him in 2023. Kane has kept adding to the record.

q: In what country were the 2014 Winter Olympics held in the town of Sochi?

q.e: The 2014 Winter Olympics took place in Sochi, Russia, a resort city on the coast of the Black Sea with alpine events hosted in the nearby Caucasus Mountains.

q: Which NBA player won Most Valuable Player for the 1999-2000 season?

q.e: Shaquille O'Neal won the 1999-2000 NBA MVP award with the Los Angeles Lakers, averaging about 30 points and 13 rebounds per game. He got all but one first-place vote.

q: Which country is hosting the 2022 FIFA World Cup?

q.e: Qatar hosted the 2022 World Cup, the first one in the Arab world and the first held in November and December to avoid the summer heat. Argentina, led by Lionel Messi, won the title.

q: The F1 season of 1994 is remembered for what tragic event?

q.e: Three-time world champion Ayrton Senna died on May 1, 1994, during the San Marino Grand Prix at Imola, just one day after Austrian driver Roland Ratzenberger was killed in qualifying.

q: What is the exact length of one non-curved part in Lane 1 of an Olympic Track?

q.e: On a standard 400 m running track, each straight is 84.39 m long in lane 1. The two curved sections make up the rest of the lap.

q: Who has played the most tournaments in the German national soccer team?

q.e: Lothar Matthäus played 150 times for Germany, a record for his country. He played in five World Cups and captained West Germany to the 1990 title.

q: Which of the following player scored a hat-trick during their Manchester United debut?

q.e: Wayne Rooney scored a hat-trick on his Manchester United debut against Fenerbahçe in 2004, just after joining from Everton at age 18. It's one of the most famous debuts in the club's history.

q: Which of these countries' national teams qualified for the 2018 FIFA World Cup in Russia?

q.e: Tunisia qualified for the 2018 World Cup in Russia as one of Africa's five representatives. Other qualifiers from the continent were Egypt, Morocco, Nigeria and Senegal.

q: What is the oldest team in the NFL?

q.e: Founded in 1898 as the Morgan Athletic Club in Chicago, the Arizona Cardinals are the oldest continuously operating professional American football club in the NFL.

q: Which of these Russian cities did NOT contain a stadium that was used in the 2018 FIFA World Cup?

q.e: The 2018 World Cup was played in 11 Russian cities, including Moscow, Saint Petersburg, Kazan and Sochi. Vladivostok, on the Pacific coast, was not among them.

q: What tool lends it's name to a last-stone advantage in an end in Curling?

q.e: In curling, the hammer refers to the final stone thrown in an end, which provides a major scoring advantage. The term comes from the idea of pounding down the final shot.

q: Which year was the third Super Bowl held?

q.e: Super Bowl III was played in January 1969, and the New York Jets of the AFL upset the heavily favored Baltimore Colts. Jets quarterback Joe Namath had famously guaranteed a win.

q: Who scored the injury time winning goal in the 1999 UEFA Champions League final between Manchester United and Bayern Munich?

q.e: Ole Gunnar Solskjær scored the winning goal in injury time at the 1999 Champions League final against Bayern Munich. United had trailed until the 91st minute and completed a famous treble that season.

q: Who is Manchester United's leading appearance maker?

q.e: Ryan Giggs holds the record for most Manchester United appearances, with 963 in more than 20 years. He won 13 Premier League titles with the club.

q: Which Italian footballer told Neuer where he's putting his shot and dragging it wide, during the match Italy-Germany, UEFA EURO 2016?

q.e: In the Euro 2016 quarterfinal shootout, Italy's Graziano Pellè told Manuel Neuer where he planned to shoot and then missed wide. Germany won the shootout 6-5 after a 1-1 draw.

q: In Canadian football, scoring a rouge is worth how many points?

q.e: In Canadian football a rouge is worth one point. It's scored when the ball is kicked into the opponent's end zone and isn't returned out.

q: Which female player won the gold medal of table tennis singles in 2016 Olympics Games?

q.e: Ding Ning of China won the women's singles table tennis gold at the 2016 Rio Olympics, beating her teammate Li Xiaoxia in the final. It completed her career Grand Slam.

q: With which doubles partner did John McEnroe have most success?

q.e: John McEnroe won most of his doubles titles with Peter Fleming, and the pair won seven Grand Slam doubles titles together. They were ranked the best team in the world in the early 1980s.
Thoroughbred horse racing earned the title The Sport of Kings because it was heavily patronized by British royalty and aristocracy, notably King Charles II in the 17th century.

q: In any programming language, what is the most common way to iterate through an array?

q.e: A "for" loop repeats a block of code once for each item or index in an array, which makes it the classic way to go through a list. Most languages also offer shortcuts like "for each" or "map".

q: In "Hexadecimal", what color would be displayed from the color code? "#00FF00"?

q.e: Hexadecimal color codes use the format RRGGBB, where the two digits represent red, green, and blue intensity from 00 to FF. In 00FF00, red and blue are set to zero while green is at maximum intensity (255), producing pure green.

q: The C programming language was created by this American computer scientist.

q.e: Dennis Ritchie created C between 1969 and 1973 at Bell Labs, where it was primarily developed to re-implement the Unix operating system. Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web.

q: According to the International System of Units, how many bytes are in a kilobyte of RAM?

q.e: In the International System of Units (SI), "kilo" means 1,000, so a kilobyte is 1,000 bytes. The count of 1,024 bytes is properly called a kibibyte, though many people still say kilobyte for it.
SSD stands for Solid State Drive, indicating that it relies on flash memory chips rather than the moving magnetic platters found in traditional hard disk drives (HDDs).

q: In computing, how many bits are in a nibble?

q.e: A nibble is a four-bit aggregation, precisely half of an eight-bit byte, often corresponding directly to a single hexadecimal digit.

q: Which computer hardware device provides an interface for all other connected devices to communicate?

q.e: The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects the processor, memory, storage and other parts so they can talk to each other. Everything else plugs into it.

q: What amount of bits commonly equals one byte?

q.e: A byte consists of 8 bits, an architecture standard popularized by the IBM System/360 in the 1960s. A 4-bit grouping is colloquially known as a nibble.

q: In web design, what does CSS stand for?

q.e: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets, first proposed by Håkon Wium Lie in 1994 to separate a web document's visual presentation from its HTML markup.
CMYK is the standard subtractive color model used in color printing, where the K stands for Key, which refers to the black plate that adds depth and fine detail.

q: What is the code name for the mobile operating system Android 7.0?

q.e: Android 7.0, released in 2016, was code-named Nougat. Google names its versions' sweet treats in alphabetical order up to Android 9, after which it switched to plain numbers.

q: In networking, what does OSPF stand for?

q.e: OSPF stands for Open Shortest Path First, a routing protocol that lets routers share information about their links and calculate the shortest path using Dijkstra's algorithm. It is widely used inside large company networks.

q: If you were to code software in this language you'd only be able to type 0's and 1's.

q.e: Binary code uses a base-2 numeral system consisting entirely of the digits 0 and 1 to represent machine instructions and data. Higher-level languages like Python and C++ use human-readable text that compilers translate into binary.

q: What is largely considered the precursor to the USB format?

q.e: USB, introduced in 1996, was designed to replace the many separate ports on older PCs. The PS/2 port, which IBM introduced in 1987 for keyboards and mice, is the one most often named as its predecessor.

q: Approximately how many Apple I personal computers were created?

q.e: About 200 Apple I computers were built by hand in 1976, mostly by Steve Wozniak, and roughly 175 were sold. It originally cost $666.66, and surviving units are now worth huge sums to collectors.

q: Moore's law originally stated that the number of transistors on a microprocessor chip would double every...

q.e: In 1965, Gordon Moore predicted that the number of transistors on a chip would double every year. In 1975 he revised it to every two years, and the idea became known as Moore's law.

q: Linus Torvalds created which of these?

q.e: Finnish software engineer Linus Torvalds released the initial version of the open-source Linux operating system kernel in September 1991. Python was created by Guido van Rossum.

q: What was the first commerically available computer processor?

q.e: The Intel 4004, released in 1971, was the first commercially available microprocessor. This 4-bit chip was first designed for a Busicom calculator.

q: Which coding language was the #1 programming language in terms of usage on GitHub in 2015?

q.e: JavaScript was the most-used language on GitHub in 2015. It runs in every web browser, which is a big reason for its popularity.

q: Which of the following is a personal computer made by the Japanese company Fujitsu?

q.e: The Fujitsu FM-7 was a home computer sold in Japan starting in 1982. Japanese companies like Fujitsu, NEC and Sharp had their own computer lines in the 1980s that never became popular in the West.

q: Which of the following languages is used as a scripting language in the Unity 3D game engine?

q.e: Unity games are scripted in C# (pronounced "C sharp"), Microsoft's object-oriented programming language. Earlier versions also supported a JavaScript-like language called UnityScript.

q: What was the name of the image that features as the default background wallpaper for Windows XP?

q.e: Bliss is an unedited photograph of green rolling hills and a blue sky taken by Charles O'Rear in 1996 in Sonoma County, California.

q: What did the name of the Tor Anonymity Network orignially stand for?

q.e: Tor originally stood for "The Onion Router". The name refers to wrapping your traffic in layers of encryption, like the layers of an onion, as it passes through several relays.

q: In the server hosting industry IaaS stands for...

q.e: IaaS is Infrastructure as a Service, where a company rents servers, storage and networking from a provider instead of buying them. Amazon Web Services' EC2 is a well-known example.

q: Generally, which component of a computer draws the most power?

q.e: The graphics card (GPU) usually draws the most power in a computer, especially during gaming or heavy rendering. Processors come second.

q: What five letter word is the motto of the IBM Computer company?

q.e: Thomas J. Watson introduced the motto 'THINK' in December 1911 while working at the National Cash Register Company, later taking it to C-T-R, which was renamed IBM in 1924. Apple later played on this motto with its famous 'Think Different' campaign.

q: When did the online streaming service "Mixer" launch?

q.e: Mixer began in 2016 as a streaming service called Beam, and was renamed Mixer in 2017 after Microsoft bought it. It shut down in 2020.

q: In programming, the ternary operator is mostly defined with what symbol(s)?

q.e: The ternary operator uses ?: and works like a short if/else: condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse. It is called "ternary" because it takes three operands.

q: Which of these programming languages is a low-level language?

q.e: Assembly language is a low-level language that maps almost one-to-one onto a processor's machine instructions. High-level languages such as Python or Java are easier for people to read and write.

q: What does the DOS in Microsoft's first operating system "MS-DOS" stand for?

q.e: MS-DOS stands for Microsoft Disk Operating System, which Microsoft originally adapted from 86-DOS (QDOS) and supplied for IBM personal computers starting in 1981.

q: In the programming language "Python", which of these statements would display the string "Hello World" correctly?

q.e: In Python, print("Hello World") displays the text. In Python 2 it was a statement without parentheses, but in Python 3 it became a regular function.

q: In programming, what do you call functions with the same name but different implementations?

q.e: Overloading means defining several functions with the same name but different parameters, and the compiler picks the right one for each call. Overriding is different: it replaces a parent class's method in a subclass.

q: What was Bitcoin's block size limit in 2010?

q.e: Bitcoin's block size limit was set to 1 MB in 2010, a cap that was added to prevent spam. It later became a hot debate about scaling.

q: .at is the top-level domain for what country?

q.e: The country code top-level domain .at belongs to Austria, derived from its Latin name Austria. Australia uses .au, Argentina uses .ar, and Angola uses .ao.

q: On which day did the World Wide Web go online?

q.e: The first web page went online at CERN on December 20, 1990, built by Tim Berners-Lee. The web opened to the general public in 1991.

q: The teapot often seen in many 3D modeling applications is called what?

q.e: The Utah teapot was modeled by Martin Newell at the University of Utah in 1975. It became a standard test object in 3D graphics because its curves are complex but easy to model.

q: Which of these people was NOT a founder of Apple Inc?

q.e: Apple was founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne. Jony Ive, who later designed products such as the iMac and iPhone, joined the company in 1992.

q: What type of sound chip does the Super Nintendo Entertainment System (SNES) have?

q.e: The SNES sound system used a Sony-designed chip, the SPC700, together with a sampler that played back short compressed sounds. That is why SNES music sounds like real instruments, rather than the simple beeps of earlier consoles.

q: What is the codename of the eighth generation Intel Core micro-architecture launched in October 2017?

q.e: Coffee Lake was the codename of Intel's eighth-generation Core processors, launched in October 2017. It was the first mainstream Intel desktop line to offer six cores.

q: What was the first company to use the term "Golden Master"?

q.e: "Golden Master" is the final version of software that is ready to be copied and sold. Apple used the term, which it still uses for its pre-release builds.

q: Which of these was the name of a bug found in April 2014 in the publicly available OpenSSL cryptography library?

q.e: Heartbleed, found in April 2014, was a serious flaw in OpenSSL's heartbeat feature that let attackers read memory from affected servers. It put passwords and encryption keys at risk across a large share of the web.

Radia Perlman invented the Spanning Tree Protocol in 1985 while working at Digital Equipment Corporation. It prevents loops in Ethernet networks, and she is sometimes called the "Mother of the Internet".

q: What was the name of the security vulnerability found in Bash in 2014?

q.e: Shellshock was a major flaw in the Bash command shell, disclosed in September 2014. It let attackers run commands on affected Unix, Linux and macOS systems.

q: What port does HTTP run on?

q.e: HTTP uses port 80 by default, while HTTPS uses port 443. A port number tells a computer which service a network connection is meant for.

q: What does the International System of Quantities refer 1024 bytes as?

q.e: The International System of Quantities uses "kibibyte" (KiB) for 1,024 bytes, with the "kilobyte" (kB) meaning 1,000 bytes. The binary prefixes were created in 1998 to end the confusion.

q: America Online (AOL) started out as which of these online service providers?

q.e: AOL began as Quantum Link, or Q-Link, a 1985 online service for the Commodore 64. The company became America Online in 1991.

q: Which of these is not a layer in the OSI model for data communications?

q.e: The OSI model has seven layers: physical, data link, network, transport, session, presentation and application. "Connection layer" isn't among them.

q: What major programming language does Unreal Engine 4 use?

q.e: Unreal Engine 4 is programmed mainly in C++, and it also has a visual scripting system called Blueprints. Many games on it mix the two.

q: What is the name of the process that sends one qubit of information using two bits of classical information?

q.e: Quantum teleportation transfers the state of one qubit using a shared entangled pair of particles plus two classical bits of information. It doesn't move matter, and it cannot send information faster than light.

q: CMOS is tech used for constructing integrated circuits. What does CMOS stand for?

q.e: CMOS stands for complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor, the technology used for most modern computer chips because it uses very little power when idle. It is also the name of the small memory chip that stored BIOS settings in older PCs.

q: What chess piece was on Paladins calling card?

q.e: Paladin, the hero of the Western Have Gun - Will Travel (1957-63), carried a calling card showing a white knight chess piece. It fit his role as a gentleman gunfighter for hire.

q: In Star Trek: The Next Generation, what is the name of Data's cat?

q.e: Data's orange tabby cat in Star Trek: The Next Generation is named Spot. The android's affection for his pet is a recurring way the show explores his humanity.

q: What is the name of Chris's brother in "Everybody Hates Chris"?

q.e: Drew is Chris's younger brother in Everybody Hates Chris, which is based on comedian Chris Rock's childhood in 1980s Brooklyn. Tonya is his sister, and Rock narrates the show.

q: In DuckTales, what is the name of the city where all the main characters live?

q.e: Duckburg was created by legendary comic artist Carl Barks in 1944 and serves as the hometown for Scrooge McDuck, Donald Duck, and Huey, Dewey, and Louie.

q: In the show "Tengen Toppa Gurren Lagann" what is the name of the character who force everyone to live underground?

q.e: Lordgenome, the Spiral King, rules the surface in Gurren Lagann and forces humans to live in underground villages. Simon and Kamina, the heroes, break out and challenge him.

q: Which show is known for the songs "You are a Pirate", "Cooking by the Book" and "We Are Number One"?

q.e: LazyTown is an Icelandic children's show created by Magnus Scheving. Songs from it, like "We Are Number One" sung by villain Robbie Rotten, became internet memes years later.

q: On the show "Rick and Morty", in episode "Total Rickall", who was a parasite?

q.e: In the Rick and Morty episode "Total Rickall", Pencilvester is one of the fake characters the alien parasites plant in the family's memories. The parasites imitate loved ones to feed on the family.

q: What is the name of the planet that the Doctor from television series "Doctor Who" comes from?

q.e: Gallifrey is the home world of the Time Lords, located in the constellation of Kasterborous. Skaro is the home planet of the Daleks, and Mondas is the original home of the Cybermen.

q: In which British seaside town was the BBC sitcom "Fawlty Towers" set?

q.e: John Cleese set Fawlty Towers in Torquay along the English Riviera, inspired by a stay at the town's Gleneagles Hotel where he observed real-life eccentric hotelier Donald Sinclair.

q: Who is the star of the AMC series Breaking Bad?

q.e: Walter White, played by Bryan Cranston, is a high school chemistry teacher who begins cooking methamphetamine after receiving a terminal lung cancer diagnosis.

q: Which Star Trek race advances itself through assimilation?

q.e: Introduced in Star Trek: The Next Generation in 1989, the Borg operate as a hive mind connected to a collective consciousness, forcibly assimilating individuals and technology with the phrase Resistance is futile.

q: Which character was played by Dustin Diamond in the sitcom 'Saved by the Bell'?

q.e: Dustin Diamond played the nerdy Samuel "Screech" Powers in Saved by the Bell, which ran from 1989 to 1992. He was one of the main cast in the whole series.

q: How many seasons did the Sci-Fi television show "Stargate Universe" have?

q.e: Stargate Universe lasted two seasons, 2009 to 2011, before it was cancelled. It was a darker, more serious entry in the Stargate franchise.

q: Who was the first ever actor to play "The Doctor" on "Doctor Who"?

q.e: William Hartnell originated the title role of Doctor Who when the BBC science-fiction series premiered in November 1963, starring until poor health forced his regeneration in 1966. Tom Baker portrayed the popular Fourth Doctor in the 1970s.

q: Which company has exclusive rights to air episodes of the "The Grand Tour"?

q.e: The Grand Tour, from Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May, streams on Amazon Prime Video. The trio started it in 2016 after leaving the BBC's Top Gear.

q: Which of these characters in "Stranger Things" has the power of Telekinesis?

q.e: Eleven has telekinesis and other psychic powers in Stranger Things, which she gained from experiments at Hawkins National Laboratory. Her abilities cause her nosebleeds when she overuses them.

q: What TV show is about a grandfather dragging his grandson around on adventures?

q.e: Rick and Morty premiered on Adult Swim in 2013, following the cynical mad scientist Rick Sanchez and his anxious grandson Morty Smith across interdimensional adventures.

q: What was the name of the the first episode of Doctor Who to air in 1963?

q.e: The first episode of Doctor Who, "An Unearthly Child", aired on the BBC on November 23, 1963. It was the first of four parts introducing the First Doctor and his granddaughter Susan.

q: In the television show Breaking Bad, what is the street name of Walter and Jesse's notorious product?

q.e: Walter White and Jesse Pinkman's distinctive crystal methamphetamine is known on the street as Blue Sky due to its sky-blue tint, an unintentional byproduct of Walter's chemical synthesis using methylamine. Baby Blue is the 1971 Badfinger song played during the series finale.

q: What episode of "Mr. Bean" saw him trying to prevent people from seeing him naked?

q.e: Mr. Bean, played by Rowan Atkinson, is a British comedy character who barely speaks and gets into awkward situations. The series ran from 1990 to 1995 and has been enjoyed around the world.

q: The first half-hour CGI cartoon, ReBoot, aired on which year?

q.e: ReBoot premiered in 1994 and is regarded as the first fully computer-animated TV series. Vancouver studio Mainframe Entertainment made it, and it is set inside a computer.

q: In Game of Thrones what is the name of Jon Snow's sword?

q.e: Longclaw is the Valyrian steel sword that Lord Commander Jeor Mormont gives Jon Snow in Game of Thrones. Its pommel was a bear, the symbol of House Mormont, until it was reforged as a wolf's head for Jon.

q: In the show "The Office" who does Michael Scott eventually end up with?

q.e: Michael Scott ends up with Holly Flax in The Office. She is a human resources rep who replaced Toby, and they eventually move away together.

q: Cesar Romero played which iconic Batman villain from the 1960's TV show?

q.e: Cesar Romero played the Joker in the 1960s Batman series with Adam West. He famously refused to shave his mustache, so makeup was painted over it.

q: Which movie served as the KTMA pilot episode for the show "Mystery Science Theater 3000"?
The Robot Vs. The Aztec Mummy

q.e: Mystery Science Theater 3000 started on a local Minnesota station, KTMA, in 1988, and the pilot episode used the film The Green Slime. Joel Hodgson created the show.

q: Who co-founded the YouTube Let's Play channel "Game Grumps" alongside Newgrounds animator Egoraptor?

q.e: Jon "JonTron" Jafari co-founded Game Grumps with Arin "Egoraptor" Hanson in 2012. He left in 2013 and Dan Avidan, from Ninja Sex Party, took his place.

q: What breed of dog is "Scooby Doo"?

q.e: Hanna-Barbera animator Iwao Takamoto designed Scooby-Doo as a Great Dane, deliberately giving him traits opposite to show dogs, such as bowed legs and a double chin.

q: In the Netflix show, Stranger Things, what song would Will sing to himself as he was missing?
Should I Stay or Should I Go?

q.e: Will sings The Clash's "Should I Stay or Should I Go" in Stranger Things while he is missing in the Upside Down. The song is a favorite of his brother Jonathan, and it features throughout the first season.

q: Who was the winner of the 2016 WWE Royal Rumble?

q.e: Triple H won the 2016 Royal Rumble, entering at number 30 and eliminating Roman Reigns last. It was his second Royal Rumble win.
Nickelodeon began as Pinwheel, a children's channel launched in 1977 on a Columbus, Ohio, cable system. It was renamed Nickelodeon in 1979.

q: In the Black Mirror episode "Bandersnatch", PAC-MAN stands for:

q.e: In the Black Mirror: Bandersnatch game within the film, PAC-MAN is explained as "Program and Control Man". The film lets viewers choose the story's path.

q: In the original Doctor Who series (1963), fourth doctor Tom Baker's scarf was how long?

q.e: Tom Baker's knitted scarf as the Fourth Doctor was famously huge, about 6 to 7 meters long in its original version. Its creator, Begonia Pope, had been given a lot of wool and kept knitting.

q: Which actor was not a major character in TV Show Freaks and Geeks?

q.e: Jonah Hill was not in Freaks and Geeks. The show starred Linda Cardellini, John Francis Daley, James Franco, Seth Rogen, Jason Segel and others, and ran for just one season in 1999-2000.

q: Alan Reed is known for providing the voice of which character?

q.e: Alan Reed provided the voice of Fred Flintstone in the original run of The Flintstones, including the catchphrase "Yabba Dabba Doo!". The show premiered in 1960.

q: When did Spongebob Squarepants first air?

q.e: SpongeBob SquarePants first aired on Nickelodeon on May 1, 1999. It was created by marine biologist and animator Stephen Hillenburg.

q: What actor portrays Hogan "Wash" Washburne in the TV Show Firefly?

q.e: Alan Tudyk played Hoban "Wash" Washburne, the pilot of Serenity, in Firefly. The sci-fi Western aired in 2002 and was cancelled after one season, but it returned as a film in 2005.

q: Out of the 3 Tots in Tots TV, who speaks French in the UK Version and Spanish in the US Version?

q.e: Tots TV, a British children's show from the 1990s, followed three rag-doll toddlers: Tilly, Tom and Tiny. It was shown in many countries, and some versions have the characters speak different languages.

q: What is the name of the race horse that Tony Soprano becomes attached to?

q.e: Pie-O-My is a racehorse owned by Ralph Cifaretto, whom Tony Soprano becomes fond of in the third season of The Sopranos. Tony's feelings for the horse are one of the show's rare tender moments.

q: In what year did "The Big Bang Theory" debut on CBS?

q.e: The Big Bang Theory premiered on CBS on September 24, 2007. It ran for 12 seasons and became one of the most-watched sitcoms of its time.

q: Which of the following figures did NOT have a cameo on "The Drew Carey Show" (1995-2004)?

q.e: The Drew Carey Show ran on ABC from 1995 to 2004 and was set in Cleveland, Ohio. It starred Drew Carey as an office worker and often featured guest stars.

q: Which of these television shows makes everyone look under their chair?

q.e: On a famous 2004 episode of The Oprah Winfrey Show, host Oprah Winfrey told every audience member to look under their seat, where they found car keys. She gave away 276 cars.

q: In the Sci-Fi television show Doctor Who, who plays the Tenth Doctor?

q.e: David Tennant portrayed the Tenth Doctor from 2005 to 2010 after Christopher Eccleston's Ninth Doctor regenerated. William Hartnell was the First Doctor in 1963, Peter Davison played the Fifth Doctor, and Peter Capaldi played the Twelfth.

q: The theme for the popular science fiction series "Doctor Who" was composed by who?

q.e: Ron Grainer composed the Doctor Who theme, and it was realized in 1963 by Delia Derbyshire of the BBC Radiophonic Workshop. It's one of the first TV themes to use electronic music.

q: In "Star Trek", who was the founder of the Klingon Empire and its philosophy?
Lady Lukara of the Great Hall

q.e: Kahless the Unforgettable is the founder of the Klingon Empire and its code of honor in Star Trek. According to legend, he fought a tyrant for 12 days and nights.

q: In season one of the US Kitchen Nightmares, Gordan Ramsay tried to save 10 different restaurants. How many ended up closing afterwards?

q.e: Kitchen Nightmares, Gordon Ramsay's show on Fox, began in the US in 2007 and was based on his UK series of the same name. Many of the restaurants he helped later closed, even after his makeovers.

q: In "Donkey Kong Country", why does Donkey Kong want to know the secret of the crystal coconut?
To find out where all the bananas are.

q.e: Donkey Kong Country, a 1990s TV series, was one of the first fully computer-animated cartoons and followed Donkey Kong and Diddy Kong. It was based on the Rare video game series of the same name.

q: What was the name of the inflatable duck sacrified to the crowd at the end of Episode 34 of the 18th season of Big Brother?

q.e: Big Brother's 18th US season aired on CBS in summer 2016. The show locks contestants in a house and evicts them one by one.

q: In 2008, British celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay believes he almost died after suffering what accident in Iceland while filming?
Slipping off a cliff, and nearly drowning in icy water
Crash landing when arriving at Keflavík airport
A minor car accident in a snowstorm
Being served under-cooked chicken at his hotel

q.e: In 2008, Gordon Ramsay was filming in Iceland when he slipped off a cliff into freezing water while hunting puffins, and he was lucky to survive. He has often talked about the scare.

q: What was the callsign of Commander William Adama in Battlestar Galactica (2004)?

q.e: "Husker" was Commander William Adama's call sign when he flew as a pilot in Battlestar Galactica (2004). The series was a darker retelling of the 1978 original.
In Phineas and Ferb, the bumbling villain is Dr. Heinz Doofenshmirtz, head of Doofenshmirtz Evil Incorporated. He was created and voiced by series co-creator Dan Povenmire.

q: What was the UK "Who Wants to be a Millionaire?" cheating scandal known as?

q.e: The UK Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? scandal involved Major Charles Ingram, who was convicted in 2003 of cheating his way to the top prize in 2001. Coughs from a person in the audience, Tecwen Whittock, had signaled him the right answers.

q: Which car tire manufacturer is famous for its "P Zero" line?

q.e: Pirelli is an Italian tire company founded in Milan in 1872. Its P Zero line is made for high-performance cars, and Pirelli has been Formula 1's exclusive tire supplier since 2011.

q: Where are the cars of the brand "Ferrari" manufactured?

q.e: Ferrari builds its cars in Maranello, Italy, where the company is based. Enzo Ferrari founded the racing team in 1929 and the first car carrying his name appeared in 1947.

q: What is the fastest road legal car in the world?

q.e: In 2017 a Koenigsegg Agera RS averaged about 284 mph on a closed stretch of Nevada highway, setting a production-car speed record at the time. New claims by other carmakers have followed since.

q: Which of the following vehicles from Ford is named after a WW2 Fighter Plane?

q.e: Ford stylist John Najjar proposed the name Mustang after the legendary World War II fighter plane, the North American P-51 Mustang. It debuted in April 1964 and created the 'pony car' class.

q: Which of these automotive brands originated in Sweden?

q.e: Volvo was founded in Gothenburg, Sweden, in 1927. Acura is a Japanese luxury marque launched by Honda, and Lincoln is an American brand under Ford.

q: What UK Train does NOT go over 125MPH?

q.e: "Sprinter" diesel trains are built for short regional trips and top out at roughly 75 to 90 mph. Faster InterCity 125 and Azuma trains can reach 125 mph.

q: The LS1 engine is how many cubic inches?

q.e: The General Motors LS1 is a 5.7-liter V8, which works out to about 346 cubic inches. It debuted in the 1997 Chevrolet Corvette and became a favorite for engine swaps.

q: Which car tire manufacturer is famous for its "Eagle" brand of tires, and is the official tire supplier of NASCAR?

q.e: Goodyear has supplied tires to NASCAR since 1954 and became its exclusive supplier for top series in 1997, branding its racing tires under the famous Eagle name.

q: What is the name of Nissan's most popular electric car?

q.e: Launched in 2010, the Nissan Leaf became the first mass-market, all-electric passenger car and had surpassed 650,000 global sales by 2023.

q: Automobiles produced by Tesla Motors operate on which form of energy?

q.e: Tesla designs and manufactures all-electric battery-powered vehicles, relying on rechargeable lithium-ion battery packs rather than internal combustion engines using petrol or diesel fuels.

q: How many wheels does a unicycle have?

q.e: The name unicycle comes from the Latin prefix uni-, meaning one, and the Greek word kyklos, meaning wheel. Vehicles with two wheels are bicycles, while three-wheeled versions are tricycles.

q: Which of these companies does NOT manufacture motorcycles?

q.e: Unlike its Japanese competitors Honda, Yamaha, and Kawasaki, which all have prominent motorcycle divisions, Toyota focuses strictly on automobiles and commercial vehicles.

q: During World War 2, with tank was the most fear by the allies?

q.e: The Panther (Panzerkampfwagen V) entered service in 1943 and combined thick sloped armor with a powerful long-barreled 75 mm gun, so Allied crews feared it. The heavier Tiger had a fearsome reputation too.

q: The Italian automaker Lamborghini uses what animal as its logo?

q.e: Founder Ferruccio Lamborghini chose a raging bull as the emblem because his astrological sign was Taurus and he held a lifelong passion for Spanish fighting bulls.

q: Jaguar Cars was previously owned by which car manfacturer?

q.e: Ford acquired Jaguar Cars in 1989 for roughly 2.5 billion dollars, managing it under its Premier Automotive Group until selling Jaguar and Land Rover to Tata Motors in 2008.

q: What are the cylinder-like parts that pump up and down within the engine?

q.e: Pistons move up and down inside an engine's cylinders, transferring the force of expanding combustion gases via connecting rods to the crankshaft.

q: Which of the following vehicles featured a full glass roof at base model?

q.e: The Renault Avantime, built from 2001 to 2003, had a huge glass roof and a coupe-minivan shape that was ahead of its time. It sold poorly and production ended after only a couple of years.

q: What was the first vehicle that came with air conditioning as a factory standard?

q.e: Packard offered the first factory-installed car air conditioning in 1939. It was a bulky and expensive option that few buyers chose, and it took decades before air conditioning became common.

q: Which country has the international vehicle registration letter 'A'?

q.e: Austria uses the vehicle registration code 'A', stemming from its English and Latin name. Australia uses 'AUS', Afghanistan uses 'AFG', and Armenia uses 'AM'.

q: What part of an automobile engine uses lobes to open and close intake and exhaust valves, and allows an air/fuel mixture into the engine?

q.e: A camshaft uses egg-shaped lobes to push valves open at precise moments in the combustion cycle, while the crankshaft converts piston movement into rotational force.

q: Which of the following passenger jets is the longest?

q.e: At about 76.3 meters long, the Boeing 747-8 is the longest passenger airliner ever built. It stretched the original 747 design to carry more passengers and cargo.

q: What do the 4 Rings in Audi's Logo represent?
States in which Audi makes the most sales
Countries in which Audi makes the most sales

q.e: Audi's four interlocking rings represent the 1932 merger of four independent German automobile manufacturers: Audi, DKW, Horch, and Wanderer, which formed Auto Union.

q: What country is the Hussarya supercar, made by the car manufacturer "Arrinera", assembled in?

q.e: The Arrinera Hussarya is a Polish supercar assembled in Poland. It was meant to be the country's first supercar, and its builders aimed at track performance.

q: Which of these cars is NOT considered one of the 5 Modern Supercars by Ferrari?

q.e: Ferrari's best-known supercars are the 288 GTO, F40, F50, Enzo and LaFerrari. The Testarossa of the 1980s was a famous grand tourer and sports car, but it is not on that list.

q: Which one is NOT the function of engine oil in car engines?

q.e: Engine oil provides lubrication, reduces friction, cools internal parts, and cleans debris, but it is not intended to burn. Fuel, such as gasoline or diesel, is what undergoes combustion to generate power.

q: Which car brand does NOT belong to General Motors?

q.e: Ford Motor Company was founded independently by Henry Ford in 1903. Buick, Cadillac, and Chevrolet are all divisions under General Motors.

q: Which of the following is NOT a Russian car manufacturer?

q.e: BYD is a Chinese company based in Shenzhen, and it is one of the world's biggest makers of electric vehicles. Russian car brands include Lada, GAZ and UAZ.

q: Which of the following countries has officially banned the civilian use of dash cams in cars?

q.e: Austria's privacy laws effectively ban private dash cams, with fines for recording in public. Rules differ a lot from country to country, so it is worth checking before using one abroad.
Cadillac was founded in 1902 by Henry Leland and named after Antoine de la Mothe Cadillac, who founded Detroit in 1701. It became General Motors' luxury brand in 1909.

q: Which one of the following is not made by Ford?

q.e: The Camry is a popular mid-size sedan manufactured by Toyota, whereas the F-150, Model A, and Fusion are all vehicles produced by the Ford Motor Company.

q: Enzo Ferrari was originally an auto racer for what manufacturer before founding his own car company?

q.e: Enzo Ferrari joined Alfa Romeo as a racing driver in 1920 before establishing Scuderia Ferrari in 1929 as Alfa Romeo's official racing division. He eventually began manufacturing his own cars under the Ferrari marque in 1947.

q: Which supercar company is from Sweden?

q.e: Koenigsegg was founded in 1994 by Christian von Koenigsegg in Ängelholm, Sweden, and is renowned for high-performance hypercars like the Jesko and Agera.

q: What nickname was given to Air Canada Flight 143 after it ran out of fuel and glided to safety in 1983?

q.e: On July 23, 1983, Air Canada Flight 143, a Boeing 767, ran out of fuel mid-air because of a pounds-versus-kilograms mix-up. The pilots glided it to a safe landing at a former air base in Gimli, Manitoba, earning the "Gimli Glider" nickname.

q: Which Japanese company is the world's largest manufacturer of motorcycles?

q.e: Honda has produced more than 400 million motorcycles since starting production in 1949 and has remained the world's largest motorcycle manufacturer since 1959.

q: What manufacturer made the car used in Back to the Future?

q.e: The time machine in Back to the Future was built from a 1981 DeLorean DMC-12, famous for its gull-wing doors and stainless-steel body panels.

q: Which one of the following is NOT a sub-company of the Volkswagen Group?

q.e: Opel is a German automotive brand owned by Stellantis, having previously been part of General Motors, whereas Porsche, Bentley, and Audi are brands within the Volkswagen Group.

q: What was the name of the first front-wheel-drive car produced by Datsun (now Nissan)?

q.e: The Datsun Cherry, launched in 1970, was the company's first front-wheel-drive car. Nissan later sold it in some markets under other names.

q: How much horsepower is produced by the SD40-2 Locomotive?

q.e: The EMD SD40-2 is a famous diesel-electric locomotive rated at about 3,000 horsepower, and it was built in large numbers from 1972 to 1989. It was so reliable that many are still in service today.

q: What kind of train was Stepney, a train on the Bluebell Railway notable for his appearance in "The Railway Series"?

q.e: Stepney is a real locomotive, an LB&SCR A1X "Terrier" tank engine built in 1875. He appears in the Reverend W. Awdry's Railway Series (Thomas the Tank Engine) and now runs on the Bluebell Railway in Sussex.

q: Which of these is NOT a car model produced by Malaysian car manufacturer Proton?

q.e: The Kelisa is a Perodua model, not a Proton. Perodua and Proton are Malaysia's two national car makers, and Proton's models include the Saga, Wira and Persona.

q: What car manufacturer gave away their patent for the seat-belt in the interest of saving lives?

q.e: Volvo engineer Nils Bohlin invented the modern three-point seat belt in 1959. Volvo opened the patent royalty-free to all automakers to encourage widespread vehicle safety adoption.

q: Which of the following FIA Rally cars was approved for use in the Group B class first?

q.e: Group B was a rally category that ran from 1982 to 1986 and allowed extremely powerful, lightly regulated cars like the Audi Quattro, Lancia 037 and Peugeot 205 T16. It was shut down after serious accidents.

q: Which Audi does not use Haldex based all wheel drive system?

q.e: The Audi A8 uses a Torsen-based quattro system rather than a Haldex clutch. Haldex was mostly used by Audi on smaller front-engine-sideways models, such as the A3 and TT.

q: In 2014, over 6 million General Motors vehicles were recalled due to what critical flaw?

q.e: In 2014 General Motors recalled millions of vehicles because a faulty ignition switch could turn off the engine and disable the airbags. It was linked to over 100 deaths and led to a large compensation fund.

q: What year did the Chevrolet LUV mini truck make its debut?

q.e: The Chevrolet LUV (Light Utility Vehicle) was a small pickup that first went on sale in 1972. It was built by Isuzu in Japan and sold under the Chevrolet name in the United States.

q: What model was the sports car gifted to Yuri Gagarin by the French government in 1965?

q.e: Yuri Gagarin, the first human in space, was given a Matra Djet sports car in 1965. It was a small French car with a mid-mounted engine and a fiberglass body.

q: Which Variable Valve Timing technology is used by BMW?

q.e: VANOS is BMW's variable valve timing system, first used in 1992. The name comes from the German "Variable Nockenwellensteuerung", or variable camshaft control.

q: Volkswagen's legendary VR6 engine has cylinders positioned at what degree angle?

q.e: The VR6 is a narrow-angle V6 whose cylinders sit at just 15 degrees, so it fits in a compact space like an inline engine. Volkswagen introduced it in 1991.

q: Which car is the first mass-produced hybrid vehicle?

q.e: The Toyota Prius launched in Japan in December 1997, becoming the world's first mass-produced gasoline-electric hybrid car before expanding globally in 2000.

q: What engine is in the Lexus SC400?

q.e: The Lexus SC400 uses the 1UZ-FE, a 4.0-liter V8 also found in the LS400 sedan. This engine is respected for its smoothness and long life.

q: What year was the game "Overwatch" revealed?

q.e: Blizzard revealed Overwatch at BlizzCon in November 2014, and the team shooter launched in May 2016. It grew out of the company's cancelled MMO project, Titan.

q: Who is the main protagonist of Dead Space?

q.e: Isaac Clarke is a ship systems engineer who battles mutated creatures called Necromorphs aboard the mining vessel USG Ishimura. His name combines science fiction authors Isaac Asimov and Arthur C. Clarke.

q: Which of the following is not a faction in Tom Clancy's The Division?

q.e: The Division (2016) is set in a New York overrun by a deadly virus released on Black Friday. Its enemy groups include Rioters, Cleaners, the Rikers and the Last Man Battalion, but the CDC is not one of its factions.

q: What was the name of the canceled projected by Blizzard Entertainment that would be later become Overwatch?

q.e: Project Titan was an unannounced massively multiplayer online game developed by Blizzard for several years before its cancellation in 2014, after which its core team repurposed its assets into Overwatch.

q: In Undertale, what's the prize for answering correctly?

q.e: Undertale is a 2015 indie RPG by Toby Fox, famous for its humor and for letting players spare enemies instead of fighting them. Its quirky dialogue and surprises are a big part of its charm.

q: In Minecraft, which two items must be combined to craft a torch?

q.e: Placing a stick in the crafting grid beneath a piece of coal (or charcoal) crafts four torches. Torches provide a light level of 14, preventing hostile mobs from spawning within that radius.

q: What minimum level in the Defence skill is needed to equip Dragon Armour in the MMO RuneScape?

q.e: In RuneScape, armor tiers require set Defence levels: rune armor needs level 40, and dragon armor needs level 60. Higher tiers are meant to take more time to unlock.

q: Before it's redesign of the company logo in the year 2000, which 3D shape is NOT represented in the Electronic Arts logo?

q.e: Before its 2000 redesign, the EA logo was a set of 3D shapes: a cube, a sphere and a cone. A cylinder was never part of it.

q: What does Solid Snake use to hide himself with?

q.e: The cardboard box is an iconic stealth tool introduced in the 1987 Metal Gear game, allowing Snake to slip past patrolling guards unnoticed as long as he stays still.

q: Who is the leader of Team Valor in Pokémon Go?

q.e: Candela is the leader of Team Valor in Pokémon Go, the red team. Blanche leads Team Mystic and Spark leads Team Instinct.

q: In Super Mario Bros., who informs Mario that the princess is in another castle?

q.e: After Mario defeats Bowser's decoy at the end of worlds 1 through 7 in Super Mario Bros., Toad delivers the famous line: 'Thank you Mario! But our princess is in another castle!' Princess Peach is only rescued after conquering World 8-4.

q: What is the name of the adventurer you meet at the mines in Stardew Valley?

q.e: In Stardew Valley, Marlon runs the Adventurer's Guild near the mines. He sells weapons and gives out rewards for slaying monsters.

q: What Nationality is D.Va from Overwatch?

q.e: D.Va, whose real name is Hana Song, is a former professional StarCraft esports player from Busan, South Korea, who pilots a mech for the MEKA squad.

q: In the game Nuclear Throne, what character is only usable in a play through with Melting?

q.e: Nuclear Throne is a fast top-down shooter and roguelike from Vlambeer, where each mutant character has its own abilities. Some characters only unlock after you meet particular conditions.

q: What were the first two blocks in "Minecraft"?

q.e: When Markus Persson created the earliest pre-classic build in May 2009 (initially called Cave Game), grass and cobblestone were the only blocks implemented to test rendering and physics.

q: What power does Max Caulfield from "Life is Strange" have?

q.e: Max Caulfield discovers her ability to rewind time in the opening chapter of the 2015 adventure game Life is Strange after witnessing the shooting of Chloe Price.

q: How many Chaos Emeralds are there in the "Sonic the Hedgehog" universe?

q.e: While the original 1991 Sega Genesis game featured only six Chaos Emeralds, Sonic the Hedgehog 2 introduced the seventh, which allows Sonic to transform into Super Sonic.

q: League of Legends, DOTA 2, Smite and Heroes of the Storm are all part of which game genre?

q.e: Multiplayer Online Battle Arena games originated as custom modifications of real-time strategy titles like StarCraft and Warcraft III, emphasizing single-character control over base management.

q: In the game Sonic Forces, which of the following was not from a previous game?

q.e: Infinite is the villain created for Sonic Forces (2017), a masked jackal who wields the Phantom Ruby. The other characters in the game had already appeared in earlier Sonic titles.

q: What happened to Half-Life 2 prior to its release, which resulted in Valve starting over the development of the game?
They weren't satisfied with the result
The story was not good enough
Way too many bugs to be fixed

q.e: In 2003, hackers stole Half-Life 2's source code and leaked it online, a major setback that contributed to the release being pushed back to November 2004. Valve and its president, Gabe Newell, publicly asked fans for help finding the culprit.

q: In the game Tom Clancy's Rainbow 6 Siege, what organization is Valkyrie from?

q.e: Valkyrie, from Rainbow Six Siege, is Meghan Castellano, a former US Navy SEAL. She deploys cameras that give her team extra information.

q: How many playable characters were there in Street Fighter II: Champion Edition?

q.e: Street Fighter II: Champion Edition (1992) made the four boss characters playable, bringing the roster to 12. It also allowed mirror matches, so two players could pick the same fighter.

q: Who's the creator of Geometry Dash?

q.e: Geometry Dash was made by Robert Topala, who goes by "RobTop", a Swedish developer. The rhythm-based platformer came out in 2013 and is known for being hard.

q: Who is credited with having created the world's first video game Easter Egg?

q.e: Warren Robinett secretly programmed the text 'Created by Warren Robinett' into a hidden room in the 1979 Atari 2600 game Adventure because Atari did not credit developers at the time.

q: What animal is featured in "Bloons TD Battles"?

q.e: In the Bloons tower defense series developed by Ninja Kiwi, players deploy various monkey towers, such as Dart Monkeys and Super Monkeys, to pop invading balloons.

q: In the beginning of the game "Sonic Adventure", what color Chaos Emerald does Tails own?

q.e: Sonic Adventure (1998) was Sonic's first fully 3D adventure on the Sega Dreamcast. It gave each of several characters, including Tails and Knuckles, their own storylines.

q: What is a Tetris piece called?

q.e: A tetromino is a geometric shape composed of four connected squares. Tetris creator Alexey Pajitnov named the game by combining the Greek numerical prefix tetra- (four) with tennis.

q: During the game's development, what was the first ever created Pokémon?

q.e: The Rhyhorn family, Rhyhorn and its evolution Rhydon, is usually named as the first Pokémon designed during development. It was drawn by Kouji Nishino for the original Game Boy games.

q: The character Wario was first introduced in which game of the Mario video game franchise?

q.e: Wario debuted as the main antagonist and final boss in the 1992 Game Boy title Super Mario Land 2: 6 Golden Coins before starring as the protagonist in 1994's Wario Land.

q: In Monster Hunter Generations, which of the following monsters are a part of the "Fated Four"?

q.e: The "Fated Four" in Monster Hunter Generations are Mizutsune, Astalos, Gammoth and Glavenus. Astalos is an electric flying wyvern that looks like a bat-winged dragon.

q: In "Clash Royale" what is Arena 4 called?

q.e: Clash Royale's arenas are themed battlegrounds you unlock as you earn trophies, and their order has changed over time as updates added new ones. Spell Valley is one of the early arenas.

q: What were the first two Pokémon games released?

q.e: Pocket Monsters: Red and Green debuted in Japan on February 27, 1996. The Blue version was released in Japan later that year with updated code, which served as the basis for the international Red and Blue releases in 1998.

q: How many stars are there to collect in Super Mario 64?

q.e: Super Mario 64 features 120 Power Stars: 105 across 15 main courses (7 per course) and 15 secret castle stars. Collecting all 120 unlocks the cannon outside the castle that launches Mario to the roof to meet Yoshi.

q: In Minecraft: Java Edition, which of the following feature/block was added to Survival mode in Beta 1.3?

q.e: Beds were added in Minecraft Beta 1.3 in 2011. Sleeping skips the night and sets your spawn point.

q: In the Mario series, which game introduced Mario's Backflip ability?

q.e: Mario's backflip first appeared in the 1994 Game Boy version of Donkey Kong, which began as a remake of the arcade game and then added around 100 levels. Super Mario 64 later made the move famous.

q: Which team won the first Overwatch League championship?

q.e: The London Spitfire won the first Overwatch League championship in 2018, beating the Philadelphia Fusion in the Grand Finals. The league used a city-based team format similar to traditional sports.

q: In Overwatch, how old is Reinhardt Wilhelm?

q.e: Reinhardt Wilhelm, Overwatch's armored German knight, is 61 years old. He is a veteran of the Omnic Crisis who fights with a rocket hammer and a large energy shield.

q: What was the name of the Secret Organization in the Hotline Miami series?

q.e: In Hotline Miami, a shadowy group called the 50 Blessings sends coded phone messages that set up the protagonist's violent missions. The game's neon style and soundtrack are widely praised.

q: Which horror movie had a sequel in the form of a video game released in August 20, 2002?

q.e: The Thing, a 2002 game, was a sequel to John Carpenter's 1982 horror film of the same name. It continued the movie's story of an alien that can imitate people.

q: Which musical artist was NOT featured as playable avatars in the game "DJ Hero"?

q.e: DJ Hero (2009) was a rhythm game with a turntable controller, featuring avatars of real DJs and artists like Daft Punk, Grandmaster Flash and DJ Shadow. Dr. Dre was not one of the playable avatars.

q: In the game Destiny, who succeeded Peter Dinklage in voicing the protagonist's "Ghost"?

q.e: Nolan North replaced Peter Dinklage as the voice of Ghost, the companion robot in Destiny. Dinklage's flat delivery was widely mocked by fans, and Bungie re-recorded the lines for Destiny 2.

q: Which puzzle game was designed by a Russian programmer, featuring Russian buildings and music?

q.e: Tetris was created in 1985 by Russian software engineer Alexey Pajitnov at the Academy of Sciences in Moscow. Later editions famously incorporated the Russian folk tune Korobeiniki and images of Saint Basil's Cathedral.

q: In "Sonic the Hedgehog 2" for the Sega Genesis, what do you input in the sound test screen to access the secret level select?
The first release date of "Sonic the Hedgehog"
The date Sonic Team was founded
The first release date of "Sonic the Hedgehog 2"

q.e: On the Sega Genesis, entering the sound-test numbers 19, 65, 09, 17 unlocks the level select in Sonic the Hedgehog 2. Those numbers are the September 17, 1965, birthday of Sonic Team's lead programmer, Yuji Naka.

q: Which gaming series includes "The Diabolical Box" and "The Curious Village"?

q.e: Developed by Level-5, the Professor Layton series follows archaeologist Hershel Layton and his apprentice Luke Triton as they solve logic puzzles to unravel town mysteries.

q: Which Kingdom Hearts game featured the cast of "The World Ends With You"?

q.e: Kingdom Hearts 3D: Dream Drop Distance (2012) included characters from The World Ends With You, including Neku. Both games were made by Square Enix.

q: Where are Terror Fiends more commonly found in the Nintendo game Miitopia?

q.e: Miitopia is a Nintendo role-playing game for the 3DS where the cast is made from Mii characters, so friends, family and celebrities can play the heroes. Monsters called Terror Fiends appear in specific regions of the game.

q: What was the world's first video game?

q.e: A draughts (checkers) program written by Christopher Strachey around 1951 and 1952 is counted among the first computer games. OXO (1952) and Tennis for Two (1958) are also often called the first.

q: In the Animal Crossing series, which flower is erroneously called the "Jacob's Ladder"?

q.e: In Animal Crossing, players can grow and cross-breed flowers, and in-game descriptions can use informal or alternate names. Lily of the valley is a white, bell-shaped flower in the games.

q: In the Nintendo Game Splatoon 2, what is Marina's screen name?

q.e: Marina is half of the in-game pop duo Off the Hook in Splatoon 2, with Pearl. She uses the DJ name "DJ Hyperfresh".

q: Which one of these characters appeared in Marvel vs Capcom: Infinite?

q.e: Marvel vs. Capcom: Infinite (2017) brings Marvel and Capcom fighters together in two-character teams that use the powers of the Infinity Stones. Its roster mixes comic-book heroes with video-game icons.
